IsBot.code: IsBot.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] (a : α) : Prop
IsBot.comment:
`a : α` is a bottom element of `α` if it is less than or equal to any other element of `α`.
This predicate is roughly an unbundled version of `OrderBot`, except that a preorder may have
several bottom elements. When `α` is linear, this is useful to make a case disjunction on
`NoMinOrder α` within a proof.
IsBot.fullDefinition: def IsBot (a : α) : Prop :=   ∀ b, a ≤ b
IsBot.description: An element in a partially ordered set is considered a bottom element if it is less than or equal to every other element in that set.

IsTop.code: IsTop.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] (a : α) : Prop
IsTop.comment:
`a : α` is a top element of `α` if it is greater than or equal to any other element of `α`.
This predicate is roughly an unbundled version of `OrderBot`, except that a preorder may have
several top elements. When `α` is linear, this is useful to make a case disjunction on
`NoMaxOrder α` within a proof.
IsTop.fullDefinition: def IsTop (a : α) : Prop :=   ∀ b, b ≤ a
IsTop.description: An element in a partially ordered set is considered a top element if it is greater than or equal to every other element in that set.

IsMin.code: IsMin.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] (a : α) : Prop
IsMin.comment:
`a` is a minimal element of `α` if no element is strictly less than it. We spell it without `<`
to avoid having to convert between `≤` and `<`. Instead, `isMin_iff_forall_not_lt` does the
conversion.
IsMin.fullDefinition: def IsMin (a : α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ≤ a → a ≤ b
IsMin.description: An element is considered minimal in a partially ordered set if there is no other element that is strictly smaller than it.

IsMax.code: IsMax.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] (a : α) : Prop
IsMax.comment:
`a` is a maximal element of `α` if no element is strictly greater than it. We spell it without
`<` to avoid having to convert between `≤` and `<`. Instead, `isMax_iff_forall_not_lt` does the
conversion.
IsMax.fullDefinition: def IsMax (a : α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃b⦄, a ≤ b → b ≤ a
IsMax.description: An element in a partially ordered set is considered maximal if there is no other element that is strictly greater than it.

Monotone.code: Monotone.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : Prop
Monotone.comment: A function `f` is monotone if `a ≤ b` implies `f a ≤ f b`.
Monotone.fullDefinition: def Monotone (f : α → β) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃a b⦄, a ≤ b → f a ≤ f b
Monotone.description: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

Antitone.code: Antitone.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : Prop
Antitone.comment: A function `f` is antitone if `a ≤ b` implies `f b ≤ f a`.
Antitone.fullDefinition: def Antitone (f : α → β) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃a b⦄, a ≤ b → f b ≤ f a
Antitone.description: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.

MonotoneOn.code: MonotoneOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop
MonotoneOn.comment: A function `f` is monotone on `s` if, for all `a, b ∈ s`, `a ≤ b` implies `f a ≤ f b`.
MonotoneOn.fullDefinition: def MonotoneOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃a⦄ (_ : a ∈ s) ⦃b⦄ (_ : b ∈ s), a ≤ b → f a ≤ f b
MonotoneOn.description: A function is considered monotone on a set if, whenever two inputs from that set relate in terms of order, the outputs corresponding to those inputs maintain the same order relationship.

AntitoneOn.description: A function is considered antitone on a set if, whenever two inputs from that set relate in terms of order, the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.

StrictMono.description: A function is considered strictly monotone if it maintains the order relationship such that whenever one input is strictly less than another, the output corresponding to the first input is also strictly less than the output corresponding to the second input.

  [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder β] {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (h : AntitoneOn f s) (hl : BddBelow (f '' s))
  (hu : BddAbove (f '' s)) : ∃ g, Antitone g ∧ EqOn f g s
AntitoneOn.exists_antitone_extension.comment:
If a function is antitone and is bounded on a set `s`, then it admits an antitone extension to
the whole space.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.BddBelow: This definition states that a set is considered bounded below if there exists at least one element that serves as a lower bound for all elements in the set within a preorder structure.
explanatories.BddAbove: This definition states that a set is considered bounded above if there exists at least one element that serves as an upper bound for all elements in the set within a preorder structure.
explanatories.Set.EqOn: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.

AntitoneOn.exists_antitone_extension.description: If a function is antitone on a bounded set, then it can be extended to an antitone function defined on the entire space.

Monotone.seq_le_seq.code:
Monotone.seq_le_seq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x y : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f) (n : ℕ)
  (h₀ : x 0 ≤ y 0) (hx : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → x (k + 1) ≤ f (x k)) (hy : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → f (y k) ≤ y (k + 1)) :
  x n ≤ y n
Monotone.seq_le_seq.description: If a monotone function is applied to two sequences under certain conditions, the value of the first sequence at a given index will be less than or equal to the value of the second sequence at the same index.

Monotone.seq_pos_lt_seq_of_lt_of_le.code:
Monotone.seq_pos_lt_seq_of_lt_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x y : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f)
  {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (h₀ : x 0 ≤ y 0) (hx : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → x (k + 1) < f (x k))
  (hy : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → f (y k) ≤ y (k + 1)) : x n < y n
Monotone.seq_pos_lt_seq_of_lt_of_le.description: If a monotone function is applied to two sequences under certain conditions, the value of the first sequence at a given index will be strictly less than the value of the second sequence at the same index when the first sequence starts less than or equal to the second.

Monotone.seq_pos_lt_seq_of_le_of_lt.code:
Monotone.seq_pos_lt_seq_of_le_of_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x y : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f)
  {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (h₀ : x 0 ≤ y 0) (hx : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → x (k + 1) ≤ f (x k))
  (hy : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → f (y k) < y (k + 1)) : x n < y n
Monotone.seq_pos_lt_seq_of_le_of_lt.description: If a monotone function is applied to two sequences under certain conditions, the value of the first sequence at a given index will be strictly less than the value of the second sequence at the same index when the first sequence starts less than or equal to the second and the second sequence has strictly increasing values.

Monotone.seq_lt_seq_of_lt_of_le.code:
Monotone.seq_lt_seq_of_lt_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x y : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f) (n : ℕ)
  (h₀ : x 0 < y 0) (hx : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → x (k + 1) < f (x k)) (hy : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → f (y k) ≤ y (k + 1)) :
  x n < y n
Monotone.seq_lt_seq_of_lt_of_le.description: If a monotone function is applied to two sequences under certain conditions, the value of the first sequence at a given index will be strictly less than the value of the second sequence at the same index when the first sequence starts strictly less than the second.

Monotone.seq_lt_seq_of_le_of_lt.code:
Monotone.seq_lt_seq_of_le_of_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x y : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f) (n : ℕ)
  (h₀ : x 0 < y 0) (hx : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → x (k + 1) ≤ f (x k)) (hy : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < n → f (y k) < y (k + 1)) :
  x n < y n
Monotone.seq_lt_seq_of_le_of_lt.description: If a monotone function is applied to two sequences under certain conditions, the value of the first sequence at a given index will be strictly less than the value of the second sequence at the same index when the first sequence starts strictly less than the second and the first sequence has non-decreasing values while the second sequence has strictly increasing values.

Monotone.le_iterate_comp_of_le.code:
Monotone.le_iterate_comp_of_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {β : Type u_2} {g : β → β} {h : β → α}
  (hf : Monotone f) (H : h ∘ g ≤ f ∘ h) (n : ℕ) : h ∘ g^[n] ≤ f^[n] ∘ h
Monotone.le_iterate_comp_of_le.description: If a monotone function satisfies a certain composition inequality with another function, then the n-th iterate of the composition of the second function with a third function will be less than or equal to the n-th iterate of the first function composed with the third function.

Monotone.iterate_comp_le_of_le.code:
Monotone.iterate_comp_le_of_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {β : Type u_2} {g : β → β} {h : β → α}
  (hf : Monotone f) (H : f ∘ h ≤ h ∘ g) (n : ℕ) : f^[n] ∘ h ≤ h ∘ g^[n]
Monotone.iterate_comp_le_of_le.description: If a monotone function is applied iteratively under specific conditions, the composition of this function with another function will be less than or equal to the composition of a different function also applied iteratively.

Monotone.iterate_le_of_le.code:
Monotone.iterate_le_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f g : α → α} (hf : Monotone f) (h : f ≤ g) (n : ℕ) :
  f^[n] ≤ g^[n]
Monotone.iterate_le_of_le.comment: If `f ≤ g` and `f` is monotone, then `f^[n] ≤ g^[n]`.
Monotone.iterate_le_of_le.description: If one monotone function is less than or equal to another, then the n-th iterate of the first function will also be less than or equal to the n-th iterate of the second function.

Monotone.le_iterate_of_le.code:
Monotone.le_iterate_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f g : α → α} (hg : Monotone g) (h : f ≤ g) (n : ℕ) :
  f^[n] ≤ g^[n]
Monotone.le_iterate_of_le.comment: If `f ≤ g` and `g` is monotone, then `f^[n] ≤ g^[n]`.
Monotone.le_iterate_of_le.description: If one function is less than or equal to another and the second function is monotone, then the n-th iterate of the first function will also be less than or equal to the n-th iterate of the second function.

Function.id_le_iterate_of_id_le.code: Function.id_le_iterate_of_id_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} (h : id ≤ f) (n : ℕ) : id ≤ f^[n]
Function.id_le_iterate_of_id_le.comment:
If $x ≤ f x$ for all $x$ (we write this as `id ≤ f`), then the same is true for any iterate
`f^[n]` of `f`.
Function.id_le_iterate_of_id_le.description: If the identity function isless than or equal to another function for all inputs, then this relationship also holds for any iterate of that function.

Function.iterate_le_id_of_le_id.code: Function.iterate_le_id_of_le_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} (h : f ≤ id) (n : ℕ) : f^[n] ≤ id
Function.iterate_le_id_of_le_id.description: If a function is less than or equal to the identity function, then its n-th iterate will also be less than or equal to the identity function.

Function.monotone_iterate_of_id_le.code: Function.monotone_iterate_of_id_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} (h : id ≤ f) : Monotone fun m => f^[m]
Function.monotone_iterate_of_id_le.description: If a function is greater than or equal to the identity function, then its multiple iterations will form a monotone sequence.

Function.antitone_iterate_of_le_id.code: Function.antitone_iterate_of_le_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} (h : f ≤ id) : Antitone fun m => f^[m]
Function.antitone_iterate_of_le_id.description: If a function is less than or equal to the identity function, then its iterates form a non-increasing sequence.

Function.Commute.iterate_le_of_map_le.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_le_of_map_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : Monotone f) (hg : Monotone g) {x : α} (hx : f x ≤ g x) (n : ℕ) : f^[n] x ≤ g^[n] x
Function.Commute.iterate_le_of_map_le.description: If two monotone functions commute and one function maps a value to something less than or equal to what the other function maps it to, then the n-th iterate of the first function at that value will also be less than or equal to the n-th iterate of the second function at the same value.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_of_map_l.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_of_map_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : Monotone f) (hg : StrictMono g) {x : α} (hx : f x < g x) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x < g^[n] x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_of_map_l.description: If two functions commute, one function is monotone, the other is strictly monotone, and the first function maps a value to something less than what the second function maps it to, then the n-th iterate of the first function at that value will also remain less than the n-th iterate of the second function at the same value, provided n is positive.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_of_map_l.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_of_map_lt'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : StrictMono f) (hg : Monotone g) {x : α} (hx : f x < g x) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x < g^[n] x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_of_map_l.description: If two functions commute, the first function is strictly monotone, the second function is monotone, and the first function maps a value to something less than what the second function maps it to, then the n-th iterate of the first function at that value will also remain less than the n-th iterate of the second function at the same value, provided n is positive.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_iff_map_.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_iff_map_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : Monotone f) (hg : StrictMono g) {x : α} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x < g^[n] x ↔ f x < g x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_iff_map_.description: If two functions commute, the first function is monotone and the second function is strictly monotone, then the n-th iterate of the first function at a value is less than the n-th iterate of the second function at that value if and only if the first function at that value is less than the second function at the same value, provided n is positive.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_iff_map_.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_iff_map_lt'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : StrictMono f) (hg : Monotone g) {x : α} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x < g^[n] x ↔ f x < g x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_lt_iff_map_.description: If two functions commute, the first function is strictly monotone and the second function is monotone, then the n-th iterate of the first function at a value is less than the n-th iterate of the second function at that value if and only if the first function at that value is less than the second function at the same value, provided n is positive.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_le_iff_map_.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_le_iff_map_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : Monotone f) (hg : StrictMono g) {x : α} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x ≤ g^[n] x ↔ f x ≤ g x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_le_iff_map_.description: If two functions commute, the first function is monotone, the second function is strictly monotone, and n is positive, then the n-th iterate of the first function at a value is less than or equal to the n-th iterate of the second function at that value if and only if the first function at that value is less than or equal to the second function at the same value.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_le_iff_map_.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_le_iff_map_le'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : StrictMono f) (hg : Monotone g) {x : α} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x ≤ g^[n] x ↔ f x ≤ g x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_le_iff_map_.description: Under certain conditions, the n-th iterate of one function will be less than or equal to the n-th iterate of another function if and only if the first function evaluated at a point is less than or equal to the second function evaluated at the same point.

Function.Commute.iterate_pos_eq_iff_map_.code:
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_eq_iff_map_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {f g : α → α} (h : Commute f g)
  (hf : Monotone f) (hg : StrictMono g) {x : α} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : f^[n] x = g^[n] x ↔ f x = g x
Function.Commute.iterate_pos_eq_iff_map_.description: If two functions commute under certain monotonicity conditions, then the n-th iterate of the first function at a point equals the n-th iterate of the second function at that point if and only if the two functions produce the same value at that point.

Monotone.monotone_iterate_of_le_map.code:
Monotone.monotone_iterate_of_le_map.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : Monotone f)
  (hx : x ≤ f x) : Monotone fun n => f^[n] x
Monotone.monotone_iterate_of_le_map.comment:
If `f` is a monotone map and `x ≤ f x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x` form
a monotone sequence.
Monotone.monotone_iterate_of_le_map.description: If a function is monotone and its initial value is less than or equal to its image under that function, then the iterates of that function at that value will form a monotone sequence.

Monotone.antitone_iterate_of_map_le.code:
Monotone.antitone_iterate_of_map_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : Monotone f)
  (hx : f x ≤ x) : Antitone fun n => f^[n] x
Monotone.antitone_iterate_of_map_le.comment:
If `f` is a monotone map and `f x ≤ x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x` form
an antitone sequence.
Monotone.antitone_iterate_of_map_le.description: If a monotone function applied to a value is less than or equal to that value, then the sequence of its successive iterates at that value will be antitone.

StrictMono.strictMono_iterate_of_lt_map.code:
StrictMono.strictMono_iterate_of_lt_map.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : StrictMono f)
  (hx : x < f x) : StrictMono fun n => f^[n] x
StrictMono.strictMono_iterate_of_lt_map.comment:
If `f` is a strictly monotone map and `x < f x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x`
form a strictly monotone sequence.
StrictMono.strictMono_iterate_of_lt_map.description: If a function is strictly monotone and its initial value is less than its image under that function, then the iterates of that function at that value will form a strictly monotone sequence.

StrictMono.strictAnti_iterate_of_map_lt.code:
StrictMono.strictAnti_iterate_of_map_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : StrictMono f)
  (hx : f x < x) : StrictAnti fun n => f^[n] x
StrictMono.strictAnti_iterate_of_map_lt.comment:
If `f` is a strictly antitone map and `f x < x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x`
form a strictly antitone sequence.
StrictMono.strictAnti_iterate_of_map_lt.description: If a strictly monotone function maps a value to something less than itself, then its successive iterations at that value will form a strictly decreasing sequence.

SemilatticeSup.mk'.code:
SemilatticeSup.mk'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Sup α] (sup_comm : ∀ (a b : α), a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a)
  (sup_assoc : ∀ (a b c : α), a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)) (sup_idem : ∀ (a : α), a ⊔ a = a) : SemilatticeSup α
SemilatticeSup.mk'.comment:
A type with a commutative, associative and idempotent binary `sup` operation has the structure of a
join-semilattice.

The partial order is defined so that `a ≤ b` unfolds to `a ⊔ b = b`; cf. `sup_eq_right`.
SemilatticeSup.mk'.fullDefinition: def SemilatticeSup.mk' {α : Type*} [Sup α] (sup_comm : ∀ a b : α, a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a)     (sup_assoc : ∀ a b c : α, a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)) (sup_idem : ∀ a : α, a ⊔ a = a) :     SemilatticeSup α where   sup := (· ⊔ ·)   le a b := a ⊔ b = b   le_refl := sup_idem   le_trans a b c hab hbc := by dsimp; rw [← hbc, ← sup_assoc, hab]   le_antisymm a b hab hba := by rwa [← hba, sup_comm]   le_sup_left a b := by dsimp; rw [← sup_assoc, sup_idem]   le_sup_right a b := by dsimp; rw [sup_comm, sup_assoc, sup_idem]   sup_le a b c hac hbc := by dsimp; rwa [sup_assoc, hbc]
SemilatticeSup.mk'.description: A type equipped with a commutative, associative, and idempotent binary operation for the supremum forms the structure of a join-semilattice.

SemilatticeSup.le_sup_left.code: SemilatticeSup.le_sup_left.{u} {α : Type u} [self : SemilatticeSup α] (a b : α) : a ≤ a ⊔ b
SemilatticeSup.le_sup_left.comment: The supremum is an upper bound on the first argument
SemilatticeSup.le_sup_left.description: The supremum of two elements serves as an upper bound for the first element.

le_sup_left.code: le_sup_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a ≤ a ⊔ b

explanatories.SemilatticeSup.le_sup_left: The supremum of two elements serves as an upper bound for the first element.

le_sup_left.description: The supremum of two elements serves as an upper bound for the first element.

SemilatticeSup.le_sup_right.code: SemilatticeSup.le_sup_right.{u} {α : Type u} [self : SemilatticeSup α] (a b : α) : b ≤ a ⊔ b
SemilatticeSup.le_sup_right.comment: The supremum is an upper bound on the second argument
SemilatticeSup.le_sup_right.description: The supremum of two elements acts as an upper bound for the second element.

le_sup_right.code: le_sup_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : b ≤ a ⊔ b

explanatories.SemilatticeSup.le_sup_right: The supremum of two elements acts as an upper bound for the second element.

le_sup_right.description: The supremum of two elements serves as an upper bound for the second element.

le_sup_of_le_left.code: le_sup_of_le_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} (h : c ≤ a) : c ≤ a ⊔ b
le_sup_of_le_left.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, it is also less than or equal to the supremum of that element and a third element.

le_sup_of_le_right.code: le_sup_of_le_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} (h : c ≤ b) : c ≤ a ⊔ b
le_sup_of_le_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, it is also less than or equal to their supremum with a third element.

lt_sup_of_lt_left.code: lt_sup_of_lt_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} (h : c < a) : c < a ⊔ b
lt_sup_of_lt_left.description: If one element is less than another, it is also less than the supremum of that element and a third element.

lt_sup_of_lt_right.code: lt_sup_of_lt_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} (h : c < b) : c < a ⊔ b
lt_sup_of_lt_right.description: If one element is less than another, it is also less than the supremum of that element and a third element.

SemilatticeSup.sup_le.code: SemilatticeSup.sup_le.{u} {α : Type u} [self : SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ≤ c → b ≤ c → a ⊔ b ≤ c
SemilatticeSup.sup_le.comment: The supremum is the *least* upper bound
SemilatticeSup.sup_le.description: The supremum of two elements is the least upper bound for those elements.

sup_le.code: sup_le.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} : a ≤ c → b ≤ c → a ⊔ b ≤ c

explanatories.SemilatticeSup.sup_le: The supremum of two elements is the least upper bound for those elements.

sup_le.description: If two elements are each less than or equal to a third element, then their supremum is also less than or equal to that third element.

sup_le_iff.code: sup_le_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} : a ⊔ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ c ∧ b ≤ c
sup_le_iff.description: The supremum of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if and only if each of the two elements is less than or equal to that third element.

sup_eq_left.code: sup_eq_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a ⊔ b = a ↔ b ≤ a
sup_eq_left.description: The supremum of two elements equals the first element if and only if the second element is less than or equal to the first.

sup_eq_right.code: sup_eq_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a ⊔ b = b ↔ a ≤ b
sup_eq_right.description: The supremum of two elements equals the second element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the second.

left_eq_sup.code: left_eq_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a = a ⊔ b ↔ b ≤ a
left_eq_sup.description: An element is equal to the supremum of itself and another element if and only if that other element is less than or equal to it.

right_eq_sup.code: right_eq_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : b = a ⊔ b ↔ a ≤ b
right_eq_sup.description: The equality of an element with its supremum and that element implies that the element is less than or equal to the supremum.

sup_of_le_left.code: sup_of_le_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : b ≤ a → a ⊔ b = a
sup_of_le_left.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, their supremum is equal to the larger element.

sup_of_le_right.code: sup_of_le_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a ≤ b → a ⊔ b = b
sup_of_le_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, their supremum is equal to the larger element.

le_of_sup_eq.code: le_of_sup_eq.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a ⊔ b = b → a ≤ b
le_of_sup_eq.description: If the supremum of two elements is equal to one of them, then that element is less than or equal to the other.

left_lt_sup.code: left_lt_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a < a ⊔ b ↔ ¬b ≤ a
left_lt_sup.description: One element is less than the supremum of itself and another element if and only if the second element is not less than or equal to the first.

right_lt_sup.code: right_lt_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : b < a ⊔ b ↔ ¬a ≤ b
right_lt_sup.description: The statement describes a condition where one element is less than the supremum of itself and another element if and only if the first element is not less than or equal to the second element.

left_or_right_lt_sup.code: left_or_right_lt_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} (h : a ≠ b) : a < a ⊔ b ∨ b < a ⊔ b
left_or_right_lt_sup.description: If two elements are distinct, then at least one of them is less than their supremum.

le_iff_exists_sup.code: le_iff_exists_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} : a ≤ b ↔ ∃ c, b = a ⊔ c
le_iff_exists_sup.description: An element is less than or equal to another if and only if there exists a third element such that the second element equals the supremum of the first element and that third element.

sup_le_sup.code: sup_le_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c d : α} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (h₂ : c ≤ d) : a ⊔ c ≤ b ⊔ d
sup_le_sup.description: The supremum of two elements is less than or equal to the supremum of their respective upper bounds.

sup_le_sup_left.code: sup_le_sup_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (c : α) : c ⊔ a ≤ c ⊔ b
sup_le_sup_left.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, then the supremum of a third element with the first is less than or equal to the supremum of that third element with the second.

sup_le_sup_right.code: sup_le_sup_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (c : α) : a ⊔ c ≤ b ⊔ c
sup_le_sup_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, then the supremum of the first element and any third element is less than or equal to the supremum of the second element and that same third element.

sup_idem.code: sup_idem.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a : α) : a ⊔ a = a
sup_idem.description: The supremum of an element with itself is equal to that element.

sup_comm.code: sup_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a
sup_comm.description: The supremum of two elements is commutative, meaning that the order in which they are considered does not affect their least upper bound.

sup_assoc.code: sup_assoc.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)
sup_assoc.description: The supremum operation is associative, meaning the supremum of three elements can be computed in any grouping.

sup_left_right_swap.code: sup_left_right_swap.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ b ⊔ c = c ⊔ b ⊔ a
sup_left_right_swap.description: The supremum operation is associative with respect to the order of elements being combined.

sup_left_idem.code: sup_left_idem.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ (a ⊔ b) = a ⊔ b
sup_left_idem.description: Taking the supremum of one element and the supremum of that element with another results in the same value as just taking the supremum of the two elements.

sup_right_idem.code: sup_right_idem.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ b ⊔ b = a ⊔ b
sup_right_idem.description: Taking the supremum of an element and another distinct element twice is equivalent to taking it once.

sup_left_comm.code: sup_left_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ (b ⊔ c) = b ⊔ (a ⊔ c)
sup_left_comm.description: The supremum operation is commutative when applied to three elements in a semilattice.

sup_right_comm.code: sup_right_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ c ⊔ b
sup_right_comm.description: The supremum of three elements can be rearranged without changing the result.

sup_sup_sup_comm.code: sup_sup_sup_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c d : α) : a ⊔ b ⊔ (c ⊔ d) = a ⊔ c ⊔ (b ⊔ d)
sup_sup_sup_comm.description: The supremum of two pairs of elements is invariant under swapping the second elements within each pair.

sup_sup_distrib_left.code: sup_sup_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ (b ⊔ c) = a ⊔ b ⊔ (a ⊔ c)
sup_sup_distrib_left.description: The supremum operation distributes over the supremum of a sum from the left.

sup_sup_distrib_right.code: sup_sup_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ c ⊔ (b ⊔ c)
sup_sup_distrib_right.description: Taking the supremum of two elements with a third results in the same value as taking the supremum of the first element with the third and then the supremum of the second element with the third.

sup_congr_left.code: sup_congr_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} (hb : b ≤ a ⊔ c) (hc : c ≤ a ⊔ b) : a ⊔ b = a ⊔ c
sup_congr_left.description: If one element is less than or equal to the supremum of two other elements and vice versa, then the supremum of the first two elements is equal to the supremum of the first and third elements.

sup_congr_right.code: sup_congr_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ b ⊔ c) (hb : b ≤ a ⊔ c) : a ⊔ c = b ⊔ c
sup_congr_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to the supremum of two other elements and the second element is also less than or equal to the same supremum, then the supremum of the first element and the third element is equal to the supremum of the second element and the third element.

sup_eq_sup_iff_left.code: sup_eq_sup_iff_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} : a ⊔ b = a ⊔ c ↔ b ≤ a ⊔ c ∧ c ≤ a ⊔ b
sup_eq_sup_iff_left.description: The equality of the supremum of two elements with a third element is equivalent to both the first and third elements being upper bounds for each other with respect to the supremum of the first element.

sup_eq_sup_iff_right.code: sup_eq_sup_iff_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b c : α} : a ⊔ c = b ⊔ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c
sup_eq_sup_iff_right.description: The equality of the supremum of two pairs of elements is equivalent to each element being less than or equal to the supremum of the other pair.

Ne.lt_sup_or_lt_sup.code: Ne.lt_sup_or_lt_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) : a < a ⊔ b ∨ b < a ⊔ b
Ne.lt_sup_or_lt_sup.description: If two elements are distinct, then at least one of them is less than their supremum.

SemilatticeSup.ext.description: Two semilattices are equal if and only if they have the same ordering relation for all their elements.

ite_le_sup.code: ite_le_sup.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] (s s' : α) (P : Prop) [Decidable P] : (if P then s else s') ≤ s ⊔ s'

SemilatticeInf.inf_le_right.comment: The infimum is a lower bound on the second argument
SemilatticeInf.inf_le_right.description: The infimum of two elements is less than or equal to the second element.

SemilatticeInf.le_inf.comment: The infimum is the *greatest* lower bound
SemilatticeInf.le_inf.description: If one element is less than or equal to two others, it is also less than or equal to their infimum.

OrderDual.instSemilatticeSup.fullDefinition: instance OrderDual.instSemilatticeSup (α) [SemilatticeInf α] : SemilatticeSup αᵒᵈ where   __ := inferInstanceAs (PartialOrder αᵒᵈ)   __ := inferInstanceAs (Sup αᵒᵈ)   le_sup_left := @SemilatticeInf.inf_le_left α _   le_sup_right := @SemilatticeInf.inf_le_right α _   sup_le := fun _ _ _ hca hcb => @SemilatticeInf.le_inf α _ _ _ _ hca hcb

inf_le_of_left_le.description: If one element is less than or equal to a third element, then it is also less than or equal to the infimum of itself and a second element.

inf_le_of_right_le.code: inf_le_of_right_le.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} (h : b ≤ c) : a ⊓ b ≤ c
inf_le_of_right_le.description: The infimum of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if one of those elements is less than or equal to the third.

inf_lt_of_left_lt.code: inf_lt_of_left_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} (h : a < c) : a ⊓ b < c
inf_lt_of_left_lt.description: If one element is less than a third element, then the infimum of that element with another is also less than the third element.

inf_lt_of_right_lt.code: inf_lt_of_right_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} (h : b < c) : a ⊓ b < c
inf_lt_of_right_lt.description: If one element is less than a third element, then the infimum of that element with another is also less than the third element.

le_inf_iff.code: le_inf_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} : a ≤ b ⊓ c ↔ a ≤ b ∧ a ≤ c
le_inf_iff.description: An element is less than or equal to the infimum of two others if and only if it is less than or equal to each of those two elements individually.

inf_eq_left.code: inf_eq_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ b = a ↔ a ≤ b
inf_eq_left.description: The infimum of two elements equals the first element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the second.

inf_eq_right.code: inf_eq_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ b = b ↔ b ≤ a
inf_eq_right.description: The infimum of two elements is equal to one of them if and only if that element is less than or equal to the other.

left_eq_inf.code: left_eq_inf.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a = a ⊓ b ↔ a ≤ b
left_eq_inf.description: An element equals the infimum of itself and another element if and only if it is less than or equal to that other element.

right_eq_inf.code: right_eq_inf.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : b = a ⊓ b ↔ b ≤ a
right_eq_inf.description: An element is equal to the infimum of itself and another element if and only if it is less than or equal to that other element.

inf_of_le_left.code: inf_of_le_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a ≤ b → a ⊓ b = a
inf_of_le_left.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, then their infimum is equal to the first element.

le_of_inf_eq.code: le_of_inf_eq.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ b = a → a ≤ b
le_of_inf_eq.description: If the infimum of two elements equals the first element, then the first element is less than or equal to the second.

inf_of_le_right.code: inf_of_le_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : b ≤ a → a ⊓ b = b
inf_of_le_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, then their infimum equals the lesser element.

inf_lt_left.code: inf_lt_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ b < a ↔ ¬a ≤ b
inf_lt_left.description: The infimum of two elements is less than the first element if and only if the first element is not less than or equal to the second element.

inf_lt_right.code: inf_lt_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ b < b ↔ ¬b ≤ a
inf_lt_right.description: The infimum of two elements is less than the second element if and only if the second element is not less than or equal to the first element.

inf_lt_left_or_right.code: inf_lt_left_or_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b : α} (h : a ≠ b) : a ⊓ b < a ∨ a ⊓ b < b
inf_lt_left_or_right.description: If two distinct elements are considered, then their infimum is less than at least one of those elements.

inf_le_inf.code: inf_le_inf.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c d : α} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (h₂ : c ≤ d) : a ⊓ c ≤ b ⊓ d
inf_le_inf.description: The infimum of two elements taken from distinct pairs is less than or equal to the infimum of their respective larger elements.

inf_le_inf_right.code: inf_le_inf_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a : α) {b c : α} (h : b ≤ c) : b ⊓ a ≤ c ⊓ a
inf_le_inf_right.description: The infimum of two elements combined with a third element is less than or equal to the infimum of the second element and the third element, given that the second element is less than or equal to the third element.

inf_le_inf_left.code: inf_le_inf_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a : α) {b c : α} (h : b ≤ c) : a ⊓ b ≤ a ⊓ c
inf_le_inf_left.description: The infimum of a third element combined with two other elements is less than or equal to the infimum of that third element combined with the larger of the two, provided that the first element is less than or equal to the second.

inf_comm.code: inf_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b : α) : a ⊓ b = b ⊓ a
inf_comm.description: The infimum of two elements is equal regardless of their order.

inf_assoc.code: inf_assoc.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b c : α) : a ⊓ b ⊓ c = a ⊓ (b ⊓ c)
inf_assoc.description: The infimum operation is associative, meaning the grouping of three elements does not affect their greatest lower bound.

inf_left_right_swap.description: The infimum operation is associative with respect to the order of elements being combined.

inf_left_idem.code: inf_left_idem.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b : α) : a ⊓ (a ⊓ b) = a ⊓ b
inf_left_idem.description: The infimum of an element and the infimum of itself with another element equals the infimum of those two elements.

inf_right_idem.code: inf_right_idem.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b : α) : a ⊓ b ⊓ b = a ⊓ b
inf_right_idem.description: The infimum of two elements with a repeated second element is equal to the infimum of the two distinct elements.

inf_left_comm.code: inf_left_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b c : α) : a ⊓ (b ⊓ c) = b ⊓ (a ⊓ c)
inf_left_comm.description: The infimum operation is left-commutative, allowing for a reordering of the first two elements without affecting their greatest lower bound.

inf_right_comm.code: inf_right_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b c : α) : a ⊓ b ⊓ c = a ⊓ c ⊓ b
inf_right_comm.description: The infimum operation is commutative for three elements, meaning the order in which the elements are combined does not affect the result.

inf_inf_inf_comm.code: inf_inf_inf_comm.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b c d : α) : a ⊓ b ⊓ (c ⊓ d) = a ⊓ c ⊓ (b ⊓ d)
inf_inf_inf_comm.description: The infimum of four elements is invariant under the permutation of pairs, meaning the result remains the same regardless of how the pairs are grouped.

inf_inf_distrib_left.code: inf_inf_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b c : α) : a ⊓ (b ⊓ c) = a ⊓ b ⊓ (a ⊓ c)
inf_inf_distrib_left.description: The infimum of an element with the infimum of two other elements is equal to the infimum of the first element with one of those elements and then taking the infimum with the other element.

inf_inf_distrib_right.code: inf_inf_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b c : α) : a ⊓ b ⊓ c = a ⊓ c ⊓ (b ⊓ c)
inf_inf_distrib_right.description: The infimum of three elements is equal to the infimum of one of those elements with a third element and the infimum of the other two elements.

inf_congr_left.code: inf_congr_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} (hb : a ⊓ c ≤ b) (hc : a ⊓ b ≤ c) : a ⊓ b = a ⊓ c

inf_congr_right.code: inf_congr_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} (h1 : b ⊓ c ≤ a) (h2 : a ⊓ c ≤ b) : a ⊓ c = b ⊓ c
inf_congr_right.description: If two elements are related by certain inequalities with a third element, then their infimum with that third element is equal.

inf_eq_inf_iff_left.code: inf_eq_inf_iff_left.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} : a ⊓ b = a ⊓ c ↔ a ⊓ c ≤ b ∧ a ⊓ b ≤ c
inf_eq_inf_iff_left.description: The infimum of two elements with a common first argument is equal if and only if the infimum of that first argument with each of the other two elements serves as a lower bound for the respective second element.

inf_eq_inf_iff_right.code: inf_eq_inf_iff_right.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {a b c : α} : a ⊓ c = b ⊓ c ↔ b ⊓ c ≤ a ∧ a ⊓ c ≤ b
inf_eq_inf_iff_right.description: The infimum of two elements combined with a third element is equal if and only if each combined element is less than or equal to the other combined element.

Lattice.mk'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Sup α] [Inf α] (sup_comm : ∀ (a b : α), a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a)
  (sup_assoc : ∀ (a b c : α), a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)) (inf_comm : ∀ (a b : α), a ⊓ b = b ⊓ a)
  (inf_assoc : ∀ (a b c : α), a ⊓ b ⊓ c = a ⊓ (b ⊓ c)) (sup_inf_self : ∀ (a b : α), a ⊔ a ⊓ b = a)
  (inf_sup_self : ∀ (a b : α), a ⊓ (a ⊔ b) = a) : Lattice α
Lattice.mk'.comment:
A type with a pair of commutative and associative binary operations which satisfy two absorption
laws relating the two operations has the structure of a lattice.

The partial order is defined so that `a ≤ b` unfolds to `a ⊔ b = b`; cf. `sup_eq_right`.

Lattice.mk'.fullDefinition: def Lattice.mk' {α : Type*} [Sup α] [Inf α] (sup_comm : ∀ a b : α, a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a)     (sup_assoc : ∀ a b c : α, a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)) (inf_comm : ∀ a b : α, a ⊓ b = b ⊓ a)     (inf_assoc : ∀ a b c : α, a ⊓ b ⊓ c = a ⊓ (b ⊓ c)) (sup_inf_self : ∀ a b : α, a ⊔ a ⊓ b = a)     (inf_sup_self : ∀ a b : α, a ⊓ (a ⊔ b) = a) : Lattice α :=   have sup_idem : ∀ b : α, b ⊔ b = b := fun b =>     calc       b ⊔ b = b ⊔ b ⊓ (b ⊔ b) := by rw [inf_sup_self]       _ = b := by rw [sup_inf_self]
Lattice.mk'.description: A lattice is defined as a structure with two commutative and associative binary operations that follow absorption laws relating the two operations.

Prod.mk_sup_mk.code:

Prod.mk_sup_mk.description: The supremum of two pairs formed by elements from different sets is equal to the pair formed by the suprema of the individual components.

Prod.fst_inf.code: Prod.fst_inf.{u, v} (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [Inf α] [Inf β] (p q : α × β) : (p ⊓ q).1 = p.1 ⊓ q.1

Prod.snd_sup.code: Prod.snd_sup.{u, v} (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [Sup α] [Sup β] (p q : α × β) : (p ⊔ q).2 = p.2 ⊔ q.2

Prod.swap_sup.code: Prod.swap_sup.{u, v} (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [Sup α] [Sup β] (p q : α × β) : (p ⊔ q).swap = p.swap ⊔ q.swap

le_top.description: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.

isTop_top.description: The designated maximum element of an ordered type that contains a top element is confirmed to be a top element itself.

isMax_top.description: The designated maximum element of a preordered type that has a top element is confirmed to be a maximum element.

not_top_lt.code: not_top_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : ¬⊤ < a
not_top_lt.description: The maximum element of an ordered type that has a top element cannot be less than any other element in that type.

ne_top_of_lt.description: If one element in an ordered type that has a maximum element is less than another element, then the first element cannot be the maximum element.

isMax_iff_eq_top.code: isMax_iff_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : IsMax a ↔ a = ⊤
isMax_iff_eq_top.description: An element in an ordered type that has a maximum element is maximal if and only if it is equal to the maximum element.

isTop_iff_eq_top.code: isTop_iff_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : IsTop a ↔ a = ⊤
isTop_iff_eq_top.description: An element in an ordered type with a maximum element is top if and only if it is equal to the maximum element.

not_isMax_iff_ne_top.code: not_isMax_iff_ne_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : ¬IsMax a ↔ a ≠ ⊤
not_isMax_iff_ne_top.description: An element in an ordered type with a maximum element is not maximal if and only if it is not equal to the maximum element.

not_isTop_iff_ne_top.code: not_isTop_iff_ne_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : ¬IsTop a ↔ a ≠ ⊤
not_isTop_iff_ne_top.description: An element in an ordered type with a maximum element is not the largest element if and only if it is not equal to the maximum element.

IsMax.eq_top.code: IsMax.eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : IsMax a → a = ⊤
IsMax.eq_top.description: An element in a partially ordered set with a maximum element is the largest element if and only if it has the property of being a maximal element.

IsTop.eq_top.description: An element in an ordered type with a maximum is equal to that maximum if it satisfies the property of being a top element.

top_le_iff.code: top_le_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : ⊤ ≤ a ↔ a = ⊤
top_le_iff.description: An element in an ordered type with a maximum element is less than or equal to the maximum element if and only if it is equal to the maximum element.

top_unique.code: top_unique.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} (h : ⊤ ≤ a) : a = ⊤
top_unique.description: In an ordered type with a unique maximum element, any element that is at least as large as this maximum element must be equal to it.

eq_top_iff.description: An element in a partially ordered set is equal to the maximum element if and only if the maximum element is less than or equal to that element.

eq_top_mono.description: In a partially ordered set with a maximum element, if one element is equal to the maximum and is less than or equal to another element, then the second element must also be equal to the maximum.

lt_top_iff_ne_top.code: lt_top_iff_ne_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : a < ⊤ ↔ a ≠ ⊤
lt_top_iff_ne_top.description: An element in a partially ordered type with a maximum element is less than the maximum element if and only if it is not equal to the maximum element.

not_lt_top_iff.code: not_lt_top_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} : ¬a < ⊤ ↔ a = ⊤
not_lt_top_iff.description: An element in an ordered type with a maximum element is not less than the maximum element if and only if it is equal to the maximum element.

eq_top_or_lt_top.code: eq_top_or_lt_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] (a : α) : a = ⊤ ∨ a < ⊤

Ne.lt_top.code: Ne.lt_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} (h : a ≠ ⊤) : a < ⊤
Ne.lt_top.description: In a partially ordered type with a maximum element, if an element is not equal to the maximum, it must be less than the maximum element.

Ne.lt_top'.code: Ne.lt_top'.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a : α} (h : ⊤ ≠ a) : a < ⊤
Ne.lt_top'.description: In an ordered type with a maximum element, if an element is not equal to the maximum, then that element is less than the maximum element.

ne_top_of_le_ne_top.code: ne_top_of_le_ne_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a b : α} (hb : b ≠ ⊤) (hab : a ≤ b) : a ≠ ⊤
ne_top_of_le_ne_top.description: In a partially ordered type with a maximum element, if an element is less than or equal to another element that is not equal to the maximum, then it must also not be equal to the maximum.

explanatories.StrictMono.apply_eq_top_iff: A strictly monotonic function from an ordered type to another preserves the property of reaching the maximum element if and only if its input is the maximum element.

StrictAnti.apply_eq_top_iff.description: A strictly antitonic function from an ordered type with a maximum element to another type assigns the maximum element to itself if and only if the input is the maximum element.

not_isMin_top.code: not_isMin_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] [Nontrivial α] : ¬IsMin ⊤
not_isMin_top.description: In a nontrivial partially ordered set with a maximum element, the maximum element cannot be a minimal element.

StrictMono.maximal_preimage_top.code:

OrderTop.toTop.code: OrderTop.toTop.{u} {α : Type u} [LE α] [self : OrderTop α] : Top α
OrderTop.toTop.description: In an ordered type, the defined representation allows one to access the maximum element.

OrderTop.ext_top.code:

explanatories.PSum.inl: This theorem describes a function that takes an element from one type and injects it into a sum type composed of two types.

bot_le.code: bot_le.{u} {α : Type u} [LE α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : ⊥ ≤ a

isBot_bot.code: isBot_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [LE α] [OrderBot α] : IsBot ⊥
isBot_bot.description: The minimum element in an ordered type with a minimum is indeed the minimum element.

OrderDual.ofDual_top.description: The dual of the maximum element in an ordered type with a minimum element is equal to the minimum element.

OrderDual.toDual_bot.description: The least element in an ordered type with a greatest element corresponds to the greatest element in its dual order.

OrderDual.toDual_top.description: The greatest element in an ordered type with a least element corresponds to the least element in its dual order.

isMin_bot.code: isMin_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] [OrderBot α] : IsMin ⊥
isMin_bot.description: The least element in an ordered type that has a bottom element is a minimal element.

not_lt_bot.code: not_lt_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : ¬a < ⊥

ne_bot_of_gt.description: In a preordered set with a minimum element, if one element is less than another, then the second element cannot be the minimum.

isMin_iff_eq_bot.description: An element in a partially ordered type with a minimum is the minimum element if and only if it is equal to the minimum element.

isBot_iff_eq_bot.code: isBot_iff_eq_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : IsBot a ↔ a = ⊥
isBot_iff_eq_bot.description: An element in an ordered type that has a minimum element is minimal if and only if it is equal to the minimum element.

not_isMin_iff_ne_bot.code: not_isMin_iff_ne_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : ¬IsMin a ↔ a ≠ ⊥
not_isMin_iff_ne_bot.description: An element in a partially ordered set with a minimum element is not minimal if and only if it is not equal to the minimum element.

not_isBot_iff_ne_bot.code: not_isBot_iff_ne_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : ¬IsBot a ↔ a ≠ ⊥
not_isBot_iff_ne_bot.description: An element in a partially ordered set with a minimum element is not the minimum if and only if it is not equal to the minimum element.

IsMin.eq_bot.code: IsMin.eq_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : IsMin a → a = ⊥
IsMin.eq_bot.description: An element in a partially ordered set with a minimum element is the smallest element if and only if it has the property of being a minimal element.

IsBot.eq_bot.code: IsBot.eq_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : IsBot a → a = ⊥

explanatories.IsMin.eq_bot: An element in a partially ordered set with a minimum element is the smallest element if and only if it has the property of being a minimal element.

IsBot.eq_bot.description: If an element in a partially ordered type with a minimum element is classified as a bottom element, then it is equal to that minimum element.

le_bot_iff.code: le_bot_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : a ≤ ⊥ ↔ a = ⊥

bot_unique.code: bot_unique.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} (h : a ≤ ⊥) : a = ⊥

bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.code: bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} : ⊥ < a ↔ a ≠ ⊥

not_bot_lt_iff.description: In a partially ordered set with a least element, an element is not greater than the minimum element if and only if that element is equal to the minimum element.

eq_bot_or_bot_lt.code: eq_bot_or_bot_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] (a : α) : a = ⊥ ∨ ⊥ < a

eq_bot_of_minimal.code: eq_bot_of_minimal.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a : α} (h : ∀ (b : α), ¬b < a) : a = ⊥

ne_bot_of_le_ne_bot.description: If an element in a partially ordered set with a minimum element is greater than or equal to another element that is not the minimum, then the first element cannot be the minimum.

monotone_le.code: monotone_le.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] {x : α} : Monotone fun x_1 => x ≤ x_1
monotone_le.description: In a preordered type, the function that maps an element to every element greater than or equal to it is monotone, meaning that if one element is less than another, its image will also respect that order.

monotone_lt.code: monotone_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] {x : α} : Monotone fun x_1 => x < x_1
monotone_lt.description: In a preorder structure, the function that maps any element to its comparison with that element is monotonic.

antitone_le.code: antitone_le.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] {x : α} : Antitone fun x_1 => x_1 ≤ x
antitone_le.description: The function that maps any element to whether it is less than or equal to a fixed element is antitonic in an ordered type.

antitone_lt.code: antitone_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [Preorder α] {x : α} : Antitone fun x_1 => x_1 < x
antitone_lt.description: A function that maintains the order by being antitone results in the property where values less than a particular element are preserved under its application.

Monotone.forall.code:
Monotone.forall.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] {P : β → α → Prop} (hP : ∀ (x : β), Monotone (P x)) :
  Monotone fun y => ∀ (x : β), P x y
Monotone.forall.description: If a property is monotone for every argument in a given type, then the functional relationship defined by that property is also monotone in its second argument.

Antitone.forall.code:
Antitone.forall.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] {P : β → α → Prop} (hP : ∀ (x : β), Antitone (P x)) :
  Antitone fun y => ∀ (x : β), P x y

explanatories.Monotone.forall: If a property is monotone for every argument in a given type, then the functional relationship defined by that property is also monotone in its second argument.

Antitone.forall.description: If a property is antitonic with respect to each element of a second type, then the property defined by taking the supremum over the second type also remains antitonic.

Monotone.ball.code:
Monotone.ball.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] {P : β → α → Prop} {s : Set β}
  (hP : ∀ (x : β), x ∈ s → Monotone (P x)) : Monotone fun y => ∀ (x : β), x ∈ s → P x y
Monotone.ball.description: If a predicate is monotonic for all elements of a set, then the function assigning to each element the property of holding that predicate for all elements in the set is also monotonic.

Antitone.ball.code:
Antitone.ball.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] {P : β → α → Prop} {s : Set β}
  (hP : ∀ (x : β), x ∈ s → Antitone (P x)) : Antitone fun y => ∀ (x : β), x ∈ s → P x y

explanatories.Monotone.ball: If a predicate is monotonic for all elements of a set, then the function assigning to each element the property of holding that predicate for all elements in the set is also monotonic.

Antitone.ball.description: If a predicate is antitonic for all elements of a set, then the function that assigns to each element the property of satisfying that predicate for all elements in the set is also antitonic.

exists_ge_and_iff_exists.code:
exists_ge_and_iff_exists.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeSup α] {P : α → Prop} {x₀ : α} (hP : Monotone P) :
  (∃ x, x₀ ≤ x ∧ P x) ↔ ∃ x, P x
exists_ge_and_iff_exists.description: If a predicate is monotonic in a semilattice, then the existence of an element greater than or equal to a specific element satisfying that predicate is equivalent to the existence of any element satisfying the predicate.

exists_le_and_iff_exists.code:
exists_le_and_iff_exists.{u} {α : Type u} [SemilatticeInf α] {P : α → Prop} {x₀ : α} (hP : Antitone P) :
  (∃ x, x ≤ x₀ ∧ P x) ↔ ∃ x, P x
exists_le_and_iff_exists.description: In a structure with an infimum, the existence of an element that is less than or equal to a given element and satisfies a property is equivalent to the existence of an element that satisfies that property.

Pi.bot_apply.code: Pi.bot_apply.{u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_3} {α' : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → Bot (α' i)] (i : ι) : ⊥ i = ⊥
Pi.bot_apply.description: In a type indexed by a set, the bottom element of the indexed type corresponds to the bottom element of any individual type in that index.

Pi.bot_def.code: Pi.bot_def.{u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_3} {α' : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → Bot (α' i)] : ⊥ = fun x => ⊥
Pi.bot_def.description: The least element in a product of types, where each type has a least element, corresponds to the function that assigns the least element to every input.

Pi.top_apply.code: Pi.top_apply.{u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_3} {α' : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → Top (α' i)] (i : ι) : ⊤ i = ⊤
Pi.top_apply.description: In a type where each index maps to a top element, the top element at any index remains the top element.

Pi.top_def.code: Pi.top_def.{u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_3} {α' : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → Top (α' i)] : ⊤ = fun x => ⊤
Pi.top_def.description: The universal top element in a family of types is a function that outputs the top element for each type in the family.

eq_bot_of_bot_eq_top.code: eq_bot_of_bot_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] (hα : ⊥ = ⊤) (x : α) : x = ⊥
eq_bot_of_bot_eq_top.description: If in a bounded ordered set the minimum element is equal to the maximum element, then every element in that set must also be equal to the minimum element.

eq_top_of_bot_eq_top.code: eq_top_of_bot_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] (hα : ⊥ = ⊤) (x : α) : x = ⊤
eq_top_of_bot_eq_top.description: In a bounded ordered type where the least element equals the greatest element, every element must also equal the greatest element.

subsingleton_of_top_le_bot.code: subsingleton_of_top_le_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] (h : ⊤ ≤ ⊥) : Subsingleton α
subsingleton_of_top_le_bot.description: In a bounded ordered type where the greatest element is less than or equal to the least element, every element must be identical.

subsingleton_of_bot_eq_top.code: subsingleton_of_bot_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] (hα : ⊥ = ⊤) : Subsingleton α
subsingleton_of_bot_eq_top.description: If the minimum and maximum elements of a bounded partially ordered type are equal, then the type contains only one element.

subsingleton_iff_bot_eq_top.code: subsingleton_iff_bot_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] : ⊥ = ⊤ ↔ Subsingleton α
subsingleton_iff_bot_eq_top.description: In a bounded ordered type, the minimum element is equal to the maximum element if and only if the type contains only a single element.

OrderTop.lift.code:
OrderTop.lift.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [LE α] [Top α] [LE β] [OrderTop β] (f : α → β)
  (map_le : ∀ (a b : α), f a ≤ f b → a ≤ b) (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) : OrderTop α

explanatories.OrderTop.le_top: Every element in an ordered type that has a maximum element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.

OrderTop.lift.fullDefinition: abbrev OrderTop.lift [LE α] [Top α] [LE β] [OrderTop β] (f : α → β)     (map_le : ∀ a b, f a ≤ f b → a ≤ b) (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) : OrderTop α :=   ⟨fun a =>     map_le _ _ <| by       rw [map_top]       -- Porting note: lean3 didn't need the type annotation       exact @le_top β _ _ _⟩
OrderTop.lift.description: A function that lifts an ordered type with a maximum element to another ordered type with a maximum element while preserving order relations and the maximum element.

OrderBot.lift.code:
OrderBot.lift.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [LE α] [Bot α] [LE β] [OrderBot β] (f : α → β)
  (map_le : ∀ (a b : α), f a ≤ f b → a ≤ b) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) : OrderBot α

explanatories.OrderBot.bot_le: The least element in an ordered type is less than or equal to any other element in that type.
explanatories.bot_le: The least element of an ordered type that has a bottom element is less than or equal to all other elements in that type.
explanatories.OrderTop.lift: A function that lifts an ordered type with a maximum element to another ordered type with a maximum element while preserving order relations and the maximum element.

OrderBot.lift.fullDefinition: abbrev OrderBot.lift [LE α] [Bot α] [LE β] [OrderBot β] (f : α → β)     (map_le : ∀ a b, f a ≤ f b → a ≤ b) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) : OrderBot α :=   ⟨fun a =>     map_le _ _ <| by       rw [map_bot]       -- Porting note: lean3 didn't need the type annotation       exact @bot_le β _ _ _⟩
OrderBot.lift.description: This definition describes a way to transform a partially ordered type with a least element into another partially ordered type with a least element by applying a function that preserves order and maps the least element to the least element.

BoundedOrder.lift.code:
BoundedOrder.lift.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [LE α] [Top α] [Bot α] [LE β] [BoundedOrder β] (f : α → β)
  (map_le : ∀ (a b : α), f a ≤ f b → a ≤ b) (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) : BoundedOrder α

explanatories.OrderTop.lift: A function that lifts an ordered type with a maximum element to another ordered type with a maximum element while preserving order relations and the maximum element.
explanatories.OrderBot.lift: This definition describes a way to transform a partially ordered type with a least element into another partially ordered type with a least element by applying a function that preserves order and maps the least element to the least element.

BoundedOrder.lift.fullDefinition: abbrev BoundedOrder.lift [LE α] [Top α] [Bot α] [LE β] [BoundedOrder β] (f : α → β)     (map_le : ∀ a b, f a ≤ f b → a ≤ b) (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) :     BoundedOrder α where   __ := OrderTop.lift f map_le map_top   __ := OrderBot.lift f map_le map_bot
BoundedOrder.lift.description: A bounded order can be constructed for one type by using a function that preserves order, maps the greatest element to the greatest element, and maps the least element to the least element from another bounded order.

Subtype.orderBot.code: Subtype.orderBot.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [LE α] [OrderBot α] (hbot : p ⊥) : OrderBot { x // p x }
Subtype.orderBot.comment: A subtype remains a `⊥`-order if the property holds at `⊥`.

explanatories.OrderBot.bot_le: The least element in an ordered type is less than or equal to any other element in that type.
explanatories.bot_le: The least element of an ordered type that has a bottom element is less than or equal to all other elements in that type.

Subtype.orderBot.fullDefinition: protected abbrev orderBot [LE α] [OrderBot α] (hbot : p ⊥) : OrderBot { x : α // p x } where   bot := ⟨⊥, hbot⟩   bot_le _ := bot_le
Subtype.orderBot.description: A subtype retains a minimum element in its order structure if this property is satisfied at the minimum element of the original type.

Subtype.orderTop.code: Subtype.orderTop.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [LE α] [OrderTop α] (htop : p ⊤) : OrderTop { x // p x }
Subtype.orderTop.comment: A subtype remains a `⊤`-order if the property holds at `⊤`.

explanatories.OrderTop.le_top: Every element in an ordered type that has a maximum element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.

Subtype.orderTop.fullDefinition: protected abbrev orderTop [LE α] [OrderTop α] (htop : p ⊤) : OrderTop { x : α // p x } where   top := ⟨⊤, htop⟩   le_top _ := le_top
Subtype.orderTop.description: A subtype inherits the structure of having a maximum element if the property defining the subtype holds for that maximum element.

Subtype.boundedOrder.code:
Subtype.boundedOrder.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [LE α] [BoundedOrder α] (hbot : p ⊥) (htop : p ⊤) :
  BoundedOrder (Subtype p)
Subtype.boundedOrder.comment: A subtype remains a bounded order if the property holds at `⊥` and `⊤`.

explanatories.Subtype.orderBot: A subtype retains a minimum element in its order structure if this property is satisfied at the minimum element of the original type.
explanatories.Subtype.orderTop: A subtype inherits the structure of having a maximum element if the property defining the subtype holds for that maximum element.

Subtype.boundedOrder.fullDefinition: protected abbrev boundedOrder [LE α] [BoundedOrder α] (hbot : p ⊥) (htop : p ⊤) :     BoundedOrder (Subtype p) where   __ := Subtype.orderTop htop   __ := Subtype.orderBot hbot
Subtype.boundedOrder.description: A subtype of a bounded ordered type retains the property of being a bounded order if the defining property holds true for both the least and greatest elements.

Subtype.mk_bot.code:
Subtype.mk_bot.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] [OrderBot (Subtype p)] (hbot : p ⊥) :
  ⟨⊥, hbot⟩ = ⊥
Subtype.mk_bot.description: In a partially ordered type with a least element, the subtype consisting of elements satisfying a property is equal to the least element if that property holds for the least element.

Subtype.mk_top.code:
Subtype.mk_top.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] [OrderTop (Subtype p)] (htop : p ⊤) :
  ⟨⊤, htop⟩ = ⊤
Subtype.mk_top.description: The maximum element in an ordered type, when restricted to a specified property, is itself the maximum element of the subtype defined by that property.

Subtype.coe_bot.code:
Subtype.coe_bot.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] [OrderBot (Subtype p)] (hbot : p ⊥) :
  ↑⊥ = ⊥
Subtype.coe_bot.description: The least element in a partially ordered set remains the least element when considered within a subtype defined by a property that holds for that element.

Subtype.coe_top.code:
Subtype.coe_top.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] [OrderTop (Subtype p)] (htop : p ⊤) :
  ↑⊤ = ⊤
Subtype.coe_top.description: The top element in a subtype of an ordered type corresponds to the top element of the original type when the top element satisfies the property defining the subtype.

Subtype.coe_eq_bot_iff.code:
Subtype.coe_eq_bot_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] [OrderBot (Subtype p)] (hbot : p ⊥)
  {x : { x // p x }} : ↑x = ⊥ ↔ x = ⊥
Subtype.coe_eq_bot_iff.description: In a partially ordered set with a least element, an element in a subtype is equal to the least element if and only if the element itself is the least element of the subtype.

Subtype.coe_eq_top_iff.code:
Subtype.coe_eq_top_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] [OrderTop (Subtype p)] (htop : p ⊤)
  {x : { x // p x }} : ↑x = ⊤ ↔ x = ⊤
Subtype.coe_eq_top_iff.description: An element of a subtype is equal to the top element if and only if the representative of that element is the top element in the overall order.

Subtype.mk_eq_bot_iff.code:
Subtype.mk_eq_bot_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] [OrderBot (Subtype p)] (hbot : p ⊥)
  {x : α} (hx : p x) : ⟨x, hx⟩ = ⊥ ↔ x = ⊥
Subtype.mk_eq_bot_iff.description: In a partially ordered set with a unique minimum element, an element in a subtype is equal to this minimum if and only if the original element is equal to the minimum.

Subtype.mk_eq_top_iff.code:
Subtype.mk_eq_top_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] [OrderTop (Subtype p)] (htop : p ⊤)
  {x : α} (hx : p x) : ⟨x, hx⟩ = ⊤ ↔ x = ⊤
Subtype.mk_eq_top_iff.description: An element in a type with a maximum is equal to the maximum of a subtype if and only if the element itself is the maximum of the original type, given that the maximum of the original type satisfies the subtype property.

ULift.down_bot.description: The downward lift of the least element in a type with a bottom element is equal to the least element itself.

ULift.down_top.description: The downward image of the maximum element in a type with a maximum is equal to that maximum element itself.

min_bot_left.code: min_bot_left.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderBot α] (a : α) : min ⊥ a = ⊥

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_bot_left.description: The minimum of a bottom element and any other element in a totally ordered set is the bottom element itself.

max_top_left.code: max_top_left.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderTop α] (a : α) : max ⊤ a = ⊤

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_top_left.description: In a linearly ordered type with a maximum element, the maximum of that maximum element and any other element is equal to the maximum element.

min_top_left.code: min_top_left.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderTop α] (a : α) : min ⊤ a = a

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_top_left.description: The minimum of a top element and any other element in a totally ordered set is that other element itself.

max_bot_left.code: max_bot_left.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderBot α] (a : α) : max ⊥ a = a

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_bot_left.description: In a linearly ordered type with a minimum element, the maximum of the minimum element and any other element is that other element itself.

min_top_right.code: min_top_right.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderTop α] (a : α) : min a ⊤ = a

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_top_right.description: The minimum of any element and a top element in a totally ordered set is that element itself.

max_bot_right.code: max_bot_right.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderBot α] (a : α) : max a ⊥ = a

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_bot_right.description: In a linear order with a minimum element, the maximum of any element and the minimum element is that element itself.

min_bot_right.code: min_bot_right.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderBot α] (a : α) : min a ⊥ = ⊥

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_bot_right.description: The minimum of an element and the minimum element in a linear ordered type is equal to the minimum element itself.

max_top_right.code: max_top_right.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderTop α] (a : α) : max a ⊤ = ⊤

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_top_right.description: In a linearly ordered set with a greatest element, the maximum of any element and the greatest element is the greatest element itself.

min_eq_bot.code: min_eq_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a b : α} : min a b = ⊥ ↔ a = ⊥ ∨ b = ⊥

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_eq_bot.description: The minimum of two elements in a linearly ordered type with a minimum is equal to the minimum element if and only if at least one of the two elements is the minimum.

max_eq_top.code: max_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a b : α} : max a b = ⊤ ↔ a = ⊤ ∨ b = ⊤

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_eq_top.description: In a linearly ordered set with a maximum element, the maximum of two elements is equal to the maximum if and only if at least one of those elements is equal to the maximum.

max_eq_bot.code: max_eq_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderBot α] {a b : α} : max a b = ⊥ ↔ a = ⊥ ∧ b = ⊥

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_eq_bot.description: The maximum of two elements in a linearly ordered set is the least element if and only if both elements are equal to the least element.

min_eq_top.code: min_eq_top.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] [OrderTop α] {a b : α} : min a b = ⊤ ↔ a = ⊤ ∧ b = ⊤

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_eq_top.description: The minimum of two elements in a linearly ordered type with a maximum element is that maximum element if and only if both elements are the maximum.

bot_ne_top.code: bot_ne_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] [Nontrivial α] : ⊥ ≠ ⊤
bot_ne_top.description: In a nontrivial bounded ordered type, the minimum element is different from the maximum element.

top_ne_bot.code: top_ne_bot.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] [Nontrivial α] : ⊤ ≠ ⊥
top_ne_bot.description: In a non-trivial partially ordered set that has bounds, the greatest element is not equal to the least element.

bot_lt_top.code: bot_lt_top.{u} {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] [BoundedOrder α] [Nontrivial α] : ⊥ < ⊤
bot_lt_top.description: The minimum element in a partially ordered type with a maximum element is less than the maximum element, provided the type is nontrivial.

explanatories.Bool.true: The value `true` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.

top_eq_true.description: The maximum element in the context of order theory is equivalent to the boolean value true.

explanatories.Bool.false: The value `false` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.

bot_eq_false.description: The least element in a logical system is equal to false.

le_min_iff.code: le_min_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : c ≤ min a b ↔ c ≤ a ∧ c ≤ b

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

le_min_iff.description: An element is less than or equal to the minimum of two others if and only if it is less than or equal to each of those two elements.

le_max_iff.code: le_max_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a ≤ max b c ↔ a ≤ b ∨ a ≤ c

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

le_max_iff.description: An element is less than or equal to the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than or equal to at least one of those two elements.

min_le_iff.code: min_le_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : min a b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ c ∨ b ≤ c

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_le_iff.description: An element is greater than or equal to the minimum of two others if and only if it is greater than or equal to at least one of those two elements.

max_le_iff.code: max_le_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : max a b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ c ∧ b ≤ c

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_le_iff.description: An element is less than or equal to the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than or equal to both of those two elements.

lt_min_iff.code: lt_min_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a < min b c ↔ a < b ∧ a < c

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

lt_min_iff.description: An element is less than the minimum of two others if and only if it is less than each of those two elements.

lt_max_iff.code: lt_max_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a < max b c ↔ a < b ∨ a < c

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

lt_max_iff.description: An element is less than the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than at least one of those two elements.

min_lt_iff.code: min_lt_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : min a b < c ↔ a < c ∨ b < c

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_lt_iff.description: An element is less than the minimum of two others if and only if it is less than at least one of those two elements.

max_lt_iff.code: max_lt_iff.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : max a b < c ↔ a < c ∧ b < c

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_lt_iff.description: An element is less than the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than each of those two elements.

max_le_max.code: max_le_max.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c d : α} : a ≤ c → b ≤ d → max a b ≤ max c d

explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

max_le_max.description: If one element is less than or equal to another and a second element is also less than or equal to a third, then the maximum of the first two elements is less than or equal to the maximum of the last two.

min_le_min.code: min_le_min.{u} {α : Type u} [LinearOrder α] {a b c d : α} : a ≤ c → b ≤ d → min a b ≤ min c d

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.

min_le_min.description: If one element is less than or equal to a second element and another element is less than or equal to a fourth element, then the minimum of the first two elements is less than or equal to the minimum of the last two elements.

Disjoint.code: Disjoint.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] (a b : α) : Prop
Disjoint.comment:
Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments.
Disjoint.fullDefinition: def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

Codisjoint.comment:
Two elements of a lattice are codisjoint if their sup is the top element.

Note that we define this without reference to `⊔`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the supremum is not unique, or where implement `Sup` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments.
Codisjoint.fullDefinition: def Codisjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃x⦄, a ≤ x → b ≤ x → ⊤ ≤ x

WithBot.not_lt_bot.description: This theorem asserts that no element in a structured type can be less than the least element included in a type that has an additional bottom element.
