WithBot.not_lt_none.description: This theorem states that a value from a type cannot be less than the representation of absence in an option type.

WithBot.lt_iff_exists_coe.code: WithBot.lt_iff_exists_coe.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LT α] {a b : WithBot α} : a < b ↔ ∃ p, b = ↑p ∧ a < ↑p
WithBot.lt_iff_exists_coe.description: This theorem expresses that an element is less than another in a type that includes an optional least element if and only if there exists an element that is equal to the latter and is strictly greater than the former.

WithBot.lt_coe_iff.code: WithBot.lt_coe_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {b : α} [LT α] {x : WithBot α} : x < ↑b ↔ ∀ (a : α), x = ↑a → a < b
WithBot.lt_coe_iff.description: This theorem states that a boxed value being less than a boxed representation of another value is equivalent to the condition that all original values equal to the boxed value are less than the corresponding unboxed value.

WithBot.bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.code: WithBot.bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LT α] {x : WithBot α} : ⊥ < x ↔ x ≠ ⊥
WithBot.bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.comment:
A version of `bot_lt_iff_ne_bot` for `WithBot` that only requires `LT α`, not
`PartialOrder α`.
WithBot.bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.description: This theorem states that an element in a type that includes a least element is considered greater than the least element if and only if it is not equal to the least element.

WithBot.preorder.code: WithBot.preorder.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] : Preorder (WithBot α)

explanatories.LE.le: The less-equal relation determines whether one element is less than or equal to another in a type that supports this ordering.
explanatories.LT.lt: This definition introduces a relation that expresses when one element is less than another within a given type.

WithBot.preorder.fullDefinition: instance preorder [Preorder α] : Preorder (WithBot α) where   le := (· ≤ ·)   lt := (· < ·)   lt_iff_le_not_le := by     intros a b     cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [lt_iff_le_not_le]   le_refl o a ha := ⟨a, ha, le_rfl⟩   le_trans o₁ o₂ o₃ h₁ h₂ a ha :=     let ⟨b, hb, ab⟩ := h₁ a ha     let ⟨c, hc, bc⟩ := h₂ b hb     ⟨c, hc, le_trans ab bc⟩
WithBot.preorder.description: This definition establishes a preorder structure on a type that includes a least element by extending the preorder properties of the original type.

WithBot.partialOrder.code: WithBot.partialOrder.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PartialOrder α] : PartialOrder (WithBot α)

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.

WithBot.partialOrder.fullDefinition: instance partialOrder [PartialOrder α] : PartialOrder (WithBot α) :=   { WithBot.preorder with     le_antisymm := fun o₁ o₂ h₁ h₂ => by       cases' o₁ with a       · cases' o₂ with b         · rfl         rcases h₂ b rfl with ⟨_, ⟨⟩, _⟩       · rcases h₁ a rfl with ⟨b, ⟨⟩, h₁'⟩         rcases h₂ b rfl with ⟨_, ⟨⟩, h₂'⟩         rw [le_antisymm h₁' h₂'] }
WithBot.partialOrder.description: This definition introduces a partial order structure on a type that includes an additional least element, extending the existing partial order of the underlying type.

WithBot.coe_mono.description: This theorem states that the function mapping elements to their boxed representations is monotonic in a preordered setting.

WithBot.monotone_iff.code:
WithBot.monotone_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : WithBot α → β} :

WithBot.monotone_iff.description: This theorem characterizes a monotone function on a type that includes a least element by relating it to the monotonicity of its restriction to non-bottom elements and ensuring that the function value at the least element is less than or equal to its values at all other elements.

WithBot.monotone_map_iff.description: This theorem states that the monotonicity of a map applied to a function is equivalent to the monotonicity of the function itself.

Monotone.withBot_map.code:

WithBot.strictMono_iff.code:
WithBot.strictMono_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : WithBot α → β} :
  StrictMono f ↔ (StrictMono fun a => f ↑a) ∧ ∀ (x : α), f ⊥ < f ↑x
WithBot.strictMono_iff.description: This theorem states that a function is strictly monotonic if and only if it is strictly monotonic when applied to the non-least elements and always maps the least element to a value that is less than its image for every other element.

WithBot.strictMono_map_iff.code:

WithBot.strictMono_map_iff.description: This theorem states that the strict monotonicity of a map applied to a function is equivalent to the strict monotonicity of the function itself.

StrictMono.withBot_map.code:
StrictMono.withBot_map.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} :

explanatories.WithBot.unbot': This defines a function that extracts a regular element from a type that includes a least element, given a default value and an element of that type.

WithBot.coe_sup.description: This theorem states that the supremum of two elements in a semilattice is equivalent to the supremum of their corresponding boxed values.

WithBot.coe_inf.code: WithBot.coe_inf.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeInf α] (a b : α) : ↑(a ⊓ b) = ↑a ⊓ ↑b
WithBot.coe_inf.description: This theorem asserts that the embedding of the infimum of two elements in a semilattice is equivalent to the infimum of their respective embeddings.

WithBot.semilatticeSup.code: WithBot.semilatticeSup.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] : SemilatticeSup (WithBot α)

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.LE.le: The less-equal relation determines whether one element is less than or equal to another in a type that supports this ordering.
explanatories.WithBot.coe_le_coe: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the ordering of boxed values and their underlying unboxed counterparts in a partially ordered type.
explanatories.And.right: The theorem allows one to derive the second component of a conjunction from a given statement that asserts both components are true.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

WithBot.semilatticeSup.fullDefinition: instance semilatticeSup [SemilatticeSup α] : SemilatticeSup (WithBot α) where   sup     -- note this is `Option.liftOrGet`, but with the right defeq when unfolding     | ⊥, ⊥ => ⊥     | (a : α), ⊥ => a     | ⊥, (b : α) => b     | (a : α), (b : α) => ↑(a ⊔ b)   le_sup_left := fun o₁ o₂ a ha => by cases ha; cases o₂ <;> simp   le_sup_right := fun o₁ o₂ a ha => by cases ha; cases o₁ <;> simp   sup_le := fun o₁ o₂ o₃ h₁ h₂ a ha => by     cases' o₁ with b <;> cases' o₂ with c <;> cases ha     · exact h₂ a rfl     · exact h₁ a rfl     · rcases h₁ b rfl with ⟨d, ⟨⟩, h₁'⟩       simp only [coe_le_coe] at h₂       exact ⟨d, rfl, sup_le h₁' h₂⟩
WithBot.semilatticeSup.description: This definition introduces a structure in which the least upper bounds of elements in an optional type are determined by the least upper bounds of the elements in the original type.

WithBot.semilatticeInf.code: WithBot.semilatticeInf.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeInf α] : SemilatticeInf (WithBot α)

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.WithBot.map₂: This definition describes a function that takes a binary function and two boxed values, producing a boxed value that represents the result of applying that binary function to the underlying values.
explanatories.WithBot.orderBot: This definition introduces a structure that defines a partially ordered type including a least element for values in a type that has a corresponding ordering.
explanatories.WithBot.partialOrder: This definition introduces a partial order structure on a type that includes an additional least element, extending the existing partial order of the underlying type.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

WithBot.semilatticeInf.fullDefinition: instance semilatticeInf [SemilatticeInf α] : SemilatticeInf (WithBot α) :=   { WithBot.partialOrder, @WithBot.orderBot α _ with     inf := WithBot.map₂ (· ⊓ ·),     inf_le_left := fun o₁ o₂ a ha => by       rcases Option.mem_map₂_iff.1 ha with ⟨a, b, (rfl : _ = _), (rfl : _ = _), rfl⟩       exact ⟨_, rfl, inf_le_left⟩,     inf_le_right := fun o₁ o₂ a ha => by       rcases Option.mem_map₂_iff.1 ha with ⟨a, b, (rfl : _ = _), (rfl : _ = _), rfl⟩       exact ⟨_, rfl, inf_le_right⟩,     le_inf := fun o₁ o₂ o₃ h₁ h₂ a ha => by       cases ha       rcases h₁ a rfl with ⟨b, ⟨⟩, ab⟩       rcases h₂ a rfl with ⟨c, ⟨⟩, ac⟩       exact ⟨_, rfl, le_inf ab ac⟩ }
WithBot.semilatticeInf.description: This defines a structure that extends the concept of a semilattice infimum to a type that includes an element representing absence.

WithBot.lattice.code: WithBot.lattice.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] : Lattice (WithBot α)

explanatories.WithBot.semilatticeSup: This definition introduces a structure in which the least upper bounds of elements in an optional type are determined by the least upper bounds of the elements in the original type.
explanatories.WithBot.semilatticeInf: This defines a structure that extends the concept of a semilattice infimum to a type that includes an element representing absence.

WithBot.lattice.fullDefinition: instance lattice [Lattice α] : Lattice (WithBot α) :=   { WithBot.semilatticeSup, WithBot.semilatticeInf with }
WithBot.lattice.description: This definition introduces a structure that allows a type with lattice properties to also exhibit lattice properties when lifted into a new type that includes an optional element.

WithBot.decidableLE.code: WithBot.decidableLE.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] [DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1] : DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1

explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.
explanatories.WithBot.some: This defines a function that constructs an element of a type that includes a least element from a regular element of that type.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.WithBot.coe_le_coe: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the ordering of boxed values and their underlying unboxed counterparts in a partially ordered type.
explanatories.Option.noConfusion: This defines a method for handling equalities between optional values, allowing properties to be inferred from them based on their equality.
explanatories.DecidableRel: A decidable relation is a type of relationship between elements that can be algorithmically determined to be true or false.
explanatories.Decidable.isTrue: This shows that if a proposition is proven to be true, then it can be classified as decidable.
explanatories.Decidable.isFalse: This theorem establishes that if a proposition is shown to be false, then it can be concluded that the proposition is decidable.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

WithBot.decidableLE.fullDefinition: instance decidableLE [LE α] [@DecidableRel α (· ≤ ·)] : @DecidableRel (WithBot α) (· ≤ ·)   | none, x => isTrue fun a h => Option.noConfusion h   | Option.some x, Option.some y =>       if h : x ≤ y then isTrue (coe_le_coe.2 h) else isFalse <| by simp [*]   | Option.some x, none => isFalse fun h => by rcases h x rfl with ⟨y, ⟨_⟩, _⟩
WithBot.decidableLE.description: This defines a decidable version of the less than or equal to relation for a type that includes a least element, enabling determination of comparability between values.

WithBot.decidableLT.code: WithBot.decidableLT.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LT α] [DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x < x_1] : DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x < x_1

explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.
explanatories.WithBot.some: This defines a function that constructs an element of a type that includes a least element from a regular element of that type.
explanatories.Option.exists: The existence of an option satisfying a property is equivalent to either the property holding for none or it holding for some value within an option.
explanatories.WithBot.exists: This theorem states that a property holds for at least one element in a type that includes a least element if and only if it holds for the least element or for at least one element of the original type.
explanatories.DecidableRel: A decidable relation is a type of relationship between elements that can be algorithmically determined to be true or false.
explanatories.Decidable.isTrue: This shows that if a proposition is proven to be true, then it can be classified as decidable.
explanatories.Decidable.isFalse: This theorem establishes that if a proposition is shown to be false, then it can be concluded that the proposition is decidable.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

WithBot.decidableLT.fullDefinition: instance decidableLT [LT α] [@DecidableRel α (· < ·)] : @DecidableRel (WithBot α) (· < ·)   | none, Option.some x => isTrue <| by exists x, rfl; rintro _ ⟨⟩   | Option.some x, Option.some y =>       if h : x < y then isTrue <| by simp [*] else isFalse <| by simp [*]   | x, none => isFalse <| by rintro ⟨a, ⟨⟨⟩⟩⟩
WithBot.decidableLT.description: This defines a decidable version of the less than relation for a type that includes a least element, allowing for algorithmic determination of the comparability of values based on that relation.

WithBot.isTotal_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] [IsTotal α fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1] :

explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.

explanatories.LE.le: The less-equal relation determines whether one element is less than or equal to another in a type that supports this ordering.
explanatories.WithBot.coe_le_coe: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the ordering of boxed values and their underlying unboxed counterparts in a partially ordered type.
explanatories.Or.inl: The left injection into a disjunction allows a proven statement to be included as a true proposition within either of the options of an "or" logical construction.
explanatories.Or.inr: The right injection operation allows one to obtain a disjunction by confirming the truth of a specific proposition.
explanatories.Or.imp: If one proves a consequence of either of two propositions, then one can derive a conclusion based on either of those propositions being true.

WithBot.isTotal_le.fullDefinition: instance isTotal_le [LE α] [IsTotal α (· ≤ ·)] : IsTotal (WithBot α) (· ≤ ·) :=   ⟨fun a b =>     match a, b with     | none, _ => Or.inl bot_le     | _, none => Or.inr bot_le     | Option.some x, Option.some y => (total_of (· ≤ ·) x y).imp coe_le_coe.2 coe_le_coe.2⟩
WithBot.isTotal_le.description: This definition establishes that the order relation on a boxed type is total if the underlying order on the unboxed type is total.

WithBot.linearOrder.code: WithBot.linearOrder.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] : LinearOrder (WithBot α)
WithBot.linearOrder.fullDefinition: instance linearOrder [LinearOrder α] : LinearOrder (WithBot α) :=   Lattice.toLinearOrder _
WithBot.linearOrder.description: This definition asserts that if a type has a linear order, then the type that includes a least element also inherits a linear order structure.

WithBot.coe_min.code: WithBot.coe_min.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] (x y : α) : ↑(min x y) = min ↑x ↑y

WithBot.instWellFoundedLT.code: WithBot.instWellFoundedLT.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LT α] [WellFoundedLT α] : WellFoundedLT (WithBot α)

explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.
explanatories.And.intro: The constructor for the "And" operation combines two propositions into a single proposition that asserts both are true.
explanatories.LT.lt: This definition introduces a relation that expresses when one element is less than another within a given type.
explanatories.WithBot.coe_lt_coe: This theorem establishes that the boxed representation of one element being less than that of another is equivalent to the original elements being in the same order of inequality.
explanatories.WithBot.not_lt_bot: This theorem asserts that no element in a structured type can be less than the least element included in a type that has an additional bottom element.
explanatories.Iff.intro: This theorem establishes that two propositions are equivalent if each can be inferred from the other.
explanatories.Acc.intro: A value is accessible if every related predecessor is also accessible, and if there are no such predecessors, the value itself is accessible and is termed a base case.
explanatories.WellFounded.intro: This theorem establishes that a relation is well-founded if every element is accessible under that relation.

WithBot.instWellFoundedLT.fullDefinition: instance instWellFoundedLT [LT α] [WellFoundedLT α] : WellFoundedLT (WithBot α) where   wf :=   have not_lt_bot : ∀ a : WithBot α, ¬ a < ⊥ := nofun   have acc_bot := ⟨_, by simp [not_lt_bot]⟩   .intro fun     | ⊥ => acc_bot     | (a : α) => (wellFounded_lt.1 a).rec fun a _ ih =>       .intro _ fun         | ⊥, _ => acc_bot         | (b : α), hlt => ih _ (coe_lt_coe.1 hlt)
WithBot.instWellFoundedLT.description: This definition establishes a well-founded ordering for a type that includes an optional absence of value, ensuring that every non-empty subset has a minimal element.

WithBot.instWellFoundedGT.code: WithBot.instWellFoundedGT.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LT α] [WellFoundedGT α] : WellFoundedGT (WithBot α)

explanatories.WithBot.some: This defines a function that constructs an element of a type that includes a least element from a regular element of that type.

explanatories.And.intro: The constructor for the "And" operation combines two propositions into a single proposition that asserts both are true.
explanatories.LT.lt: This definition introduces a relation that expresses when one element is less than another within a given type.
explanatories.WithBot.coe_lt_coe: This theorem establishes that the boxed representation of one element being less than that of another is equivalent to the original elements being in the same order of inequality.
explanatories.WithBot.not_lt_bot: This theorem asserts that no element in a structured type can be less than the least element included in a type that has an additional bottom element.
explanatories.Iff.intro: This theorem establishes that two propositions are equivalent if each can be inferred from the other.
explanatories.absurd: This operation allows one to derive any conclusion from a pair of contradictory statements.
explanatories.Acc.intro: A value is accessible if every related predecessor is also accessible, and if there are no such predecessors, the value itself is accessible and is termed a base case.
explanatories.WellFounded.intro: This theorem establishes that a relation is well-founded if every element is accessible under that relation.

WithBot.instWellFoundedGT.fullDefinition: instance _root_.WithBot.instWellFoundedGT [LT α] [WellFoundedGT α] : WellFoundedGT (WithBot α) where   wf :=   have acc_some (a : α) : Acc ((· > ·) : WithBot α → WithBot α → Prop) a :=     (wellFounded_gt.1 a).rec fun _ _ ih =>       .intro _ fun         | (b : α), hlt => ih _ (coe_lt_coe.1 hlt)         | ⊥, hlt => absurd hlt (WithBot.not_lt_bot _)   .intro fun     | (a : α) => acc_some a     | ⊥ => .intro _ fun       | (b : α), _ => acc_some b       | ⊥, hlt => absurd hlt (WithBot.not_lt_bot _)
WithBot.instWellFoundedGT.description: This defines a well-founded version of the greater than relation for a type that includes a least element, ensuring that every subset of greater elements has a minimal element.

WithBot.lt_iff_exists_coe_btwn.code:
WithBot.lt_iff_exists_coe_btwn.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] [DenselyOrdered α] [NoMinOrder α] {a b : WithBot α} :

inf_Prop_eq.description: The operation of intersecting two propositions using the infimum is equivalent to their logical conjunction.

  [FunLike F α β] : Prop
OrderHomClass.comment: `OrderHomClass F α b` asserts that `F` is a type of `≤`-preserving morphisms.

OrderHomClass.description: This defines a class that characterizes types of morphisms that preserve order structure between two types.

OrderIsoClass.map_le_map_iff.code:
OrderIsoClass.map_le_map_iff.{u_6, u_7, u_8} {F : Type u_6} {α : Type u_7} {β : Type u_8} [LE α] [LE β]
  [EquivLike F α β] [self : OrderIsoClass F α β] (f : F) {a b : α} : f a ≤ f b ↔ a ≤ b
OrderIsoClass.map_le_map_iff.description: This theorem states that an order isomorphism preserves the order relation between two types, meaning that if the image of one element is less than or equal to the image of another, then the original elements must also maintain that relationship.

OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso.code:

OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso.comment:

OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso.fullDefinition: def OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso [LE α] [LE β] [EquivLike F α β] [OrderIsoClass F α β] (f : F) :     α ≃o β :=   { EquivLike.toEquiv f with map_rel_iff' := map_le_map_iff f }
OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso.description: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order isomorphism between two types.

OrderIsoClass.toOrderHomClass.code:

le_map_inv_iff.code:

lt_map_inv_iff.code:

OrderHom.curry.fullDefinition: def curry : (α × β →o γ) ≃o (α →o β →o γ) where   toFun f := ⟨fun x ↦ ⟨Function.curry f x, fun _ _ h ↦ f.mono ⟨le_rfl, h⟩⟩, fun _ _ h _ =>     f.mono ⟨h, le_rfl⟩⟩   invFun f := ⟨Function.uncurry fun x ↦ f x, fun x y h ↦ (f.mono h.1 x.2).trans ((f y.1).mono h.2)⟩   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl   map_rel_iff' := by simp [le_def]

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.

Pi.evalOrderHom_coe.description: This theorem shows that the order-preserving map corresponding to evaluation at a specific index in a family of preordered types is equivalent to the function that evaluates at that index.

OrderHom.coeFnHom.code: OrderHom.coeFnHom.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] : (α →o β) →o α → β
OrderHom.coeFnHom.comment:
The "forgetful functor" from `α →o β` to `α → β` that takes the underlying function,
is monotone.

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone': This theorem establishes that the underlying function of an order homomorphism is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order relation between the two types.

OrderHom.coeFnHom.fullDefinition: def coeFnHom : (α →o β) →o α → β where   toFun f := f   monotone' _ _ h := h
OrderHom.coeFnHom.description: This defines a structure that allows one to extract the underlying function from an order homomorphism while ensuring it remains monotonic with respect to the original order.

OrderHom.coeFnHom_coe.code: OrderHom.coeFnHom_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] : ⇑coeFnHom = fun f => ⇑f
OrderHom.coeFnHom_coe.description: This theorem establishes that the function that corresponds to an order homomorphism's coercion matches the function obtained by applying the order homomorphism itself.

OrderHom.apply.code: OrderHom.apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (x : α) : (α →o β) →o β
OrderHom.apply.comment:
Function application `fun f => f a` (for fixed `a`) is a monotone function from the
monotone function space `α →o β` to `β`. See also `Pi.evalOrderHom`.

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.
explanatories.Pi.evalOrderHom: This defines an order-preserving function that evaluates a family of types at a specific index, producing an output in the corresponding type.

OrderHom.apply.fullDefinition: def apply (x : α) : (α →o β) →o β :=   (Pi.evalOrderHom x).comp coeFnHom
OrderHom.apply.description: This defines a monotone function that takes a fixed input from one ordered type and produces a corresponding output from another ordered type by applying an order-preserving function.

OrderHom.apply_coe.code:
OrderHom.apply_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (x : α) :
  ⇑(apply x) = Function.eval x ∘ fun f => ⇑f

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.

OrderHom.apply_coe.description: This theorem states that applying a specific order homomorphism at a point is equivalent to composing the evaluation function with the underlying functions of other order homomorphisms.

OrderHom.pi.code:
OrderHom.pi.{u_2, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {ι : Type u_6} {π : ι → Type u_7} [(i : ι) → Preorder (π i)]
  (f : (i : ι) → α →o π i) : α →o (i : ι) → π i
OrderHom.pi.comment:
Construct a bundled monotone map `α →o Π i, π i` from a family of monotone maps
`f i : α →o π i`.

explanatories.OrderHomClass.mono: This theorem states that an order homomorphism is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order between elements of the two types involved.
explanatories.OrderHom.mono: This theorem states that any order homomorphism between preordered types is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order between the input and output elements.

OrderHom.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (f : ∀ i, α →o π i) : α →o ∀ i, π i :=   ⟨fun x i => f i x, fun _ _ h i => (f i).mono h⟩
OrderHom.pi.description: This defines an order-preserving function that takes an input from one ordered set and transforms it into a product of outputs from a family of ordered sets based on corresponding monotone functions.

OrderHom.pi_coe.code:
OrderHom.pi_coe.{u_2, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {ι : Type u_6} {π : ι → Type u_7} [(i : ι) → Preorder (π i)]
  (f : (i : ι) → α →o π i) (x : α) (i : ι) : (pi f) x i = (f i) x
OrderHom.pi_coe.description: This theorem establishes that applying a product of order-preserving functions to an element produces the same result as applying the individual function for a specific index.

OrderHom.piIso.code:
OrderHom.piIso.{u_2, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {ι : Type u_6} {π : ι → Type u_7}
  [(i : ι) → Preorder (π i)] : (α →o (i : ι) → π i) ≃o ((i : ι) → α →o π i)
OrderHom.piIso.comment:
Order isomorphism between bundled monotone maps `α →o Π i, π i` and families of bundled monotone
maps `Π i, α →o π i`.

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.
explanatories.Pi.evalOrderHom: This defines an order-preserving function that evaluates a family of types at a specific index, producing an output in the corresponding type.

OrderHom.piIso.fullDefinition: def piIso : (α →o ∀ i, π i) ≃o ∀ i, α →o π i where   toFun f i := (Pi.evalOrderHom i).comp f   invFun := pi   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl   map_rel_iff' := forall_swap
OrderHom.piIso.description: This definition establishes an order isomorphism between a collection of monotone functions mapping from a preordered type to a family of other preordered types and a family of monotone functions mapping from each of those types back to the original preordered type.

OrderHom.piIso_apply.code:
OrderHom.piIso_apply.{u_2, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {ι : Type u_6} {π : ι → Type u_7}
  [(i : ι) → Preorder (π i)] (f : α →o (i : ι) → π i) (i : ι) : piIso f i = (Pi.evalOrderHom i).comp f

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.
explanatories.Pi.evalOrderHom: This defines an order-preserving function that evaluates a family of types at a specific index, producing an output in the corresponding type.

OrderHom.piIso_apply.description: This theorem establishes the equality of a certain order homomorphism applied to a function with the composition of the evaluation homomorphism and that function at a specific index.

OrderHom.piIso_symm_apply.code:
OrderHom.piIso_symm_apply.{u_2, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {ι : Type u_6} {π : ι → Type u_7}
  [(i : ι) → Preorder (π i)] (f : (i : ι) → α →o π i) : (RelIso.symm piIso) f = pi f

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderHom.piIso_symm_apply.description: This theorem establishes that the inverse of a given order homomorphism in the context of a product type corresponds to the product of the original order homomorphisms applied to each component.

OrderHom.Subtype.val.code: OrderHom.Subtype.val.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] (p : α → Prop) : Subtype p →o α
OrderHom.Subtype.val.fullDefinition: def Subtype.val (p : α → Prop) : Subtype p →o α :=   ⟨_root_.Subtype.val, fun _ _ h => h⟩
OrderHom.Subtype.val.description: This definition describes a monotone function that extracts elements from a subtype of a preordered type while preserving the order.

OrderHom.Subtype.val_coe.code: OrderHom.Subtype.val_coe.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] (p : α → Prop) : ⇑(Subtype.val p) = _root_.Subtype.val
OrderHom.Subtype.val_coe.description: This theorem establishes that the coercion of the value function for a subtype of a preordered type is identical to the standard value function for that subtype.

OrderHom.unique.code: OrderHom.unique.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Subsingleton α] : Unique (α →o α)
OrderHom.unique.comment: There is a unique monotone map from a subsingleton to itself.

explanatories.OrderHom.ext: This theorem demonstrates that if two order homomorphisms agree on their underlying functions, then they are equal as order homomorphisms.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.
explanatories.OrderHom.id: This definition establishes the identity function as an order homomorphism that preserves the order within a preordered type.
explanatories.Subsingleton.elim: If a type is a subsingleton, then any two elements of that type are equal.

OrderHom.unique.fullDefinition: instance unique [Subsingleton α] : Unique (α →o α) where   default := OrderHom.id   uniq _ := ext _ _ (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
OrderHom.unique.description: This definition asserts that there is exactly one order-preserving function from a subsingleton set to itself.

OrderHom.orderHom_eq_id.code: OrderHom.orderHom_eq_id.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Subsingleton α] (g : α →o α) : g = id
OrderHom.orderHom_eq_id.description: This theorem states that any order-preserving function on a type that has a unique element is equal to the identity function on that type.

OrderHom.dual.code: OrderHom.dual.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] : (α →o β) ≃ (αᵒᵈ →o βᵒᵈ)
OrderHom.dual.comment: Reinterpret a bundled monotone function as a monotone function between dual orders.

explanatories.OrderHomClass.mono: This theorem states that an order homomorphism is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order between elements of the two types involved.
explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.OrderHom.mono: This theorem states that any order homomorphism between preordered types is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order between the input and output elements.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

OrderHom.dual.fullDefinition: protected def dual : (α →o β) ≃ (αᵒᵈ →o βᵒᵈ) where   toFun f := ⟨(OrderDual.toDual : β → βᵒᵈ) ∘ (f : α → β) ∘     (OrderDual.ofDual : αᵒᵈ → α), f.mono.dual⟩   invFun f := ⟨OrderDual.ofDual ∘ f ∘ OrderDual.toDual, f.mono.dual⟩   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl
OrderHom.dual.description: This definition establishes a bijective equivalence between order-preserving functions and their counterparts on the dual orders, effectively allowing the reinterpretation of monotone functions in this context.

OrderHom.dual_apply_coe.code:
OrderHom.dual_apply_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α →o β) :
  ∀ (a : αᵒᵈ), (OrderHom.dual f) a = (⇑toDual ∘ ⇑f ∘ ⇑ofDual) a
OrderHom.dual_apply_coe.description: This theorem demonstrates how applying the dual of an order-preserving function to an element of a dual ordered type can be expressed as the composition of mappings that switch between original and dual types.

OrderHom.dual_symm_apply_coe.code:
OrderHom.dual_symm_apply_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : αᵒᵈ →o βᵒᵈ) :
  ∀ (a : α), (OrderHom.dual.symm f) a = (⇑ofDual ∘ ⇑f ∘ ⇑toDual) a

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderHom.dual_symm_apply_coe.description: This theorem demonstrates how the inverse of an order homomorphism from the dual of one preordered type to the dual of another can be expressed as the composition of functions involving the duality operations.

OrderHom.dual_id.code: OrderHom.dual_id.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] : OrderHom.dual id = id

explanatories.OrderHom.id: This definition establishes the identity function as an order homomorphism that preserves the order within a preordered type.

OrderHom.dual_id.description: This theorem states that the dual of the identity order homomorphism is itself the identity order homomorphism for any preordered set.

OrderHom.dual_comp.code:
OrderHom.dual_comp.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] [Preorder γ]
  (g : β →o γ) (f : α →o β) : OrderHom.dual (g.comp f) = (OrderHom.dual g).comp (OrderHom.dual f)

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.

OrderHom.dual_comp.description: This theorem establishes that the dual of the composition of two order homomorphisms is equal to the composition of their respective duals.

OrderHom.symm_dual_id.code: OrderHom.symm_dual_id.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] : OrderHom.dual.symm id = id

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.OrderHom.id: This definition establishes the identity function as an order homomorphism that preserves the order within a preordered type.

OrderHom.symm_dual_id.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the dual order homomorphism for the identity function on a preordered type is itself the identity function.

OrderHom.symm_dual_comp.code:
OrderHom.symm_dual_comp.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [Preorder α] [Preorder β]
  [Preorder γ] (g : βᵒᵈ →o γᵒᵈ) (f : αᵒᵈ →o βᵒᵈ) :
  OrderHom.dual.symm (g.comp f) = (OrderHom.dual.symm g).comp (OrderHom.dual.symm f)

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.

OrderHom.symm_dual_comp.description: This theorem demonstrates that the duality of order homomorphism composition is preserved under the equivalence of symmetrically dual order structures.

OrderHom.dualIso.code: OrderHom.dualIso.{u_8, u_9} (α : Type u_8) (β : Type u_9) [Preorder α] [Preorder β] : (α →o β) ≃o (αᵒᵈ →o βᵒᵈ)ᵒᵈ

explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

OrderHom.dualIso.fullDefinition: def dualIso (α β : Type*) [Preorder α] [Preorder β] : (α →o β) ≃o (αᵒᵈ →o βᵒᵈ)ᵒᵈ where   toEquiv := OrderHom.dual.trans OrderDual.toDual   map_rel_iff' := Iff.rfl
OrderHom.dualIso.description: This definition establishes a bijective relationship between order-preserving functions from one preordered type to another and their corresponding dual order-preserving functions, thereby showing how order can be reversed in this context.

OrderHom.withBotMap.code:
OrderHom.withBotMap.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α →o β) :
  WithBot α →o WithBot β
OrderHom.withBotMap.comment: Lift an order homomorphism `f : α →o β` to an order homomorphism `WithBot α →o WithBot β`.

explanatories.OrderHomClass.mono: This theorem states that an order homomorphism is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order between elements of the two types involved.
explanatories.OrderHom.mono: This theorem states that any order homomorphism between preordered types is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order between the input and output elements.
explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

OrderHom.withBotMap.fullDefinition: protected def withBotMap (f : α →o β) : WithBot α →o WithBot β :=   ⟨WithBot.map f, f.mono.withBot_map⟩
OrderHom.withBotMap.description: This definition describes how to extend an order homomorphism from one preordered type to another that includes a bottom element.

OrderHom.withBotMap_coe.code:
OrderHom.withBotMap_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α →o β) :
  ⇑f.withBotMap = WithBot.map ⇑f

explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

OrderHom.withBotMap_coe.description: This theorem demonstrates that the function induced by an order homomorphism, when utilizing a mapping that includes a designated least element, is equivalent to applying the mapping on the image under the order homomorphism.

OrderHom.withTopMap.code:
OrderHom.withTopMap.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α →o β) :
  WithTop α →o WithTop β
OrderHom.withTopMap.comment: Lift an order homomorphism `f : α →o β` to an order homomorphism `WithTop α →o WithTop β`.

explanatories.OrderHomClass.mono: This theorem states that an order homomorphism is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order between elements of the two types involved.
explanatories.OrderHom.mono: This theorem states that any order homomorphism between preordered types is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order between the input and output elements.
explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

OrderHom.withTopMap.fullDefinition: protected def withTopMap (f : α →o β) : WithTop α →o WithTop β :=   ⟨WithTop.map f, f.mono.withTop_map⟩
OrderHom.withTopMap.description: This definition describes a process for extending an order homomorphism from one preordered type to another by incorporating a top element in the domain.

OrderHom.withTopMap_coe.code:
OrderHom.withTopMap_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α →o β) :
  ⇑f.withTopMap = WithTop.map ⇑f

explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

OrderHom.withTopMap_coe.description: This theorem shows that the image of an order homomorphism extended with an additional top element corresponds exactly to mapping the original homomorphism through the WithTop structure.

RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.code:
RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β]
  (f : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) ↪r fun x x_1 => x < x_1) : α ↪o β
RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.comment: Embeddings of partial orders that preserve `<` also preserve `≤`.
RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.fullDefinition: def RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β]     (f : ((· < ·) : α → α → Prop) ↪r ((· < ·) : β → β → Prop)) : α ↪o β :=   { f with     map_rel_iff' := by       intros       simp [le_iff_lt_or_eq, f.map_rel_iff, f.injective.eq_iff] }
RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.description: This defines an order embedding from one partial order to another, given an embedding that preserves the strict inequality relation.

RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.code:
RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α]
  [PartialOrder β] {f : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) ↪r fun x x_1 => x < x_1} {x : α} : f.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding x = f x
RelEmbedding.orderEmbeddingOfLTEmbedding.description: This theorem asserts that applying a relation embedding to an element in a partially ordered set yields the same result as applying the embedding directly to that element.

OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding.code:
OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) ↪r fun x x_1 => x < x_1
OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding.comment: `<` is preserved by order embeddings of preorders.
OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding.fullDefinition: def ltEmbedding : ((· < ·) : α → α → Prop) ↪r ((· < ·) : β → β → Prop) :=   { f with map_rel_iff' := by intros; simp [lt_iff_le_not_le, f.map_rel_iff] }
OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding.description: This defines a way to relate the order relation of two preordered types through an order embedding, ensuring that the order is preserved.

OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding_apply.code:
OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β)
  (x : α) : f.ltEmbedding x = f x
OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying an order embedding to an element yields the same result as its corresponding less-than embedding.

OrderEmbedding.le_iff_le.code:
OrderEmbedding.le_iff_le.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) {a b : α} :
  f a ≤ f b ↔ a ≤ b
OrderEmbedding.le_iff_le.description: This theorem asserts that the order relation is preserved under an order embedding, such that the images of two elements maintain their order if and only if the original elements do.

OrderEmbedding.lt_iff_lt.code:
OrderEmbedding.lt_iff_lt.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) {a b : α} :
  f a < f b ↔ a < b
OrderEmbedding.lt_iff_lt.description: This theorem states that for an order embedding, the relation between the images of two elements under the embedding is equivalent to the relation between the original elements, thus preserving the order.

OrderEmbedding.eq_iff_eq.code:
OrderEmbedding.eq_iff_eq.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) {a b : α} :
  f a = f b ↔ a = b
OrderEmbedding.eq_iff_eq.description: This theorem states that an order embedding preserves the distinctness of elements, meaning if two elements are mapped to the same image, then the original elements must also be equal.

OrderEmbedding.monotone.code: OrderEmbedding.monotone.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) : Monotone ⇑f

explanatories.OrderHomClass.monotone: This theorem states that any order-preserving morphism between preordered types is monotone.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone: This theorem asserts that any order homomorphism between two preordered types is a monotone function.

OrderEmbedding.monotone.description: This theorem establishes that any order embedding is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order of elements between the two preordered types.

OrderEmbedding.strictMono.code:
OrderEmbedding.strictMono.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  StrictMono ⇑f
OrderEmbedding.strictMono.description: This theorem asserts that any order embedding is strictly monotonic, meaning it preserves the strict order between elements when applied.

OrderEmbedding.acc.code:
OrderEmbedding.acc.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) (a : α) :
  Acc (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) (f a) → Acc (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) a
OrderEmbedding.acc.description: This theorem asserts that if a certain element is well-ordered in one ordered set under an order embedding, then the corresponding element in the original set is also well-ordered.

OrderEmbedding.wellFounded.code:
OrderEmbedding.wellFounded.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  (WellFounded fun x x_1 => x < x_1) → WellFounded fun x x_1 => x < x_1
OrderEmbedding.wellFounded.description: This theorem states that if one preordered type has a well-founded relation, then the other preordered type maintains a well-founded relation under the given order embedding.

OrderEmbedding.isWellOrder.code:
OrderEmbedding.isWellOrder.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β)
  [IsWellOrder β fun x x_1 => x < x_1] : IsWellOrder α fun x x_1 => x < x_1
OrderEmbedding.isWellOrder.description: This theorem establishes that if an order embedding preserves the order in one type, and the target type is well-ordered, then the original type is also well-ordered under the same order relation.

OrderEmbedding.dual.code: OrderEmbedding.dual.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) : αᵒᵈ ↪o βᵒᵈ
OrderEmbedding.dual.comment: An order embedding is also an order embedding between dual orders.

explanatories.OrderHom.dual: This definition establishes a bijective equivalence between order-preserving functions and their counterparts on the dual orders, effectively allowing the reinterpretation of monotone functions in this context.

OrderEmbedding.dual.fullDefinition: protected def dual : αᵒᵈ ↪o βᵒᵈ :=   ⟨f.toEmbedding, f.map_rel_iff⟩
OrderEmbedding.dual.description: This definition states that an order embedding between two preordered types induces an order embedding between their corresponding dual preordered types.

OrderEmbedding.wellFoundedLT.code:
OrderEmbedding.wellFoundedLT.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β)
  [WellFoundedLT β] : WellFoundedLT α
OrderEmbedding.wellFoundedLT.comment: A preorder which embeds into a well-founded preorder is itself well-founded.
OrderEmbedding.wellFoundedLT.description: This theorem asserts that a preorder that can be embedded into a well-founded preorder is also well-founded.

OrderEmbedding.withBotMap.code:
OrderEmbedding.withBotMap.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  WithBot α ↪o WithBot β
OrderEmbedding.withBotMap.comment: A version of `WithBot.map` for order embeddings.

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.
explanatories.OrderHom.withBotMap: This definition describes how to extend an order homomorphism from one preordered type to another that includes a bottom element.

OrderEmbedding.withBotMap.fullDefinition: protected def withBotMap (f : α ↪o β) : WithBot α ↪o WithBot β :=   { f.toEmbedding.optionMap with     toFun := WithBot.map f,     map_rel_iff' := @fun a b => WithBot.map_le_iff f f.map_rel_iff a b }
OrderEmbedding.withBotMap.description: This defines a mapping that transforms an order embedding between two types into an order embedding between their extended forms that include a bottom element.

OrderEmbedding.withBotMap_apply.code:
OrderEmbedding.withBotMap_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  ⇑f.withBotMap = WithBot.map ⇑f

explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.
explanatories.OrderHom.withBotMap: This definition describes how to extend an order homomorphism from one preordered type to another that includes a bottom element.

OrderEmbedding.withBotMap_apply.description: This theorem establishes that the mapping of an order embedding that includes a bot element is equivalent to applying the bot transformation followed by the original mapping.

OrderEmbedding.withTopMap.code:
OrderEmbedding.withTopMap.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  WithTop α ↪o WithTop β
OrderEmbedding.withTopMap.comment: A version of `WithTop.map` for order embeddings.

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.
explanatories.OrderHom.dual: This definition establishes a bijective equivalence between order-preserving functions and their counterparts on the dual orders, effectively allowing the reinterpretation of monotone functions in this context.
explanatories.OrderHom.withTopMap: This definition describes a process for extending an order homomorphism from one preordered type to another by incorporating a top element in the domain.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.dual: This definition states that an order embedding between two preordered types induces an order embedding between their corresponding dual preordered types.

OrderEmbedding.withTopMap.fullDefinition: protected def withTopMap (f : α ↪o β) : WithTop α ↪o WithTop β :=   { f.dual.withBotMap.dual with toFun := WithTop.map f }
OrderEmbedding.withTopMap.description: This definition specifies a mapping from an order embedding of one preordered type to another that extends the structure to include a top element.

OrderEmbedding.withTopMap_apply.code:
OrderEmbedding.withTopMap_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α ↪o β) :
  ⇑f.withTopMap = WithTop.map ⇑f

explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.
explanatories.OrderHom.withTopMap: This definition describes a process for extending an order homomorphism from one preordered type to another by incorporating a top element in the domain.

OrderEmbedding.withTopMap_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying the map associated with an order embedding that includes a top element is equivalent to applying the top element map followed by the original embedding.

OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff.code:
OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β)
  (hf : ∀ (a b : α), f a ≤ f b ↔ a ≤ b) : α ↪o β
OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff.comment:
To define an order embedding from a partial order to a preorder it suffices to give a function
together with a proof that it satisfies `f a ≤ f b ↔ a ≤ b`.
OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff.fullDefinition: def ofMapLEIff {α β} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) (hf : ∀ a b, f a ≤ f b ↔ a ≤ b) :     α ↪o β :=   RelEmbedding.ofMapRelIff f hf
OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff.description: This defines a method to create an order embedding from a partial order to a preorder by providing a function and demonstrating that it preserves the order relation.

OrderEmbedding.coe_ofMapLEIff.code:
OrderEmbedding.coe_ofMapLEIff.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β}
  (h : ∀ (a b : α), f a ≤ f b ↔ a ≤ b) : ⇑(ofMapLEIff f h) = f

explanatories.OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff: This defines a method to create an order embedding from a partial order to a preorder by providing a function and demonstrating that it preserves the order relation.

OrderEmbedding.coe_ofMapLEIff.description: This theorem states that if a function maintains the order relation between two preordered types, then the order embedding corresponding to this function is equivalent to the function itself.

OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono.code:
OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} [LinearOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β)
  (h : StrictMono f) : α ↪o β
OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono.comment: A strictly monotone map from a linear order is an order embedding.

explanatories.OrderEmbedding.le_iff_le: This theorem asserts that the order relation is preserved under an order embedding, such that the images of two elements maintain their order if and only if the original elements do.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff: This defines a method to create an order embedding from a partial order to a preorder by providing a function and demonstrating that it preserves the order relation.

OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono.fullDefinition: def ofStrictMono {α β} [LinearOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) (h : StrictMono f) : α ↪o β :=   ofMapLEIff f fun _ _ => h.le_iff_le
OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono.description: This definition describes a construction that establishes an order embedding from a strictly monotone function originating from a linear order.

OrderEmbedding.coe_ofStrictMono.code:
OrderEmbedding.coe_ofStrictMono.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} [LinearOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β}
  (h : StrictMono f) : ⇑(ofStrictMono f h) = f

explanatories.OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono: This definition describes a construction that establishes an order embedding from a strictly monotone function originating from a linear order.

OrderEmbedding.coe_ofStrictMono.description: This theorem confirms that the canonical embedding of a strictly monotonic function from a linearly ordered type to a preordered type is equal to the function itself.

OrderEmbedding.subtype.code: OrderEmbedding.subtype.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] (p : α → Prop) : Subtype p ↪o α
OrderEmbedding.subtype.comment: Embedding of a subtype into the ambient type as an `OrderEmbedding`.

explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

OrderEmbedding.subtype.fullDefinition: def subtype (p : α → Prop) : Subtype p ↪o α :=   ⟨Function.Embedding.subtype p, Iff.rfl⟩
OrderEmbedding.subtype.description: This definition establishes a way to embed a subtype with a property into a larger preordered type while preserving the order relation.

OrderEmbedding.subtype_apply.code: OrderEmbedding.subtype_apply.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Preorder α] (p : α → Prop) : ⇑(subtype p) = Subtype.val
OrderEmbedding.subtype_apply.description: This theorem states that the canonical function associated with a subtype order embedding is equivalent to the value function of the subtype.

OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom.code: OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom.{u_6, u_7} {X : Type u_6} {Y : Type u_7} [Preorder X] [Preorder Y] (f : X ↪o Y) : X →o Y

explanatories.OrderHomClass.monotone: This theorem states that any order-preserving morphism between preordered types is monotone.
explanatories.OrderHomClass.toOrderHom: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order homomorphism between two preordered types.
explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone': This theorem establishes that the underlying function of an order homomorphism is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order relation between the two types.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone: This theorem asserts that any order homomorphism between two preordered types is a monotone function.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.monotone: This theorem establishes that any order embedding is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order of elements between the two preordered types.

OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom.fullDefinition: def toOrderHom {X Y : Type*} [Preorder X] [Preorder Y] (f : X ↪o Y) : X →o Y where   toFun := f   monotone' := f.monotone
OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom.description: This definition describes a method for converting an order embedding into an order homomorphism.

OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom_coe.code:
OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom_coe.{u_6, u_7} {X : Type u_6} {Y : Type u_7} [Preorder X] [Preorder Y] (f : X ↪o Y) :
  ⇑f.toOrderHom = ⇑f

explanatories.OrderHomClass.toOrderHom: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order homomorphism between two preordered types.

OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom_coe.description: This theorem asserts that the function obtained from an order embedding, when viewed as an order homomorphism, is equal to the original order embedding function itself.

OrderEmbedding.ofIsEmpty.code: OrderEmbedding.ofIsEmpty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] [IsEmpty α] : α ↪o β
OrderEmbedding.ofIsEmpty.comment: The trivial embedding from an empty preorder to another preorder

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.

OrderEmbedding.ofIsEmpty.fullDefinition: @[simps] def ofIsEmpty [IsEmpty α] : α ↪o β where   toFun := isEmptyElim   inj' := isEmptyElim   map_rel_iff' {a} := isEmptyElim a
OrderEmbedding.ofIsEmpty.description: This defines a trivial order embedding from an empty preordered type to any other preordered type.

Disjoint.of_orderEmbedding.code:
Disjoint.of_orderEmbedding.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] (f : α ↪o β)
  [OrderBot α] [OrderBot β] {a₁ a₂ : α} : Disjoint (f a₁) (f a₂) → Disjoint a₁ a₂
Disjoint.of_orderEmbedding.comment:
If the images by an order embedding of two elements are disjoint,
then they are themselves disjoint.
Disjoint.of_orderEmbedding.description: This theorem states that if two elements' images under an order embedding are disjoint, then the original elements themselves must also be disjoint.

Codisjoint.of_orderEmbedding.code:
Codisjoint.of_orderEmbedding.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] (f : α ↪o β)
  [OrderTop α] [OrderTop β] {a₁ a₂ : α} : Codisjoint (f a₁) (f a₂) → Codisjoint a₁ a₂
Codisjoint.of_orderEmbedding.comment:
If the images by an order embedding of two elements are codisjoint,
then they are themselves codisjoint.

explanatories.Disjoint.of_orderEmbedding: This theorem states that if two elements' images under an order embedding are disjoint, then the original elements themselves must also be disjoint.

Codisjoint.of_orderEmbedding.description: This theorem states that if two elements are codisjoint after being mapped by an order embedding, then the original elements are also codisjoint in their respective ordered sets.

RelHom.toOrderHom.code:
RelHom.toOrderHom.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β]
  (f : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) →r fun x x_1 => x < x_1) : α →o β
RelHom.toOrderHom.comment:
A bundled expression of the fact that a map between partial orders that is strictly monotone
is weakly monotone.

explanatories.OrderHomClass.monotone: This theorem states that any order-preserving morphism between preordered types is monotone.
explanatories.OrderHomClass.toOrderHom: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order homomorphism between two preordered types.
explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone': This theorem establishes that the underlying function of an order homomorphism is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order relation between the two types.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone: This theorem asserts that any order homomorphism between two preordered types is a monotone function.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.monotone: This theorem establishes that any order embedding is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order of elements between the two preordered types.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom: This definition describes a method for converting an order embedding into an order homomorphism.

RelHom.toOrderHom.fullDefinition: def toOrderHom : α →o β where   toFun := f   monotone' := StrictMono.monotone fun _ _ => f.map_rel
RelHom.toOrderHom.description: This definition describes a way to construct an order homomorphism from a strictly monotone function between partial orders, ensuring that the resulting function is weakly monotone.

RelHom.toOrderHom_coe.code:
RelHom.toOrderHom_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β]
  (f : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) →r fun x x_1 => x < x_1) : ⇑f.toOrderHom = ⇑f

explanatories.OrderHomClass.toOrderHom: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order homomorphism between two preordered types.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom: This definition describes a method for converting an order embedding into an order homomorphism.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.toOrderHom_coe: This theorem asserts that the function obtained from an order embedding, when viewed as an order homomorphism, is equal to the original order embedding function itself.

RelHom.toOrderHom_coe.description: This theorem states that a relation homomorphism from a partially ordered set to a preordered set maintains the original function when viewed as an order homomorphism.

RelEmbedding.toOrderHom_injective.code:
RelEmbedding.toOrderHom_injective.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β]
  (f : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) ↪r fun x x_1 => x < x_1) : Function.Injective ⇑f.toRelHom.toOrderHom
RelEmbedding.toOrderHom_injective.description: This theorem establishes that the embedding of a relation into a preorder is injective when considered as a function that preserves order, ensuring that distinct relations map to distinct order homomorphisms.

OrderIso.toFun_eq_coe.code: OrderIso.toFun_eq_coe.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] {f : α ≃o β} : f.toFun = ⇑f

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.OrderHom.toFun_eq_coe: This theorem asserts that the underlying function of an order homomorphism is equal to its coercion into a function, affirming the consistency between these representations.

OrderIso.toFun_eq_coe.description: This theorem establishes that the function associated with an order isomorphism is equal to its coercion to a function.

OrderIso.ext.code: OrderIso.ext.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] {f g : α ≃o β} (h : ⇑f = ⇑g) : f = g

OrderIso.toOrderEmbedding.code: OrderIso.toOrderEmbedding.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) : α ↪o β
OrderIso.toOrderEmbedding.comment: Reinterpret an order isomorphism as an order embedding.
OrderIso.toOrderEmbedding.fullDefinition: def toOrderEmbedding (e : α ≃o β) : α ↪o β :=   e.toRelEmbedding
OrderIso.toOrderEmbedding.description: This defines a way to view an order isomorphism as an order-preserving function from one ordered set to another.

OrderIso.coe_toOrderEmbedding.code:
OrderIso.coe_toOrderEmbedding.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) :
  ⇑e.toOrderEmbedding = ⇑e

explanatories.OrderIso.toOrderEmbedding: This defines a way to view an order isomorphism as an order-preserving function from one ordered set to another.

OrderIso.coe_toOrderEmbedding.description: This theorem states that the function associated with an order isomorphism, when viewed as an order embedding, remains unchanged.

OrderIso.bijective.code: OrderIso.bijective.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) : Function.Bijective ⇑e
OrderIso.bijective.description: This theorem demonstrates that an order isomorphism is a bijective function, meaning it establishes a one-to-one correspondence between two ordered sets.

OrderIso.injective.code: OrderIso.injective.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) : Function.Injective ⇑e
OrderIso.injective.description: This theorem states that an order isomorphism between two preordered types is injective when considering the underlying functions.

OrderIso.surjective.code: OrderIso.surjective.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) : Function.Surjective ⇑e
OrderIso.surjective.description: This theorem demonstrates that an order isomorphism between two preordered types is a surjective function, meaning every element in the target can be reached by some element in the domain.

OrderIso.apply_eq_iff_eq.code:
OrderIso.apply_eq_iff_eq.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) {x y : α} :

OrderIso.apply_eq_iff_eq.description: This theorem asserts that an order isomorphism preserves equality, such that two elements are equal under the isomorphism if and only if they are equal in their original order.

OrderIso.refl.code: OrderIso.refl.{u_6} (α : Type u_6) [LE α] : α ≃o α
OrderIso.refl.fullDefinition: def refl (α : Type*) [LE α] : α ≃o α :=   RelIso.refl (· ≤ ·)
OrderIso.refl.description: This defines an identity order isomorphism on an ordered type that establishes a one-to-one correspondence while preserving the order.

OrderIso.coe_refl.code: OrderIso.coe_refl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [LE α] : ⇑(refl α) = id

explanatories.OrderIso.refl: This defines an identity order isomorphism on an ordered type that establishes a one-to-one correspondence while preserving the order.

OrderIso.coe_refl.description: This theorem asserts that the reflection of an order isomorphism from a type to itself coincides with the identity function on that type.

OrderIso.refl_apply.code: OrderIso.refl_apply.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [LE α] (x : α) : (refl α) x = x
OrderIso.refl_apply.description: This theorem establishes that the reflexive order isomorphism applied to any element returns that same element, confirming the property of identity.

OrderIso.refl_toEquiv.code: OrderIso.refl_toEquiv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [LE α] : (refl α).toEquiv = Equiv.refl α
OrderIso.refl_toEquiv.description: This theorem shows that the reflection property of an order isomorphism coincides with the reflection of the equivalence relation on the same type.

OrderIso.symm.code: OrderIso.symm.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) : β ≃o α

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderIso.symm.fullDefinition: def symm (e : α ≃o β) : β ≃o α := RelIso.symm e
OrderIso.symm.description: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.

OrderIso.apply_symm_apply.code: OrderIso.apply_symm_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) (x : β) : e (e.symm x) = x

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.

OrderIso.apply_symm_apply.description: This theorem establishes that applying an order isomorphism to an element obtained by its inverse yields the original element.

OrderIso.symm_apply_apply.code: OrderIso.symm_apply_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) (x : α) : e.symm (e x) = x

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderIso.symm_apply_apply.description: This theorem confirms that applying an order isomorphism to an element and then applying its inverse returns the original element, demonstrating the property of invertibility.

OrderIso.symm_refl.code: OrderIso.symm_refl.{u_6} (α : Type u_6) [LE α] : (refl α).symm = refl α

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.OrderIso.refl: This defines an identity order isomorphism on an ordered type that establishes a one-to-one correspondence while preserving the order.

OrderIso.symm_refl.description: This theorem asserts that the symmetrization of the identity order isomorphism is itself the identity order isomorphism.

OrderIso.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply.code:
OrderIso.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) (x : α)

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.

OrderIso.symm_apply_eq.code:
OrderIso.symm_apply_eq.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) {x : α} {y : β} :

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderIso.symm_apply_eq.description: This theorem states that the inverse of an order isomorphism applied to an element equals another element if and only if the original element equals the image of that element under the isomorphism.

OrderIso.symm_symm.code: OrderIso.symm_symm.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (e : α ≃o β) : e.symm.symm = e

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderIso.symm_symm.description: This theorem demonstrates that taking the symmetric of an order isomorphism twice yields the original isomorphism.

OrderIso.symm_bijective.code: OrderIso.symm_bijective.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] : Function.Bijective symm

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
