explanatories.OrderIso.ofRelIsoLT: This definition transforms a relational isomorphism based on the less-than relation into an order isomorphism between two partially ordered sets.

OrderIso.toRelIsoLT_ofRelIsoLT.description: This theorem establishes that a specific relationship between ordered types, described in terms of 'less than' relations, is preserved under a given order isomorphism.

OrderIso.ofCmpEqCmp.code:
OrderIso.ofCmpEqCmp.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β] (f : α → β) (g : β → α)
  (h : ∀ (a : α) (b : β), cmp a (g b) = cmp (f a) b) : α ≃o β
OrderIso.ofCmpEqCmp.comment:
To show that `f : α → β`, `g : β → α` make up an order isomorphism of linear orders,
it suffices to prove `cmp a (g b) = cmp (f a) b`.

explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.
explanatories.And.intro: The constructor for the "And" operation combines two propositions into a single proposition that asserts both are true.
explanatories.OrderHom.apply: This defines a monotone function that takes a fixed input from one ordered type and produces a corresponding output from another ordered type by applying an order-preserving function.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.
explanatories.Iff.intro: This theorem establishes that two propositions are equivalent if each can be inferred from the other.

OrderIso.ofCmpEqCmp.fullDefinition: def ofCmpEqCmp {α β} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β] (f : α → β) (g : β → α)     (h : ∀ (a : α) (b : β), cmp a (g b) = cmp (f a) b) : α ≃o β :=   have gf : ∀ a : α, a = g (f a) := by     intro     rw [← cmp_eq_eq_iff, h, cmp_self_eq_eq]   { toFun := f, invFun := g, left_inv := fun a => (gf a).symm,     right_inv := by       intro       rw [← cmp_eq_eq_iff, ← h, cmp_self_eq_eq],     map_rel_iff' := by       intros a b       apply le_iff_le_of_cmp_eq_cmp       convert (h a (f b)).symm       apply gf }
OrderIso.ofCmpEqCmp.description: This definition states that two functions form an order isomorphism between linear orders if their comparison results are consistent across all pairs of elements from each order.

OrderIso.ofHomInv.comment:
To show that `f : α →o β` and `g : β →o α` make up an order isomorphism it is enough to show
that `g` is the inverse of `f`

explanatories.OrderHomClass: This defines a class that characterizes types of morphisms that preserve order structure between two types.
explanatories.OrderHomClass.monotone: This theorem states that any order-preserving morphism between preordered types is monotone.
explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone: This theorem asserts that any order homomorphism between two preordered types is a monotone function.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.monotone: This theorem establishes that any order embedding is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order of elements between the two preordered types.
explanatories.OrderIso.monotone: This theorem states that any order isomorphism is a monotone function, meaning it preserves the order between elements of the two types it relates.

OrderIso.ofHomInv.fullDefinition: def ofHomInv {F G : Type*} [FunLike F α β] [OrderHomClass F α β] [FunLike G β α]     [OrderHomClass G β α] (f : F) (g : G)     (h₁ : (f : α →o β).comp (g : β →o α) = OrderHom.id)     (h₂ : (g : β →o α).comp (f : α →o β) = OrderHom.id) :     α ≃o β where   toFun := f   invFun := g   left_inv := DFunLike.congr_fun h₂   right_inv := DFunLike.congr_fun h₁   map_rel_iff' := @fun a b =>     ⟨fun h => by       replace h := map_rel g h       rwa [Equiv.coe_fn_mk, show g (f a) = (g : β →o α).comp (f : α →o β) a from rfl,         show g (f b) = (g : β →o α).comp (f : α →o β) b from rfl, h₂] at h,       fun h => (f : α →o β).monotone h⟩
OrderIso.ofHomInv.description: This definition specifies that two order homomorphisms are inverses of each other if their compositions yield the identity order homomorphism, thus establishing an order isomorphism between the two preordered types.

OrderIso.funUnique.code: OrderIso.funUnique.{u_6, u_7} (α : Type u_6) (β : Type u_7) [Unique α] [Preorder β] : (α → β) ≃o β
OrderIso.funUnique.comment: Order isomorphism between `α → β` and `β`, where `α` has a unique element.

explanatories.OrderHom.le_def: This theorem characterizes the order between two order homomorphisms in terms of their values at all points in the domain, establishing that one is less than or equal to the other if and only if it produces less than or equal outputs for every input.

OrderIso.funUnique.fullDefinition: def funUnique (α β : Type*) [Unique α] [Preorder β] : (α → β) ≃o β where   toEquiv := Equiv.funUnique α β   map_rel_iff' := by simp [Pi.le_def, Unique.forall_iff]
OrderIso.funUnique.description: This defines an order isomorphism between the set of functions from a unique element type to another preordered type and the second preordered type itself.

OrderIso.funUnique_apply.code:
OrderIso.funUnique_apply.{u_6, u_7} (α : Type u_6) (β : Type u_7) [Unique α] [Preorder β]
  (f : (i : α) → (fun a => β) i) : (funUnique α β) f = f default
OrderIso.funUnique_apply.description: This theorem states that for a unique type and a preordered type, applying a function to the unique element of the type yields a result that is equal to using a unique function to map that element.

OrderIso.funUnique_toEquiv.code:
OrderIso.funUnique_toEquiv.{u_6, u_7} (α : Type u_6) (β : Type u_7) [Unique α] [Preorder β] :
  (funUnique α β).toEquiv = Equiv.funUnique α β
OrderIso.funUnique_toEquiv.description: This theorem confirms that the order isomorphism between functions from a unique element type to another preordered type is equivalent to a specific equivalence relation on those types.

OrderIso.funUnique_symm_apply.code:
OrderIso.funUnique_symm_apply.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} [Unique α] [Preorder β] :
  ⇑(funUnique α β).symm = Function.const α

OrderIso.funUnique_symm_apply.description: This theorem indicates that the inverse of a unique function order isomorphism, when applied, results in a constant function mapping every element of the unique type to a single value.

Equiv.toOrderIso.code:
Equiv.toOrderIso.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (e : α ≃ β) (h₁ : Monotone ⇑e)
  (h₂ : Monotone ⇑e.symm) : α ≃o β
Equiv.toOrderIso.comment:
If `e` is an equivalence with monotone forward and inverse maps, then `e` is an
order isomorphism.

explanatories.OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order isomorphism between two types.

explanatories.OrderIso.symm_apply_apply: This theorem confirms that applying an order isomorphism to an element and then applying its inverse returns the original element, demonstrating the property of invertibility.

Equiv.toOrderIso.fullDefinition: def toOrderIso (e : α ≃ β) (h₁ : Monotone e) (h₂ : Monotone e.symm) : α ≃o β :=   ⟨e, ⟨fun h => by simpa only [e.symm_apply_apply] using h₂ h, fun h => h₁ h⟩⟩
Equiv.toOrderIso.description: This defines a construction that transforms an equivalence between two preordered types into an order isomorphism if both the forward and inverse mappings are monotone.

Equiv.coe_toOrderIso.code:
Equiv.coe_toOrderIso.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (e : α ≃ β) (h₁ : Monotone ⇑e)
  (h₂ : Monotone ⇑e.symm) : ⇑(e.toOrderIso h₁ h₂) = ⇑e

explanatories.OrderIsoClass.toOrderIso: This defines a conversion that allows an element of a type satisfying certain conditions to be treated as an order isomorphism between two types.
explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.toOrderIso: This defines a construction that transforms an equivalence between two preordered types into an order isomorphism if both the forward and inverse mappings are monotone.

Equiv.coe_toOrderIso.description: This theorem shows that the natural transformation from an equivalence to an order isomorphism retains the order structure when both the equivalence and its inverse are monotonic.

Equiv.toOrderIso_toEquiv.code:
Equiv.toOrderIso_toEquiv.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (e : α ≃ β)

Equiv.toOrderIso_toEquiv.description: This theorem shows that the equivalence between two preordered types can be represented as an order isomorphism that, when converted back to an equivalence, yields the original equivalence.

StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse.code:
StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LinearOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β)
  (h_mono : StrictMono f) (g : β → α) (hg : Function.RightInverse g f) : α ≃o β
StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse.comment: A strictly monotone function with a right inverse is an order isomorphism.

explanatories.OrderHom.toFun: This defines the underlying function of an order homomorphism, which maps elements from one preordered type to another while preserving their order relationships.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono: This definition describes a construction that establishes an order embedding from a strictly monotone function originating from a linear order.
explanatories.OrderIso.injective: This theorem states that an order isomorphism between two preordered types is injective when considering the underlying functions.

StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse.fullDefinition: def orderIsoOfRightInverse (g : β → α) (hg : Function.RightInverse g f) : α ≃o β :=   { OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono f h_mono with     toFun := f,     invFun := g,     left_inv := fun _ => h_mono.injective <| hg _,     right_inv := hg }
StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse.description: This definition asserts that if a strictly monotone function has a right inverse, it establishes an order isomorphism between two ordered types.

StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse_apply.code:
StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LinearOrder α] [Preorder β]
  (f : α → β) (h_mono : StrictMono f) (g : β → α) (hg : Function.RightInverse g f) :
  ⇑(orderIsoOfRightInverse f h_mono g hg) = f
StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse_apply.description: This theorem shows that if a strictly monotone function has a right inverse, then the order isomorphism formed by this function and its right inverse is equivalent to the original function.

StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse_symm_a.code:
StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse_symm_apply.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LinearOrder α] [Preorder β]
  (f : α → β) (h_mono : StrictMono f) (g : β → α) (hg : Function.RightInverse g f) :
  ⇑(RelIso.symm (orderIsoOfRightInverse f h_mono g hg)) = g

StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse_symm_a.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of an order isomorphism constructed from a strictly monotonic function and its right inverse coincides with the right inverse function itself.

OrderIso.dual.code: OrderIso.dual.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [LE β] (f : α ≃o β) : αᵒᵈ ≃o βᵒᵈ
OrderIso.dual.comment: An order isomorphism is also an order isomorphism between dual orders.

explanatories.OrderHom.dual: This definition establishes a bijective equivalence between order-preserving functions and their counterparts on the dual orders, effectively allowing the reinterpretation of monotone functions in this context.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.dual: This definition states that an order embedding between two preordered types induces an order embedding between their corresponding dual preordered types.

OrderIso.dual.fullDefinition: protected def OrderIso.dual [LE α] [LE β] (f : α ≃o β) : αᵒᵈ ≃o βᵒᵈ :=   ⟨f.toEquiv, f.map_rel_iff⟩
OrderIso.dual.description: This definition indicates that an order isomorphism between two ordered types also corresponds to an order isomorphism between their dual orders.

OrderIso.map_bot'.code:
OrderIso.map_bot'.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [PartialOrder β] (f : α ≃o β) {x : α} {y : β}
  (hx : ∀ (x' : α), x ≤ x') (hy : ∀ (y' : β), y ≤ y') : f x = y
OrderIso.map_bot'.description: This theorem states that if an order isomorphism maps an element from one partially ordered set to another, and the first element is less than or equal to all elements in its order, then it is equal to a specific element in the second order as long as that element is less than or equal to all elements of that order.

OrderIso.map_bot.code:
OrderIso.map_bot.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [PartialOrder β] [OrderBot α] [OrderBot β]
  (f : α ≃o β) : f ⊥ = ⊥
OrderIso.map_bot.description: This theorem states that an order isomorphism preserves the least element, meaning the image of the least element from one ordered set is the least element in the corresponding ordered set.

OrderIso.map_top'.code:
OrderIso.map_top'.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [PartialOrder β] (f : α ≃o β) {x : α} {y : β}
  (hx : ∀ (x' : α), x' ≤ x) (hy : ∀ (y' : β), y' ≤ y) : f x = y
OrderIso.map_top'.description: This theorem states that if an order isomorphism maps an upper bound in one partially ordered set to an upper bound in another, then it equates the image of that bound to the corresponding element in the second set.

OrderIso.map_top.code:
OrderIso.map_top.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LE α] [PartialOrder β] [OrderTop α] [OrderTop β]
  (f : α ≃o β) : f ⊤ = ⊤
OrderIso.map_top.description: This theorem states that an order isomorphism maps the greatest element of one directed set to the greatest element of another directed set.

OrderEmbedding.map_inf_le.code:
OrderEmbedding.map_inf_le.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeInf α] [SemilatticeInf β] (f : α ↪o β)
  (x y : α) : f (x ⊓ y) ≤ f x ⊓ f y
OrderEmbedding.map_inf_le.description: This theorem establishes that an order embedding between two semilattices preserves the infimum, meaning the image of the infimum of two elements is less than or equal to the infimum of their images.

OrderEmbedding.le_map_sup.code:
OrderEmbedding.le_map_sup.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeSup α] [SemilatticeSup β] (f : α ↪o β)
  (x y : α) : f x ⊔ f y ≤ f (x ⊔ y)
OrderEmbedding.le_map_sup.description: This theorem establishes that an order embedding preserves the least upper bound of two elements under the mapping.

OrderIso.map_inf.code:
OrderIso.map_inf.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeInf α] [SemilatticeInf β] (f : α ≃o β) (x y : α) :
  f (x ⊓ y) = f x ⊓ f y
OrderIso.map_inf.description: This theorem asserts that an order isomorphism preserves the infimum operation, meaning the image of the infimum of two elements is equal to the infimum of their images.

OrderIso.map_sup.code:
OrderIso.map_sup.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeSup α] [SemilatticeSup β] (f : α ≃o β) (x y : α) :
  f (x ⊔ y) = f x ⊔ f y
OrderIso.map_sup.description: This theorem asserts that an order isomorphism preserves the least upper bound operation between two elements in two semilattices.

Disjoint.map_orderIso.code:
Disjoint.map_orderIso.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeInf α] [OrderBot α] [SemilatticeInf β]
  [OrderBot β] {a b : α} (f : α ≃o β) (ha : Disjoint a b) : Disjoint (f a) (f b)
Disjoint.map_orderIso.comment: Note that this goal could also be stated `(Disjoint on f) a b`
Disjoint.map_orderIso.description: This theorem asserts that if two elements are disjoint in one ordered semilattice, their images under an order isomorphism remain disjoint in another ordered semilattice.

Codisjoint.map_orderIso.code:

disjoint_map_orderIso_iff.code:
disjoint_map_orderIso_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeInf α] [OrderBot α] [SemilatticeInf β]

codisjoint_map_orderIso_iff.code:
codisjoint_map_orderIso_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeSup α] [OrderTop α] [SemilatticeSup β]

codisjoint_map_orderIso_iff.description: This theorem states that the codisjoint nature of two elements is preserved under an order isomorphism between two semilattices with top elements.

WithBot.toDualTopEquiv_coe.code: WithBot.toDualTopEquiv_coe.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [LE α] (a : α) : WithBot.toDualTopEquiv ↑(toDual a) = toDual ↑a

explanatories.CompleteLatticeHom.comp: This definition describes the composition of two complete lattice homomorphisms resulting in another complete lattice homomorphism that connects the first and last complete lattices.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Set.image_comp: The image of a set under the composition of two functions is equal to the image of the set under the second function followed by the first function applied to the resulting set.
explanatories.Equiv.symm_comp_self: This theorem states that composing an equivalence relation with its inverse yields the identity function.
explanatories.Set.image_id': The image of a set under the identity function is equal to the set itself.
explanatories.Equiv.self_comp_symm: This theorem establishes that the composition of an equivalence and its inverse results in the identity function.
explanatories.Set.monotone_image: The image of a monotone function preserves the monotonicity property.

Equiv.toOrderIsoSet.fullDefinition: def Equiv.toOrderIsoSet (e : α ≃ β) : Set α ≃o Set β where   toFun s := e '' s   invFun s := e.symm '' s   left_inv s := by simp only [← image_comp, Equiv.symm_comp_self, id, image_id']   right_inv s := by simp only [← image_comp, Equiv.self_comp_symm, id, image_id']   map_rel_iff' :=     ⟨fun h => by simpa using @monotone_image _ _ e.symm _ _ h, fun h => monotone_image h⟩
Equiv.toOrderIsoSet.description: This definition establishes that an equivalence between two types induces an order isomorphism between the sets of their subsets.

supsSupHom.code: supsSupHom.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] : sSupHom (α × α) α
supsSupHom.comment: The map `(a, b) ↦ a ⊔ b` as a `sSupHom`.

explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.sSupHom.toFun: This definition describes the underlying function associated with a supremum-preserving homomorphism between two ordered structures.
explanatories.sSupHom.map_sSup': This theorem asserts that a function preserving suprema commutes with the supremum operation, meaning that applying the function to the supremum of a set is equivalent to taking the supremum of the function's images of the set's elements.
explanatories.sInfHom.toFun: This definition specifies the function associated with an infimum-preserving homomorphism between two ordered structures.
explanatories.InfHom.toFun: This definition specifies the function associated with an infimum-preserving homomorphism between two ordered structures.
explanatories.FrameHom.map_sSup': This theorem asserts that applying a frame homomorphism to the supremum of a set results in the same value as taking the supremum of the images of the elements in that set under the frame homomorphism.
explanatories.CompleteLatticeHom.map_sSup': This theorem states that a complete lattice homomorphism preserves the supremum of a set by mapping the supremum of that set in the source lattice to the supremum of the image of the set in the target lattice.
explanatories.Prod.fst_sSup: This theorem states that the first component of the supremum of a set of pairs equals the supremum of the images of the first components of those pairs.
explanatories.Prod.snd_sSup: This theorem establishes that the second component of the supremum of a set of pairs is equal to the supremum of the second components of those pairs.
explanatories.sSup_image: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of the image of a set under a function is equal to the supremum of the function evaluated at each element of that set.
explanatories.iSup_sup_eq: This theorem states that the supremum of the pointwise maximum of two functions is equal to the maximum of their individual suprema.

supsSupHom.fullDefinition: def supsSupHom : sSupHom (α × α) α where   toFun x := x.1 ⊔ x.2   map_sSup' s := by simp_rw [Prod.fst_sSup, Prod.snd_sSup, sSup_image, iSup_sup_eq]
supsSupHom.description: This definition describes a supremum-preserving homomorphism that takes a pair of elements from a complete lattice and maps it to their supremum.

infsInfHom.code: infsInfHom.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] : sInfHom (α × α) α
infsInfHom.comment: The map `(a, b) ↦ a ⊓ b` as an `sInfHom`.

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.
explanatories.sSupHom.toFun: This definition describes the underlying function associated with a supremum-preserving homomorphism between two ordered structures.
explanatories.sInfHom.toFun: This definition specifies the function associated with an infimum-preserving homomorphism between two ordered structures.
explanatories.sInfHom.map_sInf': This theorem asserts that a homomorphism preserving infima between two sets commutes with the infimum operation, such that applying the homomorphism to the infimum of a set equals the infimum of the images of the elements in that set.
explanatories.InfHom.toFun: This definition specifies the function associated with an infimum-preserving homomorphism between two ordered structures.
explanatories.Prod.fst_sInf: This theorem asserts that the first component of the infimum of a set of pairs is equal to the infimum of the images of the first components of those pairs.
explanatories.Prod.snd_sInf: This theorem states that the second component of the infimum of a set of pairs is equal to the infimum of the images of the second components of those pairs.
explanatories.sInf_image: This theorem asserts that the infimum of the image of a set under a function is equal to the infimum of the function evaluated at each element of the original set.
explanatories.iInf_inf_eq: This theorem states that the infimum of the infimums of two functions evaluated at the same index is equal to the infimum of the pointwise infimums of those functions.

infsInfHom.fullDefinition: def infsInfHom : sInfHom (α × α) α where   toFun x := x.1 ⊓ x.2   map_sInf' s := by simp_rw [Prod.fst_sInf, Prod.snd_sInf, sInf_image, iInf_inf_eq]
infsInfHom.description: This definition establishes a homomorphism that maps pairs of elements from a complete lattice to their infimum within that lattice.

supsSupHom_apply.description: This theorem states that the supremum-preserving homomorphism applied to a pair of elements in a complete lattice is equal to the supremum of those two elements.

infsInfHom_apply.code: infsInfHom_apply.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (x : α × α) : infsInfHom x = x.1 ⊓ x.2
infsInfHom_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that the homomorphism mapping pairs of elements to their infimum in a complete lattice produces the infimum of the individual elements of the pair.

fst_hnot.description: The first component of the negation of a pair of elements is equal to the negation of its first component.

snd_hnot.code: snd_hnot.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [HNot α] [HNot β] (a : α × β) : (￢a).2 = ￢a.2

HeytingAlgebra.ofHImp.fullDefinition: abbrev HeytingAlgebra.ofHImp [DistribLattice α] [BoundedOrder α] (himp : α → α → α)     (le_himp_iff : ∀ a b c, a ≤ himp b c ↔ a ⊓ b ≤ c) : HeytingAlgebra α :=   { ‹DistribLattice α›, ‹BoundedOrder α› with     himp,     compl := fun a => himp a ⊥,     le_himp_iff,     himp_bot := fun a => rfl }

HeytingAlgebra.ofCompl.fullDefinition: abbrev HeytingAlgebra.ofCompl [DistribLattice α] [BoundedOrder α] (compl : α → α)     (le_himp_iff : ∀ a b c, a ≤ compl b ⊔ c ↔ a ⊓ b ≤ c) : HeytingAlgebra α where   himp := (compl · ⊔ ·)   compl := compl   le_himp_iff := le_himp_iff   himp_bot _ := sup_bot_eq _
HeytingAlgebra.ofCompl.description: A Heyting algebra can be constructed from a distributive lattice and bounded order using a complement operator and a specific condition relating elements of the lattice.

explanatories.SDiff.sdiff: This definition specifies a set difference operation that yields all elements from one set that are not present in another set.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The symmetric difference of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if and only if one of those elements is less than or equal to the join of the other element and the third element.
explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.top_sdiff: The difference between the greatest element and any element in a biheyting algebra is equal to the negation of that element.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

CoheytingAlgebra.ofSDiff.fullDefinition: abbrev CoheytingAlgebra.ofSDiff [DistribLattice α] [BoundedOrder α] (sdiff : α → α → α)     (sdiff_le_iff : ∀ a b c, sdiff a b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c) : CoheytingAlgebra α :=   { ‹DistribLattice α›, ‹BoundedOrder α› with     sdiff,     hnot := fun a => sdiff ⊤ a,     sdiff_le_iff,     top_sdiff := fun a => rfl }
CoheytingAlgebra.ofSDiff.description: A coheyting algebra can be constructed from a distributive lattice and a bounded order using a defined difference operation that satisfies a particular inequality condition.

explanatories.SDiff.sdiff: This definition specifies a set difference operation that yields all elements from one set that are not present in another set.
explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The symmetric difference of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if and only if one of those elements is less than or equal to the join of the other element and the third element.
explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.top_sdiff: The difference between the greatest element and any element in a biheyting algebra is equal to the negation of that element.

CoheytingAlgebra.ofHNot.fullDefinition: abbrev CoheytingAlgebra.ofHNot [DistribLattice α] [BoundedOrder α] (hnot : α → α)     (sdiff_le_iff : ∀ a b c, a ⊓ hnot b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c) : CoheytingAlgebra α where   sdiff a b := a ⊓ hnot b   hnot := hnot   sdiff_le_iff := sdiff_le_iff   top_sdiff _ := top_inf_eq _
CoheytingAlgebra.ofHNot.description: A co-Heyting algebra can be created using the operations of difference and Heyting negation under specific conditions of a distributive lattice and bounded order.

GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.le_himp_iff.code:

le_himp_iff.code: le_himp_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ≤ b ⇨ c ↔ a ⊓ b ≤ c

explanatories.GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.le_himp_iff: The relationship between the left and right implications in a generalized Heyting algebra can be characterized by an equivalence involving the meet operation.

le_himp_iff.description: An element is less than or equal to the implication of two other elements if and only if the meet of the first two elements is less than or equal to the third element.

le_himp_iff'.code: le_himp_iff'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ≤ b ⇨ c ↔ b ⊓ a ≤ c
le_himp_iff'.description: The implication relation between two elements in a generalized heyting algebra corresponds to the meet of the second element with the first being less than or equal to the third element.

le_himp_comm.code: le_himp_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ≤ b ⇨ c ↔ b ≤ a ⇨ c
le_himp_comm.description: The implication relating two elements in a generalized heyting algebra is commutative with respect to the implication operation when rearranged.

le_himp.code: le_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ b ⇨ a
le_himp.description: If one element is less than or equal to another in a generalized Heyting algebra, then the implication from the second element to the first element holds.

le_himp_iff_left.code: le_himp_iff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ a ⇨ b ↔ a ≤ b
le_himp_iff_left.description: The left-hand side of an implication involving two elements in a generalized Heyting algebra is less than or equal to the second element if and only if the first element itself is less than or equal to the second element.

himp_self.code: himp_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a ⇨ a = ⊤
himp_self.description: The Heyting implication of an element with itself is equal to the top element in a generalized Heyting algebra.

himp_inf_le.code: himp_inf_le.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : (a ⇨ b) ⊓ a ≤ b
himp_inf_le.description: The conjunction of an implication and one of its antecedents is always less than or equal to the consequent in a generalized heyting algebra.

inf_himp_le.code: inf_himp_le.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ (a ⇨ b) ≤ b
inf_himp_le.description: The conjunction of an element and its implication to another element is less than or equal to the second element.

inf_himp.code: inf_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⊓ (a ⇨ b) = a ⊓ b
inf_himp.description: The intersection of an element and the implication of that element to another is equivalent to the intersection of the element with the other element in a generalized heyting algebra.

himp_inf_self.code: himp_inf_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : (a ⇨ b) ⊓ a = b ⊓ a
himp_inf_self.description: The conjunction of an implication and its premise is equivalent to the conjunction of the conclusion and the premise.

himp_eq_top_iff.code: himp_eq_top_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ⇨ b = ⊤ ↔ a ≤ b
himp_eq_top_iff.comment:
The **deduction theorem** in the Heyting algebra model of intuitionistic logic:
an implication holds iff the conclusion follows from the hypothesis.
himp_eq_top_iff.description: An implication in a generalized Heyting algebra is equivalent to a top element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the second.

himp_top.code: himp_top.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a ⇨ ⊤ = ⊤
himp_top.description: The implication of any element to the top element in a generalized Heyting algebra is equal to the top element itself.

top_himp.code: top_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : ⊤ ⇨ a = a
top_himp.description: In a generalized heyting algebra, the greatest element implies any element is equal to that element.

himp_himp.code: himp_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⇨ b ⇨ c = a ⊓ b ⇨ c
himp_himp.description: The nested Heyting implication can be expressed as the implication of the conjunction of the first two elements implying the third element.

himp_le_himp_himp_himp.code: himp_le_himp_himp_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : b ⇨ c ≤ (a ⇨ b) ⇨ a ⇨ c
himp_le_himp_himp_himp.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, the implication from one element to another combined with the implication from a different element to the first element leads to an implication from the first element to the final element.

himp_left_comm.code: himp_left_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⇨ b ⇨ c = b ⇨ a ⇨ c
himp_left_comm.description: The Heyting implication is left commutative in a generalized Heyting algebra, meaning the order of the first two elements does not affect the implication's outcome when followed by a third element.

himp_idem.code: himp_idem.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : b ⇨ b ⇨ a = b ⇨ a
himp_idem.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, the implication from an element to itself combined with the implication to another element is equivalent to just the implication to that second element.

himp_inf_distrib.code: himp_inf_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⇨ b ⊓ c = (a ⇨ b) ⊓ (a ⇨ c)
himp_inf_distrib.description: The implication operation distributes over the infimum in a generalized heyting algebra.

sup_himp_distrib.code: sup_himp_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⊔ b ⇨ c = (a ⇨ c) ⊓ (b ⇨ c)
sup_himp_distrib.description: The implication of the supremum of two elements is equal to the meet of the implications of each element with a third element.

himp_le_himp_left.code: himp_le_himp_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : a ≤ b) : c ⇨ a ≤ c ⇨ b
himp_le_himp_left.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the implication from a third element to the first is also less than or equal to the implication from that third element to the second.

himp_le_himp_right.code: himp_le_himp_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : a ≤ b) : b ⇨ c ≤ a ⇨ c
himp_le_himp_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another, then the implication of the second element with a third is less than or equal to the implication of the first element with the same third.

himp_le_himp.code:
himp_le_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c d : α} (hab : a ≤ b) (hcd : c ≤ d) :
  b ⇨ c ≤ a ⇨ d
himp_le_himp.description: If one element is less than or equal to another and a third is also less than or equal to a fourth, then the implication from the second to the third is less than or equal to the implication from the first to the fourth in a generalized Heyting algebra.

sup_himp_self_left.code: sup_himp_self_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ b ⇨ a = b ⇨ a
sup_himp_self_left.description: The implication of the supremum of two elements to the first element is equal to the implication of the second element to the first element in a generalized Heyting algebra.

sup_himp_self_right.code: sup_himp_self_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ b ⇨ b = a ⇨ b
sup_himp_self_right.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, the implication from the join of two elements to the second element is equal to the implication from the first element to the second element.

Codisjoint.himp_eq_right.code: Codisjoint.himp_eq_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Codisjoint a b) : b ⇨ a = a
Codisjoint.himp_eq_right.description: If two elements in a generalized Heyting algebra are codisjoint, then the implication from the second element to the first equals the first element itself.

Codisjoint.himp_eq_left.code: Codisjoint.himp_eq_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Codisjoint a b) : a ⇨ b = b
Codisjoint.himp_eq_left.description: In a generalized heyting algebra, if two elements are codisjoint, then the implication from one element to the other is equal to the second element.

Codisjoint.himp_inf_cancel_right.code:
Codisjoint.himp_inf_cancel_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Codisjoint a b) :
  a ⇨ a ⊓ b = b
Codisjoint.himp_inf_cancel_right.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, if two elements are codisjoint, then the implication from the first element to the meet of itself and the second element equals the second element.

Codisjoint.himp_inf_cancel_left.code:
Codisjoint.himp_inf_cancel_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Codisjoint a b) :
  b ⇨ a ⊓ b = a
Codisjoint.himp_inf_cancel_left.description: The implication of an element by the meet of two elements is equal to one of the elements if those two elements are codisjoint.

Codisjoint.himp_le_of_right_le.code:
Codisjoint.himp_le_of_right_le.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (hac : Codisjoint a c)
  (hba : b ≤ a) : c ⇨ b ≤ a
Codisjoint.himp_le_of_right_le.comment: See `himp_le` for a stronger version in Boolean algebras.
Codisjoint.himp_le_of_right_le.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, if one element is codisjoint with another and a third element is less than or equal to the first, then the implication from the second to the third is less than or equal to the first element.

le_himp_himp.code: le_himp_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ (a ⇨ b) ⇨ b
le_himp_himp.description: An element is less than or equal to the implication of itself with another element, which in turn is less than or equal to that second element.

himp_eq_himp_iff.code: himp_eq_himp_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : b ⇨ a = a ⇨ b ↔ a = b
himp_eq_himp_iff.description: The equality of two Heyting implications holds if and only if the two elements involved are equal.

himp_triangle.code: himp_triangle.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : (a ⇨ b) ⊓ (b ⇨ c) ≤ a ⇨ c
himp_triangle.description: In a generalized Heyting algebra, the conjunction of implications from one element to another and from that second element to a third is less than or equal to the implication from the first element to the third.

himp_inf_himp_cancel.code:
himp_inf_himp_cancel.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (hba : b ≤ a) (hcb : c ≤ b) :
  (a ⇨ b) ⊓ (b ⇨ c) = a ⇨ c
himp_inf_himp_cancel.description: In a generalized heyting algebra, the meet of two implications is equal to the implication from the first element to the third when the second element is less than or equal to both the first and second elements.

explanatories.GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.le_himp_iff: The relationship between the left and right implications in a generalized Heyting algebra can be characterized by an equivalence involving the meet operation.
explanatories.le_himp_iff: An element is less than or equal to the implication of two other elements if and only if the meet of the first two elements is less than or equal to the third element.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.toDistribLatti.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.toDistribLattice : DistribLattice α :=   DistribLattice.ofInfSupLe fun a b c => by     simp_rw [inf_comm a, ← le_himp_iff, sup_le_iff, le_himp_iff, ← sup_le_iff]; rfl
GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.toDistribLatti.description: Every generalized Heyting algebra can be regarded as a distributive lattice.

Prod.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.code:
Prod.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α]
  [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra β] : GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (α × β)

explanatories.GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.le_himp_iff: The relationship between the left and right implications in a generalized Heyting algebra can be characterized by an equivalence involving the meet operation.
explanatories.le_himp_iff: An element is less than or equal to the implication of two other elements if and only if the meet of the first two elements is less than or equal to the third element.
explanatories.and_congr: This theorem asserts that the conjunction of two propositions is equivalent to the conjunction of two other propositions if each pair of propositions is equivalent to one another.

Prod.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.fullDefinition: instance Prod.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra β] :     GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (α × β) where   le_himp_iff _ _ _ := and_congr le_himp_iff le_himp_iff
Prod.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.description: The product of two generalized Heyting algebras is also a generalized Heyting algebra.

Pi.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.code:
Pi.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_4}
  [(i : ι) → GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (α i)] : GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra ((i : ι) → α i)

explanatories.GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.le_himp_iff: The relationship between the left and right implications in a generalized Heyting algebra can be characterized by an equivalence involving the meet operation.
explanatories.le_himp_iff: An element is less than or equal to the implication of two other elements if and only if the meet of the first two elements is less than or equal to the third element.
explanatories.Prod.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra: The product of two generalized Heyting algebras is also a generalized Heyting algebra.

Pi.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.fullDefinition: instance Pi.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra {α : ι → Type*} [∀ i, GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (α i)] :     GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (∀ i, α i) where   le_himp_iff i := by simp [le_def]
Pi.instGeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.description: The concept defines a generalized Heyting algebra structure for the type of functions that map from an index set to elements of generalized Heyting algebras.

GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff.code:
GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff.{u_4} {α : Type u_4} [self : GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) :
  a \ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c
GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff.comment: `\ a` is right adjoint to `⊔ a`

explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The symmetric difference of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if and only if one of those elements is less than or equal to the join of the other element and the third element.

GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff.description: The difference of two elements being less than or equal to a third element is equivalent to the first element being less than or equal to the join of the second and third elements.

sdiff_le_iff.code: sdiff_le_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a \ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c

explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The symmetric difference of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if and only if one of those elements is less than or equal to the join of the other element and the third element.
explanatories.GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The difference of two elements being less than or equal to a third element is equivalent to the first element being less than or equal to the join of the second and third elements.

sdiff_le_iff.description: The difference of one element from another is less than or equal to a third element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the join of the second and third elements.

sdiff_le_iff'.code: sdiff_le_iff'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a \ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ c ⊔ b
sdiff_le_iff'.description: The condition that the set difference of two elements is less than or equal to a third element is equivalent to saying that the first element is less than or equal to the join of the two original elements.

sdiff_le_comm.code: sdiff_le_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a \ b ≤ c ↔ a \ c ≤ b
sdiff_le_comm.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the difference between two elements being less than or equal to a third element is equivalent to the difference between the first element and that third element being less than or equal to the second element.

sdiff_le.code: sdiff_le.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ b ≤ a
sdiff_le.description: In a generalized co-Heyting algebra, the difference of an element from another is less than or equal to the original element.

Disjoint.disjoint_sdiff_left.code:
Disjoint.disjoint_sdiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : Disjoint a b) :
  Disjoint (a \ c) b
Disjoint.disjoint_sdiff_left.description: If two elements are disjoint, then the difference of one element from a third element remains disjoint from the second element.

Disjoint.disjoint_sdiff_right.code:
Disjoint.disjoint_sdiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : Disjoint a b) :
  Disjoint a (b \ c)
Disjoint.disjoint_sdiff_right.description: In a generalized co-Heyting algebra, if two elements are disjoint, then one of them remains disjoint from the set difference of the other element and a third element.

sdiff_le_iff_left.code: sdiff_le_iff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ b ≤ b ↔ a ≤ b
sdiff_le_iff_left.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the difference of one element from another is less than or equal to the second element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the second element.

sdiff_self.code: sdiff_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a \ a = ⊥
sdiff_self.description: The difference of any element with itself in a generalized coheyting algebra results in the least element.

le_sup_sdiff.code: le_sup_sdiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ b ⊔ a \ b
le_sup_sdiff.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, an element is less than or equal to the supremum of itself and the difference between another element and itself.

le_sdiff_sup.code: le_sdiff_sup.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ a \ b ⊔ b
le_sdiff_sup.description: The inequality of an element compared to the set difference of itself and another element joined with that other element holds true in a generalized coheyting algebra.

sup_sdiff_left.code: sup_sdiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ⊔ a \ b = a
sup_sdiff_left.description: The supremum of an element and the symmetric difference of that element with another is equal to the original element itself.

sup_sdiff_right.code: sup_sdiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ b ⊔ a = a
sup_sdiff_right.description: The symmetric difference of one element and another joined with the first element is equal to the first element itself in a generalized coheyting algebra.

inf_sdiff_left.code: inf_sdiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ b ⊓ a = a \ b
inf_sdiff_left.description: The infimum of the difference between two elements and one of these elements is equal to the difference of the two elements.

inf_sdiff_right.code: inf_sdiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ⊓ a \ b = a \ b
inf_sdiff_right.description: The infimum of an element and the difference of that element with another is equal to the difference of the first element with the second.

sup_sdiff_self.code: sup_sdiff_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ b \ a = a ⊔ b
sup_sdiff_self.description: The supremum of an element and the difference of that element from another is equal to the supremum of the two original elements.

sdiff_sup_self.code: sdiff_sup_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : b \ a ⊔ a = b ⊔ a
sdiff_sup_self.description: In a generalized co-Heyting algebra, the supremum of the set difference between one element and another with the second element is equal to the supremum of the second element and the first element.

sup_sdiff_self_left.code: sup_sdiff_self_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : b \ a ⊔ a = b ⊔ a
sup_sdiff_self_left.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the supremum of the difference between one element and another with that second element is equal to the supremum of the second element and the first element.

sup_sdiff_self_right.code: sup_sdiff_self_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⊔ b \ a = a ⊔ b
sup_sdiff_self_right.description: The union of two elements minus the first one is equal to the union of the two elements.

sup_sdiff_eq_sup.code: sup_sdiff_eq_sup.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : c ≤ a) : a ⊔ b \ c = a ⊔ b
sup_sdiff_eq_sup.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the supremum of an element and another element subtracting a third element is equal to the supremum of the first two elements when the third element is less than or equal to the first element.

sup_sdiff_cancel'.code:
sup_sdiff_cancel'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (hab : a ≤ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) :
  b ⊔ c \ a = c
sup_sdiff_cancel'.description: The join of an element with another element minus a third element equals the second element if the first is less than the second and the second is less than the third in a generalized coheyting algebra.

sup_sdiff_cancel_right.code: sup_sdiff_cancel_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : a ⊔ b \ a = b
sup_sdiff_cancel_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another in a generalized co-Heyting algebra, then the join of these two elements with respect to the difference operation equals the larger element.

sdiff_sup_cancel.code: sdiff_sup_cancel.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : a \ b ⊔ b = a
sdiff_sup_cancel.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the supremum of the difference between two elements and one of the elements is equal to the original element when the second element is less than or equal to the first.

sup_le_of_le_sdiff_left.code:
sup_le_of_le_sdiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : b ≤ c \ a) (hac : a ≤ c) :
  a ⊔ b ≤ c
sup_le_of_le_sdiff_left.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to the difference of another element from a third, and the first element is less than or equal to the third, then the supremum of the first and second elements is less than or equal to the third element.

sup_le_of_le_sdiff_right.code:
sup_le_of_le_sdiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : a ≤ c \ b)
  (hbc : b ≤ c) : a ⊔ b ≤ c
sup_le_of_le_sdiff_right.description: If one element is less than the difference of a second element from a third, and the second element is less than or equal to the third in a generalized coheyting algebra, then the join of the first and second elements is less than or equal to the third element.

sdiff_eq_bot_iff.code: sdiff_eq_bot_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ b = ⊥ ↔ a ≤ b
sdiff_eq_bot_iff.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the symmetric difference of one element from another is equal to the bottom element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the second element.

sdiff_bot.code: sdiff_bot.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a \ ⊥ = a
sdiff_bot.description: The symmetric difference of an element with the bottom element in a generalized coheyting algebra is equal to the original element.

bot_sdiff.code: bot_sdiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : ⊥ \ a = ⊥
bot_sdiff.description: The difference between the least element and any element in a generalized co-Heyting algebra equals the least element itself.

sdiff_sdiff_sdiff_le_sdiff.code: sdiff_sdiff_sdiff_le_sdiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : (a \ b) \ (a \ c) ≤ c \ b
sdiff_sdiff_sdiff_le_sdiff.description: The difference of two differences is less than or equal to the difference of the second element and the first element from the original set.

sdiff_sdiff.code: sdiff_sdiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : (a \ b) \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c)
sdiff_sdiff.description: The difference of the first element by the second and then by the third equals the difference of the first element by the join of the second and third elements in a generalized co-Heyting algebra.

sdiff_sdiff_left.code: sdiff_sdiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : (a \ b) \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c)
sdiff_sdiff_left.description: The symmetric difference of the left element with another element is equal to the symmetric difference of the left element with the join of the other two elements in a generalized coheyting algebra.

sdiff_right_comm.code: sdiff_right_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : (a \ b) \ c = (a \ c) \ b
sdiff_right_comm.description: The theorem states that in a generalized coheyting algebra, the operation of taking the set difference is commutative when applied in a specific order involving three elements.

sdiff_sdiff_comm.code: sdiff_sdiff_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : (a \ b) \ c = (a \ c) \ b
sdiff_sdiff_comm.description: The symmetric difference between two elements in a generalized coheyting algebra is commutative when subtracting a third element.

sdiff_idem.code: sdiff_idem.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : (a \ b) \ b = a \ b
sdiff_idem.description: The difference of one element with another, when taken again with the second element, is equivalent to the original difference of those two elements in a generalized co-Heyting algebra.

sdiff_sdiff_self.code: sdiff_sdiff_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : (a \ b) \ a = ⊥
sdiff_sdiff_self.description: The difference of an element by another and then by itself results in the least element in a generalized co-Heyting algebra.

sup_sdiff_distrib.code: sup_sdiff_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : (a ⊔ b) \ c = a \ c ⊔ b \ c
sup_sdiff_distrib.description: The distribution of set difference over joins in a generalized Coheyting algebra states that the difference of the join of two elements and a third element is equal to the join of the differences of each of the first two elements and the third one.

sdiff_inf_distrib.code: sdiff_inf_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a \ (b ⊓ c) = a \ b ⊔ a \ c
sdiff_inf_distrib.description: The difference of an element from the infimum of two other elements equals the supremum of the differences of the element from each of those two elements in a generalized coheyting algebra.

sup_sdiff.code: sup_sdiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : (a ⊔ b) \ c = a \ c ⊔ b \ c
sup_sdiff.description: The set difference of the join of two elements and a third element is equal to the join of the set differences of each element from the third.

sup_sdiff_right_self.code: sup_sdiff_right_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : (a ⊔ b) \ b = a \ b
sup_sdiff_right_self.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the difference between the supremum of two elements and the second element is equal to the difference between the first element and the second element.

sup_sdiff_left_self.code: sup_sdiff_left_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : (a ⊔ b) \ a = b \ a
sup_sdiff_left_self.description: In a generalized co-Heyting algebra, the difference between the supremum of two elements and one of those elements is equal to the difference of the other element from the first.

sdiff_le_sdiff_right.code: sdiff_le_sdiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : a ≤ b) : a \ c ≤ b \ c
sdiff_le_sdiff_right.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the difference of the first element with a third element is also less than or equal to the difference of the second element with the same third element.

sdiff_le_sdiff_left.code: sdiff_le_sdiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : a ≤ b) : c \ b ≤ c \ a
sdiff_le_sdiff_left.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the set difference of a third element with respect to the second element is less than or equal to the set difference of that third element with respect to the first element.

sdiff_le_sdiff.code:
sdiff_le_sdiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c d : α} (hab : a ≤ b) (hcd : c ≤ d) :
  a \ d ≤ b \ c
sdiff_le_sdiff.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another and a third element is less than or equal to a fourth, then the difference between the first element and the fourth is less than or equal to the difference between the second element and the third.

sdiff_inf.code: sdiff_inf.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a \ (b ⊓ c) = a \ b ⊔ a \ c
sdiff_inf.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the difference of an element and the infimum of two other elements is equal to the supremum of the differences of the first element with each of those two elements.

sdiff_inf_self_left.code: sdiff_inf_self_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a \ (a ⊓ b) = a \ b
sdiff_inf_self_left.description: The difference of an element with the infimum of itself and another element is equal to the difference of that element with the other element.

sdiff_inf_self_right.code: sdiff_inf_self_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : b \ (a ⊓ b) = b \ a
sdiff_inf_self_right.description: The symmetric difference of an element with the infimum of itself and another element is equal to the symmetric difference of that element with the other element.

Disjoint.sdiff_eq_left.code: Disjoint.sdiff_eq_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) : a \ b = a
Disjoint.sdiff_eq_left.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if two elements are disjoint, then the difference of the first element and the second equals the first element itself.

Disjoint.sdiff_eq_right.code: Disjoint.sdiff_eq_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) : b \ a = b
Disjoint.sdiff_eq_right.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if two elements are disjoint, the difference of the second element and the first is equal to the second element itself.

Disjoint.sup_sdiff_cancel_left.code:
Disjoint.sup_sdiff_cancel_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) :
  (a ⊔ b) \ a = b
Disjoint.sup_sdiff_cancel_left.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, if two elements are disjoint, then the difference of their supremum and one element equals the other element.

Disjoint.sup_sdiff_cancel_right.code:
Disjoint.sup_sdiff_cancel_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) :
  (a ⊔ b) \ b = a
Disjoint.sup_sdiff_cancel_right.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the operation of taking the supremum of two disjoint elements followed by set difference with the second element yields the first element.

Disjoint.le_sdiff_of_le_left.code:
Disjoint.le_sdiff_of_le_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (hac : Disjoint a c)
  (hab : a ≤ b) : a ≤ b \ c
Disjoint.le_sdiff_of_le_left.comment: See `le_sdiff` for a stronger version in generalised Boolean algebras.
Disjoint.le_sdiff_of_le_left.description: If one element is disjoint from a third element and less than or equal to a second element, then it is also less than or equal to the difference between the second element and the third element.

sdiff_sdiff_le.code: sdiff_sdiff_le.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ (a \ b) ≤ b
sdiff_sdiff_le.description: The difference between an element and the difference of itself with another element is less than or equal to that other element in a generalized coheyting algebra.

sdiff_eq_sdiff_iff.code: sdiff_eq_sdiff_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a \ b = b \ a ↔ a = b
sdiff_eq_sdiff_iff.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the equality of the difference between two elements in both orders implies that the elements are identical.

sdiff_triangle.code: sdiff_triangle.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a \ c ≤ a \ b ⊔ b \ c
sdiff_triangle.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the difference between two elements in relation to a third element is less than or equal to the join of their respective differences from that third element.

sdiff_sup_sdiff_cancel.code:
sdiff_sup_sdiff_cancel.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (hba : b ≤ a) (hcb : c ≤ b) :
  a \ b ⊔ b \ c = a \ c
sdiff_sup_sdiff_cancel.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the supremum of the difference between one element and another, along with the difference between the second element and a third, equals the difference between the first element and the third when the second is less than or equal to the first and the third is less than or equal to the second.

sdiff_le_sdiff_of_sup_le_sup_left.code:
sdiff_le_sdiff_of_sup_le_sup_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : c ⊔ a ≤ c ⊔ b) :
  a \ c ≤ b \ c
sdiff_le_sdiff_of_sup_le_sup_left.description: If the supremum of two elements with a third element is less than or equal to the supremum of the first with the second, then the difference of the first by the third is less than or equal to the difference of the second by the same third element in a generalized coheyting algebra.

sdiff_le_sdiff_of_sup_le_sup_right.code:
sdiff_le_sdiff_of_sup_le_sup_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α}
  (h : a ⊔ c ≤ b ⊔ c) : a \ c ≤ b \ c
sdiff_le_sdiff_of_sup_le_sup_right.description: If the supremum of one element and another is less than or equal to the supremum of a second element and the same other element, then the symmetric difference of the first element with the other element is less than or equal to the symmetric difference of the second element with the same other element.

inf_sdiff_sup_left.code: inf_sdiff_sup_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a \ c ⊓ (a ⊔ b) = a \ c
inf_sdiff_sup_left.description: The symmetric difference of one element and another intersected with the join of that element and a third yields the same result as the symmetric difference with the first element alone in a generalized coheyting algebra.

inf_sdiff_sup_right.code: inf_sdiff_sup_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a \ c ⊓ (b ⊔ a) = a \ c
inf_sdiff_sup_right.description: In a generalized coheyting algebra, the infimum of the difference between one element and another combined with the supremum of that element and a third one is equal to the difference between the first and third elements.

GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.toLattice.code: GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.toLattice.{u_4} {α : Type u_4} [self : GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] : Lattice α
GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.toLattice.description: A generalized coheyting algebra can be associated with a lattice structure.

explanatories.BiheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The symmetric difference of two elements is less than or equal to a third element if and only if one of those elements is less than or equal to the join of the other element and the third element.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.
explanatories.GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra.toDistribLatti: Every generalized Heyting algebra can be regarded as a distributive lattice.
explanatories.GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The difference of two elements being less than or equal to a third element is equivalent to the first element being less than or equal to the join of the second and third elements.

GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.toDistribLat.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.toDistribLattice : DistribLattice α :=   { ‹GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α› with     le_sup_inf :=       fun a b c => by simp_rw [← sdiff_le_iff, le_inf_iff, sdiff_le_iff, ← le_inf_iff]; rfl }
GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.toDistribLat.description: A generalized coheyting algebra can be viewed as a distributive lattice.

explanatories.and_congr: This theorem asserts that the conjunction of two propositions is equivalent to the conjunction of two other propositions if each pair of propositions is equivalent to one another.
explanatories.GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.sdiff_le_iff: The difference of two elements being less than or equal to a third element is equivalent to the first element being less than or equal to the join of the second and third elements.
explanatories.sdiff_le_iff: The difference of one element from another is less than or equal to a third element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the join of the second and third elements.

Prod.instGeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.fullDefinition: instance Prod.instGeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra β] :     GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra (α × β) where   sdiff_le_iff _ _ _ := and_congr sdiff_le_iff sdiff_le_iff
Prod.instGeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.description: The product of two generalized coheyting algebras is itself a generalized coheyting algebra.

Pi.instGeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_4}

HeytingAlgebra.himp_bot.description: In a Heyting algebra, the implication from any element to the bottom element is equivalent to the complement of that element.

himp_bot.code: himp_bot.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : a ⇨ ⊥ = aᶜ

explanatories.HeytingAlgebra.himp_bot: In a Heyting algebra, the implication from any element to the bottom element is equivalent to the complement of that element.

himp_bot.description: The implication of an element with the least element is equal to the complement of that element.

bot_himp.code: bot_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : ⊥ ⇨ a = ⊤
bot_himp.description: In a heyting algebra, the implication from the bottom element to any element is equal to the top element.

compl_sup_distrib.code: compl_sup_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : (a ⊔ b)ᶜ = aᶜ ⊓ bᶜ
compl_sup_distrib.description: In a heyting algebra, the complement of the join of two elements is equal to the meet of their individual complements.

compl_sup.code: compl_sup.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : (a ⊔ b)ᶜ = aᶜ ⊓ bᶜ
compl_sup.description: The complement of the supremum of two elements in a Heyting algebra is equal to the infimum of their complements.

compl_le_himp.code: compl_le_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : aᶜ ≤ a ⇨ b
compl_le_himp.description: The complement of an element in a Heyting algebra is less than or equal to the Heyting implication of that element with another element.

compl_sup_le_himp.code: compl_sup_le_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : aᶜ ⊔ b ≤ a ⇨ b
compl_sup_le_himp.description: The supremum of the complement of one element and another element is less than or equal to the Heyting implication of the first element and the second in a Heyting algebra.

sup_compl_le_himp.code: sup_compl_le_himp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : b ⊔ aᶜ ≤ a ⇨ b
sup_compl_le_himp.description: In a Heyting algebra, the supremum of an element and the complement of another is less than or equal to the implication from the second element to the first.

himp_compl.code: himp_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : a ⇨ aᶜ = aᶜ
himp_compl.description: In a Heyting algebra, the implication from an element to its complement is equal to the complement of that element.

himp_compl_comm.code: himp_compl_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇨ bᶜ = b ⇨ aᶜ
himp_compl_comm.description: The implication of one element with the complement of another is symmetric in a Heyting algebra.

le_compl_iff_disjoint_right.code: le_compl_iff_disjoint_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ bᶜ ↔ Disjoint a b
le_compl_iff_disjoint_right.description: The condition that one element is less than or equal to the complement of another is equivalent to the two elements being disjoint.

le_compl_iff_disjoint_left.code: le_compl_iff_disjoint_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ bᶜ ↔ Disjoint b a
le_compl_iff_disjoint_left.description: In a Heyting algebra, an element is less than or equal to the complement of another element if and only if the two elements are disjoint.

le_compl_comm.code: le_compl_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ bᶜ ↔ b ≤ aᶜ
le_compl_comm.description: The relationship between one element being less than or equal to the complement of another element in a Heyting algebra is symmetric.

Disjoint.le_compl_right.code: Disjoint.le_compl_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : Disjoint a b → a ≤ bᶜ
Disjoint.le_compl_right.description: In a Heyting algebra, if two elements are disjoint, then one element is less than or equal to the complement of the other.

Disjoint.le_compl_left.code: Disjoint.le_compl_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : Disjoint b a → a ≤ bᶜ
Disjoint.le_compl_left.description: If two elements in a Heyting algebra are disjoint, then one element is less than or equal to the complement of the other.

le_compl_iff_le_compl.code: le_compl_iff_le_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ bᶜ ↔ b ≤ aᶜ
le_compl_iff_le_compl.description: The relationship between one element being less than or equal to the complement of another is equivalent to the second element being less than or equal to the complement of the first.

le_compl_of_le_compl.code: le_compl_of_le_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ≤ bᶜ → b ≤ aᶜ
le_compl_of_le_compl.description: In a heyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to the complement of another, then that other element is less than or equal to the complement of the first element.

disjoint_compl_left.code: disjoint_compl_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : Disjoint aᶜ a
disjoint_compl_left.description: The complement of an element in a Heyting algebra is disjoint from the element itself.

disjoint_compl_right.code: disjoint_compl_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : Disjoint a aᶜ
disjoint_compl_right.description: In a Heyting algebra, an element is disjoint from its complement.

LE.le.disjoint_compl_left.code: LE.le.disjoint_compl_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : Disjoint aᶜ b
LE.le.disjoint_compl_left.description: In a Heyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the complement of the first element and the second element are disjoint.

LE.le.disjoint_compl_right.code: LE.le.disjoint_compl_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : Disjoint a bᶜ
LE.le.disjoint_compl_right.description: If one element is less than or equal to another in a Heyting algebra, then that element and the complement of the other element are disjoint.

IsCompl.compl_eq.code: IsCompl.compl_eq.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : IsCompl a b) : aᶜ = b
IsCompl.compl_eq.description: In a Heyting algebra, if two elements are complements, then the complement of the first element equals the second element.

IsCompl.eq_compl.code: IsCompl.eq_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : IsCompl a b) : a = bᶜ
IsCompl.eq_compl.description: In a heyting algebra, if two elements are complementary, one is equal to the negation of the other.

compl_unique.code: compl_unique.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h₀ : a ⊓ b = ⊥) (h₁ : a ⊔ b = ⊤) : aᶜ = b
compl_unique.description: In a Heyting algebra, if two elements are such that their infimum is the bottom element and their supremum is the top element, then the complement of the first element equals the second element.

inf_compl_self.code: inf_compl_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : a ⊓ aᶜ = ⊥
inf_compl_self.description: The infimum of an element and its complement in a Heyting algebra is equal to the least element.

compl_inf_self.code: compl_inf_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : aᶜ ⊓ a = ⊥
compl_inf_self.description: In a Heyting algebra, the meet of an element's complement and the element itself is equal to the least element.

inf_compl_eq_bot.code: inf_compl_eq_bot.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a ⊓ aᶜ = ⊥
inf_compl_eq_bot.description: The intersection of an element and its complement in a Heyting algebra is equal to the least element.

compl_inf_eq_bot.code: compl_inf_eq_bot.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : aᶜ ⊓ a = ⊥
compl_inf_eq_bot.description: In a heyting algebra, the intersection of the complement of an element with that element itself is equal to the bottom element.

compl_top.description: The complement of the top element in a Heyting algebra is the least element.

compl_bot.description: In a Heyting algebra, the complement of the bottom element is equal to the top element.

le_compl_self.code: le_compl_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a ≤ aᶜ ↔ a = ⊥
le_compl_self.description: In a heyting algebra, an element is less than or equal to its complement if and only if that element is the least element of the algebra.

ne_compl_self.code: ne_compl_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} [Nontrivial α] : a ≠ aᶜ
ne_compl_self.description: In a nontrivial Heyting algebra, an element is not equal to its own complement.

le_compl_compl.code: le_compl_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a : α} : a ≤ aᶜᶜ
le_compl_compl.description: In a Heyting algebra, an element is less than or equal to the double complement of itself.

compl_anti.code: compl_anti.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] : Antitone compl
compl_anti.description: The complement operation is an antitone function in a Heyting algebra, meaning it reverses the order of elements.

compl_le_compl.code: compl_le_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : bᶜ ≤ aᶜ
compl_le_compl.description: In a Heyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the complement of the second is less than or equal to the complement of the first.

compl_compl_compl.code: compl_compl_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : aᶜᶜᶜ = aᶜ
compl_compl_compl.description: In a heyting algebra, the triple negation of an element is equal to the negation of that element.

disjoint_compl_compl_left_iff.code: disjoint_compl_compl_left_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : Disjoint aᶜᶜ b ↔ Disjoint a b
disjoint_compl_compl_left_iff.description: In a Heyting algebra, two elements are disjoint if and only if their double complements are disjoint.

disjoint_compl_compl_right_iff.code: disjoint_compl_compl_right_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : Disjoint a bᶜᶜ ↔ Disjoint a b
disjoint_compl_compl_right_iff.description: In a heyting algebra, two elements are disjoint if and only if one element is disjoint from the complement of the complement of the other.

compl_sup_compl_le.code: compl_sup_compl_le.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] {a b : α} : aᶜ ⊔ bᶜ ≤ (a ⊓ b)ᶜ
compl_sup_compl_le.description: The join of the complements of two elements is less than or equal to the complement of their meet in a Heyting algebra.

compl_compl_inf_distrib.code: compl_compl_inf_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : (a ⊓ b)ᶜᶜ = aᶜᶜ ⊓ bᶜᶜ
compl_compl_inf_distrib.description: In a Heyting algebra, the complement of the meet of two elements is equal to the meet of the complements of those elements taken twice.

compl_compl_himp_distrib.code: compl_compl_himp_distrib.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a b : α) : (a ⇨ b)ᶜᶜ = aᶜᶜ ⇨ bᶜᶜ
compl_compl_himp_distrib.description: In a Heyting algebra, the double complement of the imply operation between two elements equals the imply operation between their double complements.

ofDual_hnot.code: ofDual_hnot.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : αᵒᵈ) : ofDual (￢a) = (ofDual a)ᶜ
ofDual_hnot.description: The negation of an element in the dual of a heyting algebra is equal to the complement of its image under the duality.

toDual_compl.code: toDual_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [HeytingAlgebra α] (a : α) : toDual aᶜ = ￢toDual a
toDual_compl.description: The dual of the complement of an element in a heyting algebra is equal to the negation of the dual of that element.

GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra.toGeneralizedC.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra.toGeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra :     GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α where   __ := ‹GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α›   __ := GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra.toOrderBot   sdiff := (· \ ·)   sdiff_le_iff y x z :=     ⟨fun h =>       le_of_inf_le_sup_le         (le_of_eq           (calc             y ⊓ y \ x = y \ x := inf_of_le_right sdiff_le'             _ = x ⊓ y \ x ⊔ z ⊓ y \ x := by               rw [inf_eq_right.2 h, inf_sdiff_self_right, bot_sup_eq]             _ = (x ⊔ z) ⊓ y \ x := by rw [← inf_sup_right]))         (calc           y ⊔ y \ x = y := sup_of_le_left sdiff_le'           _ ≤ y ⊔ (x ⊔ z) := le_sup_left           _ = y \ x ⊔ x ⊔ z := by rw [← sup_assoc, ← @sdiff_sup_self' _ x y]           _ = x ⊔ z ⊔ y \ x := by ac_rfl),       fun h =>       le_of_inf_le_sup_le         (calc           y \ x ⊓ x = ⊥ := inf_sdiff_self_left           _ ≤ z ⊓ x := bot_le)         (calc           y \ x ⊔ x = y ⊔ x := sdiff_sup_self'           _ ≤ x ⊔ z ⊔ x := sup_le_sup_right h x           _ ≤ z ⊔ x := by rw [sup_assoc, sup_comm, sup_assoc, sup_idem])⟩
