disjoint_sdiff_self_left.code: disjoint_sdiff_self_left.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : Disjoint (y \ x) x
disjoint_sdiff_self_left.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from another is disjoint from the first element.

disjoint_sdiff_self_right.code: disjoint_sdiff_self_right.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : Disjoint x (y \ x)
disjoint_sdiff_self_right.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, an element is disjoint from the set difference of another element from itself.

le_sdiff.code: le_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x ≤ y \ z ↔ x ≤ y ∧ Disjoint x z
le_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, an element is less than or equal to the set difference of two elements if and only if it is less than or equal to the first element and is disjoint from the second element.

sdiff_eq_left.code: sdiff_eq_left.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ y = x ↔ Disjoint x y
sdiff_eq_left.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the equality of the set difference of one element from another and the first element holds if and only if the two elements are disjoint.

Disjoint.sdiff_eq_of_sup_eq.code:
Disjoint.sdiff_eq_of_sup_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hi : Disjoint x z)
  (hs : x ⊔ z = y) : y \ x = z
Disjoint.sdiff_eq_of_sup_eq.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is disjoint from another and their supremum equals a third element, then the set difference of the third element from the first equals the second element.

Disjoint.sdiff_unique.code:
Disjoint.sdiff_unique.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hd : Disjoint x z) (hz : z ≤ y)
  (hs : y ≤ x ⊔ z) : y \ x = z
Disjoint.sdiff_unique.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is disjoint from another and is less than or equal to a third element that is a join of the first and the disjoint element, then the set difference of the third element from the first equals the disjoint element.

disjoint_sdiff_iff_le.code:
disjoint_sdiff_iff_le.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hz : z ≤ y) (hx : x ≤ y) :
  Disjoint z (y \ x) ↔ z ≤ x
disjoint_sdiff_iff_le.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, an element is disjoint from the set difference of another element from a third element if and only if it is less than or equal to the first element.

le_iff_disjoint_sdiff.code:
le_iff_disjoint_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hz : z ≤ y) (hx : x ≤ y) :
  z ≤ x ↔ Disjoint z (y \ x)
le_iff_disjoint_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, one element is less than or equal to another if and only if it is disjoint from the set difference of the second element and the first.

inf_sdiff_eq_bot_iff.code:
inf_sdiff_eq_bot_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hz : z ≤ y) (hx : x ≤ y) :
  z ⊓ y \ x = ⊥ ↔ z ≤ x
inf_sdiff_eq_bot_iff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the infimum of an element and another element minus a third equals the bottom element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the third element.

le_iff_eq_sup_sdiff.code:
le_iff_eq_sup_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hz : z ≤ y) (hx : x ≤ y) :
  x ≤ z ↔ y = z ⊔ y \ x
le_iff_eq_sup_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, one element is less than or equal to another if and only if the second element is equal to the join of the first element and the set difference of the second element from the first.

sdiff_sup.code: sdiff_sup.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : y \ (x ⊔ z) = y \ x ⊓ y \ z
sdiff_sup.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of an element from the supremum of two elements equals the meet of the set differences of that element from each of the two elements.

sdiff_eq_sdiff_iff_inf_eq_inf.code: sdiff_eq_sdiff_iff_inf_eq_inf.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : y \ x = y \ z ↔ y ⊓ x = y ⊓ z
sdiff_eq_sdiff_iff_inf_eq_inf.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from another is equal to the set difference from a third element if and only if the meet of the first element with the second equals the meet of the first element with the third.

sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint.code: sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ y = x ↔ Disjoint y x
sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, an element is equal to the set difference from another element if and only if the two elements are disjoint.

sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint'.code: sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint'.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ y = x ↔ Disjoint x y
sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint'.description: The set difference of one element from another equals the first element if and only if the two elements are disjoint in a generalized Boolean algebra.

sdiff_lt.code: sdiff_lt.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hx : y ≤ x) (hy : y ≠ ⊥) : x \ y < x
sdiff_lt.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another and is not the bottom element, then the set difference between the first element and the second is strictly less than the first element.

le_sdiff_iff.code: le_sdiff_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x ≤ y \ x ↔ x = ⊥
le_sdiff_iff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, one element is less than or equal to the set difference of another element from itself if and only if the first element is the bottom element.

sdiff_eq_right.code: sdiff_eq_right.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ y = y ↔ x = ⊥ ∧ y = ⊥
sdiff_eq_right.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from another equals the second element if and only if both elements are the bottom element.

sdiff_lt_sdiff_right.code: sdiff_lt_sdiff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (h : x < y) (hz : z ≤ x) : x \ z < y \ z
sdiff_lt_sdiff_right.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is strictly less than another and a third element is less than or equal to the first, then the set difference of the first element from the third is strictly less than the set difference of the second element from the third.

sup_inf_inf_sdiff.code: sup_inf_inf_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x ⊓ y ⊓ z ⊔ y \ z = x ⊓ y ⊔ y \ z
sup_inf_inf_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the meet of three elements with a fourth disjoint from the second equals the same meet combined with the set difference of the second element from the third.

sdiff_sdiff_right.code: sdiff_sdiff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ (y \ z) = x \ y ⊔ x ⊓ y ⊓ z
sdiff_sdiff_right.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from another set difference is equal to the union of the set difference of the first element from the first set and the intersection of the first element with both sets.

sdiff_sdiff_right'.code: sdiff_sdiff_right'.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ (y \ z) = x \ y ⊔ x ⊓ z
sdiff_sdiff_right'.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from the set difference of two others can be expressed as the join of the set difference from the first element and the meet of the first element with the second.

sdiff_sdiff_eq_sdiff_sup.code:
sdiff_sdiff_eq_sdiff_sup.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (h : z ≤ x) :
  x \ (y \ z) = x \ y ⊔ z
sdiff_sdiff_eq_sdiff_sup.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the set difference of the first element from the set difference of the second element and the first is equal to the join of the set difference of the first element from the second and the initial second element.

sdiff_sdiff_right_self.code: sdiff_sdiff_right_self.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ (x \ y) = x ⊓ y
sdiff_sdiff_right_self.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of an element from the difference of itself and another element equals the meet of the two elements.

sdiff_sdiff_eq_self.code: sdiff_sdiff_eq_self.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (h : y ≤ x) : x \ (x \ y) = y
sdiff_sdiff_eq_self.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the set difference of the second element from the first element is equal to the second element itself.

sdiff_eq_symm.code: sdiff_eq_symm.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hy : y ≤ x) (h : x \ y = z) : x \ z = y
sdiff_eq_symm.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another and the set difference of the second from the first equals a third element, then the set difference of the first element from the third equals the second element.

sdiff_eq_comm.code:
sdiff_eq_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hy : y ≤ x) (hz : z ≤ x) :
  x \ y = z ↔ x \ z = y
sdiff_eq_comm.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from a second element equals a third element if and only if the set difference of the same element from the third element equals the first element, given that both the second and third elements are less than or equal to the first.

eq_of_sdiff_eq_sdiff.code:
eq_of_sdiff_eq_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (hxz : x ≤ z) (hyz : y ≤ z)
  (h : z \ x = z \ y) : x = y
eq_of_sdiff_eq_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if two elements are both less than or equal to a third element and their respective set differences from that third element are equal, then the two elements are equal.

sdiff_sdiff_left'.code: sdiff_sdiff_left'.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : (x \ y) \ z = x \ y ⊓ x \ z
sdiff_sdiff_left'.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from another and a third element equals the intersection of the set differences of the first element from the second and from the third.

sdiff_sdiff_sup_sdiff.code:
sdiff_sdiff_sup_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] :
  z \ (x \ y ⊔ y \ x) = z ⊓ (z \ x ⊔ y) ⊓ (z \ y ⊔ x)
sdiff_sdiff_sup_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from the union of two other set differences equals the meet of the element with the unions of the respective set differences.

sdiff_sdiff_sup_sdiff'.code:
sdiff_sdiff_sup_sdiff'.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] :
  z \ (x \ y ⊔ y \ x) = z ⊓ x ⊓ y ⊔ z \ x ⊓ z \ y
sdiff_sdiff_sup_sdiff'.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from the union of two other set differences equals the meet of that element with both of the other elements separately, combined with the set difference of the first element from the second element and the set difference of the first element from the third element.

inf_sdiff.code: inf_sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : (x ⊓ y) \ z = x \ z ⊓ y \ z
inf_sdiff.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of the meet of two elements from a third element equals the meet of the set differences of each element from the third element.

inf_sdiff_assoc.code: inf_sdiff_assoc.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : (x ⊓ y) \ z = x ⊓ y \ z
inf_sdiff_assoc.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of the infimum of two elements and a third element is equal to the infimum of those two elements and the set difference from the third element.

inf_sdiff_right_comm.code: inf_sdiff_right_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x \ z ⊓ y = (x ⊓ y) \ z
inf_sdiff_right_comm.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of the first element from the third, combined with the second element, is equal to the set difference of the meet of the first and second elements from the third.

inf_sdiff_distrib_left.code: inf_sdiff_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⊓ b \ c = (a ⊓ b) \ (a ⊓ c)
inf_sdiff_distrib_left.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the intersection of the first element with the second, minus the third, is equal to the set difference of the intersection of the first and second elements from the intersection of the first and third elements.

inf_sdiff_distrib_right.code: inf_sdiff_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a \ b ⊓ c = (a ⊓ c) \ (b ⊓ c)
inf_sdiff_distrib_right.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the set difference of one element from another intersected with a third element is equal to the set difference of the intersection of the first and third elements with the intersection of the second and third elements.

disjoint_sdiff_comm.code: disjoint_sdiff_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : Disjoint (x \ z) y ↔ Disjoint x (y \ z)
disjoint_sdiff_comm.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the disjointness of the set difference of one element from another with a third element is equivalent to the disjointness of the first element with the set difference of the third element from the second.

sup_eq_sdiff_sup_sdiff_sup_inf.code: sup_eq_sdiff_sup_sdiff_sup_inf.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : x ⊔ y = x \ y ⊔ y \ x ⊔ x ⊓ y
sup_eq_sdiff_sup_sdiff_sup_inf.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, the supremum of two elements equals the supremum of their respective set differences and their meet.

sup_lt_of_lt_sdiff_left.code:
sup_lt_of_lt_sdiff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (h : y < z \ x) (hxz : x ≤ z) :
  x ⊔ y < z
sup_lt_of_lt_sdiff_left.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is less than the set difference of another element from a third and the first element is less than or equal to the third, then the supremum of the first and second elements is less than the third element.

sup_lt_of_lt_sdiff_right.code:
sup_lt_of_lt_sdiff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z : α} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (h : x < z \ y) (hyz : y ≤ z) :
  x ⊔ y < z
sup_lt_of_lt_sdiff_right.description: In a generalized Boolean algebra, if one element is less than the set difference of another and a third, and the second is less than or equal to the third, then the supremum of the first and second elements is also less than the third.

Function.Injective.booleanAlgebra.fullDefinition: protected abbrev Function.Injective.booleanAlgebra [Sup α] [Inf α] [Top α] [Bot α] [HasCompl α]     [SDiff α] [BooleanAlgebra β] (f : α → β) (hf : Injective f)     (map_sup : ∀ a b, f (a ⊔ b) = f a ⊔ f b) (map_inf : ∀ a b, f (a ⊓ b) = f a ⊓ f b)     (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) (map_compl : ∀ a, f aᶜ = (f a)ᶜ)     (map_sdiff : ∀ a b, f (a \ b) = f a \ f b) : BooleanAlgebra α where   __ := hf.generalizedBooleanAlgebra f map_sup map_inf map_bot map_sdiff   compl := compl   top := ⊤   le_top a := (@le_top β _ _ _).trans map_top.ge   bot_le a := map_bot.le.trans bot_le   inf_compl_le_bot a := ((map_inf _ _).trans <| by rw [map_compl, inf_compl_eq_bot, map_bot]).le   top_le_sup_compl a := ((map_sup _ _).trans <| by rw [map_compl, sup_compl_eq_top, map_top]).ge   sdiff_eq a b := by     refine hf ((map_sdiff _ _).trans (sdiff_eq.trans ?_))     rw [map_inf, map_compl]
Function.Injective.booleanAlgebra.description: An injective function can induce a Boolean algebra structure on the original set by mapping the operations and elements from the codomain while preserving their properties.

Estimator.improveUntilAux.fullDefinition: def Estimator.improveUntilAux     (a : Thunk α) (p : α → Bool) [Estimator a ε]     [WellFoundedGT (range (bound a : ε → α))]     (e : ε) (r : Bool) : Except (Option ε) ε :=     if p (bound a e) then       return e     else       match improve a e, improve_spec e with       | none, _ => .error <| if r then none else e       | some e', _ =>         improveUntilAux a p e' true termination_by (⟨_, mem_range_self e⟩ : range (bound a))
Estimator.improveUntilAux.description: This definition outlines a method for iteratively improving an estimator within specified conditions until a certain property is satisfied, returning a refined estimate or indicating the absence of one.

Estimator.improveUntilAux.eq_1.code:
Estimator.improveUntilAux.eq_1.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {ε : Type u_2} (a : Thunk α) (p : α → Bool)
  [Estimator a ε] [WellFoundedGT ↑(range (bound a))] (e : ε) (r : Bool) :
  improveUntilAux a p e r =
    if p (bound a e) = true then pure e
    else
      match improve a e, ⋯ with
      | none, x => Except.error (if r = true then none else some e)
      | some e', x => improveUntilAux a p e' true

symmDiff_le.code:

symmDiff_left_surjective.description: This theorem states that in a generalized Boolean algebra, the symmetric difference operation with any element is a surjective function.

symmDiff_right_surjective.code: symmDiff_right_surjective.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Surjective fun x => a ∆ x
symmDiff_right_surjective.description: This theorem proves that the function mapping any element to its symmetric difference with a fixed element in a generalized boolean algebra is surjective.

symmDiff_left_inj.code: symmDiff_left_inj.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ∆ b = c ∆ b ↔ a = c
symmDiff_left_inj.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a generalized Boolean algebra, the equality of symmetric differences involving a common element implies the equivalence of the other two elements.

symmDiff_right_inj.code: symmDiff_right_inj.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ∆ b = a ∆ c ↔ b = c
symmDiff_right_inj.description: This theorem states that in a generalized Boolean algebra, if the symmetric difference of one element with two others is equal, then those two elements must be equal.

symmDiff_eq_left.code: symmDiff_eq_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ∆ b = a ↔ b = ⊥
symmDiff_eq_left.description: This theorem establishes that the symmetric difference of two elements in a generalized Boolean algebra is equal to one of the elements if and only if the other element is the bottom element.

symmDiff_eq_right.code: symmDiff_eq_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ∆ b = b ↔ a = ⊥
symmDiff_eq_right.description: This theorem states that the symmetric difference between two elements is equal to the second element if and only if the first element is the least element in the structure.

Disjoint.symmDiff_left.code:
Disjoint.symmDiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (ha : Disjoint a c)
  (hb : Disjoint b c) : Disjoint (a ∆ b) c
Disjoint.symmDiff_left.description: This theorem establishes that if two elements are disjoint from a third element in a generalized Boolean algebra, then their symmetric difference is also disjoint from that third element.

Disjoint.symmDiff_right.code:
Disjoint.symmDiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (ha : Disjoint a b)
  (hb : Disjoint a c) : Disjoint a (b ∆ c)
Disjoint.symmDiff_right.description: This theorem asserts that in a generalized Boolean algebra, if an element is disjoint from two other elements, it is also disjoint from their symmetric difference.

symmDiff_eq_iff_sdiff_eq.code:
symmDiff_eq_iff_sdiff_eq.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ c) :
  a ∆ b = c ↔ c \ a = b
symmDiff_eq_iff_sdiff_eq.description: This theorem asserts that in a generalized boolean algebra, the symmetric difference of two elements equals a third element if and only if the difference of the third element and one of the first two equals the other element.

inf_himp_bihimp.code: inf_himp_bihimp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b ⇨ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b
inf_himp_bihimp.description: This theorem asserts that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional of two elements implies their infimum is equal to their supremum.

codisjoint_bihimp_sup.code: codisjoint_bihimp_sup.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : Codisjoint (a ⇔ b) (a ⊔ b)
codisjoint_bihimp_sup.description: This theorem states that in a boolean algebra, the bi-implication of two elements is codisjoint from their supremum.

himp_bihimp_left.code: himp_bihimp_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇨ a ⇔ b = a ⇨ b
himp_bihimp_left.description: This theorem shows that in a Boolean algebra, the implication of an element with itself is equivalent to the implication of another element with a given element.

himp_bihimp_right.code: himp_bihimp_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : b ⇨ a ⇔ b = b ⇨ a
himp_bihimp_right.description: This theorem establishes that in a Boolean algebra, the implication of one element by another is equivalent to that element being equal to itself.

bihimp_himp_left.code: bihimp_himp_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b ⇨ a = a ⊔ b
bihimp_himp_left.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the bi-implication of two elements being equivalent is satisfied if and only if their disjunction is equal to one of the elements combined with the other.

bihimp_himp_right.code: bihimp_himp_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b ⇨ b = a ⊔ b
bihimp_himp_right.description: This theorem asserts that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional of an element with the result of the right-hand implication of that element equates to the supremum of both elements.

bihimp_eq_inf.code: bihimp_eq_inf.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = a ⊓ b ↔ Codisjoint a b

explanatories.Codisjoint.bihimp_eq_inf: This theorem states that in a generalized heyting algebra, if two elements are codisjoint, their bi-implication is equivalent to their infimum.

bihimp_eq_inf.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the equivalence between two elements is equal to their meet if and only if those elements are codisjoint.

bihimp_le_iff_left.code: bihimp_le_iff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b ≤ a ↔ Codisjoint a b
bihimp_le_iff_left.description: This theorem indicates that in a Boolean algebra, the bi-implication between two elements holds if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the second element, which implies that they are disjoint.

bihimp_le_iff_right.code: bihimp_le_iff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b ≤ b ↔ Codisjoint a b
bihimp_le_iff_right.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the equivalence of two elements implies one is less than or equal to the other if and only if they are codisjoint.

bihimp_assoc.code: bihimp_assoc.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⇔ b ⇔ c = a ⇔ (b ⇔ c)
bihimp_assoc.description: This theorem asserts that the bi-implication operation is associative in the context of a Boolean algebra.

bihimp_isAssociative.code: bihimp_isAssociative.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] : Std.Associative fun x x_1 => x ⇔ x_1

explanatories.bihimp_assoc: This theorem asserts that the bi-implication operation is associative in the context of a Boolean algebra.

bihimp_isAssociative.description: This definition specifies that the bi-implication operation is associative in a Boolean algebra.

bihimp_left_comm.code: bihimp_left_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⇔ (b ⇔ c) = b ⇔ (a ⇔ c)
bihimp_left_comm.description: This theorem establishes that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional operation satisfies a left commutative property among three elements.

bihimp_right_comm.code: bihimp_right_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b c : α) : a ⇔ b ⇔ c = a ⇔ c ⇔ b
bihimp_right_comm.description: This theorem establishes the right commutativity of the bi-implication operation in a Boolean algebra.

bihimp_bihimp_bihimp_comm.code: bihimp_bihimp_bihimp_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b c d : α) : a ⇔ b ⇔ (c ⇔ d) = a ⇔ c ⇔ (b ⇔ d)
bihimp_bihimp_bihimp_comm.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a Boolean algebra, a three-way equivalence relationship involving four elements can be rearranged without changing its overall equivalence.

bihimp_bihimp_cancel_left.code: bihimp_bihimp_cancel_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ (a ⇔ b) = b
bihimp_bihimp_cancel_left.description: This theorem establishes that in a Boolean algebra, an element combined with the equivalence of itself and another element results in the other element.

bihimp_bihimp_cancel_right.code: bihimp_bihimp_cancel_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : b ⇔ a ⇔ a = b
bihimp_bihimp_cancel_right.description: This theorem states that in a boolean algebra, if the bi-implication between two elements holds, then the second element is equivalent to the first element.

bihimp_bihimp_self.code: bihimp_bihimp_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b ⇔ a = b
bihimp_bihimp_self.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional of two elements being mutually equivalent is equivalent to them being equal.

bihimp_left_involutive.code: bihimp_left_involutive.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Involutive fun x => x ⇔ a
bihimp_left_involutive.description: This theorem shows that in a Boolean algebra, the operation of bi-implication with a fixed element is involutive, meaning applying it twice returns the original element.

bihimp_right_involutive.code: bihimp_right_involutive.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Involutive fun x => a ⇔ x
bihimp_right_involutive.description: This theorem shows that in a Boolean algebra, the bi-implication operation is involutive for a given element.

bihimp_left_injective.code: bihimp_left_injective.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Injective fun x => x ⇔ a
bihimp_left_injective.description: This theorem establishes that in a boolean algebra, the function mapping any element to its bi-implication with a fixed element is injective.

bihimp_right_injective.code: bihimp_right_injective.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Injective fun x => a ⇔ x
bihimp_right_injective.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the operation of taking the biconditional with a fixed element is injective, meaning different elements yield different biconditional results with that fixed element.

bihimp_left_surjective.code: bihimp_left_surjective.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Surjective fun x => x ⇔ a
bihimp_left_surjective.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a Boolean algebra, the function that associates each element with its biconditional relationship to a given element is surjective.

bihimp_right_surjective.code: bihimp_right_surjective.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : Surjective fun x => a ⇔ x
bihimp_right_surjective.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a Boolean algebra, the implication from a fixed element to any other element is surjective, meaning that for every element there exists at least one element that satisfies the implication to it.

bihimp_left_inj.code: bihimp_left_inj.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ⇔ b = c ⇔ b ↔ a = c
bihimp_left_inj.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, if two elements are bi-implicationally related to a third element, then those two elements must be equal to each other.

bihimp_right_inj.code: bihimp_right_inj.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} : a ⇔ b = a ⇔ c ↔ b = c
bihimp_right_inj.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, if two bi-implications with the same element are equal, then their second arguments must also be equal.

bihimp_eq_left.code: bihimp_eq_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ⇔ b = a ↔ b = ⊤
bihimp_eq_left.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, two elements are bi-implicative if and only if they are equal to the top element.

bihimp_eq_right.code: bihimp_eq_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b : α} : a ⇔ b = b ↔ a = ⊤
bihimp_eq_right.description: This theorem establishes that the equivalence of two elements in a boolean algebra is equal to the equivalence of the second element with truth when the first element is equivalent to the second.

Codisjoint.bihimp_left.code:
Codisjoint.bihimp_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (ha : Codisjoint a c) (hb : Codisjoint b c) :
  Codisjoint (a ⇔ b) c
Codisjoint.bihimp_left.description: This theorem states that in a boolean algebra, if two elements are codisjoint from a third element, then their bi-implication is also codisjoint from that third element.

Codisjoint.bihimp_right.code:
Codisjoint.bihimp_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (ha : Codisjoint a b)
  (hb : Codisjoint a c) : Codisjoint a (b ⇔ c)
Codisjoint.bihimp_right.description: This theorem states that in a boolean algebra, if an element is codisjoint from two other elements, then it is also codisjoint from their bi-implication.

symmDiff_eq.code: symmDiff_eq.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a ⊓ bᶜ ⊔ b ⊓ aᶜ
symmDiff_eq.description: This theorem describes the symmetric difference of two elements in a Boolean algebra as the union of their intersections with the complement of the other.

bihimp_eq.code: bihimp_eq.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (a ⊔ bᶜ) ⊓ (b ⊔ aᶜ)
bihimp_eq.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional of two elements is equivalent to their joint conjunction with their complements in a specific form.

symmDiff_eq'.code: symmDiff_eq'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = (a ⊔ b) ⊓ (aᶜ ⊔ bᶜ)
symmDiff_eq'.description: This theorem states that the symmetric difference between two elements in a Boolean algebra is equal to the intersection of their union and the union of their complements.

bihimp_eq'.code: bihimp_eq'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = a ⊓ b ⊔ aᶜ ⊓ bᶜ
bihimp_eq'.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the bi-implication between two elements is equal to the sum of their joint intersection and the intersection of their complements.

symmDiff_top.code: symmDiff_top.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : a ∆ ⊤ = aᶜ
symmDiff_top.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the symmetric difference of an element with the top element equals the complement of that element.

top_symmDiff.code: top_symmDiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : ⊤ ∆ a = aᶜ
top_symmDiff.description: This theorem asserts that in a Boolean algebra, the symmetric difference between the top element and any element is equal to the complement of that element.

compl_symmDiff.code: compl_symmDiff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : (a ∆ b)ᶜ = a ⇔ b
compl_symmDiff.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the complement of the symmetric difference of two elements is equivalent to the condition that one element is equal to the complement of the other.

compl_bihimp.code: compl_bihimp.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : (a ⇔ b)ᶜ = a ∆ b
compl_bihimp.description: This theorem establishes that in a Boolean algebra, the complement of the biconditional of two elements is equal to their symmetric difference.

compl_symmDiff_compl.code: compl_symmDiff_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : aᶜ ∆ bᶜ = a ∆ b
compl_symmDiff_compl.description: This theorem shows that the symmetric difference of the complements of two elements in a Boolean algebra is equal to the symmetric difference of the elements themselves.

compl_bihimp_compl.code: compl_bihimp_compl.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : aᶜ ⇔ bᶜ = a ⇔ b
compl_bihimp_compl.description: This theorem shows that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional of the complements of two elements is equal to the biconditional of the elements themselves.

symmDiff_eq_top.code: symmDiff_eq_top.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = ⊤ ↔ IsCompl a b

explanatories.IsCompl.symmDiff_eq_top: This theorem states that in a coheyting algebra, if two elements are complementary, their symmetric difference equals the top element.

symmDiff_eq_top.description: This theorem states that in a boolean algebra, the symmetric difference of two elements is equal to the top element if and only if the two elements are complements of each other.

bihimp_eq_bot.code: bihimp_eq_bot.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = ⊥ ↔ IsCompl a b

explanatories.IsCompl.bihimp_eq_bot: This theorem states that in a Heyting algebra, if two elements are complements of each other, then their bi-implication is equal to the bottom element.

bihimp_eq_bot.description: This theorem establishes that in a Boolean algebra, the biconditional of two elements being false is equivalent to those elements being complements of each other.

compl_symmDiff_self.code: compl_symmDiff_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : aᶜ ∆ a = ⊤
compl_symmDiff_self.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a Boolean algebra, the symmetric difference between an element and its complement is equal to the top element.

symmDiff_compl_self.code: symmDiff_compl_self.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a : α) : a ∆ aᶜ = ⊤
symmDiff_compl_self.description: This theorem states that in a Boolean algebra, the symmetric difference between an element and its complement is equal to the top element.

symmDiff_symmDiff_right'.code:
symmDiff_symmDiff_right'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] (a b c : α) :
  a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a ⊓ b ⊓ c ⊔ a ⊓ bᶜ ⊓ cᶜ ⊔ aᶜ ⊓ b ⊓ cᶜ ⊔ aᶜ ⊓ bᶜ ⊓ c
symmDiff_symmDiff_right'.description: This theorem demonstrates that the symmetric difference of an element with the symmetric difference of two other elements in a Boolean algebra can be expressed as a combination of meets and joins of the elements involved.

Disjoint.le_symmDiff_sup_symmDiff_left.code:
Disjoint.le_symmDiff_sup_symmDiff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : Disjoint a b) :
  c ≤ a ∆ c ⊔ b ∆ c
Disjoint.le_symmDiff_sup_symmDiff_left.description: This theorem states that if two elements are disjoint in a Boolean algebra, then any element is less than or equal to the join of the symmetric differences of that element with each of the disjoint elements.

Disjoint.le_symmDiff_sup_symmDiff_right.code:
Disjoint.le_symmDiff_sup_symmDiff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : Disjoint b c) :
  a ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ a ∆ c
Disjoint.le_symmDiff_sup_symmDiff_right.description: This theorem asserts that in a Boolean algebra, if two elements are disjoint, then another element is less than or equal to the supremum of the symmetric differences with each of the disjoint elements.

Codisjoint.bihimp_inf_bihimp_le_left.code:
Codisjoint.bihimp_inf_bihimp_le_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : Codisjoint a b) :
  a ⇔ c ⊓ b ⇔ c ≤ c
Codisjoint.bihimp_inf_bihimp_le_left.description: This theorem asserts that for two codisjoint elements in a Boolean algebra, the bi-implication with a third element and the conjunction with the same element is less than or equal to that third element.

Codisjoint.bihimp_inf_bihimp_le_right.code:
Codisjoint.bihimp_inf_bihimp_le_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [BooleanAlgebra α] {a b c : α} (h : Codisjoint b c) :
  a ⇔ b ⊓ a ⇔ c ≤ a
Codisjoint.bihimp_inf_bihimp_le_right.description: This theorem shows that in a Boolean algebra, if two elements are codisjoint, the biconditional between one element and the intersection of another with a third is less than or equal to the first element.

symmDiff_fst.code:
symmDiff_fst.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra β]
  (a b : α × β) : (a ∆ b).1 = a.1 ∆ b.1
symmDiff_fst.description: This theorem shows that the first component of the symmetric difference between two pairs is equal to the symmetric difference of their respective first components in a generalized coheyting algebra.

symmDiff_snd.code:
symmDiff_snd.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra β]
  (a b : α × β) : (a ∆ b).2 = a.2 ∆ b.2
symmDiff_snd.description: This theorem establishes that the second component of the symmetric difference of two pairs is equal to the symmetric difference of their respective second components.

bihimp_fst.code:
bihimp_fst.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra β]
  (a b : α × β) : (a ⇔ b).1 = a.1 ⇔ b.1
bihimp_fst.description: This theorem describes a relationship in a generalized heyting algebra that maintains the equivalence of the first components of pairs when their equivalence is established.

bihimp_snd.code:
bihimp_snd.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra α] [GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra β]
  (a b : α × β) : (a ⇔ b).2 = a.2 ⇔ b.2
bihimp_snd.description: This theorem establishes that in a generalized Heyting algebra, the second component of a biconditional equality between two pairs is equivalent to the biconditional equality of their respective second components.

Pi.symmDiff_def.code:
Pi.symmDiff_def.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {π : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra (π i)]
  (a b : (i : ι) → π i) : a ∆ b = fun i => a i ∆ b i
Pi.symmDiff_def.description: This theorem defines the symmetric difference of two functions as a new function that computes the symmetric difference of their outputs for each input from the same index set.

Pi.bihimp_def.code:
Pi.bihimp_def.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {π : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (π i)]
  (a b : (i : ι) → π i) : a ⇔ b = fun i => a i ⇔ b i
Pi.bihimp_def.description: This theorem states that the biconditional equality of two functions is equivalent to the biconditional equality of their corresponding values at each input.

Pi.symmDiff_apply.code:
Pi.symmDiff_apply.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {π : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra (π i)]
  (a b : (i : ι) → π i) (i : ι) : (a ∆ b) i = a i ∆ b i
Pi.symmDiff_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a system of generalized coheyting algebras indexed by a type, the symmetric difference of two functions evaluated at a specific index equals the symmetric difference of their evaluations at that index.

Pi.bihimp_apply.code:
Pi.bihimp_apply.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {π : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → GeneralizedHeytingAlgebra (π i)]
  (a b : (i : ι) → π i) (i : ι) : (a ⇔ b) i = a i ⇔ b i
Pi.bihimp_apply.description: This theorem shows that in a family of generalized Heyting algebras, the evaluation of the bi-implication between two functions at a fixed index is equal to the bi-implication of their values at that index.

WellFounded.isAsymm.code: WellFounded.isAsymm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {r : α → α → Prop} (h : WellFounded r) : IsAsymm α r
WellFounded.isAsymm.description: This theorem establishes that a well-founded relation is asymmetric.

WellFounded.isIrrefl.code: WellFounded.isIrrefl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {r : α → α → Prop} (h : WellFounded r) : IsIrrefl α r

explanatories.IsAsymm.isIrrefl: A theorem stating that if a relation is asymmetric, then it is also irreflexive.

WellFounded.isIrrefl.description: This theorem demonstrates that a well-founded relation is irreflexive.

WellFounded.mono.code:
WellFounded.mono.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {r r' : α → α → Prop} (hr : WellFounded r) (h : ∀ (a b : α), r' a b → r a b) :
  WellFounded r'
WellFounded.mono.description: This theorem states that if one well-founded relation is refined by another, the latter is also well-founded.

WellFounded.onFun.code:
WellFounded.onFun.{u_4, u_5} {α : Sort u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {r : β → β → Prop} {f : α → β} :
  WellFounded r → WellFounded (r on f)
WellFounded.onFun.description: This theorem shows that if a relation is well-founded, then the relation obtained by restricting it to the image of a function is also well-founded.

WellFounded.has_min.code:
WellFounded.has_min.{u_4} {α : Type u_4} {r : α → α → Prop} (H : WellFounded r) (s : Set α) :
  s.Nonempty → ∃ a ∈ s, ∀ x ∈ s, ¬r x a
WellFounded.has_min.comment:

Acc.induction_bot'.code:
Acc.induction_bot'.{u_4, u_5} {α : Sort u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {r : α → α → Prop} {a bot : α} (ha : Acc r a) {C : β → Prop}
  {f : α → β} (ih : ∀ (b : α), f b ≠ f bot → C (f b) → ∃ c, r c b ∧ C (f c)) : C (f a) → C (f bot)
Acc.induction_bot'.comment:
Let `r` be a relation on `α`, let `f : α → β` be a function, let `C : β → Prop`, and
let `bot : α`. This induction principle shows that `C (f bot)` holds, given that
* some `a` that is accessible by `r` satisfies `C (f a)`, and
* for each `b` such that `f b ≠ f bot` and `C (f b)` holds, there is `c`
  satisfying `r c b` and `C (f c)`.
Acc.induction_bot'.description: This theorem establishes that if a property holds for an element in a well-founded set and can be shown to be preserved under certain conditions involving another element in that set, then it must also hold for a specific base case.

Acc.induction_bot.comment:
Let `r` be a relation on `α`, let `C : α → Prop` and let `bot : α`.
This induction principle shows that `C bot` holds, given that
* some `a` that is accessible by `r` satisfies `C a`, and
* for each `b ≠ bot` such that `C b` holds, there is `c` satisfying `r c b` and `C c`.
Acc.induction_bot.description: This theorem presents an induction principle that allows establishing a property for a particular element based on its accessibility through a relation and the validity of the property for other elements related to it.

  (ih : ∀ (b : α), b ≠ bot → C b → ∃ c, r c b ∧ C c) : C a → C bot
WellFounded.induction_bot.comment:
Let `r` be a well-founded relation on `α`, let `C : α → Prop`, and let `bot : α`.
This induction principle shows that `C bot` holds, given that
* some `a` satisfies `C a`, and
* for each `b` that satisfies `C b`, there is `c` satisfying `r c b` and `C c`.

The naming is inspired by the fact that when `r` is transitive, it follows that `bot` is
the smallest element w.r.t. `r` that satisfies `C`.

CircularPreorder.sbtw_trans_left.code:
CircularPreorder.sbtw_trans_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [self : CircularPreorder α] {a b c d : α} :
  sbtw a b c → sbtw b d c → sbtw a d c
CircularPreorder.sbtw_trans_left.comment:
For any fixed `c`, `fun a b ↦ sbtw a b c` is a transitive relation.

I.e., given `a` `b` `d` `c` in that "order", if we have `b` strictly between `a` and `c`, and `d`
strictly between `b` and `c`, then `d` is strictly between `a` and `c`.

CircularPreorder.sbtw_trans_left.description: In a circular preorder, if one element is strictly between two others and a second element is also strictly between a third element and the same second element, then the first element is strictly between the third element and the same second element.

CircularPreorder.sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw.code:
CircularPreorder.sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [self : CircularPreorder α] {a b c : α} :
  sbtw a b c ↔ btw a b c ∧ ¬btw c b a
CircularPreorder.sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw.comment:
Strict betweenness is given by betweenness in one direction and non-betweenness in the other.

I.e., if `b` is between `a` and `c` but not between `c` and `a`, then we say `b` is strictly
between `a` and `c`.

explanatories.Preorder.lt_iff_le_not_le: This theorem characterizes the strict inequality in a preorder by stating that one element is less than another if and only if it is related to it but not the other way around.

Preorder.toCircularPreorder.fullDefinition: abbrev Preorder.toCircularPreorder (α : Type*) [Preorder α] : CircularPreorder α where   btw a b c := a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c ∨ b ≤ c ∧ c ≤ a ∨ c ≤ a ∧ a ≤ b   sbtw a b c := a < b ∧ b < c ∨ b < c ∧ c < a ∨ c < a ∧ a < b   btw_refl a := Or.inl ⟨le_rfl, le_rfl⟩   btw_cyclic_left {a b c} h := by     dsimp     rwa [← or_assoc, or_comm]   sbtw_trans_left {a b c d} := by     rintro (⟨hab, hbc⟩ | ⟨hbc, hca⟩ | ⟨hca, hab⟩) (⟨hbd, hdc⟩ | ⟨hdc, hcb⟩ | ⟨hcb, hbd⟩)     · exact Or.inl ⟨hab.trans hbd, hdc⟩     · exact (hbc.not_lt hcb).elim     · exact (hbc.not_lt hcb).elim     · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hdc, hca⟩)     · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hdc, hca⟩)     · exact (hbc.not_lt hcb).elim     · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hdc, hca⟩)     · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hdc, hca⟩)     · exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hca, hab.trans hbd⟩)   sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw {a b c} := by     simp_rw [lt_iff_le_not_le]     have h1 := le_trans a b c     have h2 := le_trans b c a     have h3 := le_trans c a b     -- Porting note: was `tauto`, but this is a much faster tactic proof     revert h1 h2 h3     generalize (a ≤ b) = p1     generalize (b ≤ a) = p2     generalize (a ≤ c) = p3     generalize (c ≤ a) = p4     generalize (b ≤ c) = p5     by_cases p1 <;> by_cases p2 <;> by_cases p3 <;> by_cases p4 <;> by_cases p5 <;> simp [*]
Preorder.toCircularPreorder.description: A circular preorder is formed by treating a standard preorder as if it wraps around in a loop.

explanatories.SBtw.sbtw: A definition of a relation that indicates one element is strictly positioned between two others in a circular order.
explanatories.CircularPreorder.btw_refl: In a circular preorder, any element is considered to be between itself and itself.
explanatories.CircularPreorder.btw_cyclic_left: If one element is positioned between two others in a circular order, then the last element is positioned between the first two elements in reverse order.
explanatories.CircularPreorder.sbtw_trans_left: In a circular preorder, if one element is strictly between two others and a second element is also strictly between a third element and the same second element, then the first element is strictly between the third element and the same second element.
explanatories.btw_cyclic_right: In a circular preorder, if one element is positioned between two others, then the last element is also positioned between the first and the second in the opposite direction.
explanatories.CircularPreorder.sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw: In a circular preorder, an element is considered strictly between two others if it is positioned between them in one direction while not being positioned between them in the reverse direction.
explanatories.sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw: In a circular preorder, an element is positioned between two others if and only if it is between them in one order while not being between them in the reverse order.
explanatories.SBtw.sbtw.btw: In a circular preorder, if one element is strictly between two others, then it is also positioned between those two elements in a non-strict sense, serving as an alias for a previously established theorem.
explanatories.SBtw.sbtw.trans_right: In a circular preorder, if one element is strictly between two others and also strictly positioned between the first element and a third, then it is strictly positioned between the first and the last element as well.
explanatories.OrderDual.btw: This defines a relation indicating that one element is positioned between two others in the dual order of a given structure.
explanatories.OrderDual.sbtw: The definition establishes that a strict between relation in one order is equivalent to a strict between relation in the dual order of that set.

OrderDual.circularPreorder.fullDefinition: instance circularPreorder (α : Type*) [CircularPreorder α] : CircularPreorder αᵒᵈ :=   { OrderDual.btw α,     OrderDual.sbtw α with     btw_refl := fun _ => @btw_refl α _ _     btw_cyclic_left := fun {_ _ _} => @btw_cyclic_right α _ _ _ _     sbtw_trans_left := fun {_ _ _ _} habc hbdc => hbdc.trans_right habc     sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw := fun {a b c} => @sbtw_iff_btw_not_btw α _ c b a }
OrderDual.circularPreorder.description: The definition establishes that the circular preorder structure can be mirrored in its dual form, maintaining the same relational properties.

OrderDual.circularPartialOrder.code: OrderDual.circularPartialOrder.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [CircularPartialOrder α] : CircularPartialOrder αᵒᵈ

explanatories.CircularPartialOrder.btw_antisymm: In a circular partial order, if one element is positioned between two others and that same element is also positioned between the other two in the reverse order, then at least two of those elements must be the same.
explanatories.OrderDual.circularPreorder: The definition establishes that the circular preorder structure can be mirrored in its dual form, maintaining the same relational properties.

OrderDual.circularPartialOrder.fullDefinition: instance circularPartialOrder (α : Type*) [CircularPartialOrder α] : CircularPartialOrder αᵒᵈ :=   { OrderDual.circularPreorder α with     btw_antisymm := fun {_ _ _} habc hcba => @btw_antisymm α _ _ _ _ hcba habc }
OrderDual.circularPartialOrder.description: The dual structure of a circular partial order is itself a circular partial order.

Set.uIcc.code: Set.uIcc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] (a b : α) : Set α
Set.uIcc.comment:
`uIcc a b` is the set of elements lying between `a` and `b`, with `a` and `b` included.
Note that we define it more generally in a lattice as `Set.Icc (a ⊓ b) (a ⊔ b)`. In a product type,
`uIcc` corresponds to the bounding box of the two elements.

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

Set.uIcc.fullDefinition: def uIcc (a b : α) : Set α := Icc (a ⊓ b) (a ⊔ b)
Set.uIcc.description: This definition describes a set containing all elements in a lattice that lie between two specified elements, inclusive of those endpoints.

Set.uIcc_of_lt.description: This theorem asserts that for two elements in a lattice, when the first is less than the second, the inclusive interval defined by these elements is equivalent to the standard interval between them.

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

Set.uIcc_of_gt.description: This theorem states that for two elements in a lattice where one is greater than the other, the set between them, inclusive, is equal to the closed interval from the smaller to the larger element.

Set.uIcc_self.description: This theorem asserts that the set defined by a single element with itself forms a set containing just that element.

Set.nonempty_uIcc.description: This theorem states that the interval defined by two elements in a lattice is non-empty whenever the first element is less than or equal to the second.

Set.Icc_subset_uIcc.code: Set.Icc_subset_uIcc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] {a b : α} : Icc a b ⊆ [[a, b]]
Set.Icc_subset_uIcc.description: This theorem establishes that the closed interval formed by two elements in a lattice is a subset of the set defined by those elements, inclusive.

Set.Icc_subset_uIcc'.code: Set.Icc_subset_uIcc'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] {a b : α} : Icc b a ⊆ [[a, b]]
Set.Icc_subset_uIcc'.description: This theorem asserts that the standard interval between two elements in a lattice, where the second is less than the first, is contained within the inclusive interval defined by those two elements.

Set.left_mem_uIcc.description: This theorem asserts that any element is included in the inclusive interval defined by itself and another element in a lattice.

Set.right_mem_uIcc.code: Set.right_mem_uIcc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] {a b : α} : b ∈ [[a, b]]
Set.right_mem_uIcc.description: This theorem states that the upper endpoint of an inclusive interval defined by two elements in a lattice is always an element of that interval.

Set.mem_uIcc_of_le.code: Set.mem_uIcc_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] {a b x : α} (ha : a ≤ x) (hb : x ≤ b) : x ∈ [[a, b]]
Set.mem_uIcc_of_le.description: This theorem states that if an element lies between two other elements in a lattice, then it is included in the inclusive interval defined by those two elements.

Set.mem_uIcc_of_ge.code: Set.mem_uIcc_of_ge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] {a b x : α} (hb : b ≤ x) (ha : x ≤ a) : x ∈ [[a, b]]
Set.mem_uIcc_of_ge.description: This theorem states that if an element is greater than or equal to one bound and less than or equal to another bound in a lattice, then it is included in the inclusive interval defined by those bounds.

Set.uIcc_subset_Icc.description: This theorem states that if two elements are included in a closed interval in a lattice, then the inclusive interval defined by these elements is a subset of that closed interval.

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_mem.code:

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_mem.description: This theorem states that the inclusion of one closed interval between two elements in a lattice within another such interval is equivalent to both endpoints of the first interval being contained in the second.

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le'.code:

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_left.description: This theorem establishes that if an element belongs to a closed interval defined by two elements in a lattice, then the interval defined by one endpoint and that element is contained within the larger interval.

Set.uIcc_prod_uIcc.code:

explanatories.MonotoneOn.mapsTo_uIcc: This theorem states that if a function is monotonic on a closed interval, then it maps that interval to the corresponding interval of its outputs.

AntitoneOn.mapsTo_uIcc.description: This theorem states that if a function is antitonic on a closed interval, then it maps that interval to the corresponding interval of its outputs.

MonotoneOn.image_uIcc_subset.code:
MonotoneOn.image_uIcc_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [LinearOrder α] [Lattice β] {f : α → β} {a b : α}
  (hf : MonotoneOn f [[a, b]]) : f '' [[a, b]] ⊆ [[f a, f b]]
MonotoneOn.image_uIcc_subset.description: This theorem states that if a function is monotone on a closed interval defined by two ordered elements, then the image of that interval under the function will be contained within the interval defined by the function's values at those two elements.

AntitoneOn.image_uIcc_subset.code:
AntitoneOn.image_uIcc_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [LinearOrder α] [Lattice β] {f : α → β} {a b : α}
  (hf : AntitoneOn f [[a, b]]) : f '' [[a, b]] ⊆ [[f a, f b]]

explanatories.MonotoneOn.image_uIcc_subset: This theorem states that if a function is monotone on a closed interval defined by two ordered elements, then the image of that interval under the function will be contained within the interval defined by the function's values at those two elements.

AntitoneOn.image_uIcc_subset.description: This theorem establishes that if a function is antitone on a closed interval between two elements, then the image of this interval under the function is contained within the closed interval defined by the images of the endpoints.

Set.Icc_min_max.code: Set.Icc_min_max.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : Icc (min a b) (max a b) = [[a, b]]

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.
explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

Set.Icc_min_max.description: This theorem states that the closed interval defined by the minimum and maximum of two ordered elements is equal to the closed interval defined by those two elements.

Set.uIcc_of_not_le.code: Set.uIcc_of_not_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} (h : ¬a ≤ b) : [[a, b]] = Icc b a

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

Set.uIcc_of_not_le.description: This theorem states that if one element is not less than or equal to another, then the closed interval defined by these two elements is equal to the interval defined in the reverse order.

Set.uIcc_of_not_ge.code: Set.uIcc_of_not_ge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} (h : ¬b ≤ a) : [[a, b]] = Icc a b

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

Set.uIcc_of_not_ge.description: This theorem asserts that if one element is not less than or equal to another in a linear order, then the inclusive interval defined by these two elements is equal to the closed interval between them.

Set.uIcc_eq_union.code: Set.uIcc_eq_union.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : [[a, b]] = Icc a b ∪ Icc b a

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

Set.uIcc_eq_union.description: This theorem establishes that the inclusive interval between two elements is equal to the union of the intervals defined in each order.

Set.mem_uIcc.code: Set.mem_uIcc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a ∈ [[b, c]] ↔ b ≤ a ∧ a ≤ c ∨ c ≤ a ∧ a ≤ b
Set.mem_uIcc.description: This theorem characterizes membership in a closed interval by stating that an element belongs to the interval if it is between the two endpoints in either order.

Set.not_mem_uIcc_of_lt.code: Set.not_mem_uIcc_of_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (ha : c < a) (hb : c < b) : c ∉ [[a, b]]
Set.not_mem_uIcc_of_lt.description: This theorem asserts that if an element is less than both endpoints of an inclusive interval, then it cannot be a member of that interval.

Set.not_mem_uIcc_of_gt.code: Set.not_mem_uIcc_of_gt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (ha : a < c) (hb : b < c) : c ∉ [[a, b]]
Set.not_mem_uIcc_of_gt.description: This theorem demonstrates that if two elements are both less than a third element, then that third element is not contained within the closed interval defined by the first two elements.

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le.code:
Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : α} :
  [[a₁, b₁]] ⊆ [[a₂, b₂]] ↔ min a₂ b₂ ≤ min a₁ b₁ ∧ max a₁ b₁ ≤ max a₂ b₂

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.
explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le.description: This theorem establishes that one closed interval is a subset of another if and only if the minimum of the endpoints of the second interval is less than or equal to the minimum of the endpoints of the first interval and the maximum of the first interval is less than or equal to the maximum of the second interval.

Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_union_uIcc.code: Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_union_uIcc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : [[a, c]] ⊆ [[a, b]] ∪ [[b, c]]
Set.uIcc_subset_uIcc_union_uIcc.description: This theorem states that the interval between two elements is contained within the union of two adjacent intervals formed by a third element, illustrating a form of the triangle inequality.

Set.monotone_or_antitone_iff_uIcc.code:
Set.monotone_or_antitone_iff_uIcc.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β] {f : α → β} :
  Monotone f ∨ Antitone f ↔ ∀ (a b c : α), c ∈ [[a, b]] → f c ∈ [[f a, f b]]

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.
explanatories.Antitone: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.

Set.monotone_or_antitone_iff_uIcc.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between a function being monotonic or antitonic and the preservation of inclusion within intervals under that function's mapping.

Set.monotoneOn_or_antitoneOn_iff_uIcc.code:
Set.monotoneOn_or_antitoneOn_iff_uIcc.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β]
  {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
  MonotoneOn f s ∨ AntitoneOn f s ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, ∀ c ∈ s, c ∈ [[a, b]] → f c ∈ [[f a, f b]]

explanatories.MonotoneOn: A function is considered monotone on a set if, whenever two inputs from that set relate in terms of order, the outputs corresponding to those inputs maintain the same order relationship.
explanatories.AntitoneOn: A function is considered antitone on a set if, whenever two inputs from that set relate in terms of order, the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.

Set.monotoneOn_or_antitoneOn_iff_uIcc.description: This theorem establishes a condition for a function to be either monotonically increasing or decreasing over a set, which is equivalent to the function's values remaining within the interval defined by its endpoints whenever the input is within the interval formed by two elements of the set.

Set.uIoc.code: Set.uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] : α → α → Set α
Set.uIoc.comment: The open-closed uIcc with unordered bounds.

explanatories.Min.min: The minimum operation determines the smaller of two given values.
explanatories.Max.max: The maximum operation identifies the larger of two given values.
explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.

Set.uIoc.fullDefinition: def uIoc : α → α → Set α := fun a b => Ioc (min a b) (max a b)
Set.uIoc.description: This definition introduces a set that represents an open-closed interval in a linear order, extending from one element to another without including the first element but including the second.

Set.termΙ.comment:
`Ι a b` denotes the open-closed interval with unordered bounds. Here, `Ι` is a capital iota,
distinguished from a capital `i`.

Set.uIoc_of_le.code: Set.uIoc_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : Ι a b = Ioc a b

explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.

Set.uIoc_of_le.description: This theorem establishes that in a linearly ordered set, the interval that includes the first element but excludes the second is equal to the open interval defined by the two elements.

Set.uIoc_of_ge.code: Set.uIoc_of_ge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : Ι a b = Ioc b a

explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.

Set.uIoc_of_ge.description: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another, the open interval defined from the first element to the second is equal to the set of elements between them, excluding the first endpoint and including the second.

Set.uIoc_eq_union.code: Set.uIoc_eq_union.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : Ι a b = Ioc a b ∪ Ioc b a

explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.

Set.uIoc_eq_union.description: This theorem states that the open interval between two elements is equivalent to the union of the open intervals from the first element to the second and from the second element to the first.

Set.mem_uIoc.code: Set.mem_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a ∈ Ι b c ↔ b < a ∧ a ≤ c ∨ c < a ∧ a ≤ b
Set.mem_uIoc.description: This theorem establishes that an element belongs to the open interval defined by two bounds if it lies between them, considering the order relations in either direction.

Set.not_mem_uIoc.code: Set.not_mem_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a ∉ Ι b c ↔ a ≤ b ∧ a ≤ c ∨ c < a ∧ b < a
Set.not_mem_uIoc.description: This theorem establishes a logical equivalence concerning an element's membership in a certain interval, indicating that the element is not within the open interval defined by two other elements if and only if it is less than or equal to both or greater than both.

Set.left_mem_uIoc.code: Set.left_mem_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : a ∈ Ι a b ↔ b < a
Set.left_mem_uIoc.description: This theorem characterizes the membership of an element in the left-open interval defined by two elements in a linear order, indicating that it holds if and only if the second element is less than the first.

Set.right_mem_uIoc.code: Set.right_mem_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : b ∈ Ι a b ↔ a < b
Set.right_mem_uIoc.description: This theorem states that the right endpoint is included in the open interval between two elements if and only if the first element is strictly less than the second element.

Set.forall_uIoc_iff.code:
Set.forall_uIoc_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} {P : α → Prop} :
  (∀ x ∈ Ι a b, P x) ↔ (∀ x ∈ Ioc a b, P x) ∧ ∀ x ∈ Ioc b a, P x

explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.

Set.forall_uIoc_iff.description: This theorem establishes that a property holds for all elements in a specified interval if and only if it holds for elements in two distinct open-closed intervals formed by reversing the bounds.

Set.uIoc_subset_uIoc_of_uIcc_subset_uIcc.code:
Set.uIoc_subset_uIoc_of_uIcc_subset_uIcc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c d : α} (h : [[a, b]] ⊆ [[c, d]]) :

Set.uIoc_subset_uIoc_of_uIcc_subset_uIcc.description: This theorem asserts that if one open interval is a subset of another open interval, then the interval defined by the endpoints of the first is also a subset of the interval defined by the endpoints of the second.

Set.uIoc_comm.code: Set.uIoc_comm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] (a b : α) : Ι a b = Ι b a
Set.uIoc_comm.description: This theorem establishes that the open interval defined by two elements can be reversed without changing its value.

Set.Ioc_subset_uIoc.code: Set.Ioc_subset_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : Ioc a b ⊆ Ι a b
Set.Ioc_subset_uIoc.description: This theorem demonstrates that the open interval between two elements is contained within the corresponding closed interval formed by the same two elements.

Set.Ioc_subset_uIoc'.code: Set.Ioc_subset_uIoc'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} : Ioc a b ⊆ Ι b a
Set.Ioc_subset_uIoc'.description: This theorem establishes that the set of elements strictly between two given elements in a linear order is a subset of the open interval defined from the second element to the first.

Set.eq_of_mem_uIoc_of_mem_uIoc.code: Set.eq_of_mem_uIoc_of_mem_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : a ∈ Ι b c → b ∈ Ι a c → a = b
Set.eq_of_mem_uIoc_of_mem_uIoc.description: This theorem indicates that if one element belongs to an open interval defined by two other elements and the second element also belongs to an open interval defined by the first and the same third element, then the two elements must be equal.

Set.eq_of_mem_uIoc_of_mem_uIoc'.code: Set.eq_of_mem_uIoc_of_mem_uIoc'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} : b ∈ Ι a c → c ∈ Ι a b → b = c
Set.eq_of_mem_uIoc_of_mem_uIoc'.description: This theorem states that if two numbers are found in a particular interval defined by two other numbers, then they must be equal to each other.

Set.eq_of_not_mem_uIoc_of_not_mem_uIoc.code:
Set.eq_of_not_mem_uIoc_of_not_mem_uIoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ c) (hb : b ≤ c) :

Set.eq_of_not_mem_uIoc_of_not_mem_uIoc.description: This theorem concludes that if two elements are both less than or equal to a third element and neither of them belongs to an open interval defined by the other and the third element, then they must be equal.

Set.ordConnected_iff_uIcc_subset_right.code:
Set.ordConnected_iff_uIcc_subset_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {s : Set α} {x : α} (hx : x ∈ s) :

Set.ordConnected_iff_uIcc_subset_right.description: This theorem establishes that a set is order-connected if and only if, for a fixed element within the set, the closed interval from any other element in the set to this fixed element also resides within the set.

In a linear ordered field, the whole field is order isomorphic to the open interval `(-1, 1)`.
We consider the actual implementation to be a "black box", so it is irreducible.

explanatories.Set.Ioo: This definition specifies the set of elements that lie strictly between two given elements in a preorder structure, creating a left-open and right-open interval.
explanatories.StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse: This definition asserts that if a strictly monotone function has a right inverse, it establishes an order isomorphism between two ordered types.
explanatories.Set.codRestrict: The definition specifies a function that restricts the codomain of another function to a specified subset while ensuring that the outputs of the original function belong to that subset.
explanatories.abs_lt: This theorem characterizes the condition under which the absolute value of an element is less than another element, relating it to a pair of linear inequalities involving both the element and the other element's negation in the context of a linear order and additive group.
explanatories.abs_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the absolute value of an element is always non-negative in the context of a lattice and additive group.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.lt_one_add: This theorem demonstrates that any element in a partially ordered set is always less than one added to that element.
explanatories.abs_div: This theorem expresses that the absolute value of the division of two elements in a linear ordered field is equal to the division of their absolute values.
explanatories.abs_of_pos: This theorem establishes that if an element is positive within a lattice and additive group, then its absolute value is equal to the element itself.
explanatories.div_lt_one: This theorem states that in a linear ordered semifield, an element divided by a positive element is less than one if and only if the original element is less than that positive element.
explanatories.strictMono_of_odd_strictMonoOn_nonneg: An odd function defined on a linear ordered additive commutative group is strictly monotone on the entire group if it is strictly monotone on the non-negative elements of the group.
explanatories.StrictMono.codRestrict: The theorem states that if a function is strictly monotonic and its image is entirely contained within a specified set, then the codomain restricted function remains strictly monotonic.
explanatories.abs_neg: This theorem states that the absolute value of the negation of an element is equal to the absolute value of the element itself in the context of a lattice and additive group.
explanatories.neg_div: This theorem states that in a division monoid with the ability to distribute negation, the quotient of the negation of a second element by the first element is equal to the negation of the quotient of the second element by the first element.
explanatories.abs_of_nonneg: The theorem establishes that if an element is non-negative in the context of a lattice and additive group, then its absolute value is equal to the element itself.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.div_lt_div_iff: This theorem states that in a linear ordered semifield, the division of one element by a positive element is less than the division of another element by another positive element if and only if the product of the first element and the second positive element is less than the product of the other element and the first positive element.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.sub_pos: This theorem states that the positivity of the difference between two elements in an additive group is equivalent to the first element being greater than the second element.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne': A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then the two elements cannot be equal.

orderIsoIooNegOneOne.fullDefinition: def orderIsoIooNegOneOne (k : Type*) [LinearOrderedField k] : k ≃o Ioo (-1 : k) 1 := by   refine StrictMono.orderIsoOfRightInverse ?_ ?_ (fun x ↦ x / (1 - |↑x|)) ?_   · refine codRestrict (fun x ↦ x / (1 + |x|)) _ fun x ↦ abs_lt.1 ?_     have H : 0 < 1 + |x| := (abs_nonneg x).trans_lt (lt_one_add _)     calc       |x / (1 + |x|)| = |x| / (1 + |x|) := by rw [abs_div, abs_of_pos H]       _ < 1 := (div_lt_one H).2 (lt_one_add _)   · refine (strictMono_of_odd_strictMonoOn_nonneg ?_ ?_).codRestrict _     · intro x       simp only [abs_neg, neg_div]     · rintro x (hx : 0 ≤ x) y (hy : 0 ≤ y) hxy       simp [abs_of_nonneg, mul_add, mul_comm x y, div_lt_div_iff, hx.trans_lt (lt_one_add _),         hy.trans_lt (lt_one_add _), *]   · refine fun x ↦ Subtype.ext ?_     have : 0 < 1 - |(x : k)| := sub_pos.2 (abs_lt.2 x.2)     field_simp [abs_div, this.ne', abs_of_pos this]
orderIsoIooNegOneOne.description: This definition asserts that in any linear ordered field, there exists an order isomorphism between the entire field and the open interval from negative one to one.

If `x`, `y`, `x'`, and `y'` are functions `Π i : ι, α i`, then
the set difference between the box `[x, y]` and the product of the open intervals `(x' i, y' i)`
is covered by the union of the following boxes: for each `i : ι`, we take
`[x, update y i (x' i)]` and `[update x i (y' i), y]`.

E.g., if `x' = x` and `y' = y`, then this lemma states that the difference between a closed box
`[x, y]` and the corresponding open box `{z | ∀ i, x i < z i < y i}` is covered by the union
of the faces of `[x, y]`.

Set.ordConnectedComponent.fullDefinition: def ordConnectedComponent (s : Set α) (x : α) : Set α :=   { y | [[x, y]] ⊆ s }
Set.ordConnectedComponent.description: This definition describes the order-connected component of a point in a set as the collection of points that, along with the point, form a closed interval within the set, and this component is empty if the point is not included in the set.

Set.ordSeparatingSet.comment:
Given two sets `s t : Set α`, the set `Set.orderSeparatingSet s t` is the set of points that
belong both to some `Set.ordConnectedComponent tᶜ x`, `x ∈ s`, and to some
`Set.ordConnectedComponent sᶜ x`, `x ∈ t`. In the case of two disjoint closed sets, this is the
union of all open intervals $(a, b)$ such that their endpoints belong to different sets.

explanatories.Set.ordConnectedComponent: This definition describes the order-connected component of a point in a set as the collection of points that, along with the point, form a closed interval within the set, and this component is empty if the point is not included in the set.

Set.ordSeparatingSet.fullDefinition: def ordSeparatingSet (s t : Set α) : Set α :=   (⋃ x ∈ s, ordConnectedComponent tᶜ x) ∩ ⋃ x ∈ t, ordConnectedComponent sᶜ x
Set.ordSeparatingSet.description: This definition describes a set consisting of points that lie in the order-connected components of the complements of two sets.

Set.ordSeparatingSet_comm.code:
Set.ordSeparatingSet_comm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] (s t : Set α) :
  s.ordSeparatingSet t = t.ordSeparatingSet s
Set.ordSeparatingSet_comm.description: The order-separating set of one set with respect to another is the same as the order-separating set of the second set with respect to the first.

explanatories.Set.ordSeparatingSet: This definition describes a set consisting of points that lie in the order-connected components of the complements of two sets.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_left_ordSeparatingSet.description: The set of points separating two disjoint sets is itself disjoint from the first set.

Set.disjoint_right_ordSeparatingSet.code:

explanatories.Set.ordSeparatingSet: This definition describes a set consisting of points that lie in the order-connected components of the complements of two sets.

Set.ordT5Nhd.comment:

explanatories.Set.ordConnectedComponent: This definition describes the order-connected component of a point in a set as the collection of points that, along with the point, form a closed interval within the set, and this component is empty if the point is not included in the set.
