some s, some t =>         if h : s.fst ≤ t.snd ∧ t.fst ≤ s.snd then           WithBot.some             ⟨⟨s.fst ⊔ t.fst, s.snd ⊓ t.snd⟩,               sup_le (le_inf s.fst_le_snd h.1) <| le_inf h.2 t.fst_le_snd⟩         else ⊥     inf_le_left := fun s t =>       match s, t with       | ⊥, ⊥ => bot_le       | ⊥, some _ => bot_le       | some s, ⊥ => bot_le       | some s, some t => by         change dite _ _ _ ≤ _         split_ifs         · exact WithBot.coe_le_coe.2 ⟨le_sup_left, inf_le_left⟩         · exact bot_le     inf_le_right := fun s t =>       match s, t with       | ⊥, ⊥ => bot_le       | ⊥, some t => bot_le       | some _, ⊥ => bot_le       | some s, some t => by         change dite _ _ _ ≤ _         split_ifs         · exact WithBot.coe_le_coe.2 ⟨le_sup_right, inf_le_right⟩         · exact bot_le     le_inf := fun s t c =>       match s, t, c with       | ⊥, t, c => fun _ _ => bot_le       | (s : NonemptyInterval α), t, c => fun hb hc => by         lift t to NonemptyInterval α using ne_bot_of_le_ne_bot WithBot.coe_ne_bot hb         lift c to NonemptyInterval α using ne_bot_of_le_ne_bot WithBot.coe_ne_bot hc         change _ ≤ dite _ _ _         simp only [WithBot.coe_le_coe] at hb hc ⊢         rw [dif_pos, WithBot.coe_le_coe]         · exact ⟨sup_le hb.1 hc.1, le_inf hb.2 hc.2⟩         -- Porting note: had to add the next 6 lines including the changes because         -- it seems that lean cannot automatically turn `NonemptyInterval.toDualProd s`         -- into `s.toProd` anymore.         rcases hb with ⟨hb₁, hb₂⟩         rcases hc with ⟨hc₁, hc₂⟩         change t.toProd.fst ≤ s.toProd.fst at hb₁         change s.toProd.snd ≤ t.toProd.snd at hb₂         change c.toProd.fst ≤ s.toProd.fst at hc₁         change s.toProd.snd ≤ c.toProd.snd at hc₂         -- Porting note: originally it just had `hb.1` etc. in this next line         exact ⟨hb₁.trans <| s.fst_le_snd.trans hc₂, hc₁.trans <| s.fst_le_snd.trans hb₂⟩ }

LocallyFiniteOrder.ofIcc'.fullDefinition: def LocallyFiniteOrder.ofIcc' (α : Type*) [Preorder α] [DecidableRel ((· ≤ ·) : α → α → Prop)]     (finsetIcc : α → α → Finset α) (mem_Icc : ∀ a b x, x ∈ finsetIcc a b ↔ a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b) :     LocallyFiniteOrder α :=   { finsetIcc     finsetIco := fun a b => (finsetIcc a b).filter fun x => ¬b ≤ x     finsetIoc := fun a b => (finsetIcc a b).filter fun x => ¬x ≤ a     finsetIoo := fun a b => (finsetIcc a b).filter fun x => ¬x ≤ a ∧ ¬b ≤ x     finset_mem_Icc := mem_Icc     finset_mem_Ico := fun a b x => by rw [Finset.mem_filter, mem_Icc, and_assoc, lt_iff_le_not_le]     finset_mem_Ioc := fun a b x => by       rw [Finset.mem_filter, mem_Icc, and_right_comm, lt_iff_le_not_le]     finset_mem_Ioo := fun a b x => by       rw [Finset.mem_filter, mem_Icc, and_and_and_comm, lt_iff_le_not_le, lt_iff_le_not_le] }

Finset.uIcc.comment:
`Finset.uIcc a b` is the set of elements lying between `a` and `b`, with `a` and `b` included.
Note that we define it more generally in a lattice as `Finset.Icc (a ⊓ b) (a ⊔ b)`. In a
product type, `Finset.uIcc` corresponds to the bounding box of the two elements.

OrderEmbedding.locallyFiniteOrder.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def OrderEmbedding.locallyFiniteOrder [LocallyFiniteOrder β] (f : α ↪o β) :     LocallyFiniteOrder α where   finsetIcc a b := (Icc (f a) (f b)).preimage f f.toEmbedding.injective.injOn   finsetIco a b := (Ico (f a) (f b)).preimage f f.toEmbedding.injective.injOn   finsetIoc a b := (Ioc (f a) (f b)).preimage f f.toEmbedding.injective.injOn   finsetIoo a b := (Ioo (f a) (f b)).preimage f f.toEmbedding.injective.injOn   finset_mem_Icc a b x := by rw [mem_preimage, mem_Icc, f.le_iff_le, f.le_iff_le]   finset_mem_Ico a b x := by rw [mem_preimage, mem_Ico, f.le_iff_le, f.lt_iff_lt]   finset_mem_Ioc a b x := by rw [mem_preimage, mem_Ioc, f.lt_iff_lt, f.le_iff_le]   finset_mem_Ioo a b x := by rw [mem_preimage, mem_Ioo, f.lt_iff_lt, f.lt_iff_lt]

Finset.mem_uIcc_of_le.code:

Finset.mem_uIcc_of_ge.code:

Finset.uIcc_subset_Icc.description: The theorem states that if two elements are within a closed interval defined by two other elements in a locally finite ordered structure, then the set containing those two elements is a subset of the same closed interval.

Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_mem.code:
Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_mem.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Lattice α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] {a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : α} :

Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_mem.description: The theorem characterizes the subset relation of closed intervals in a locally finite ordered structure, stating that one closed interval is a subset of another if and only if both endpoints of the first interval belong to the second interval.

Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le'.code:
Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Lattice α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] {a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : α} :
  [[a₁, b₁]] ⊆ [[a₂, b₂]] ↔ a₂ ⊓ b₂ ≤ a₁ ⊓ b₁ ∧ a₁ ⊔ b₁ ≤ a₂ ⊔ b₂
Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_iff_le'.description: The theorem expresses that one interval is a subset of another in a locally finite ordered structure if and only if the infimum of the endpoints of the first interval is less than or equal to the infimum of the second interval and the supremum of the first interval is greater than or equal to the supremum of the second interval.

Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_right.code:

Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_left.code:

Finset.uIcc_subset_uIcc_left.description: The theorem states that if a value is within a closed interval defined by two other values in a locally finite ordered structure, then the smaller closed interval defined by the first two values and this value is a subset of the larger closed interval.

transGen_covBy_of_lt.code:

transGen_covBy_of_lt.description: The theorem establishes that if one element is strictly less than another in a locally finite ordered structure, then there is a transitive relation connecting them through a sequence of elements that are less than the successive ones.

le_iff_reflTransGen_covBy.description: The theorem asserts that in a locally finite partial order, one element is less than or equal to another if and only if the first element is related to the second through a sequence of strictly less than relations.

lt_iff_transGen_covBy.code:

monotone_iff_forall_covBy.description: The theorem establishes that a function defined on a locally finite partial order is monotone if and only if it maintains the order when applied to pairs of elements for which one is covered by the other.

strictMono_iff_forall_covBy.code:

Directed.code: Directed.{u, w} {α : Type u} {ι : Sort w} (r : α → α → Prop) (f : ι → α) : Prop
Directed.comment:
A family of elements of α is directed (with respect to a relation `≼` on α)
if there is a member of the family `≼`-above any pair in the family.
Directed.fullDefinition: def Directed (f : ι → α) :=   ∀ x y, ∃ z, f x ≼ f z ∧ f y ≼ f z
Directed.description: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.

DirectedOn.code: DirectedOn.{u} {α : Type u} (r : α → α → Prop) (s : Set α) : Prop
DirectedOn.comment:
A subset of α is directed if there is an element of the set `≼`-above any
pair of elements in the set.

tacticBddDefault.comment:
Sets are automatically bounded or cobounded in complete lattices. To use the same statements
in complete and conditionally complete lattices but let automation fill automatically the
boundedness proofs in complete lattices, we use the tactic `bddDefault` in the statements,
in the form `(hA : BddAbove A := by bddDefault)`.

ScottContinuous.comment:
A function between preorders is said to be Scott continuous if it preserves `IsLUB` on directed
sets. It can be shown that a function is Scott continuous if and only if it is continuous wrt the
Scott topology.

The dual notion

```lean
∀ ⦃d : Set α⦄, d.Nonempty → DirectedOn (· ≥ ·) d → ∀ ⦃a⦄, IsGLB d a → IsGLB (f '' d) (f a)
```

does not appear to play a significant role in the literature, so is omitted here.

explanatories.IsLUB: This definition characterizes an element as the least upper bound of a set if it is an upper bound for the set and no other upper bound is smaller than it within a preorder structure.
explanatories.DirectedOn: A subset of elements is directed if there exists an element within the set that is greater than or equal to every pair of elements in that set.

ScottContinuous.fullDefinition: def ScottContinuous (f : α → β) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃d : Set α⦄, d.Nonempty → DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) d → ∀ ⦃a⦄, IsLUB d a → IsLUB (f '' d) (f a)
ScottContinuous.description: A function between preorders is defined as Scott continuous if it preserves the least upper bounds of directed sets.

completeLatticeOfInf.fullDefinition: def completeLatticeOfInf (α : Type*) [H1 : PartialOrder α] [H2 : InfSet α]     (isGLB_sInf : ∀ s : Set α, IsGLB s (sInf s)) : CompleteLattice α where   __ := H1; __ := H2   bot := sInf univ   bot_le x := (isGLB_sInf univ).1 trivial   top := sInf ∅   le_top a := (isGLB_sInf ∅).2 <| by simp   sup a b := sInf { x : α | a ≤ x ∧ b ≤ x }   inf a b := sInf {a, b}   le_inf a b c hab hac := by     apply (isGLB_sInf _).2     simp [*]   inf_le_right a b := (isGLB_sInf _).1 <| mem_insert_of_mem _ <| mem_singleton _   inf_le_left a b := (isGLB_sInf _).1 <| mem_insert _ _   sup_le a b c hac hbc := (isGLB_sInf _).1 <| by simp [*]   le_sup_left a b := (isGLB_sInf _).2 fun x => And.left   le_sup_right a b := (isGLB_sInf _).2 fun x => And.right   le_sInf s a ha := (isGLB_sInf s).2 ha   sInf_le s a ha := (isGLB_sInf s).1 ha   sSup s := sInf (upperBounds s)   le_sSup s a ha := (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds s)).2 fun b hb => hb ha   sSup_le s a ha := (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds s)).1 ha

poor definitional equalities.  If other fields are known explicitly, they should be
provided; for example, if `inf` is known explicitly, construct the `CompleteLattice`
instance as
```
instance : CompleteLattice my_T where
  inf := better_inf
  le_inf := ...
  inf_le_right := ...
  inf_le_left := ...
  -- don't care to fix sup, sInf, bot, top
  __ := completeLatticeOfSup my_T _
```

iSup_const_mono.{u_1, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {ι' : Sort u_6} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α} (h : ι → ι') :
  ⨆ x, a ≤ ⨆ x, a
iSup_const_mono.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a constant element is greater than or equal to that constant element in a complete lattice.

iInf_const_mono.code:
iInf_const_mono.{u_1, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {ι' : Sort u_6} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α} (h : ι' → ι) :
  ⨅ x, a ≤ ⨅ x, a
iInf_const_mono.description: This theorem establishes that under a complete lattice, the infimum of a constant function over an indexed family of elements is equal to the constant itself.

iSup_iInf_le_iInf_iSup.code:
iSup_iInf_le_iInf_iSup.{u_1, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {ι' : Sort u_6} [CompleteLattice α]
  (f : ι → ι' → α) : ⨆ i, ⨅ j, f i j ≤ ⨅ j, ⨆ i, f i j
iSup_iInf_le_iInf_iSup.description: This theorem states that the supremum of the infimums of a two-variable function is less than or equal to the infimum of the supremums of the same function in a complete lattice.

biSup_mono.code:
biSup_mono.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α} {p q : ι → Prop}
  (hpq : ∀ (i : ι), p i → q i) : ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : p i), f i ≤ ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : q i), f i
biSup_mono.description: This theorem demonstrates that if a property holds for certain indices, then the supremum of the function evaluated over those indices is less than or equal to the supremum evaluated over indices satisfying a different property.

biInf_mono.code:
biInf_mono.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α} {p q : ι → Prop}
  (hpq : ∀ (i : ι), p i → q i) : ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : q i), f i ≤ ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : p i), f i
biInf_mono.description: This theorem asserts that if one property implies another for all indices, then the infimum of a function evaluated at points satisfying the second property is less than or equal to the infimum of the function evaluated at points satisfying the first property.

iSup_le_iff.code:
iSup_le_iff.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  iSup f ≤ a ↔ ∀ (i : ι), f i ≤ a
iSup_le_iff.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function over a set of indices is less than or equal to a certain value if and only if each value of the function at those indices is less than or equal to that same value.

le_iInf_iff.code:
le_iInf_iff.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  a ≤ iInf f ↔ ∀ (i : ι), a ≤ f i
le_iInf_iff.description: This theorem states that a certain value is less than or equal to the infimum of a family of functions if and only if it is less than or equal to each individual function in that family.

iSup₂_le_iff.code:
iSup₂_le_iff.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α}
  {f : (i : ι) → κ i → α} : ⨆ i, ⨆ j, f i j ≤ a ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), f i j ≤ a
iSup₂_le_iff.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function taken over two indices is less than or equal to a certain value if and only if the function evaluated at each pair of indices is less than or equal to that value for all pairs.

le_iInf₂_iff.code:
le_iInf₂_iff.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α}
  {f : (i : ι) → κ i → α} : a ≤ ⨅ i, ⨅ j, f i j ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), a ≤ f i j
le_iInf₂_iff.description: This theorem establishes that an element is less than or equal to the infimum of a nested family of functions if and only if it is less than or equal to each of those function values for all pairs of indices from specified sets in a complete lattice.

iSup_lt_iff.code:
iSup_lt_iff.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  iSup f < a ↔ ∃ b < a, ∀ (i : ι), f i ≤ b
iSup_lt_iff.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of a function is less than a certain value if and only if there exists a value lower than that, such that all function outputs are less than or equal to it.

lt_iInf_iff.code:
lt_iInf_iff.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  a < iInf f ↔ ∃ b, a < b ∧ ∀ (i : ι), b ≤ f i
lt_iInf_iff.description: This theorem establishes that an element is less than the infimum of a family of elements if and only if there exists an upper bound that is greater than the element and is less than or equal to every element of the family.

sSup_eq_iSup.code: sSup_eq_iSup.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {s : Set α} : sSup s = ⨆ a ∈ s, a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

sSup_eq_iSup.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of a set in a complete lattice is equal to the supremum of its elements.

sInf_eq_iInf.code: sInf_eq_iInf.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {s : Set α} : sInf s = ⨅ a ∈ s, a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

sInf_eq_iInf.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a set in a complete lattice is equal to the greatest lower bound of its elements.

Monotone.le_map_iSup.code:
Monotone.le_map_iSup.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {s : ι → α}
  [CompleteLattice β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : ⨆ i, f (s i) ≤ f (iSup s)
Monotone.le_map_iSup.description: This theorem states that if a function is monotonic, then the supremum of the function applied to a set of elements is less than or equal to the function applied to the supremum of those elements.

Antitone.le_map_iInf.code:
Antitone.le_map_iInf.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {s : ι → α}
  [CompleteLattice β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : ⨆ i, f (s i) ≤ f (iInf s)
Antitone.le_map_iInf.description: This theorem asserts that for an antitone function, the supremum of the images of a set under the function is less than or equal to the image of the infimum of the set.

Monotone.le_map_iSup₂.description: This theorem asserts that for a monotone function, the supremum of the images of pairs from a function is less than or equal to the image of the supremum of those pairs.

Antitone.le_map_iInf₂.description: This theorem states that if a function is antitone and maps values from a complete lattice to another complete lattice, then the supremum of the function evaluated at a collection of inputs is less than or equal to the function evaluated at the infimum of those inputs.

Monotone.le_map_sSup.code:
Monotone.le_map_sSup.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] {s : Set α}
  {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : ⨆ a ∈ s, f a ≤ f (sSup s)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Monotone.le_map_sSup.description: This theorem states that if a function is monotonic, then the supremum of the function evaluated over a set is less than or equal to the function evaluated at the supremum of that set.

Antitone.le_map_sInf.code:
Antitone.le_map_sInf.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] {s : Set α}
  {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : ⨆ a ∈ s, f a ≤ f (sInf s)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Antitone.le_map_sInf.description: This theorem states that if a function is antitone, then the supremum of its values over a set is less than or equal to the value of that function at the infimum of the set in complete lattices.

OrderIso.map_iSup.code:
OrderIso.map_iSup.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β]
  (f : α ≃o β) (x : ι → α) : f (⨆ i, x i) = ⨆ i, f (x i)
OrderIso.map_iSup.description: This theorem states that an order isomorphism preserves the supremum of a set of elements when mapping from one complete lattice to another.

OrderIso.map_iInf.code:
OrderIso.map_iInf.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β]
  (f : α ≃o β) (x : ι → α) : f (⨅ i, x i) = ⨅ i, f (x i)
OrderIso.map_iInf.description: This theorem asserts that an order isomorphism preserves the infimum of a family of elements, meaning the infimum of a transformed set equals the transformed infimum in complete lattices.

OrderIso.map_sSup.code:
OrderIso.map_sSup.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] (f : α ≃o β)
  (s : Set α) : f (sSup s) = ⨆ a ∈ s, f a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

OrderIso.map_sSup.description: This theorem establishes that an order isomorphism preserves the supremum of a set by stating that the image of the supremum under the isomorphism is equal to the supremum of the images of the elements in that set.

OrderIso.map_sInf.code:
OrderIso.map_sInf.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] (f : α ≃o β)
  (s : Set α) : f (sInf s) = ⨅ a ∈ s, f a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

OrderIso.map_sInf.description: This theorem asserts that when there is an order isomorphism between two complete lattices, the image under this isomorphism of the infimum of a set in one lattice equals the infimum of the images of the set's elements in the other lattice.

iSup_comp_le.code:
iSup_comp_le.{u_1, u_5, u_9} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {ι' : Sort u_9} (f : ι' → α)
  (g : ι → ι') : ⨆ x, f (g x) ≤ ⨆ y, f y
iSup_comp_le.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function composed with another function over one index set is less than or equal to the supremum of the original function over the larger index set.

le_iInf_comp.code:
le_iInf_comp.{u_1, u_5, u_9} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {ι' : Sort u_9} (f : ι' → α)
  (g : ι → ι') : ⨅ y, f y ≤ ⨅ x, f (g x)
le_iInf_comp.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a family of elements is less than or equal to the infimum of the transformed family obtained by applying a function to the indexing set.

Monotone.iSup_comp_eq.code:
Monotone.iSup_comp_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [Preorder β]
  {f : β → α} (hf : Monotone f) {s : ι → β} (hs : ∀ (x : β), ∃ i, x ≤ s i) : ⨆ x, f (s x) = ⨆ y, f y
Monotone.iSup_comp_eq.description: This theorem demonstrates that the supremum of a function composed with another function from a preordered set is equal to the supremum of the original function when the composing function is monotone and every element in the codomain is less than or equal to at least one element in the domain.

Monotone.iInf_comp_eq.code:
Monotone.iInf_comp_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [Preorder β]
  {f : β → α} (hf : Monotone f) {s : ι → β} (hs : ∀ (x : β), ∃ i, s i ≤ x) : ⨅ x, f (s x) = ⨅ y, f y
Monotone.iInf_comp_eq.description: This theorem asserts that for a monotone function, the infimum of the function evaluated at a sequence that is bounded below is equal to the infimum of the function over the range of that sequence in a complete lattice.

Antitone.map_iSup_le.code:
Antitone.map_iSup_le.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {s : ι → α}
  [CompleteLattice β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : f (iSup s) ≤ ⨅ i, f (s i)
Antitone.map_iSup_le.description: This theorem states that for an antitone function, the image of the supremum of a family of elements is less than or equal to the infimum of the images of those elements.

Monotone.map_iInf_le.code:
Monotone.map_iInf_le.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {s : ι → α}
  [CompleteLattice β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : f (iInf s) ≤ ⨅ i, f (s i)
Monotone.map_iInf_le.description: This theorem indicates that if a function is monotone, then the value of that function at the infimum of a set is less than or equal to the infimum of the function applied to the elements of that set.

explanatories.OrderIso.map_iSup: This theorem states that an order isomorphism preserves the supremum of a set of elements when mapping from one complete lattice to another.

Antitone.map_iSup₂_le.description: This theorem asserts that if a function is antitone and it is applied to the supremum of a double-indexed family of elements, then the result is less than or equal to the infimum of the function applied to each of those elements in a complete lattice.

explanatories.OrderIso.map_iInf: This theorem asserts that an order isomorphism preserves the infimum of a family of elements, meaning the infimum of a transformed set equals the transformed infimum in complete lattices.

Monotone.map_iInf₂_le.description: This theorem states that if a function is monotone and is applied to a double infimum of a set of indexed elements, then the result is less than or equal to the infimum of the function applied to the double set of those elements.

Antitone.map_sSup_le.code:
Antitone.map_sSup_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] {s : Set α}
  {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : f (sSup s) ≤ ⨅ a ∈ s, f a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Antitone.map_sSup_le.description: This theorem states that if a function is antitone, then the image of the supremum of a set is less than or equal to the infimum of the images of the elements in that set within complete lattices.

Monotone.map_sInf_le.code:
Monotone.map_sInf_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] {s : Set α}
  {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : f (sInf s) ≤ ⨅ a ∈ s, f a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Monotone.map_sInf_le.description: This theorem states that for a monotone function between complete lattices, the image of the infimum of a set is less than or equal to the infimum of the images of that set's elements.

iSup_const_le.code: iSup_const_le.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α} : ⨆ x, a ≤ a
iSup_const_le.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a constant element is always less than or equal to that element itself in a complete lattice.

le_iInf_const.code: le_iInf_const.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α} : a ≤ ⨅ x, a
le_iInf_const.description: This theorem states that any element is less than or equal to the infimum of a constant value across all indices in a complete lattice.

iSup_const.code: iSup_const.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α} [Nonempty ι] : ⨆ x, a = a

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

iSup_const.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a constant value over a non-empty index set in a complete lattice is equal to that constant value.

iInf_const.code: iInf_const.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {a : α} [Nonempty ι] : ⨅ x, a = a

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

iInf_const.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a constant function over a nonempty index set in a complete lattice is equal to the constant value itself.

iSup_bot.code: iSup_bot.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] : ⨆ x, ⊥ = ⊥
iSup_bot.description: This theorem states that the supremum of an empty set in a complete lattice is defined to be the least element of the lattice.

iInf_top.code: iInf_top.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] : ⨅ x, ⊤ = ⊤
iInf_top.description: This theorem states that the infimum of all elements in a complete lattice is equal to the top element of that lattice.

iSup_eq_bot.code: iSup_eq_bot.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {s : ι → α} : iSup s = ⊥ ↔ ∀ (i : ι), s i = ⊥
iSup_eq_bot.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a set of indexed values is equal to the minimum element if and only if every indexed value in the set is equal to that minimum element.

iInf_eq_top.code: iInf_eq_top.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {s : ι → α} : iInf s = ⊤ ↔ ∀ (i : ι), s i = ⊤
iInf_eq_top.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function equals the top element if and only if the function takes the top value for every input.

iSup₂_eq_bot.code:
iSup₂_eq_bot.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} [CompleteLattice α]
  {f : (i : ι) → κ i → α} : ⨆ i, ⨆ j, f i j = ⊥ ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), f i j = ⊥
iSup₂_eq_bot.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a double indexed function equals the bottom element if and only if every individual function value is equal to the bottom element.

iInf₂_eq_top.code:
iInf₂_eq_top.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} [CompleteLattice α]
  {f : (i : ι) → κ i → α} : ⨅ i, ⨅ j, f i j = ⊤ ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), f i j = ⊤
iInf₂_eq_top.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a family of elements is equal to the top element if and only if every element in that family is equal to the top element in a complete lattice.

iSup_pos.code: iSup_pos.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} {f : p → α} (hp : p) : ⨆ (h : p), f h = f hp
iSup_pos.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function over a proposition is equal to the function's value at a specific instance of that proposition.

iInf_pos.code: iInf_pos.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} {f : p → α} (hp : p) : ⨅ (h : p), f h = f hp
iInf_pos.description: This theorem asserts that in a complete lattice, the infimum of a function over a proposition is equal to the function's value at the specific proof of that proposition.

iSup_neg.code: iSup_neg.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} {f : p → α} (hp : ¬p) : ⨆ (h : p), f h = ⊥
iSup_neg.description: This theorem states that if a proposition is false, then the supremum of a function defined on that proposition yields the bottom element in a complete lattice.

iInf_neg.code: iInf_neg.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} {f : p → α} (hp : ¬p) : ⨅ (h : p), f h = ⊤
iInf_neg.description: This theorem states that if a proposition is false, the infimum of a function defined on that proposition is equal to the top element of the complete lattice.

iSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists.code:
iSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {b : α}
  {f : ι → α} (h₁ : ∀ (i : ι), f i ≤ b) (h₂ : ∀ w < b, ∃ i, w < f i) : ⨆ i, f i = b
iSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists.comment:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the supremum of `f`: it suffices to check that `b`
is larger than `f i` for all `i`, and that this is not the case of any `w<b`.
See `ciSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt` for a version in conditionally complete
lattices.
iSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists.description: This theorem states that a value is the supremum of a function across a set of indices if it is greater than or equal to all function values and any value less than it has a corresponding function value that exceeds it.

iInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists.code:
iInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → α}
  {b : α} : (∀ (i : ι), b ≤ f i) → (∀ (w : α), b < w → ∃ i, f i < w) → ⨅ i, f i = b
iInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists.comment:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the infimum of `f`: it suffices to check that `b`
is smaller than `f i` for all `i`, and that this is not the case of any `w>b`.
See `ciInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt` for a version in conditionally complete
lattices.
iInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists.description: This theorem establishes that a value is the infimum of a family of elements if it is less than or equal to all of them and if any value greater than it has at least one element in the family that is less than that value, within the context of a complete lattice.

iSup_eq_dif.code:
iSup_eq_dif.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} [Decidable p] (a : p → α) :
  ⨆ (h : p), a h = if h : p then a h else ⊥
iSup_eq_dif.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function defined on a proposition is equal to the value of that function when the proposition is true, or to a minimum element when it is false.

iSup_eq_if.code: iSup_eq_if.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} [Decidable p] (a : α) : ⨆ (_ : p), a = if p then a else ⊥
iSup_eq_if.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a constant element over a proposition, when the proposition is decidable, equals that element if the proposition holds and the bottom element otherwise.

iInf_eq_dif.code:
iInf_eq_dif.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} [Decidable p] (a : p → α) :
  ⨅ (h : p), a h = if h : p then a h else ⊤
iInf_eq_dif.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a complete lattice, the infimum of a function defined on a proposition is equal to the value of that function when the proposition holds, or to the top element of the lattice when it does not.

iInf_eq_if.code: iInf_eq_if.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p : Prop} [Decidable p] (a : α) : ⨅ (_ : p), a = if p then a else ⊤
iInf_eq_if.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a collection of elements is equal to a given element when a specific condition is true, and is equal to the top element when the condition is false in a complete lattice.

iSup_comm.code:
iSup_comm.{u_1, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {ι' : Sort u_6} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → ι' → α} :
  ⨆ i, ⨆ j, f i j = ⨆ j, ⨆ i, f i j
iSup_comm.description: This theorem states that the supremum computed by first varying over one index and then another is equal to the supremum obtained by reversing the order of the indices in a complete lattice.

iInf_comm.code:
iInf_comm.{u_1, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} {ι' : Sort u_6} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ι → ι' → α} :
  ⨅ i, ⨅ j, f i j = ⨅ j, ⨅ i, f i j
iInf_comm.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated over two indices can be computed in any order of the indices within a complete lattice.

iSup₂_comm.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of a function over multiple indexed variables remains the same regardless of the order in which the indices are taken.

iInf₂_comm.description: This theorem establishes that the infimum of a function over multiple indexed variables is invariant under the reordering of the indices involved.

iSup_iSup_eq_left.code:
iSup_iSup_eq_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {b : β} {f : (x : β) → x = b → α} :
  ⨆ x, ⨆ (h : x = b), f x h = f b ⋯
iSup_iSup_eq_left.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function evaluated at all elements in a set, conditioned on those elements being equal to a specific element, is equal to the direct evaluation of that function at that specific element.

iInf_iInf_eq_left.code:
iInf_iInf_eq_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {b : β} {f : (x : β) → x = b → α} :
  ⨅ x, ⨅ (h : x = b), f x h = f b ⋯
iInf_iInf_eq_left.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a complete lattice, taking the infimum first over a variable and then over the condition that this variable equals a specific element results in the same value as directly applying the function to that specific element.

iSup_iSup_eq_right.code:
iSup_iSup_eq_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {b : β} {f : (x : β) → b = x → α} :
  ⨆ x, ⨆ (h : b = x), f x h = f b ⋯
iSup_iSup_eq_right.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function evaluated over all elements equal to a given value is equal to the function evaluated at that value in a complete lattice.

iInf_iInf_eq_right.code:
iInf_iInf_eq_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {b : β} {f : (x : β) → b = x → α} :
  ⨅ x, ⨅ (h : b = x), f x h = f b ⋯
iInf_iInf_eq_right.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of the infimum values of a function is equal to the function's value at a specific element when that element is treated as a variable.

iSup_subtype.code:
iSup_subtype.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : Subtype p → α} :
  iSup f = ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f ⟨i, h⟩
iSup_subtype.description: This theorem demonstrates that the supremum of a function defined on a subtype can be expressed as the supremum of the supremum of the function evaluated at each index fulfilling a specific property.

iInf_subtype.code:
iInf_subtype.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : Subtype p → α} :
  iInf f = ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f ⟨i, h⟩
iInf_subtype.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function over a subtype can be expressed as the infimum taken over all elements of the base set and their corresponding values in the function.

iSup_subtype'.code:
iSup_subtype'.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : (i : ι) → p i → α} :
  ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f i h = ⨆ x, f ↑x ⋯
iSup_subtype'.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function defined on a subtype, indexed by a predicate, is equal to the supremum of the original function considered over the index set by the elements satisfying that predicate.

iInf_subtype'.code:
iInf_subtype'.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : (i : ι) → p i → α} :
  ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f i h = ⨅ x, f ↑x ⋯
iInf_subtype'.description: This theorem establishes an equality between the infimum of a family of values indexed by a property and the infimum of the corresponding function values over all instances satisfying that property within a complete lattice.

iSup_subtype''.code:
iSup_subtype''.{u_1, u_9} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {ι : Type u_9} (s : Set ι) (f : ι → α) :
  ⨆ i, f ↑i = ⨆ t ∈ s, f t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iSup_subtype''.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of a function over a subtype is equal to the supremum of that function evaluated over elements belonging to the set defining the subtype.

iInf_subtype''.code:
iInf_subtype''.{u_1, u_9} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {ι : Type u_9} (s : Set ι) (f : ι → α) :
  ⨅ i, f ↑i = ⨅ t ∈ s, f t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iInf_subtype''.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated over all elements in a subtype is equal to the infimum of the same function evaluated over a specified subset of those elements.

biSup_const.code:
biSup_const.{u_1, u_9} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {ι : Type u_9} {a : α} {s : Set ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) :
  ⨆ i ∈ s, a = a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

biSup_const.description: This theorem concludes that the supremum of a constant value over a non-empty set is equal to that constant value itself.

biInf_const.code:
biInf_const.{u_1, u_9} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {ι : Type u_9} {a : α} {s : Set ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) :
  ⨅ i ∈ s, a = a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

biInf_const.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a constant value over a non-empty set is equal to that constant value itself in a complete lattice.

iSup_sup_eq.code:
iSup_sup_eq.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f g : ι → α} :
  ⨆ x, f x ⊔ g x = (⨆ x, f x) ⊔ ⨆ x, g x
iSup_sup_eq.description: This theorem states that the supremum of the pointwise maximum of two functions is equal to the maximum of their individual suprema.

iInf_inf_eq.code:
iInf_inf_eq.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {f g : ι → α} :
  ⨅ x, f x ⊓ g x = (⨅ x, f x) ⊓ ⨅ x, g x
iInf_inf_eq.description: This theorem states that the infimum of the infimums of two functions evaluated at the same index is equal to the infimum of the pointwise infimums of those functions.

Equiv.biSup_comp.code:
Equiv.biSup_comp.{u_1, u_9, u_10} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {ι : Type u_9} {ι' : Type u_10} {g : ι' → α}
  (e : ι ≃ ι') (s : Set ι') : ⨆ i ∈ ⇑e.symm '' s, g (e i) = ⨆ i ∈ s, g i

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.

Equiv.biSup_comp.description: This theorem demonstrates that the supremum of a function over the preimage of a set under an equivalence relation is equal to the supremum of the function over the original set in a complete lattice.

biInf_le.code:
biInf_le.{u_1, u_9} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {ι : Type u_9} {s : Set ι} (f : ι → α) {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) :
  ⨅ i ∈ s, f i ≤ f i

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

biInf_le.description: This theorem states that for any function defined on a set, the infimum of the function over that set is less than or equal to the value of the function at any specific point within the set.

iSup_sup.code:
iSup_sup.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  (⨆ x, f x) ⊔ a = ⨆ x, f x ⊔ a

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

iSup_sup.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function combined with an additional element in a complete lattice equals the supremum of the same function combined with that element.

iInf_inf.code:
iInf_inf.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  (⨅ x, f x) ⊓ a = ⨅ x, f x ⊓ a

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

iInf_inf.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a collection of elements, when intersected with another element, is equal to the intersection of the infimum of the collection and that element in a complete lattice.

sup_iSup.code:
sup_iSup.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  a ⊔ ⨆ x, f x = ⨆ x, a ⊔ f x

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

sup_iSup.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function added to a constant value is equal to the supremum of the sums of that constant value and each value of the function over a nonempty index set in a complete lattice.

inf_iInf.code:
inf_iInf.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → α} {a : α} :
  a ⊓ ⨅ x, f x = ⨅ x, a ⊓ f x

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

inf_iInf.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a set formed by taking the infimum of a function and intersecting it with a fixed element is equal to the infimum of the individual intersections of that element with each function value.

biSup_sup.code:
biSup_sup.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : (i : ι) → p i → α} {a : α}
  (h : ∃ i, p i) : (⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f i h) ⊔ a = ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f i h ⊔ a
biSup_sup.description: This theorem states that for a complete lattice, the supremum of a compound expression involving an additional element is equal to the supremum of that same expression combined with the element.

sup_biSup.code:
sup_biSup.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : (i : ι) → p i → α} {a : α}
  (h : ∃ i, p i) : a ⊔ ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f i h = ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), a ⊔ f i h
sup_biSup.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of the supremums taken over a predicate and a function, intersected with a fixed element, is equal to the supremum of the supremums of those functions with the fixed element incorporated at each step.

biInf_inf.code:
biInf_inf.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : (i : ι) → p i → α} {a : α}
  (h : ∃ i, p i) : (⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f i h) ⊓ a = ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f i h ⊓ a
biInf_inf.description: This theorem establishes that if there exists an index in a given family of propositions, then the infimum of the infima of a function associated with those propositions combined with a certain element equals the infimum of the same infima combined with that element in a complete lattice.

inf_biInf.code:
inf_biInf.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : (i : ι) → p i → α} {a : α}
  (h : ∃ i, p i) : a ⊓ ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f i h = ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), a ⊓ f i h
inf_biInf.description: This theorem states that the infimum of an element with the infimum of a function, restricted to a property, is equal to the infimum of the element combined with the function's values over that property in a complete lattice.

iSup_false.code: iSup_false.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {s : False → α} : iSup s = ⊥
iSup_false.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function that outputs values based on an impossible condition is equal to the bottom element of a complete lattice.

iInf_false.code: iInf_false.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {s : False → α} : iInf s = ⊤
iInf_false.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function defined on a false proposition in a complete lattice is the greatest element of that lattice.

iSup_true.code: iSup_true.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {s : True → α} : iSup s = s trivial

explanatories.trivial: This theorem provides a proof that a trivial proposition affirming the truth of the statement "True" is indeed true.

iSup_true.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function defined for a true proposition in a complete lattice is equal to the value of that function at the single true instance.

iInf_true.code: iInf_true.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {s : True → α} : iInf s = s trivial

explanatories.trivial: This theorem provides a proof that a trivial proposition affirming the truth of the statement "True" is indeed true.

iInf_true.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the infimum of a function defined for a true proposition is equal to the value of that function at the proof of that proposition.

iSup_exists.code:
iSup_exists.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : Exists p → α} :
  ⨆ (x : Exists p), f x = ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f ⋯
iSup_exists.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function defined on the existences of a property is equal to the supremum taken over the indices satisfying that property, within a complete lattice framework.

iInf_exists.code:
iInf_exists.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {p : ι → Prop} {f : Exists p → α} :
  ⨅ (x : Exists p), f x = ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f ⋯
iInf_exists.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the infimum of a function over a set of existing elements is equal to the infimum of that function when taken over the indices satisfying a given property.

iSup_and.code: iSup_and.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p q : Prop} {s : p ∧ q → α} : iSup s = ⨆ (h₁ : p), ⨆ (h₂ : q), s ⋯
iSup_and.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of a function defined over the conjunction of two properties is equal to the supremum taken first over one property and then over the other.

iInf_and.code: iInf_and.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p q : Prop} {s : p ∧ q → α} : iInf s = ⨅ (h₁ : p), ⨅ (h₂ : q), s ⋯
iInf_and.description: This theorem shows that the infimum of a function defined on the conjunction of two propositions can be expressed as the infimum of the function evaluated separately on each proposition in a complete lattice.

iSup_and'.code:
iSup_and'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p q : Prop} {s : p → q → α} :
  ⨆ (h₁ : p), ⨆ (h₂ : q), s h₁ h₂ = ⨆ (h : p ∧ q), s ⋯ ⋯
iSup_and'.comment: The symmetric case of `iSup_and`, useful for rewriting into a supremum over a conjunction
iSup_and'.description: This theorem shows that the supremum of a function over two propositions can be expressed as the supremum of the same function when evaluated over the conjunction of those propositions.

iInf_and'.code:
iInf_and'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p q : Prop} {s : p → q → α} :
  ⨅ (h₁ : p), ⨅ (h₂ : q), s h₁ h₂ = ⨅ (h : p ∧ q), s ⋯ ⋯
iInf_and'.comment: The symmetric case of `iInf_and`, useful for rewriting into an infimum over a conjunction
iInf_and'.description: This theorem demonstrates a way to express the infimum over two separate propositions as an infimum over their conjunction in a complete lattice.

iSup_or.code:
iSup_or.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p q : Prop} {s : p ∨ q → α} :
  ⨆ (x : p ∨ q), s x = (⨆ (i : p), s ⋯) ⊔ ⨆ (j : q), s ⋯
iSup_or.description: This theorem expresses that the supremum over a disjunction of two propositions is equal to the supremum of the individual supremums taken over each proposition.

iInf_or.code:
iInf_or.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {p q : Prop} {s : p ∨ q → α} :
  ⨅ (x : p ∨ q), s x = (⨅ (i : p), s ⋯) ⊓ ⨅ (j : q), s ⋯
iInf_or.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a function defined on a disjunction of propositions is equal to the infimum of the function restricted to each propositional case, combined with the greatest lower bound of these infima.

iSup_dite.code:
iSup_dite.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
  (f : (i : ι) → p i → α) (g : (i : ι) → ¬p i → α) :
  (⨆ i, if h : p i then f i h else g i h) = (⨆ i, ⨆ (h : p i), f i h) ⊔ ⨆ i, ⨆ (h : ¬p i), g i h

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

iSup_dite.description: This theorem expresses that the supremum of a piecewise function, defined by two different cases based on a property, can be rewritten as the join of the supremum of each case evaluated over the respective conditions.

iInf_dite.code:
iInf_dite.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
  (f : (i : ι) → p i → α) (g : (i : ι) → ¬p i → α) :
  (⨅ i, if h : p i then f i h else g i h) = (⨅ i, ⨅ (h : p i), f i h) ⊓ ⨅ i, ⨅ (h : ¬p i), g i h

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

iInf_dite.description: This theorem shows that the infimum of a function determined by a property and its negation can be expressed as the infimum of the respective parts for each case combined with their greatest lower bound.

iSup_ite.code:
iSup_ite.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f g : ι → α) :
  (⨆ i, if p i then f i else g i) = (⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : p i), f i) ⊔ ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : ¬p i), g i

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

iSup_ite.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of a function defined piecewise by two other functions can be expressed as the join of the supremum of the first function over elements satisfying a condition and the supremum of the second function over elements not satisfying that condition.

iInf_ite.code:
iInf_ite.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f g : ι → α) :
  (⨅ i, if p i then f i else g i) = (⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : p i), f i) ⊓ ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : ¬p i), g i

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

iInf_ite.description: This theorem establishes an equality involving the infimum of a conditional function, equating it to the infimum of one function where the condition holds intersected with the infimum of another function where the condition does not hold, within a complete lattice.

iSup_range.code:
iSup_range.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {g : β → α} {f : ι → β} :
  ⨆ b ∈ range f, g b = ⨆ i, g (f i)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

iSup_range.description: This theorem indicates that the supremum of a function evaluated at the range of another function is equal to the supremum of the first function evaluated at the original inputs.

iInf_range.code:
iInf_range.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {g : β → α} {f : ι → β} :
  ⨅ b ∈ range f, g b = ⨅ i, g (f i)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

iInf_range.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated over the range of another function is equal to the infimum obtained by evaluating the first function at each index in a complete lattice.

sSup_image.code:
sSup_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {s : Set β} {f : β → α} :
  sSup (f '' s) = ⨆ a ∈ s, f a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

sSup_image.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of the image of a set under a function is equal to the supremum of the function evaluated at each element of that set.

sInf_image.code:
sInf_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {s : Set β} {f : β → α} :
  sInf (f '' s) = ⨅ a ∈ s, f a

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

sInf_image.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of the image of a set under a function is equal to the infimum of the function evaluated at each element of the original set.

iSup_emptyset.code: iSup_emptyset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} : ⨆ x ∈ ∅, f x = ⊥
iSup_emptyset.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum over an empty set of elements is equal to the bottom element in a complete lattice.

iInf_emptyset.code: iInf_emptyset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} : ⨅ x ∈ ∅, f x = ⊤
iInf_emptyset.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum over an empty set of a function equals the top element in a complete lattice.

iSup_univ.code: iSup_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} : ⨆ x ∈ univ, f x = ⨆ x, f x

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

iSup_univ.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function evaluated over the universal set is equal to the supremum of the function evaluated over its entire domain.

iInf_univ.code: iInf_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} : ⨅ x ∈ univ, f x = ⨅ x, f x

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

iInf_univ.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated over a universally quantified domain is equal to the infimum of that function evaluated over its entire domain in a complete lattice.

iSup_union.code:
iSup_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {s t : Set β} :
  ⨆ x ∈ s ∪ t, f x = (⨆ x ∈ s, f x) ⊔ ⨆ x ∈ t, f x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iSup_union.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function evaluated over the union of two sets is equal to the join of the supremums of the function over each set individually in a complete lattice.

iInf_union.code:
iInf_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {s t : Set β} :
  ⨅ x ∈ s ∪ t, f x = (⨅ x ∈ s, f x) ⊓ ⨅ x ∈ t, f x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iInf_union.description: This theorem establishes that the infimum of a function over the union of two sets is equal to the infimum of the function over each individual set combined using the meet operation.

iSup_split.code:
iSup_split.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (f : β → α) (p : β → Prop) :
  ⨆ i, f i = (⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : p i), f i) ⊔ ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : ¬p i), f i
iSup_split.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function defined on a set can be expressed as the join of the supremums from two disjoint subsets, one where a property holds and the other where it does not.

iInf_split.code:
iInf_split.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (f : β → α) (p : β → Prop) :
  ⨅ i, f i = (⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : p i), f i) ⊓ ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : ¬p i), f i
iInf_split.description: This theorem demonstrates that the infimum of a function over a set can be expressed as the infimum considering different conditions combined with the infimum of the function under the negation of those conditions in a complete lattice.

iSup_split_single.code:
iSup_split_single.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (f : β → α) (i₀ : β) :
  ⨆ i, f i = f i₀ ⊔ ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : i ≠ i₀), f i
iSup_split_single.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function over a set can be expressed as the maximum of the function evaluated at a specific element and the supremum of the function evaluated at all other elements in the set.

iInf_split_single.code:
iInf_split_single.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (f : β → α) (i₀ : β) :
  ⨅ i, f i = f i₀ ⊓ ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : i ≠ i₀), f i
iInf_split_single.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function over all elements is equal to the infimum of the function evaluated at a specific element combined with the infimum of the function evaluated at all other elements.

iSup_le_iSup_of_subset.code:
iSup_le_iSup_of_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {s t : Set β} :
  s ⊆ t → ⨆ x ∈ s, f x ≤ ⨆ x ∈ t, f x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iSup_le_iSup_of_subset.description: This theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, the supremum of a function over the smaller set is less than or equal to the supremum of the function over the larger set.

iInf_le_iInf_of_subset.code:
iInf_le_iInf_of_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {s t : Set β} :
  s ⊆ t → ⨅ x ∈ t, f x ≤ ⨅ x ∈ s, f x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iInf_le_iInf_of_subset.description: This theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then the infimum of a function over the larger set is less than or equal to the infimum of the function over the smaller set.

iSup_insert.code:
iSup_insert.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {s : Set β} {b : β} :
  ⨆ x ∈ insert b s, f x = f b ⊔ ⨆ x ∈ s, f x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.
explanatories.IsLUB.insert: In a semilattice, inserting an element into a set that has a least upper bound results in a new set whose least upper bound is the join of the inserted element and the original least upper bound.
explanatories.IsGLB.insert: This theorem establishes that if an element is the greatest lower bound of a set, then adding another element to that set results in a new set where the greatest lower bound is the infimum of the added element and the previous greatest lower bound.

iSup_insert.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function over a set that includes an additional element is equal to the maximum of that function evaluated at the new element and the supremum evaluated over the original set.

iInf_insert.code:
iInf_insert.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {s : Set β} {b : β} :
  ⨅ x ∈ insert b s, f x = f b ⊓ ⨅ x ∈ s, f x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.
explanatories.IsLUB.insert: In a semilattice, inserting an element into a set that has a least upper bound results in a new set whose least upper bound is the join of the inserted element and the original least upper bound.
explanatories.IsGLB.insert: This theorem establishes that if an element is the greatest lower bound of a set, then adding another element to that set results in a new set where the greatest lower bound is the infimum of the added element and the previous greatest lower bound.

iInf_insert.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated over the set that includes a specific element and another set is equal to the infimum of the function at that element combined with the infimum over the other set.

iSup_singleton.code: iSup_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {b : β} : ⨆ x ∈ {b}, f x = f b
iSup_singleton.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of a function evaluated at a singleton set is equal to the value of the function at the single element in that set.

iInf_singleton.code: iInf_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {b : β} : ⨅ x ∈ {b}, f x = f b
iInf_singleton.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated at a singleton set containing a specific element is equal to the value of the function at that element in a complete lattice.

iSup_pair.code:
iSup_pair.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {a b : β} :
  ⨆ x ∈ {a, b}, f x = f a ⊔ f b
iSup_pair.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function evaluated at a finite set containing two elements is equal to the join of the function values at those two elements.

iInf_pair.code:
iInf_pair.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → α} {a b : β} :
  ⨅ x ∈ {a, b}, f x = f a ⊓ f b
iInf_pair.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated at a pair of elements is equal to the meet of the function's values at those elements in a complete lattice.

iSup_image.code:
iSup_image.{u_1, u_2, u_9} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {γ : Type u_9} {f : β → γ} {g : γ → α}
  {t : Set β} : ⨆ c ∈ f '' t, g c = ⨆ b ∈ t, g (f b)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iSup_image.description: This theorem states that the supremum of the image of a set under a function equals the supremum of the original set after applying a second function, linking the two processes of evaluation.

iInf_image.code:
iInf_image.{u_1, u_2, u_9} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {γ : Type u_9} {f : β → γ} {g : γ → α}
  {t : Set β} : ⨅ c ∈ f '' t, g c = ⨅ b ∈ t, g (f b)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

iInf_image.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function applied to the image of a set is equal to the infimum of the composition of the two functions applied to the original set.

iSup_extend_bot.code:
iSup_extend_bot.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {e : ι → β}
  (he : Injective e) (f : ι → α) : ⨆ j, extend e f ⊥ j = ⨆ i, f i

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.Function.extend: The extension of a function defines a new mapping that combines the behavior of a given function with a secondary function to handle outputs outside the range of the first, ensuring that the resulting mapping is coherent under certain conditions.

iSup_extend_bot.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function extended with a bot value over an injective mapping is equal to the supremum of the original function in a complete lattice.

iInf_extend_top.code:
iInf_extend_top.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] {e : ι → β}
  (he : Injective e) (f : ι → α) : ⨅ j, extend e f ⊤ j = iInf f

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.Function.extend: The extension of a function defines a new mapping that combines the behavior of a given function with a secondary function to handle outputs outside the range of the first, ensuring that the resulting mapping is coherent under certain conditions.

iInf_extend_top.description: This theorem states that under certain conditions, the infimum of a function can be expressed as the infimum of the extended function mapped onto a top element in a complete lattice.

iSup_of_empty'.code: iSup_of_empty'.{u_9, u_10} {α : Type u_9} {ι : Sort u_10} [SupSet α] [IsEmpty ι] (f : ι → α) : iSup f = sSup ∅

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

iSup_of_empty'.description: This theorem states that the supremum of an empty index set is equal to the supremum of the empty set in any structure that supports suprema.

iInf_of_isEmpty.code: iInf_of_isEmpty.{u_9, u_10} {α : Type u_9} {ι : Sort u_10} [InfSet α] [IsEmpty ι] (f : ι → α) : iInf f = sInf ∅

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

iInf_of_isEmpty.description: This theorem establishes that the infimum of a function defined on an empty index set is equal to the infimum of the empty set.

iSup_of_empty.code: iSup_of_empty.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [IsEmpty ι] (f : ι → α) : iSup f = ⊥
iSup_of_empty.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function defined on an empty index set is the bottom element of the complete lattice.

iInf_of_empty.code: iInf_of_empty.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] [IsEmpty ι] (f : ι → α) : iInf f = ⊤
iInf_of_empty.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function defined on an empty index set is equal to the maximum element in a complete lattice.

iSup_bool_eq.code: iSup_bool_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {f : Bool → α} : ⨆ b, f b = f true ⊔ f false

explanatories.LT.lt.false: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if an element is strictly less than itself, it leads to a contradiction.
explanatories.Bool.false: The value `false` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.
explanatories.Bool.true: The value `true` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.

iSup_bool_eq.description: Theorem establishes that the supremum of a function defined on the Boolean values is equal to the supremum of its values at true and false.

iInf_bool_eq.code: iInf_bool_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {f : Bool → α} : ⨅ b, f b = f true ⊓ f false

explanatories.LT.lt.false: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if an element is strictly less than itself, it leads to a contradiction.
explanatories.Bool.false: The value `false` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.
explanatories.Bool.true: The value `true` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.

iInf_bool_eq.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a function defined on boolean values equals the infimum of its evaluations at true and false in a complete lattice.

sup_eq_iSup.code: sup_eq_iSup.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (x y : α) : x ⊔ y = ⨆ b, bif b then x else y
sup_eq_iSup.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of two elements in a complete lattice is equal to the least upper bound of a set defined by a binary condition based on those elements.

inf_eq_iInf.code: inf_eq_iInf.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (x y : α) : x ⊓ y = ⨅ b, bif b then x else y
inf_eq_iInf.description: This theorem states that the infimum of two elements in a complete lattice is equal to the infimum of all values obtained by choosing either of the two elements based on a boolean condition.

isGLB_biInf.code:
isGLB_biInf.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {s : Set β} {f : β → α} :
  IsGLB (f '' s) (⨅ x ∈ s, f x)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsGLB: This definition identifies an element as the greatest lower bound of a set if it is a lower bound for the set and no other lower bound is greater than it within a preorder structure, and it is unique if it exists in the context of a partial order.

isGLB_biInf.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of the image of a set under a function is the greatest lower bound of that image in a complete lattice.

isLUB_biSup.code:
isLUB_biSup.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {s : Set β} {f : β → α} :
  IsLUB (f '' s) (⨆ x ∈ s, f x)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsLUB: This definition characterizes an element as the least upper bound of a set if it is an upper bound for the set and no other upper bound is smaller than it within a preorder structure.

isLUB_biSup.description: This theorem states that the image of a set under a function achieves its least upper bound in a complete lattice if and only if that least upper bound equals the supremum of the function applied to the elements of the set.

iSup_sigma.code:
iSup_sigma.{u_1, u_2, u_9} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {p : β → Type u_9} {f : Sigma p → α} :
  ⨆ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨆ j, f ⟨i, j⟩
iSup_sigma.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function defined on a sigma type can be expressed as the supremum of the supremum of its values over the components of that sigma type.

iInf_sigma.code:
iInf_sigma.{u_1, u_2, u_9} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] {p : β → Type u_9} {f : Sigma p → α} :
  ⨅ x, f x = ⨅ i, ⨅ j, f ⟨i, j⟩
iInf_sigma.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function over a sigma type can be expressed as the infimum of infimums taken over the respective components of that type in a complete lattice.

iSup_prod.code:
iSup_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β × γ → α} :
  ⨆ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨆ j, f (i, j)
iSup_prod.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of a function defined on a product of two types can be expressed as the supremum over each element of those types taken separately.

iInf_prod.code:
iInf_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β × γ → α} :
  ⨅ x, f x = ⨅ i, ⨅ j, f (i, j)
iInf_prod.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function defined on a product of two types is equal to the infimum obtained by separately taking the infimum in each dimension and then applying the function.

biSup_prod.code:
biSup_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β × γ → α} {s : Set β}
  {t : Set γ} : ⨆ x ∈ s ×ˢ t, f x = ⨆ a ∈ s, ⨆ b ∈ t, f (a, b)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

biSup_prod.description: This theorem demonstrates that the supremum of a function defined on the Cartesian product of two sets can be expressed as the supremum obtained by separately taking the supremum over each set and then applying the function to their pairs.

biInf_prod.code:
biInf_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β × γ → α} {s : Set β}
  {t : Set γ} : ⨅ x ∈ s ×ˢ t, f x = ⨅ a ∈ s, ⨅ b ∈ t, f (a, b)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

biInf_prod.description: This theorem states that the infimum over the product of two sets can be expressed as the infimum of the infimums of a function evaluated at pairs from these sets in a complete lattice.

iSup_sum.code:
iSup_sum.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β ⊕ γ → α} :
  ⨆ x, f x = (⨆ i, f (Sum.inl i)) ⊔ ⨆ j, f (Sum.inr j)

explanatories.Or.inl: The left injection into a disjunction allows a proven statement to be included as a true proposition within either of the options of an "or" logical construction.
explanatories.Or.inr: The right injection operation allows one to obtain a disjunction by confirming the truth of a specific proposition.
explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

iSup_sum.description: This theorem asserts that the supremum of a function defined on the sum of two types is equal to the least upper bound of the supremums of the function restricted to each type.

iInf_sum.code:
iInf_sum.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β ⊕ γ → α} :
  ⨅ x, f x = (⨅ i, f (Sum.inl i)) ⊓ ⨅ j, f (Sum.inr j)

explanatories.Or.inl: The left injection into a disjunction allows a proven statement to be included as a true proposition within either of the options of an "or" logical construction.
explanatories.Or.inr: The right injection operation allows one to obtain a disjunction by confirming the truth of a specific proposition.
explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

iInf_sum.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function defined on the sum of two types is equal to the infimum of the function restricted to each component of the sum taken separately.

iSup_option.code:
iSup_option.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (f : Option β → α) :
  ⨆ o, f o = f none ⊔ ⨆ b, f (some b)

explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.

iSup_option.description: This theorem shows that the supremum of a function defined on options can be expressed as the join of the function evaluated at none and the supremum of the function evaluated at the some variants.

iInf_option.code:
iInf_option.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (f : Option β → α) :
  ⨅ o, f o = f none ⊓ ⨅ b, f (some b)

explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.

iInf_option.description: This theorem establishes that the infimum of a function over the option type, considering both the absence and presence of a value, is equal to the minimum of the function evaluated at none and the infimum of the function evaluated at all present values.

iSup_option_elim.code:
iSup_option_elim.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (a : α) (f : β → α) :

explanatories.False.elim: The principle of explosion asserts that from a contradiction, any statement can be derived, allowing for any proposition or type to be obtained from the assumption of falsehood.
explanatories.Option.elim: There exists a function that processes an option type by providing a default value and a transformation function to handle the case when the option contains a value.

iSup_option_elim.description: This theorem demonstrates that the supremum of an optional value can be expressed as the maximum of that value and the supremum of another function applied to all inputs.

iInf_option_elim.code:
iInf_option_elim.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice α] (a : α) (f : β → α) :
  ⨅ o, o.elim a f = a ⊓ ⨅ b, f b
iInf_option_elim.comment: A version of `iInf_option` useful for rewriting right-to-left.

explanatories.Exists.elim: This theorem states that if there exists an element that satisfies a property, then one can conclude another statement based on that property.
explanatories.False.elim: The principle of explosion asserts that from a contradiction, any statement can be derived, allowing for any proposition or type to be obtained from the assumption of falsehood.
explanatories.Option.elim: There exists a function that processes an option type by providing a default value and a transformation function to handle the case when the option contains a value.

iInf_option_elim.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a function evaluated at options, when eliminated, is equal to the conjunction of a given element and the infimum of the function evaluated at another set.

iSup_ne_bot_subtype.code: iSup_ne_bot_subtype.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ι → α) : ⨆ i, f ↑i = ⨆ i, f i

iSup_ne_bot_subtype.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function can be computed using only the elements that produce non-bottom values, as the inclusion of those that yield the bottom value does not affect the final supremum.

iInf_ne_top_subtype.code: iInf_ne_top_subtype.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ι → α) : ⨅ i, f ↑i = ⨅ i, f i
iInf_ne_top_subtype.comment:

dropped, without changing the result.
iInf_ne_top_subtype.description: This theorem demonstrates that when calculating the infimum of a function, any inputs that yield the top element can be excluded without affecting the overall result.

sSup_image2.code:
sSup_image2.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] {f : β → γ → α} {s : Set β}
  {t : Set γ} : sSup (image2 f s t) = ⨆ a ∈ s, ⨆ b ∈ t, f a b

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
