iSup_ge_eq_iSup_nat_add.code:
iSup_ge_eq_iSup_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (u : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) :
  ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : i ≥ n), u i = ⨆ i, u (i + n)
iSup_ge_eq_iSup_nat_add.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of a sequence starting from a given index is equal to the supremum of the sequence shifted by that index.

iInf_ge_eq_iInf_nat_add.code:
iInf_ge_eq_iInf_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (u : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) :
  ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : i ≥ n), u i = ⨅ i, u (i + n)
iInf_ge_eq_iInf_nat_add.description: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a function with restrictions on its index can be expressed as the infimum of a shifted version of that function.

Monotone.iSup_nat_add.code:
Monotone.iSup_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f) (k : ℕ) :
  ⨆ n, f (n + k) = ⨆ n, f n
Monotone.iSup_nat_add.description: This theorem asserts that in a complete lattice, if a function is monotone, then the supremum of the function values after a certain shift is equal to the supremum of the original function values.

Antitone.iInf_nat_add.code:
Antitone.iInf_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] {f : ℕ → α} (hf : Antitone f) (k : ℕ) :
  ⨅ n, f (n + k) = ⨅ n, f n
Antitone.iInf_nat_add.description: This theorem establishes that for an antitone function defined on natural numbers, the infimum of the function evaluated at indices shifted by a constant is equal to the infimum of the function evaluated at the original indices.

iSup_iInf_ge_nat_add.code:
iSup_iInf_ge_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ℕ → α) (k : ℕ) :
  ⨆ n, ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : i ≥ n), f (i + k) = ⨆ n, ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : i ≥ n), f i
iSup_iInf_ge_nat_add.description: This theorem states that in a complete lattice, the supremum of the infimums of a function indexed by natural numbers is equal whether the function is shifted by a constant or not.

iInf_iSup_ge_nat_add.code:
iInf_iSup_ge_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ℕ → α) (k : ℕ) :
  ⨅ n, ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : i ≥ n), f (i + k) = ⨅ n, ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : i ≥ n), f i
iInf_iSup_ge_nat_add.description: This theorem states that for any function defined on natural numbers, the infimum of the supremum of the function shifted by a constant is equal to the infimum of the supremum of the function itself, allowing for appropriate indexing.

sup_iSup_nat_succ.code: sup_iSup_nat_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (u : ℕ → α) : u 0 ⊔ ⨆ i, u (i + 1) = ⨆ i, u i
sup_iSup_nat_succ.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a sequence of elements indexed by natural numbers is equal to the supremum of the first element combined with the supremum of the subsequent elements in a complete lattice.

inf_iInf_nat_succ.code: inf_iInf_nat_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (u : ℕ → α) : u 0 ⊓ ⨅ i, u (i + 1) = ⨅ i, u i
inf_iInf_nat_succ.description: This theorem states that the infimum of a sequence starting from the first element and taking the infimum of its subsequent elements is equal to the infimum of the original sequence when the first element is included with the infimum of the rest.

iInf_nat_gt_zero_eq.code: iInf_nat_gt_zero_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ℕ → α) : ⨅ i, ⨅ (_ : i > 0), f i = ⨅ i, f (i + 1)
iInf_nat_gt_zero_eq.description: This theorem establishes that the infimum of a function over natural numbers greater than zero is equivalent to the infimum of the same function evaluated at the natural numbers starting from one.

iSup_nat_gt_zero_eq.code: iSup_nat_gt_zero_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ℕ → α) : ⨆ i, ⨆ (_ : i > 0), f i = ⨆ i, f (i + 1)
iSup_nat_gt_zero_eq.description: This theorem shows that the supremum of a function over positive natural numbers is equal to the supremum of the function evaluated at each natural number incremented by one.

iSup_eq_top.code:
iSup_eq_top.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLinearOrder α] (f : ι → α) :
  iSup f = ⊤ ↔ ∀ b < ⊤, ∃ i, b < f i
iSup_eq_top.description: This theorem indicates that the supremum of a function is equal to the top element in a complete linear order if and only if for every element less than the top, there exists an index such that the function value exceeds that element.

iInf_eq_bot.code:
iInf_eq_bot.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_5} [CompleteLinearOrder α] (f : ι → α) :
  iInf f = ⊥ ↔ ∀ b > ⊥, ∃ i, f i < b
iInf_eq_bot.description: This theorem establishes a condition under which the infimum of a function is equal to the least element in a complete linear order, specifically if for every element greater than this least element, there exists an input that produces a value less than it.

Function.Injective.completeLattice.fullDefinition: protected abbrev Function.Injective.completeLattice [Sup α] [Inf α] [SupSet α] [InfSet α] [Top α]     [Bot α] [CompleteLattice β] (f : α → β) (hf : Function.Injective f)     (map_sup : ∀ a b, f (a ⊔ b) = f a ⊔ f b) (map_inf : ∀ a b, f (a ⊓ b) = f a ⊓ f b)     (map_sSup : ∀ s, f (sSup s) = ⨆ a ∈ s, f a) (map_sInf : ∀ s, f (sInf s) = ⨅ a ∈ s, f a)     (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) : CompleteLattice α where   -- we cannot use BoundedOrder.lift here as the `LE` instance doesn't exist yet   __ := hf.lattice f map_sup map_inf   le_sSup _ a h := (le_iSup₂ a h).trans (map_sSup _).ge   sSup_le _ _ h := (map_sSup _).trans_le <| iSup₂_le h   sInf_le _ a h := (map_sInf _).trans_le <| iInf₂_le a h   le_sInf _ _ h := (le_iInf₂ h).trans (map_sInf _).ge   top := ⊤   le_top _ := (@le_top β _ _ _).trans map_top.ge   bot := ⊥   bot_le _ := map_bot.le.trans bot_le
Function.Injective.completeLattice.description: This definition describes how to create a complete lattice by pulling back an existing complete lattice along an injective function that preserves the lattice operations and properties.

Construct an initial segment from an order embedding into a well order, by collapsing it

explanatories.RelIso.symm: The inverse of a relation isomorphism is itself a relation isomorphism.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.isWellOrder: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.Acc.recOn: This defines a function that facilitates the recursive application of a property over elements in a well-founded relation, based on their accessibility within the structure.
explanatories.IsWellFounded.wf: A theorem stating that if a relation is well-founded on a type, then it is classified as a well-founded relation.
explanatories.WellFounded.apply: This theorem states that applying a well-founded relation to an element yields its accessibility in the context of that relation.
explanatories.trichotomous: This theorem establishes that in a trichotomous relation, for any two elements, one of the following must hold: the first is related to the second, they are equal, or the second is related to the first.
explanatories.Or.resolve_right: If either of two propositions is true and the second one is false, then the first proposition must be true.
explanatories.Or.resolve_left: If one of two propositions is true and the negation of the first proposition is also true, then the second proposition must be true.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.collapseF: This definition describes a method for creating an initial segment from an order embedding into a well-ordered set by identifying elements that are not related by the embedding with respect to the new order.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.collapseF.lt: This theorem asserts that if there is a relation embedding between two ordered types and one element relates to another in the first order, then the images of these elements under the embedding remain in order in the second type.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.collapseF.not_lt: This theorem asserts that if an element in the codomain cannot be reached from another element via a well-ordered relation, then the corresponding element in the source cannot satisfy that relation either.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.ofMonotone: Demonstrating that a function is monotone for strict relations is enough to establish it as a relation embedding.
explanatories.WellFounded.has_min: This theorem states that any nonempty set has a minimal element with respect to a well-founded relation.
explanatories.asymm: This theorem asserts that in an asymmetric relation, if the relation holds from the first element to the second, then it cannot hold in the reverse direction from the second to the first.

RelEmbedding.collapse.fullDefinition: noncomputable def collapse [IsWellOrder β s] (f : r ↪r s) : r ≼i s :=   haveI := RelEmbedding.isWellOrder f   ⟨RelEmbedding.ofMonotone (fun a => (collapseF f a).1) fun a b => collapseF.lt f, fun a b =>     Acc.recOn (IsWellFounded.wf.apply b : Acc s b)       (fun b _ _ a h => by         rcases (@IsWellFounded.wf _ r).has_min { a | ¬s (collapseF f a).1 b }           ⟨_, asymm h⟩ with ⟨m, hm, hm'⟩         refine ⟨m, ((@trichotomous _ s _ _ _).resolve_left hm).resolve_right           (collapseF.not_lt f _ fun a' h' => ?_)⟩         by_contra hn         exact hm' _ hn h')       a⟩
RelEmbedding.collapse.description: This definition specifies that an initial segment can be constructed by collapsing an order embedding into a well-ordered set to fill in any gaps.

RelEmbedding.collapse_apply.description: This theorem asserts that applying a relation embedding to an element yields a value that corresponds to the image of that element under the embedding's collapse function, demonstrating the relationship between the embedding and its collapse.

GaloisConnection.code: GaloisConnection.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (l : α → β) (u : β → α) : Prop
GaloisConnection.comment:
A Galois connection is a pair of functions `l` and `u` satisfying
`l a ≤ b ↔ a ≤ u b`. They are special cases of adjoint functors in category theory,
but do not depend on the category theory library in mathlib.
GaloisConnection.fullDefinition: def GaloisConnection [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (l : α → β) (u : β → α) :=   ∀ a b, l a ≤ b ↔ a ≤ u b
GaloisConnection.description: A Galois connection consists of two functions that establish a relationship between elements of two ordered sets, such that the order of one set is preserved in relation to the mapping of the other.

OrderIso.to_galoisConnection.comment: Makes a Galois connection from an order-preserving bijection.

explanatories.GaloisConnection: A Galois connection consists of two functions that establish a relationship between elements of two ordered sets, such that the order of one set is preserved in relation to the mapping of the other.
explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

OrderIso.to_galoisConnection.description: An order-preserving bijection creates a Galois connection between two ordered sets by relating their respective elements through the bijection and its inverse.

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

GaloisConnection.monotone_intro.description: The theorem states that if two functions are monotone and satisfy specific inequalities involving their compositions, then they form a Galois connection between two ordered sets.

explanatories.Monotone.dual: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.

GaloisConnection.dual.description: The theorem states that the duals of the functions in a Galois connection also form a Galois connection between the duals of the ordered sets.

GaloisConnection.le_iff_le.description: The theorem demonstrates that in a Galois connection, the order relation between an element in one set and an element in another set can be expressed equivalently in both directions.

GaloisConnection.l_le.description: The theorem states that if there is a Galois connection between two functions, then the order condition relating an element from the first set and an element from the second set can be used to derive an order condition involving the images of those elements under the respective functions.

GaloisConnection.le_u.code:

GaloisConnection.le_u.description: The theorem states that if there is a Galois connection between two functions, then an order condition involving the image of an element from the first set implies a corresponding order condition involving that element and the image of an element from the second set.

GaloisConnection.le_u_l.code:

GaloisConnection.le_u_l.description: The theorem asserts that for any element in the first set related by a Galois connection, that element is less than or equal to the image it maps to in the second set after applying the corresponding function.

GaloisConnection.l_u_le.code:

GaloisConnection.l_u_le.description: The theorem establishes that in a Galois connection, applying the function from the first set to the inverse image of an element in the second set results in an element that is less than or equal to the original element from the second set.

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

GaloisConnection.monotone_l.description: The theorem asserts that if two functions form a Galois connection, then the first function is monotone, meaning it preserves the order of inputs in its output.

GaloisConnection.upperBounds_l_image.code:

GaloisConnection.upperBounds_l_image.description: The theorem asserts that for a set transformed via a function that defines a Galois connection, the upper bounds of the transformed set correspond to the preimage of the upper bounds of the original set under the inverse function.

GaloisConnection.bddBelow_u_image.description: The theorem states that a set is bounded below in one ordered space if and only if its image under a function that is part of a Galois connection is also bounded below in the other ordered space.

GaloisConnection.isLUB_l_image.description: The theorem establishes that if a set has a least upper bound under a function that is part of a Galois connection, then the image of that set also has a least upper bound, which is the image of the original least upper bound.

GaloisConnection.isGLB_u_image.code:

explanatories.IsGLB: This definition identifies an element as the greatest lower bound of a set if it is a lower bound for the set and no other lower bound is greater than it within a preorder structure, and it is unique if it exists in the context of a partial order.

GaloisConnection.isGLB_u_image.description: The theorem states that if a function forms a Galois connection and a specific element is the greatest lower bound of a set, then the image of that set under the function has its greatest lower bound at the image of that element.

GaloisConnection.isLeast_l.code:

GaloisConnection.isLeast_l.description: The theorem establishes that if a function is part of a Galois connection, then a specific element's image under the function is the least element of the set of elements that are greater than or equal to the image of another element under the inverse function.

GaloisConnection.isGreatest_u.code:

explanatories.IsGreatest: This definition states that an element is considered the greatest element of a set if it is greater than or equal to every element in that set within a preorder structure, and it is unique if it exists in the context of a partial order.

GaloisConnection.isGreatest_u.description: The theorem states that under a Galois connection, the image of an upper bound in the second set is the greatest element among the pre-images in the first set that map to it in a specified order.

GaloisConnection.isGLB_l.code:
GaloisConnection.isGLB_l.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {a : α} : IsGLB {b | a ≤ u b} (l a)

explanatories.IsGLB: This definition identifies an element as the greatest lower bound of a set if it is a lower bound for the set and no other lower bound is greater than it within a preorder structure, and it is unique if it exists in the context of a partial order.

GaloisConnection.isGLB_l.description: The theorem asserts that if a function is part of a Galois connection, then the image of a specific element under the function is the greatest lower bound of the set of elements that are greater than or equal to the image of that element under the inverse function.

GaloisConnection.isLUB_u.code:
GaloisConnection.isLUB_u.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {b : β} : IsLUB {a | l a ≤ b} (u b)

explanatories.IsLUB: This definition characterizes an element as the least upper bound of a set if it is an upper bound for the set and no other upper bound is smaller than it within a preorder structure.

GaloisConnection.isLUB_u.description: The theorem asserts that for a given Galois connection, the image of an upper bound in one ordered set is the least upper bound of the preimage of that upper bound in another ordered set.

GaloisConnection.le_u_l_trans.code:
GaloisConnection.le_u_l_trans.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {x y z : α} (hxy : x ≤ u (l y)) (hyz : y ≤ u (l z)) : x ≤ u (l z)
GaloisConnection.le_u_l_trans.comment:
If `(l, u)` is a Galois connection, then the relation `x ≤ u (l y)` is a transitive relation.
If `l` is a closure operator (`Submodule.span`, `Subgroup.closure`, ...) and `u` is the coercion to
`Set`, this reads as "if `U` is in the closure of `V` and `V` is in the closure of `W` then `U` is
in the closure of `W`".
GaloisConnection.le_u_l_trans.description: The theorem establishes that if a Galois connection exists between two functions, then the transitive property holds for the order relationships among elements linked through the images of those functions.

GaloisConnection.l_u_le_trans.code:
GaloisConnection.l_u_le_trans.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {x y z : β} (hxy : l (u x) ≤ y) (hyz : l (u y) ≤ z) : l (u x) ≤ z
GaloisConnection.l_u_le_trans.description: The theorem states that under a Galois connection, if a function image of one element is less than or equal to a second element, and that second element is less than or equal to a third, then the function image of the first element is also less than or equal to the third element.

GaloisConnection.u_l_u_eq_u.code:
GaloisConnection.u_l_u_eq_u.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) (b : β) : u (l (u b)) = u b
GaloisConnection.u_l_u_eq_u.description: Under a Galois connection, applying a function and then its inverse to an element yields the same element back in the context of the preorder structures.

GaloisConnection.u_l_u_eq_u'.code:
GaloisConnection.u_l_u_eq_u'.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) : u ∘ l ∘ u = u
GaloisConnection.u_l_u_eq_u'.description: The theorem states that if two functions are part of a Galois connection, then applying the second function to the output of the first function followed by reapplying the second function again yields the same result as applying the second function alone.

GaloisConnection.u_unique.description: The theorem states that if two Galois connections are equivalent in their first components, then they are also equivalent in their second components for any element from the second ordered set.

GaloisConnection.exists_eq_u.code:
GaloisConnection.exists_eq_u.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) (a : α) : (∃ b, a = u b) ↔ a = u (l a)
GaloisConnection.exists_eq_u.comment: If there exists a `b` such that `a = u a`, then `b = l a` is one such element.
GaloisConnection.exists_eq_u.description: The theorem establishes a bi-conditional relationship between the existence of an element that shows a value maps to the first set and the equality of that value to the image of another value obtained through the first function in a Galois connection.

GaloisConnection.u_eq.code:
GaloisConnection.u_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {z : α} {y : β} : u y = z ↔ ∀ (x : α), x ≤ z ↔ l x ≤ y
GaloisConnection.u_eq.description: The theorem establishes an equivalence between a value being the output of a function in a Galois connection and the condition that all values less than or equal to another specified value are mapped under the initial function to values less than or equal to a second specified value.

GaloisConnection.l_u_l_eq_l.code:
GaloisConnection.l_u_l_eq_l.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [PartialOrder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) (a : α) : l (u (l a)) = l a
GaloisConnection.l_u_l_eq_l.description: The theorem asserts that for any element processed through a specific function in a Galois connection, applying the inverse function followed by the original function returns the same result as directly applying the original function to that element.

GaloisConnection.l_u_l_eq_l'.code:
GaloisConnection.l_u_l_eq_l'.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [PartialOrder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) : l ∘ u ∘ l = l
GaloisConnection.l_u_l_eq_l'.description: The theorem establishes that for a Galois connection, applying the first function, followed by its adjoint, and then the first function again yields the same result as directly applying the first function.

GaloisConnection.l_unique.description: The theorem establishes that if two Galois connections coincide on the outputs of their respective inverse functions, then they must produce the same output for any element from the first ordered set.

GaloisConnection.exists_eq_l.code:
GaloisConnection.exists_eq_l.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [PartialOrder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) (b : β) : (∃ a, b = l a) ↔ b = l (u b)
GaloisConnection.exists_eq_l.comment: If there exists an `a` such that `b = l a`, then `a = u b` is one such element.
GaloisConnection.exists_eq_l.description: The theorem demonstrates that for a Galois connection, the existence of an element that maps to a specific value under one function is equivalent to that value being the image of the corresponding element under the other function.

GaloisConnection.l_eq.code:
GaloisConnection.l_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [PartialOrder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}
  (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {x : α} {z : β} : l x = z ↔ ∀ (y : β), z ≤ y ↔ x ≤ u y
GaloisConnection.l_eq.description: The theorem asserts that for functions forming a Galois connection, equality between the output of the first function and an element in the second set is equivalent to an ordering condition involving that element and the second function applied to all elements in the second set.

GaloisConnection.u_eq_top.code:
GaloisConnection.u_eq_top.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] [OrderTop α] {l : α → β}
  {u : β → α} (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {x : β} : u x = ⊤ ↔ l ⊤ ≤ x
GaloisConnection.u_eq_top.description: The theorem states that for a Galois connection between two ordered sets, the image of the greatest element in the first set is the greatest element in the second set if and only if the greatest element in the first set is less than or equal to a particular element in the second set.

GaloisConnection.u_top.code:
GaloisConnection.u_top.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] [OrderTop α] [OrderTop β]
  {l : α → β} {u : β → α} (gc : GaloisConnection l u) : u ⊤ = ⊤
GaloisConnection.u_top.description: The theorem asserts that in a Galois connection, the image of the top element from one partially ordered set corresponds to the top element in another partially ordered set.

GaloisConnection.l_eq_bot.code:
GaloisConnection.l_eq_bot.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Preorder α] [PartialOrder β] [OrderBot β] {l : α → β}
  {u : β → α} (gc : GaloisConnection l u) {x : α} : l x = ⊥ ↔ x ≤ u ⊥

GaloisInsertion.monotoneIntro.fullDefinition: def GaloisInsertion.monotoneIntro {α β : Type*} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β} {u : β → α}     (hu : Monotone u) (hl : Monotone l) (hul : ∀ a, a ≤ u (l a)) (hlu : ∀ b, l (u b) = b) :     GaloisInsertion l u where   choice x _ := l x   gc := GaloisConnection.monotone_intro hu hl hul fun b => le_of_eq (hlu b)   le_l_u b := le_of_eq <| (hlu b).symm   choice_eq _ _ := rfl

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.GaloisInsertion.gc: The theorem asserts that a Galois connection can be derived from a Galois insertion between two ordered sets.
explanatories.GaloisInsertion.choice: This definition introduces a choice function that constructs an output in the target space when a specific ordering condition related to a Galois insertion is satisfied.
explanatories.GaloisInsertion.choice_eq: The theorem establishes that under a Galois insertion, the choice function yields the same result as applying the first function to an element when a certain inequality condition involving the second function is satisfied.
explanatories.GaloisCoinsertion.choice: This definition describes a constructive choice function that selects an element from the codomain based on the order relation between an element and the output of a function applied to its image.
explanatories.GaloisCoinsertion.gc: The theorem establishes that a Galois coinsertion induces a corresponding Galois connection between two preorder structures.
explanatories.GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_le: This theorem asserts that in a Galois coinsertion, applying the second function to the image of an element through the first function yields a result that is less than or equal to the original element.
explanatories.GaloisCoinsertion.choice_eq: The theorem establishes that in the context of a Galois coinsertion, the choice function produces the same result as applying the initial mapping to an element when a specific ordering condition is fulfilled.
explanatories.OrderIso.toGaloisCoinsertion: This definition creates a Galois coinsertion from an order-preserving bijection between two preordered types.

GaloisConnection.toGaloisCoinsertion.fullDefinition: def GaloisConnection.toGaloisCoinsertion {α β : Type*} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {l : α → β}     {u : β → α} (gc : GaloisConnection l u) (h : ∀ a, u (l a) ≤ a) : GaloisCoinsertion l u :=   { choice := fun x _ => u x     gc     u_l_le := h     choice_eq := fun _ _ => rfl }
GaloisConnection.toGaloisCoinsertion.description: This definition creates a Galois coinsertion from a given Galois connection under the condition that every element in the first set is greater than or equal to its image transformed by the second function.

GaloisConnection.liftOrderTop.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] [OrderTop β]

explanatories.GaloisConnection.le_u: The theorem states that if there is a Galois connection between two functions, then an order condition involving the image of an element from the first set implies a corresponding order condition involving that element and the image of an element from the second set.
explanatories.Top.top: A function that retrieves the top element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.GaloisInsertion.gc: The theorem asserts that a Galois connection can be derived from a Galois insertion between two ordered sets.
explanatories.GaloisInsertion.liftOrderTop: This definition describes a construction that elevates the top element of one ordered structure to become the top element in another structure through a Galois insertion.
explanatories.OrderTop.le_top: Every element in an ordered type that has a maximum element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.GaloisCoinsertion.gc: The theorem establishes that a Galois coinsertion induces a corresponding Galois connection between two preorder structures.
explanatories.CompleteLattice.le_top: This theorem states that any element in a complete lattice is less than or equal to the greatest element of that lattice.

GaloisConnection.liftOrderTop.fullDefinition: def GaloisConnection.liftOrderTop {α β : Type*} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] [OrderTop β]     {l : α → β} {u : β → α} (gc : GaloisConnection l u) :     OrderTop α where   top := u ⊤   le_top _ := gc.le_u <| le_top
GaloisConnection.liftOrderTop.description: This defines a structure that relates the top element of one partially ordered set to another via a Galois connection, thereby creating an order that possesses a top element.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_eq.code:
GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : α → β} {u : β → α} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β]
  (gi : GaloisCoinsertion l u) (a : α) : u (l a) = a
GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_eq.description: The theorem states that in a Galois coinsertion, applying the function from the second set to the image of an element in the first set returns the original element from the first set.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_leftInverse.code:
GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_leftInverse.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : α → β} {u : β → α} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β]

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_leftInverse.description: The theorem states that if there is a Galois coinsertion between two ordered structures, then the function from the second structure to the first acts as a left inverse to the function from the first to the second.

GaloisInsertion.l_top.code:
GaloisInsertion.l_top.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : α → β} {u : β → α} [Preorder α] [PartialOrder β]

GaloisInsertion.l_top.description: The theorem asserts that in the context of a Galois insertion, the image of the top element from one ordered set under a certain function corresponds to the top element in the other ordered set.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_surjective.code:

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_surjective.description: The theorem asserts that in a Galois coinsertion, the mapping from the second set back to the first set is surjective.

GaloisCoinsertion.l_injective.code:

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

GaloisCoinsertion.l_injective.description: The theorem states that if two functions are part of a Galois coinsertion, then the first function is injective.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_inf_l.code:

GaloisCoinsertion.u_inf_l.description: The theorem states that if there is a Galois coinsertion between two semilattices, then the image of the infimum of the two elements under the second function equals the infimum of those two elements in the first semilattice.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_iInf_l.code:

GaloisCoinsertion.u_iInf_l.description: The theorem asserts that in the context of a Galois coinsertion, the image of the infimum of a set of elements under one function equals the infimum of those elements directly.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_sInf_l_image.code:
GaloisCoinsertion.u_sInf_l_image.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : α → β} {u : β → α} [CompleteLattice α]

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_sInf_l_image.description: The theorem demonstrates that under a Galois coinsertion, the image of the infimum of the transformed set corresponds to the infimum of the original set in a complete lattice.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_sup_l.code:

GaloisCoinsertion.u_sup_l.description: The theorem shows that in a Galois coinsertion, the image under a function of the supremum of two elements in the first set is equal to the supremum of the original elements in the second set.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_iSup_l.code:

GaloisCoinsertion.u_iSup_l.description: The theorem states that for a Galois coinsertion between two complete lattices, the image of the supremum of a family of elements mapped by a function corresponds to the supremum of the original elements.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_biSup_l.code:

GaloisCoinsertion.u_biSup_l.description: The theorem asserts that for a Galois coinsertion between two complete lattices, the image of a supremum defined through a specific function corresponds to the supremum of the images defined by that function, maintaining structural integrity across the mappings.

GaloisCoinsertion.u_sSup_l_image.code:

GaloisCoinsertion.l_le_l_iff.code:

explanatories.StrictMono: A function is considered strictly monotone if it maintains the order relationship such that whenever one input is strictly less than another, the output corresponding to the first input is also strictly less than the output corresponding to the second input.

GaloisCoinsertion.strictMono_l.description: The theorem asserts that a function associated with a Galois coinsertion is strictly monotonic between two preordered sets.

GaloisCoinsertion.isGLB_of_l_image.description: The theorem states that if there is a Galois coinsertion between two ordered sets and an element is the greatest lower bound of the image of a set under one function, then the corresponding element in the original set is the greatest lower bound of that set.

GaloisCoinsertion.liftSemilatticeInf.fullDefinition: abbrev liftSemilatticeInf [SemilatticeInf β] (gi : GaloisCoinsertion l u) : SemilatticeInf α :=   { ‹PartialOrder α› with     inf_le_left := fun a b => by       exact (@OrderDual.instSemilatticeInf αᵒᵈ gi.dual.liftSemilatticeSup).inf_le_left a b     inf_le_right := fun a b => by       exact (@OrderDual.instSemilatticeInf αᵒᵈ gi.dual.liftSemilatticeSup).inf_le_right a b     le_inf := fun a b c => by       exact (@OrderDual.instSemilatticeInf αᵒᵈ gi.dual.liftSemilatticeSup).le_inf a b c     inf := fun a b => u (l a ⊓ l b) }

GaloisCoinsertion.liftSemilatticeSup.fullDefinition: abbrev liftSemilatticeSup [SemilatticeSup β] (gi : GaloisCoinsertion l u) : SemilatticeSup α :=   { ‹PartialOrder α› with     sup := fun a b =>       gi.choice (l a ⊔ l b) <|         sup_le (gi.gc.monotone_l <| gi.gc.le_u <| le_sup_left)           (gi.gc.monotone_l <| gi.gc.le_u <| le_sup_right)     le_sup_left := fun a b => by       exact (@OrderDual.instSemilatticeSup αᵒᵈ gi.dual.liftSemilatticeInf).le_sup_left a b     le_sup_right := fun a b => by       exact (@OrderDual.instSemilatticeSup αᵒᵈ gi.dual.liftSemilatticeInf).le_sup_right a b     sup_le := fun a b c => by       exact (@OrderDual.instSemilatticeSup αᵒᵈ gi.dual.liftSemilatticeInf).sup_le a b c }
GaloisCoinsertion.liftSemilatticeSup.description: This definition describes a construction that creates a structure of suprema in one set using the framework of a Galois coinsertion related to another set that already possesses a supremum operation.

CompletelyDistribLattice.toCompleteDistr.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) CompletelyDistribLattice.toCompleteDistribLattice     [CompletelyDistribLattice α] : CompleteDistribLattice α where   iInf_sup_le_sup_sInf a s := calc     _ = ⨅ b : s, ⨆ x : Bool, cond x a b := by simp_rw [iInf_subtype, iSup_bool_eq, cond]     _ = _ := iInf_iSup_eq     _ ≤ _ := iSup_le fun f => by       if h : ∀ i, f i = false then         simp [h, iInf_subtype, ← sInf_eq_iInf]       else         have ⟨i, h⟩ : ∃ i, f i = true := by simpa using h         refine le_trans (iInf_le _ i) ?_         simp [h]   inf_sSup_le_iSup_inf a s := calc     _ = ⨅ x : Bool, ⨆ y : cond x PUnit s, match x with | true => a | false => y.1 := by       simp_rw [iInf_bool_eq, cond, iSup_const, iSup_subtype, sSup_eq_iSup]     _ = _ := by exact iInf_iSup_eq     _ ≤ _ := by       simp_rw [iInf_bool_eq]       refine iSup_le fun g => le_trans ?_ (le_iSup _ (g false).1)       refine le_trans ?_ (le_iSup _ (g false).2)       rfl

Function.Injective.frame.fullDefinition: protected abbrev Function.Injective.frame [Sup α] [Inf α] [SupSet α] [InfSet α] [Top α] [Bot α]     [Frame β] (f : α → β) (hf : Injective f) (map_sup : ∀ a b, f (a ⊔ b) = f a ⊔ f b)     (map_inf : ∀ a b, f (a ⊓ b) = f a ⊓ f b) (map_sSup : ∀ s, f (sSup s) = ⨆ a ∈ s, f a)     (map_sInf : ∀ s, f (sInf s) = ⨅ a ∈ s, f a) (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) :     Frame α where   __ := hf.completeLattice f map_sup map_inf map_sSup map_sInf map_top map_bot   inf_sSup_le_iSup_inf a s := by     change f (a ⊓ sSup s) ≤ f _     rw [← sSup_image, map_inf, map_sSup s, inf_iSup₂_eq]     simp_rw [← map_inf]     exact ((map_sSup _).trans iSup_image).ge

Function.Injective.coframe.fullDefinition: protected abbrev Function.Injective.coframe [Sup α] [Inf α] [SupSet α] [InfSet α] [Top α] [Bot α]     [Coframe β] (f : α → β) (hf : Injective f) (map_sup : ∀ a b, f (a ⊔ b) = f a ⊔ f b)     (map_inf : ∀ a b, f (a ⊓ b) = f a ⊓ f b) (map_sSup : ∀ s, f (sSup s) = ⨆ a ∈ s, f a)     (map_sInf : ∀ s, f (sInf s) = ⨅ a ∈ s, f a) (map_top : f ⊤ = ⊤) (map_bot : f ⊥ = ⊥) :     Coframe α where   __ := hf.completeLattice f map_sup map_inf map_sSup map_sInf map_top map_bot   iInf_sup_le_sup_sInf a s := by     change f _ ≤ f (a ⊔ sInf s)     rw [← sInf_image, map_sup, map_sInf s, sup_iInf₂_eq]     simp_rw [← map_sup]     exact ((map_sInf _).trans iInf_image).le

CovBy.comment: `CovBy a b` means that `b` covers `a`: `a < b` and there is no element in between.

CovBy.description: One element is said to cover another if it is strictly greater and there are no intervening elements between them.

explanatories.Set.Ici: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-infinite interval.

CovBy.Ioi_eq.description: In a linearly ordered structure, if one element strictly covers another, then the interval of elements greater than the first is equal to the interval of elements greater than or equal to the second.

CovBy.Iio_eq.code: CovBy.Iio_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b : α} (h : a ⋖ b) : Iio b = Iic a

explanatories.Set.Iio: This definition represents the set of elements that are strictly less than a given element in a preorder structure, creating a left-infinite and right-open interval.
explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.

CovBy.Iio_eq.description: In a linear ordered structure, if one element densely covers another, then the interval of elements less than the second element is equal to the set of elements less than or equal to the first element.

WCovBy.le_of_lt.code: WCovBy.le_of_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (hab : a ⩿ b) (hcb : c < b) : c ≤ a
WCovBy.le_of_lt.description: In a linearly ordered structure, if one element strictly covers a second and a third element is less than the second, then the third element is less than or equal to the first.

WCovBy.ge_of_gt.code: WCovBy.ge_of_gt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (hab : a ⩿ b) (hac : a < c) : b ≤ c
WCovBy.ge_of_gt.description: If one element covers another in a linear order and the first element is strictly less than a third element, then the second element is less than or equal to the third element.

CovBy.le_of_lt.code: CovBy.le_of_lt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (hab : a ⋖ b) : c < b → c ≤ a

explanatories.WCovBy.le_of_lt: In a linearly ordered structure, if one element strictly covers a second and a third element is less than the second, then the third element is less than or equal to the first.

CovBy.le_of_lt.description: If one element in a linear order strictly covers another, then any element less than the covered one must also be less than or equal to the covering element.

CovBy.ge_of_gt.code: CovBy.ge_of_gt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (hab : a ⋖ b) : a < c → b ≤ c

explanatories.WCovBy.ge_of_gt: If one element covers another in a linear order and the first element is strictly less than a third element, then the second element is less than or equal to the third element.

CovBy.ge_of_gt.description: If one element strictly covers another in a linear order, then any element that is strictly greater than the first is also greater than or equal to the second.

CovBy.unique_left.code: CovBy.unique_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (ha : a ⋖ c) (hb : b ⋖ c) : a = b
CovBy.unique_left.description: If two elements cover the same third element in a linear order, then they must be equal.

CovBy.unique_right.code: CovBy.unique_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {a b c : α} (hb : a ⋖ b) (hc : a ⋖ c) : b = c
CovBy.unique_right.description: In a linear order, if one element densely covers two other elements, then those two elements must be equal.

CovBy.eq_of_between.code:

CovBy.eq_of_between.comment: If `a`, `b`, `c` are consecutive and `a < x < c` then `x = b`.
CovBy.eq_of_between.description: In a linear order, if one element is between two others and they are consecutive, then that element is equal to the middle element.

Set.covBy_insert.description: In any set, if an element is not already in the set, then that element covers the set formed by inserting it into the original set.

Prod.swap_wcovBy_swap.code:
Prod.swap_wcovBy_swap.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {x y : α × β} :
  x.swap ⩿ y.swap ↔ x ⩿ y
Prod.swap_wcovBy_swap.description: The swapping of pairs in a partially ordered structure shows that one pair covers another if and only if their swapped counterparts have the same covering relationship.

Prod.swap_covBy_swap.code:
Prod.swap_covBy_swap.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {x y : α × β} :
  x.swap ⋖ y.swap ↔ x ⋖ y
Prod.swap_covBy_swap.description: In a partially ordered structure, swapping the components of two ordered pairs preserves the strict covering relation between them.

Prod.fst_eq_or_snd_eq_of_wcovBy.code:
Prod.fst_eq_or_snd_eq_of_wcovBy.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β]
  {x y : α × β} : x ⩿ y → x.1 = y.1 ∨ x.2 = y.2
Prod.fst_eq_or_snd_eq_of_wcovBy.description: In a partially ordered product of two types, if one pair of elements covers another, then at least one component of the first pair is equal to the corresponding component of the second pair.

WCovBy.fst.code:
WCovBy.fst.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {x y : α × β} (h : x ⩿ y) :
  x.1 ⩿ y.1
WCovBy.fst.description: If one pair of elements covers another pair in a partially ordered context, then the first components of those pairs also cover each other.

WCovBy.snd.code:
WCovBy.snd.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {x y : α × β} (h : x ⩿ y) :
  x.2 ⩿ y.2
WCovBy.snd.description: If one pair of elements covers another in the product of two partially ordered sets, then the second component of the first pair covers the second component of the second pair.

Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff_left.code:
Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {a₁ a₂ : α}
  {b : β} : (a₁, b) ⩿ (a₂, b) ↔ a₁ ⩿ a₂
Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff_left.description: In a partially ordered structure, one pair with a common second element covers another pair if and only if the first elements of the pairs have a covering relationship.

Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff_right.code:
Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {a : α}
  {b₁ b₂ : β} : (a, b₁) ⩿ (a, b₂) ↔ b₁ ⩿ b₂
Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff_right.description: In a partially ordered structure, one pair of elements covers another if and only if the second elements of the pairs cover each other.

Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff_left.code:
Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {a₁ a₂ : α}
  {b : β} : (a₁, b) ⋖ (a₂, b) ↔ a₁ ⋖ a₂
Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff_left.description: In a partially ordered structure, one ordered pair is said to cover another if and only if the first component of the first pair covers the first component of the second pair while the second components are equal.

Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff_right.code:
Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {a : α}
  {b₁ b₂ : β} : (a, b₁) ⋖ (a, b₂) ↔ b₁ ⋖ b₂
Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff_right.description: In a partially ordered product, one pair covers another if and only if their second elements cover each other.

Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff.code:
Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {a₁ a₂ : α}
  {b₁ b₂ : β} : (a₁, b₁) ⩿ (a₂, b₂) ↔ a₁ ⩿ a₂ ∧ b₁ = b₂ ∨ b₁ ⩿ b₂ ∧ a₁ = a₂
Prod.mk_wcovBy_mk_iff.description: One pair strictly covers another if and only if the first element in each pair strictly covers the corresponding element in the other pair with the second elements being equal, or the second element in each pair strictly covers the corresponding element in the other pair with the first elements being equal.

Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff.code:
Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {a₁ a₂ : α}
  {b₁ b₂ : β} : (a₁, b₁) ⋖ (a₂, b₂) ↔ a₁ ⋖ a₂ ∧ b₁ = b₂ ∨ b₁ ⋖ b₂ ∧ a₁ = a₂
Prod.mk_covBy_mk_iff.description: In a partially ordered product structure, one ordered pair strictly covers another if and only if their first components have the same covering relationship or their second components are equal while their first components cover each other.

Prod.wcovBy_iff.code:
Prod.wcovBy_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {x y : α × β} :
  x ⩿ y ↔ x.1 ⩿ y.1 ∧ x.2 = y.2 ∨ x.2 ⩿ y.2 ∧ x.1 = y.1
Prod.wcovBy_iff.description: Two pairs of elements in a product space are said to be related by a covering relation if either the first elements of each pair cover each other while the second elements are equal, or the second elements cover each other while the first elements are equal.

Prod.covBy_iff.code:
Prod.covBy_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [PartialOrder β] {x y : α × β} :
  x ⋖ y ↔ x.1 ⋖ y.1 ∧ x.2 = y.2 ∨ x.2 ⋖ y.2 ∧ x.1 = y.1
Prod.covBy_iff.description: In a partial order, one element in a product of two types covers another if and only if either the first components have a covering relation while the second components are equal, or the second components have a covering relation while the first components are equal.

OrderHom.prevFixed.description: The previous fixed point of a monotone function is the largest fixed point that does not exceed a given point, provided that the function's output at that point is less than or equal to the point itself.

SuccOrder.ofLinearWellFoundedLT.fullDefinition: noncomputable def SuccOrder.ofLinearWellFoundedLT [WellFoundedLT α] : SuccOrder α :=   ofCore (fun a ↦ if h : (Ioi a).Nonempty then wellFounded_lt.min _ h else a)     (fun ha _ ↦ by       rw [not_isMax_iff] at ha       simp_rw [Set.Nonempty, mem_Ioi, dif_pos ha]       exact ⟨(wellFounded_lt.min_le · ha), lt_of_lt_of_le (wellFounded_lt.min_mem _ ha)⟩)     fun a ha ↦ dif_neg (not_not_intro ha <| not_isMax_iff.mpr ·)

IsWellOrder.toIsPredArchimedean.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) IsWellOrder.toIsPredArchimedean [h : IsWellOrder α (· < ·)]     [PredOrder α] : IsPredArchimedean α :=   ⟨fun {a b} => by     refine WellFounded.fix (C := fun b => a ≤ b → ∃ n, Nat.iterate pred n b = a)       h.wf ?_ b     intros b ih hab     replace hab := eq_or_lt_of_le hab     rcases hab with (rfl | hab)     · exact ⟨0, rfl⟩     rcases le_or_lt b (pred b) with hb | hb     · cases (min_of_le_pred hb).not_lt hab     dsimp at ih     obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := ih (pred b) hb (le_pred_of_lt hab)     refine ⟨k + 1, ?_⟩     rw [iterate_add_apply, iterate_one, hk]⟩
IsWellOrder.toIsPredArchimedean.description: In a linear ordered set that is well-ordered with respect to the usual less-than relation, this definition establishes that such an order is also predicatively archimedean.

  [WellFoundedGT α] (H_pred : (a : α) → ¬IsMin a → C a → C (pred a))
  (H_lim : (a : α) → IsPredLimit a → ((b : α) → b > a → C b) → C a) :
  PredOrder.limitRecOn a H_pred H_lim =
    ⋯.fix
      (fun a IH =>
        if h : IsPredLimit a then H_lim a h IH
        else
          let x := Classical.indefiniteDescription (fun x => ¬IsMin x ∧ pred x = a) ⋯;
          ⋯ ▸ H_pred ↑x ⋯ (IH ↑x ⋯))
      a

LinearLocallyFiniteOrder.isSuccArchimede.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) LinearLocallyFiniteOrder.isSuccArchimedean [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] :     IsSuccArchimedean ι where   exists_succ_iterate_of_le := by     intro i j hij     rw [le_iff_lt_or_eq] at hij     cases' hij with hij hij     swap     · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩       simpa only [Function.iterate_zero, id] using hij     by_contra! h     have h_lt : ∀ n, succ^[n] i < j := by       intro n       induction' n with n hn       · simpa only [Function.iterate_zero, id] using hij       · refine lt_of_le_of_ne ?_ (h _)         rw [Function.iterate_succ', Function.comp_apply]         exact succ_le_of_lt hn     have h_mem : ∀ n, succ^[n] i ∈ Finset.Icc i j :=       fun n ↦ Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨le_succ_iterate n i, (h_lt n).le⟩     obtain ⟨n, m, hnm, h_eq⟩ : ∃ n m, n < m ∧ succ^[n] i = succ^[m] i := by       let f : ℕ → Finset.Icc i j := fun n ↦ ⟨succ^[n] i, h_mem n⟩       obtain ⟨n, m, hnm_ne, hfnm⟩ : ∃ n m, n ≠ m ∧ f n = f m :=         Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite f       have hnm_eq : succ^[n] i = succ^[m] i := by simpa only [f, Subtype.mk_eq_mk] using hfnm       rcases le_total n m with h_le | h_le       · exact ⟨n, m, lt_of_le_of_ne h_le hnm_ne, hnm_eq⟩       · exact ⟨m, n, lt_of_le_of_ne h_le hnm_ne.symm, hnm_eq.symm⟩     have h_max : IsMax (succ^[n] i) := isMax_iterate_succ_of_eq_of_ne h_eq hnm.ne     exact not_le.mpr (h_lt n) (h_max (h_lt n).le)

LinearOrder.isPredArchimedean_of_isSuccA.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) LinearOrder.isPredArchimedean_of_isSuccArchimedean [SuccOrder ι]     [PredOrder ι] [IsSuccArchimedean ι] : IsPredArchimedean ι where   exists_pred_iterate_of_le := by     intro i j hij     have h_exists := exists_succ_iterate_of_le hij     obtain ⟨n, hn_eq, hn_lt_ne⟩ : ∃ n, succ^[n] i = j ∧ ∀ m < n, succ^[m] i ≠ j :=       ⟨Nat.find h_exists, Nat.find_spec h_exists, fun m hmn ↦ Nat.find_min h_exists hmn⟩     refine ⟨n, ?_⟩     rw [← hn_eq]     induction' n with n     · simp only [Nat.zero_eq, Function.iterate_zero, id]     · rw [pred_succ_iterate_of_not_isMax]       rw [Nat.succ_sub_succ_eq_sub, tsub_zero]       suffices succ^[n] i < succ^[n.succ] i from not_isMax_of_lt this       refine lt_of_le_of_ne ?_ ?_       · rw [Function.iterate_succ']         exact le_succ _       · rw [hn_eq]         exact hn_lt_ne _ (Nat.lt_succ_self n)

IsUpperSet.code: IsUpperSet.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] (s : Set α) : Prop
IsUpperSet.comment:
An upper set in an order `α` is a set such that any element greater than one of its members is
also a member. Also called up-set, upward-closed set.
IsUpperSet.fullDefinition: def IsUpperSet (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃a b : α⦄, a ≤ b → a ∈ s → b ∈ s
IsUpperSet.description: An upper set in an ordered structure is defined as a set such that if it contains an element, then it also contains all elements that are greater than that element.

IsLowerSet.code: IsLowerSet.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [LE α] (s : Set α) : Prop
IsLowerSet.comment:
A lower set in an order `α` is a set such that any element less than one of its members is also
a member. Also called down-set, downward-closed set.
IsLowerSet.fullDefinition: def IsLowerSet (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃a b : α⦄, b ≤ a → a ∈ s → b ∈ s
IsLowerSet.description: A lower set in an ordered structure is defined as a set such that if it contains an element, it also contains all elements that are less than that element.

ClosureOperator.conjBy.fullDefinition: def conjBy {α β} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (c : ClosureOperator α)     (e : α ≃o β) : ClosureOperator β where   toFun := e.conj c   IsClosed b := c.IsClosed (e.symm b)   monotone' _ _ h :=     (map_le_map_iff e).mpr <| c.monotone <| (map_le_map_iff e.symm).mpr h   le_closure' _ := e.symm_apply_le.mp (c.le_closure' _)   idempotent' _ :=     congrArg e <| Eq.trans (congrArg c (e.symm_apply_apply _)) (c.idempotent' _)   isClosed_iff := Iff.trans c.isClosed_iff e.eq_symm_apply
ClosureOperator.conjBy.description: This definition constructs a closure operator on one type using an existing closure operator on another type, related by an order-isomorphism.

IsWellOrder.conditionallyCompleteLinearO.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev IsWellOrder.conditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot (α : Type*)   [i₁ : _root_.LinearOrder α] [i₂ : OrderBot α] [h : IsWellOrder α (· < ·)] :     ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot α :=   { i₁, i₂, LinearOrder.toLattice with     sInf := fun s => if hs : s.Nonempty then h.wf.min s hs else ⊥     csInf_le := fun s a _ has => by       have s_ne : s.Nonempty := ⟨a, has⟩       simpa [s_ne] using not_lt.1 (h.wf.not_lt_min s s_ne has)     le_csInf := fun s a hs has => by       simp only [hs, dif_pos]       exact has (h.wf.min_mem s hs)     sSup := fun s => if hs : (upperBounds s).Nonempty then h.wf.min _ hs else ⊥     le_csSup := fun s a hs has => by       have h's : (upperBounds s).Nonempty := hs       simp only [h's, dif_pos]       exact h.wf.min_mem _ h's has     csSup_le := fun s a _ has => by       have h's : (upperBounds s).Nonempty := ⟨a, has⟩       simp only [h's, dif_pos]       simpa using h.wf.not_lt_min _ h's has     csSup_empty := by simpa using eq_bot_iff.2 (not_lt.1 <| h.wf.not_lt_min _ _ <| mem_univ ⊥)     csSup_of_not_bddAbove := by       intro s H       have B : ¬((upperBounds s).Nonempty) := H       simp only [B, dite_false, upperBounds_empty, univ_nonempty, dite_true]       exact le_antisymm bot_le (WellFounded.min_le _ (mem_univ _))     csInf_of_not_bddBelow := fun s H ↦ (H (OrderBot.bddBelow s)).elim }

conditionallyCompleteLatticeOfsSup.fullDefinition: def conditionallyCompleteLatticeOfsSup (α : Type*) [H1 : PartialOrder α] [H2 : SupSet α]     (bddAbove_pair : ∀ a b : α, BddAbove ({a, b} : Set α))     (bddBelow_pair : ∀ a b : α, BddBelow ({a, b} : Set α))     (isLUB_sSup : ∀ s : Set α, BddAbove s → s.Nonempty → IsLUB s (sSup s)) :     ConditionallyCompleteLattice α :=   { H1, H2 with     sup := fun a b => sSup {a, b}     le_sup_left := fun a b =>       (isLUB_sSup {a, b} (bddAbove_pair a b) (insert_nonempty _ _)).1 (mem_insert _ _)     le_sup_right := fun a b =>       (isLUB_sSup {a, b} (bddAbove_pair a b) (insert_nonempty _ _)).1         (mem_insert_of_mem _ (mem_singleton _))     sup_le := fun a b _ hac hbc =>       (isLUB_sSup {a, b} (bddAbove_pair a b) (insert_nonempty _ _)).2         (forall_insert_of_forall (forall_eq.mpr hbc) hac)     inf := fun a b => sSup (lowerBounds {a, b})     inf_le_left := fun a b =>       (isLUB_sSup (lowerBounds {a, b}) (Nonempty.bddAbove_lowerBounds ⟨a, mem_insert _ _⟩)             (bddBelow_pair a b)).2         fun _ hc => hc <| mem_insert _ _     inf_le_right := fun a b =>       (isLUB_sSup (lowerBounds {a, b}) (Nonempty.bddAbove_lowerBounds ⟨a, mem_insert _ _⟩)             (bddBelow_pair a b)).2         fun _ hc => hc <| mem_insert_of_mem _ (mem_singleton _)     le_inf := fun c a b hca hcb =>       (isLUB_sSup (lowerBounds {a, b}) (Nonempty.bddAbove_lowerBounds ⟨a, mem_insert _ _⟩)             ⟨c, forall_insert_of_forall (forall_eq.mpr hcb) hca⟩).1         (forall_insert_of_forall (forall_eq.mpr hcb) hca)     sInf := fun s => sSup (lowerBounds s)     csSup_le := fun s a hs ha => (isLUB_sSup s ⟨a, ha⟩ hs).2 ha     le_csSup := fun s a hs ha => (isLUB_sSup s hs ⟨a, ha⟩).1 ha     csInf_le := fun s a hs ha =>       (isLUB_sSup (lowerBounds s) (Nonempty.bddAbove_lowerBounds ⟨a, ha⟩) hs).2 fun _ hb => hb ha     le_csInf := fun s a hs ha =>       (isLUB_sSup (lowerBounds s) hs.bddAbove_lowerBounds ⟨a, ha⟩).1 ha }

conditionallyCompleteLatticeOfsInf.fullDefinition: def conditionallyCompleteLatticeOfsInf (α : Type*) [H1 : PartialOrder α] [H2 : InfSet α]     (bddAbove_pair : ∀ a b : α, BddAbove ({a, b} : Set α))     (bddBelow_pair : ∀ a b : α, BddBelow ({a, b} : Set α))     (isGLB_sInf : ∀ s : Set α, BddBelow s → s.Nonempty → IsGLB s (sInf s)) :     ConditionallyCompleteLattice α :=   { H1, H2 with     inf := fun a b => sInf {a, b}     inf_le_left := fun a b =>       (isGLB_sInf {a, b} (bddBelow_pair a b) (insert_nonempty _ _)).1 (mem_insert _ _)     inf_le_right := fun a b =>       (isGLB_sInf {a, b} (bddBelow_pair a b) (insert_nonempty _ _)).1         (mem_insert_of_mem _ (mem_singleton _))     le_inf := fun _ a b hca hcb =>       (isGLB_sInf {a, b} (bddBelow_pair a b) (insert_nonempty _ _)).2         (forall_insert_of_forall (forall_eq.mpr hcb) hca)     sup := fun a b => sInf (upperBounds {a, b})     le_sup_left := fun a b =>       (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds {a, b}) (Nonempty.bddBelow_upperBounds ⟨a, mem_insert _ _⟩)             (bddAbove_pair a b)).2         fun _ hc => hc <| mem_insert _ _     le_sup_right := fun a b =>       (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds {a, b}) (Nonempty.bddBelow_upperBounds ⟨a, mem_insert _ _⟩)             (bddAbove_pair a b)).2         fun _ hc => hc <| mem_insert_of_mem _ (mem_singleton _)     sup_le := fun a b c hac hbc =>       (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds {a, b}) (Nonempty.bddBelow_upperBounds ⟨a, mem_insert _ _⟩)             ⟨c, forall_insert_of_forall (forall_eq.mpr hbc) hac⟩).1         (forall_insert_of_forall (forall_eq.mpr hbc) hac)     sSup := fun s => sInf (upperBounds s)     le_csInf := fun s a hs ha => (isGLB_sInf s ⟨a, ha⟩ hs).2 ha     csInf_le := fun s a hs ha => (isGLB_sInf s hs ⟨a, ha⟩).1 ha     le_csSup := fun s a hs ha =>       (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds s) (Nonempty.bddBelow_upperBounds ⟨a, ha⟩) hs).2 fun _ hb => hb ha     csSup_le := fun s a hs ha =>       (isGLB_sInf (upperBounds s) hs.bddBelow_upperBounds ⟨a, ha⟩).1 ha }

explanatories.Antitone: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.

Monotone.ciSup_mem_iInter_Icc_of_antiton.description: The supremum of a monotone function across a sequence belongs to all intervals defined by that function and a corresponding antitone function, provided the first function is less than or equal to the second for all values in the sequence.

Pi.conditionallyCompleteLattice.fullDefinition: instance Pi.conditionallyCompleteLattice {ι : Type*} {α : ι → Type*}     [∀ i, ConditionallyCompleteLattice (α i)] : ConditionallyCompleteLattice (∀ i, α i) :=   { Pi.instLattice, Pi.supSet, Pi.infSet with     le_csSup := fun s f ⟨g, hg⟩ hf i =>       le_csSup ⟨g i, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun ⟨f', hf'⟩ => hg hf' i⟩ ⟨⟨f, hf⟩, rfl⟩     csSup_le := fun s f hs hf i =>       (csSup_le (by haveI := hs.to_subtype; apply range_nonempty)) fun b ⟨⟨g, hg⟩, hb⟩ =>         hb ▸ hf hg i     csInf_le := fun s f ⟨g, hg⟩ hf i =>       csInf_le ⟨g i, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun ⟨f', hf'⟩ => hg hf' i⟩ ⟨⟨f, hf⟩, rfl⟩     le_csInf := fun s f hs hf i =>       (le_csInf (by haveI := hs.to_subtype; apply range_nonempty)) fun b ⟨⟨g, hg⟩, hb⟩ =>         hb ▸ hf hg i }
Pi.conditionallyCompleteLattice.description: The product of a family of conditionally complete lattices forms a new conditionally complete lattice.

WithTop.WithBot.completeLattice.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance WithTop.WithBot.completeLattice {α : Type*}     [ConditionallyCompleteLattice α] : CompleteLattice (WithTop (WithBot α)) :=   { instInfSet, instSupSet, boundedOrder, lattice with     le_sSup := fun S a haS => (WithTop.isLUB_sSup' ⟨a, haS⟩).1 haS     sSup_le := fun S a ha => by       rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with h | h       · show ite _ _ _ ≤ a         split_ifs with h₁ h₂         · rw [h] at h₁           cases h₁         · convert bot_le (a := a)           -- Porting note: previous proof relied on convert unfolding           -- the definition of ⊥           apply congr_arg           simp only [h, preimage_empty, WithBot.sSup_empty]         · exfalso           apply h₂           use ⊥           rw [h]           rintro b ⟨⟩       · exact (WithTop.isLUB_sSup' h).2 ha     sInf_le := fun S a haS =>       show ite _ _ _ ≤ a by         simp only [OrderBot.bddBelow, not_true_eq_false, or_false]         split_ifs with h₁         · cases' a with a           · exact le_rfl           cases h₁ haS         · cases a           · exact le_top           · apply WithTop.coe_le_coe.2             refine csInf_le ?_ haS             use ⊥             intro b _             exact bot_le     le_sInf := fun S a haS => (WithTop.isGLB_sInf' ⟨a, haS⟩).2 haS }

explanatories.RelIso.map_rel_iff: A theorem asserting the identity function acts as a relation homomorphism while explicitly clarifying the type of its input.
explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.OrderIso.map_mem_minimals: This theorem asserts that if an element is minimal in one ordered set, its image under an order isomorphism will also be minimal in a corresponding ordered set.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.Equiv.left_inv: This theorem asserts that the inverse function of an equivalence relation is a left inverse of the original function.
explanatories.Equiv.right_inv: This theorem states that the inverse function of an equivalence relation has a right inverse that retrieves the original function.
explanatories.RelIso.map_rel_iff': Elements of a set are related if and only if their images under a relational isomorphism remain related.

OrderIso.mapMinimals.fullDefinition: def OrderIso.mapMinimals (f : s ≃o t) : minimals (· ≤ ·) s ≃o minimals (· ≤ ·) t where   toFun x := ⟨f ⟨x, x.2.1⟩, f.map_mem_minimals x.2⟩   invFun x := ⟨f.symm ⟨x, x.2.1⟩, f.symm.map_mem_minimals x.2⟩   left_inv x := Subtype.ext (by apply congr_arg Subtype.val <| f.left_inv ⟨x, x.2.1⟩)   right_inv x := Subtype.ext (by apply congr_arg Subtype.val <| f.right_inv ⟨x, x.2.1⟩)   map_rel_iff' {_ _} := f.map_rel_iff
OrderIso.mapMinimals.description: This definition states that if two sets are order isomorphic, then their minimal elements are also order isomorphic.

  {x : α} (hx : x ∈ maximals (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) s) : ↑(f ⟨x, ⋯⟩) ∈ maximals (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) t

explanatories.maximals: This defines a method to select the maximal elements from a set based on a given relation, effectively forming an antichain.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.symm: This theorem establishes that if a binary relation is symmetric, then holding the relation between two elements implies that it also holds in the reverse order between those elements.
explanatories.Ne.symm: This theorem establishes that if two elements are not equal in a type, then the inequality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is not equal to the other, the reverse is also true.
explanatories.OrderDual: A type synonym that defines a dual order for a given type, reversing the usual order relationships.
explanatories.Iff.symm: The theorem establishes that if two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.OrderDual.ofDual: A definition establishing a bijective correspondence between the dual order of a linear order and the original linear order.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.
explanatories.OrderIso.mapMinimals: This definition states that if two sets are order isomorphic, then their minimal elements are also order isomorphic.
explanatories.OrderIso.map_mem_maximals: This theorem states that if there is an order isomorphism between two sets, then the image of a maximal element from one set under that isomorphism is also a maximal element in the other set.

OrderIso.mapMaximals.fullDefinition: def OrderIso.mapMaximals (f : s ≃o t) : maximals (· ≤ ·) s ≃o maximals (· ≤ ·) t where   toFun x := ⟨f ⟨x, x.2.1⟩, f.map_mem_maximals x.2⟩   invFun x := ⟨f.symm ⟨x, x.2.1⟩, f.symm.map_mem_maximals x.2⟩   __ := (show OrderDual.ofDual ⁻¹' s ≃o OrderDual.ofDual ⁻¹' t from f.dual).mapMinimals   -- defeq abuse to fill in the proof fields.   -- If OrderDual ever becomes a structure, just copy the last three lines from OrderIso.mapMinimals
OrderIso.mapMaximals.description: This definition states that if two sets are related by an order isomorphism, then their maximal elements are also related by an order isomorphism.

inter_preimage_minimals_eq_of_rel_iff_re.description: This theorem establishes that the intersection of a set with the preimage of the minimal elements of another set corresponds to the minimal elements of the original set limited to the intersection of both sets, provided a specific relationship is maintained by a function.

maximals_Iic.code: maximals_Iic.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PartialOrder α] (a : α) : maximals (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) (Iic a) = {a}

explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.

maximals_Iic.description: This theorem states that the maximal elements of the set of all elements less than or equal to a given element in a partially ordered structure are precisely the set containing that element itself.

maximals_Icc.code:
maximals_Icc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PartialOrder α] {a b : α} (hab : a ≤ b) :
  maximals (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) (Icc a b) = {b}

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

maximals_Icc.description: This theorem shows that within a closed interval defined by two elements in a partially ordered set, the maximal elements with respect to the given order relation are exactly the upper endpoint of that interval.

maximals_Ioc.code:
maximals_Ioc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PartialOrder α] {a b : α} (hab : a < b) :
  maximals (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) (Ioc a b) = {b}

explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.

maximals_Ioc.description: This theorem demonstrates that the only maximal element in the open interval between two distinct elements in a partial order is the upper endpoint of that interval.

**Zorn's lemma**

If every chain has an upper bound, then there exists a maximal element.

explanatories.Part.bind_eq_bind: This theorem states that the binding operation on a partial value using either notation yields equivalent results.
explanatories.Bind.bind: The bind operation allows for chaining operations in a context by taking a value from that context and applying a function to it that returns a new value within the same context.
explanatories.and_imp: The implication that a conjunction leads to a conclusion is equivalent to the assertion that each component of the conjunction must independently imply that conclusion.
explanatories.exists_prop: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the existence of a proof for one proposition and the conjunction of two propositions under specific conditions.
explanatories.Part.mem_bind_iff: This theorem establishes an equivalence stating that an element belongs to the result of binding a partial value with a function if and only if there exists an element in the original partial value that maps to that element under the function.
explanatories.exists_imp: This theorem establishes that the existence of an element satisfying a property implies a statement is equivalent to the universal condition that if any such element exists, then the statement must also hold.
explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.
explanatories.And.intro: The constructor for the "And" operation combines two propositions into a single proposition that asserts both are true.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone: This theorem asserts that any order homomorphism between two preordered types is a monotone function.
explanatories.Iff.intro: This theorem establishes that two propositions are equivalent if each can be inferred from the other.

  [OmegaCompletePartialOrder β] (f : α →o β) : Prop
OmegaCompletePartialOrder.Continuous.comment:
A monotone function `f : α →o β` is continuous if it distributes over ωSup.

In order to distinguish it from the (more commonly used) continuity from topology
(see `Mathlib/Topology/Basic.lean`), the present definition is often referred to as
"Scott-continuity" (referring to Dana Scott). It corresponds to continuity
in Scott topological spaces (not defined here).

subsetConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev subsetConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder [Inhabited s]     (h_Sup : ∀ {t : Set s} (_ : t.Nonempty) (_h_bdd : BddAbove t), sSup ((↑) '' t : Set α) ∈ s)     (h_Inf : ∀ {t : Set s} (_ : t.Nonempty) (_h_bdd : BddBelow t), sInf ((↑) '' t : Set α) ∈ s) :     ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder s :=   { subsetSupSet s, subsetInfSet s, DistribLattice.toLattice, (inferInstance : LinearOrder s) with     le_csSup := by       rintro t c h_bdd hct       rw [← Subtype.coe_le_coe, ← subset_sSup_of_within s ⟨c, hct⟩ h_bdd (h_Sup ⟨c, hct⟩ h_bdd)]       exact (Subtype.mono_coe _).le_csSup_image hct h_bdd     csSup_le := by       rintro t B ht hB       rw [← Subtype.coe_le_coe, ← subset_sSup_of_within s ht ⟨B, hB⟩ (h_Sup ht ⟨B, hB⟩)]       exact (Subtype.mono_coe s).csSup_image_le ht hB     le_csInf := by       intro t B ht hB       rw [← Subtype.coe_le_coe, ← subset_sInf_of_within s ht ⟨B, hB⟩ (h_Inf ht ⟨B, hB⟩)]       exact (Subtype.mono_coe s).le_csInf_image ht hB     csInf_le := by       rintro t c h_bdd hct       rw [← Subtype.coe_le_coe, ← subset_sInf_of_within s ⟨c, hct⟩ h_bdd (h_Inf ⟨c, hct⟩ h_bdd)]       exact (Subtype.mono_coe s).csInf_image_le hct h_bdd     csSup_of_not_bddAbove := fun t ht ↦ by simp [ht]     csInf_of_not_bddBelow := fun t ht ↦ by simp [ht] }

explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.
explanatories.Set.Icc.boundedOrder: The set of all elements between two given values has a structure that is both bounded below and bounded above if the first value is less than or equal to the second.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty: A set is not nonempty if and only if it is equal to the empty set.

explanatories.le_csSup: Any element in a bounded above set is less than or equal to the supremum of that set.
explanatories.dite_true: The theorem establishes that, under a true proposition, a dependent eliminator produces a specific value corresponding to that truth instead of a value based on the negation.
explanatories.dite_false: The theorem establishes that, under a false proposition, a dependent eliminator produces a value based on the negation of that falsehood instead of a value corresponding to that falsehood.
explanatories.Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty: A set is non-empty if and only if it is not equal to the empty set.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.le_csInf: If a non-empty set contains elements that are all greater than or equal to a specific element, then that element is also less than or equal to the infimum of the set.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.csInf_le: In a conditionally complete lattice, the infimum of a set is less than or equal to any element within that set if the set is bounded below.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.le_sSup: This theorem states that if an element belongs to a set, then it is less than or equal to the supremum of that set in a complete semilattice.
explanatories.sSup_le: This theorem asserts that if every element of a set is less than or equal to a certain value, then the supremum of that set is also less than or equal to that value in a complete semilattice.

Set.Icc.completeLattice.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Set.Icc.completeLattice [ConditionallyCompleteLattice α]     {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : CompleteLattice (Set.Icc a b) where   __ := Set.Icc.boundedOrder h   sSup S := if hS : S = ∅ then ⟨a, le_rfl, h⟩ else ⟨sSup ((↑) '' S), by     rw [← Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty, not_not] at hS     refine ⟨?_, csSup_le (hS.image (↑)) (fun _ ⟨c, _, hc⟩ ↦ hc ▸ c.2.2)⟩     obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hS     exact c.2.1.trans (le_csSup ⟨b, fun _ ⟨d, _, hd⟩ ↦ hd ▸ d.2.2⟩ ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩)⟩   le_sSup S c hc := by     by_cases hS : S = ∅ <;> simp only [hS, dite_true, dite_false]     · simp [hS] at hc     · exact le_csSup ⟨b, fun _ ⟨d, _, hd⟩ ↦ hd ▸ d.2.2⟩ ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩   sSup_le S c hc := by     by_cases hS : S = ∅ <;> simp only [hS, dite_true, dite_false]     · exact c.2.1     · exact csSup_le ((Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr hS).image (↑))         (fun _ ⟨d, h, hd⟩ ↦ hd ▸ hc d h)   sInf S := if hS : S = ∅ then ⟨b, h, le_rfl⟩ else ⟨sInf ((↑) '' S), by     rw [← Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty, not_not] at hS     refine ⟨le_csInf (hS.image (↑)) (fun _ ⟨c, _, hc⟩ ↦ hc ▸ c.2.1), ?_⟩     obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hS     exact le_trans (csInf_le ⟨a, fun _ ⟨d, _, hd⟩ ↦ hd ▸ d.2.1⟩ ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩) c.2.2⟩   sInf_le S c hc := by     by_cases hS : S = ∅ <;> simp only [hS, dite_true, dite_false]     · simp [hS] at hc     · exact csInf_le ⟨a, fun _ ⟨d, _, hd⟩ ↦ hd ▸ d.2.1⟩ ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩   le_sInf S c hc := by     by_cases hS : S = ∅ <;> simp only [hS, dite_true, dite_false]     · exact c.2.2     · exact le_csInf ((Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr hS).image (↑))         (fun _ ⟨d, h, hd⟩ ↦ hd ▸ hc d h)

IsSimpleOrder.completeBooleanAlgebra.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def completeBooleanAlgebra : CompleteBooleanAlgebra α :=   { __ := IsSimpleOrder.completeLattice     __ := IsSimpleOrder.booleanAlgebra     iInf_sup_le_sup_sInf := fun x s => by       rcases eq_bot_or_eq_top x with (rfl | rfl)       · simp [bot_sup_eq, ← sInf_eq_iInf]       · simp only [top_le_iff, top_sup_eq, iInf_top, le_sInf_iff, le_refl]     inf_sSup_le_iSup_inf := fun x s => by       rcases eq_bot_or_eq_top x with (rfl | rfl)       · simp only [le_bot_iff, sSup_eq_bot, bot_inf_eq, iSup_bot, le_refl]       · simp only [top_inf_eq, ← sSup_eq_iSup]         exact le_rfl }

RelSeries.append.fullDefinition: def append (p q : RelSeries r) (connect : r p.last q.head) : RelSeries r where   length := p.length + q.length + 1   toFun := Fin.append p q ∘ Fin.cast (by abel)   step i := by     obtain hi | rfl | hi :=       lt_trichotomy i (Fin.castLE (by omega) (Fin.last _ : Fin (p.length + 1)))     · convert p.step ⟨i.1, hi⟩ <;> convert Fin.append_left p q _ <;> rfl     · convert connect       · convert Fin.append_left p q _       · convert Fin.append_right p q _; rfl     · set x := _; set y := _       change r (Fin.append p q x) (Fin.append p q y)       have hx : x = Fin.natAdd _ ⟨i - (p.length + 1), Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add hi <|           i.2.trans <| by omega⟩ := by         ext; dsimp [x, y]; rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel']; exact hi       have hy : y = Fin.natAdd _ ⟨i - p.length, Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add (le_of_lt hi)           (by exact i.2)⟩ := by         ext         dsimp         conv_rhs => rw [Nat.add_comm p.length 1, add_assoc,           Nat.add_sub_cancel' <| le_of_lt (show p.length < i.1 from hi), add_comm]         rfl       rw [hx, Fin.append_right, hy, Fin.append_right]       convert q.step ⟨i - (p.length + 1), Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add hi <|         by convert i.2 using 1; abel⟩       rw [Fin.succ_mk, Nat.sub_eq_iff_eq_add (le_of_lt hi : p.length ≤ i),         Nat.add_assoc _ 1, add_comm 1, Nat.sub_add_cancel]       exact hi

RelSeries.smash.fullDefinition: def smash (p q : RelSeries r) (connect : p.last = q.head) : RelSeries r where   length := p.length + q.length   toFun i :=     if H : i.1 < p.length     then p ⟨i.1, H.trans (lt_add_one _)⟩     else q ⟨i.1 - p.length,       Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add (by rwa [not_lt] at H) (by rw [← add_assoc]; exact i.2)⟩   step i := by     dsimp only     by_cases h₂ : i.1 + 1 < p.length     · have h₁ : i.1 < p.length := lt_trans (lt_add_one _) h₂       erw [dif_pos h₁, dif_pos h₂]       convert p.step ⟨i, h₁⟩ using 1     · erw [dif_neg h₂]       by_cases h₁ : i.1 < p.length       · erw [dif_pos h₁]         have h₃ : p.length = i.1 + 1 := by omega         convert p.step ⟨i, h₁⟩ using 1         convert connect.symm         · aesop         · congr; aesop       · erw [dif_neg h₁]         convert q.step ⟨i.1 - p.length, _⟩ using 1         · congr           change (i.1 + 1) - _ = _           rw [Nat.sub_add_comm]           rwa [not_lt] at h₁         · refine Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add ?_ i.2           rwa [not_lt] at h₁
