Lattice.copy.fullDefinition: def Lattice.copy (c : Lattice α)     (le : α → α → Prop) (eq_le : le = (by infer_instance : LE α).le)     (sup : α → α → α) (eq_sup : sup = (by infer_instance : Sup α).sup)     (inf : α → α → α) (eq_inf : inf = (by infer_instance : Inf α).inf) : Lattice α where   le := le   sup := sup   inf := inf   lt := fun a b ↦ le a b ∧ ¬ le b a   le_refl := by intros; simp [eq_le]   le_trans := by intro _ _ _ hab hbc; rw [eq_le] at hab hbc ⊢; exact le_trans hab hbc   le_antisymm := by intro _ _ hab hba; simp_rw [eq_le] at hab hba; exact le_antisymm hab hba   le_sup_left := by intros; simp [eq_le, eq_sup]   le_sup_right := by intros; simp [eq_le, eq_sup]   sup_le := by intro _ _ _ hac hbc; simp_rw [eq_le] at hac hbc ⊢; simp [eq_sup, hac, hbc]   inf_le_left := by intros; simp [eq_le, eq_inf]   inf_le_right := by intros; simp [eq_le, eq_inf]   le_inf := by intro _ _ _ hac hbc; simp_rw [eq_le] at hac hbc ⊢; simp [eq_inf, hac, hbc]

WellFounded.wellOrderExtension.code: WellFounded.wellOrderExtension.{u} {α : Type u} {r : α → α → Prop} (hwf : WellFounded r) : LinearOrder α
WellFounded.wellOrderExtension.comment:
An arbitrary well order on `α` that extends `r`.

The construction maps `r` into two well-orders: the first map is `WellFounded.rank`, which is not
necessarily injective but respects the order `r`; the other map is the identity (with an arbitrarily
chosen well-order on `α`), which is injective but doesn't respect `r`.

By taking the lexicographic product of the two, we get both properties, so we can pull it back and
get a well-order that extend our original order `r`. Another way to view this is that we choose an
arbitrary well-order to serve as a tiebreak between two elements of same rank.

explanatories.embeddingToCardinal: This definition establishes an embedding that associates any type with the set of cardinal numbers.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.injective: An embedding is shown to be injective, ensuring that different inputs yield different outputs when mapped to another set.

IsOrderRightAdjoint.code: IsOrderRightAdjoint.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) (g : β → α) : Prop
IsOrderRightAdjoint.comment:
We say that `g : β → α` is an order right adjoint function for `f : α → β` if it sends each `y`
to a least upper bound for `{x | f x ≤ y}`. If `α` is a partial order, and `f : α → β` has
a right adjoint, then this right adjoint is unique.

explanatories.IsLUB: This definition characterizes an element as the least upper bound of a set if it is an upper bound for the set and no other upper bound is smaller than it within a preorder structure.

IsOrderRightAdjoint.fullDefinition: def IsOrderRightAdjoint [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) (g : β → α) :=   ∀ y, IsLUB { x | f x ≤ y } (g y)
IsOrderRightAdjoint.description: This definition characterizes a function as a right adjoint if it maps each element from one ordered set to the least upper bound of elements from another set that are related by a given function.

Function.Semiconj.symm_adjoint.code:
Function.Semiconj.symm_adjoint.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [PartialOrder α] [Preorder β] {fa : α ≃o α}
  {fb : β ↪o β} {g : α → β} (h : Semiconj g ⇑fa ⇑fb) {g' : β → α} (hg' : IsOrderRightAdjoint g g') : Semiconj g' ⇑fb ⇑fa
Function.Semiconj.symm_adjoint.comment:
If an order automorphism `fa` is semiconjugate to an order embedding `fb` by a function `g`
and `g'` is an order right adjoint of `g` (i.e. `g' y = sSup {x | f x ≤ y}`), then `fb` is
semiconjugate to `fa` by `g'`.

This is a version of Proposition 2.1 from [Étienne Ghys, Groupes d'homéomorphismes du cercle et
cohomologie bornée][ghys87:groupes].

explanatories.IsOrderRightAdjoint: This definition characterizes a function as a right adjoint if it maps each element from one ordered set to the least upper bound of elements from another set that are related by a given function.

Function.Semiconj.symm_adjoint.description: This theorem states that if a function relates two ordered structures through a semiconjugation and has a right adjoint, then the right adjoint also establishes a semiconjugation between the corresponding order embeddings and automorphisms.

  {h : α → α} (H : ∀ (x : α), IsLUB (range fun g' => (f₁ g')⁻¹ ((f₂ g') x)) (h x)) (g : G) : Semiconj h ⇑(f₂ g) ⇑(f₁ g)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Function.semiconj_of_isLUB.description: This theorem states that under certain conditions involving least upper bounds, a function is semiconjugate to the image of another function when transformed by a specific relation.

Function.sSup_div_semiconj.code:
Function.sSup_div_semiconj.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {G : Type u_4} [CompleteLattice α] [Group G] (f₁ f₂ : G →* α ≃o α)
  (g : G) : Semiconj (fun x => ⨆ g', (f₁ g')⁻¹ ((f₂ g') x)) ⇑(f₂ g) ⇑(f₁ g)
Function.sSup_div_semiconj.comment:
Consider two actions `f₁ f₂ : G → α → α` of a group on a complete lattice by order
isomorphisms. Then the map `x ↦ ⨆ g : G, (f₁ g)⁻¹ (f₂ g x)` semiconjugates each `f₁ g'` to `f₂ g'`.

This is a version of Proposition 5.4 from [Étienne Ghys, Groupes d'homéomorphismes du cercle et
cohomologie bornée][ghys87:groupes].

explanatories.Function.Semiconj: A function is said to semiconjugate two mappings if applying the function before one mapping is the same as applying the other mapping after the function.

Function.sSup_div_semiconj.description: This theorem states that in the context of a complete lattice and group actions defined by order isomorphisms, a certain supremum-based function semiconjugates each group action of one isomorphism to that of another.

Function.csSup_div_semiconj.code:
Function.csSup_div_semiconj.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {G : Type u_4} [ConditionallyCompleteLattice α] [Group G]
  (f₁ f₂ : G →* α ≃o α) (hbdd : ∀ (x : α), BddAbove (range fun g => (f₁ g)⁻¹ ((f₂ g) x))) (g : G) :
  Semiconj (fun x => ⨆ g', (f₁ g')⁻¹ ((f₂ g') x)) ⇑(f₂ g) ⇑(f₁ g)
Function.csSup_div_semiconj.comment:
Consider two actions `f₁ f₂ : G → α → α` of a group on a conditionally complete lattice by order
isomorphisms. Suppose that each set $s(x)=\{f_1(g)^{-1} (f_2(g)(x)) | g \in G\}$ is bounded above.
Then the map `x ↦ sSup s(x)` semiconjugates each `f₁ g'` to `f₂ g'`.

This is a version of Proposition 5.4 from [Étienne Ghys, Groupes d'homéomorphismes du cercle et
cohomologie bornée][ghys87:groupes].

explanatories.BddAbove: This definition states that a set is considered bounded above if there exists at least one element that serves as an upper bound for all elements in the set within a preorder structure.
explanatories.Function.Semiconj: A function is said to semiconjugate two mappings if applying the function before one mapping is the same as applying the other mapping after the function.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Function.csSup_div_semiconj.description: This theorem demonstrates that under certain conditions regarding boundedness in a conditionally complete lattice, a supremum-based function semiconjugates the actions of two group elements defined by order isomorphisms.

Order.radical.comment:

This notion specializes, e.g. in the subgroup lattice of a group to the Frattini subgroup,

explanatories.IsCoatom: A coatom in a poset with a greatest element is an element that is less than the greatest element but has no other element between itself and the greatest element.

Order.idealOfCofinals.comment:
Given an element `p : P` and a family `𝒟` of cofinal subsets of a preorder `P`,
indexed by a countable type, `idealOfCofinals p 𝒟` is an ideal in `P` which
- contains `p`, according to `mem_idealOfCofinals p 𝒟`, and
- intersects every set in `𝒟`, according to `cofinal_meets_idealOfCofinals p 𝒟`.

This proves the Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma.

CompositionSeries.comment:
A `CompositionSeries X` is a finite nonempty series of elements of a
`JordanHolderLattice` such that each element is maximal inside the next. The length of a
`CompositionSeries X` is one less than the number of elements in the series.
Note that there is no stipulation that a series start from the bottom of the lattice and finish at
the top. For a composition series `s`, `s.last` is the largest element of the series,
and `s.head` is the least element.

Order.PartialIso.comment:
The type of partial order isomorphisms between `α` and `β` defined on finite subsets.
A partial order isomorphism is encoded as a finite subset of `α × β`, consisting
of pairs which should be identified.

explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.

Order.PartialIso.fullDefinition: def PartialIso : Type _ :=   { f : Finset (α × β) //     ∀ p ∈ f, ∀ q ∈ f,       cmp (Prod.fst p) (Prod.fst q) = cmp (Prod.snd p) (Prod.snd q) }
Order.PartialIso.description: A partial order isomorphism between two ordered types consists of a finite subset of pairs that identify corresponding elements in each type while preserving their order.

Order.PartialIso.exists_across.code:
Order.PartialIso.exists_across.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β]
  [DenselyOrdered β] [NoMinOrder β] [NoMaxOrder β] [Nonempty β] (f : PartialIso α β) (a : α) :
  ∃ b, ∀ p ∈ ↑f, cmp p.1 a = cmp p.2 b
Order.PartialIso.exists_across.comment:
For each `a`, we can find a `b` in the codomain, such that `a`'s relation to
the domain of `f` is `b`'s relation to the image of `f`.

Thus, if `a` is not already in `f`, then we can extend `f` by sending `a` to `b`.

explanatories.Finset.Nonempty: This definition establishes a property that denotes a finite set being non-empty, providing a convenient way to express this concept in theorem assumptions.

Order.PartialIso.exists_across.description: For every element in the domain of a partial order isomorphism between two ordered types, there exists a corresponding element in the codomain such that their relative order is preserved.

Order.PartialIso.comm.fullDefinition: protected def comm : PartialIso α β → PartialIso β α :=   Subtype.map (Finset.image (Equiv.prodComm _ _)) fun f hf p hp q hq ↦     Eq.symm <|       hf ((Equiv.prodComm α β).symm p)         (by           rw [← Finset.mem_coe, Finset.coe_image, Equiv.image_eq_preimage] at hp           rwa [← Finset.mem_coe])         ((Equiv.prodComm α β).symm q)         (by           rw [← Finset.mem_coe, Finset.coe_image, Equiv.image_eq_preimage] at hq           rwa [← Finset.mem_coe])

Order.PartialIso.definedAtLeft.fullDefinition: def definedAtLeft [DenselyOrdered β] [NoMinOrder β] [NoMaxOrder β] [Nonempty β] (a : α) :     Cofinal (PartialIso α β) where   carrier := {f | ∃ b : β, (a, b) ∈ f.val}   mem_gt f := by     cases' exists_across f a with b a_b     refine       ⟨⟨insert (a, b) f.val, fun p hp q hq ↦ ?_⟩, ⟨b, Finset.mem_insert_self _ _⟩,         Finset.subset_insert _ _⟩     rw [Finset.mem_insert] at hp hq     rcases hp with (rfl | pf) <;> rcases hq with (rfl | qf)     · simp only [cmp_self_eq_eq]     · rw [cmp_eq_cmp_symm]       exact a_b _ qf     · exact a_b _ pf     · exact f.prop _ pf _ qf

Order.PartialIso.definedAtRight.fullDefinition: def definedAtRight [DenselyOrdered α] [NoMinOrder α] [NoMaxOrder α] [Nonempty α] (b : β) :     Cofinal (PartialIso α β) where   carrier := {f | ∃ a, (a, b) ∈ f.val}   mem_gt f := by     rcases (definedAtLeft α b).mem_gt f.comm with ⟨f', ⟨a, ha⟩, hl⟩     refine ⟨f'.comm, ⟨a, ?_⟩, ?_⟩     · change (a, b) ∈ f'.val.image _       rwa [← Finset.mem_coe, Finset.coe_image, Equiv.image_eq_preimage]     · change _ ⊆ f'.val.image _       rwa [← Finset.coe_subset, Finset.coe_image, ← Equiv.symm_image_subset, ← Finset.coe_image,         Finset.coe_subset]

partialSups.code: partialSups.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] (f : ℕ → α) : ℕ →o α
partialSups.comment: The monotone sequence whose value at `n` is the supremum of the `f m` where `m ≤ n`.

explanatories.monotone_nat_of_le_succ: A function defined on natural numbers is monotone if each output is less than or equal to the next output.
explanatories.le_sup_left: The supremum of two elements serves as an upper bound for the first element.

partialSups.fullDefinition: def partialSups (f : ℕ → α) : ℕ →o α :=   ⟨@Nat.rec (fun _ => α) (f 0) fun (n : ℕ) (a : α) => a ⊔ f (n + 1),     monotone_nat_of_le_succ fun _ => le_sup_left⟩
partialSups.description: This definition describes a function that produces a monotone sequence where each term is the supremum of the values of a given function up to that term's index.

partialSups_zero.code: partialSups_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] (f : ℕ → α) : (partialSups f) 0 = f 0
partialSups_zero.description: The theorem states that the first term of the monotone sequence produced by the defined function is equal to the value of the original function at zero.

partialSups_succ.code:
partialSups_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] (f : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) :
  (partialSups f) (n + 1) = (partialSups f) n ⊔ f (n + 1)
partialSups_succ.description: The theorem asserts that the next term in the monotone sequence is equal to the supremum of the current term and the value of the original function at the next index.

partialSups_iff_forall.code:
partialSups_iff_forall.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] {f : ℕ → α} (p : α → Prop)
  (hp : ∀ {a b : α}, p (a ⊔ b) ↔ p a ∧ p b) {n : ℕ} : p ((partialSups f) n) ↔ ∀ k ≤ n, p (f k)
partialSups_iff_forall.description: The theorem establishes an equivalence that relates a property of the terms in the monotone sequence to the property being satisfied by all values of the original function up to the current index.

partialSups_le_iff.code:
partialSups_le_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] {f : ℕ → α} {n : ℕ} {a : α} :
  (partialSups f) n ≤ a ↔ ∀ k ≤ n, f k ≤ a
partialSups_le_iff.description: The theorem establishes a condition in which a term in the monotone sequence is less than or equal to a value if and only if all preceding terms from the original function do not exceed that value.

le_partialSups_of_le.code: le_partialSups_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] (f : ℕ → α) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : f m ≤ (partialSups f) n
le_partialSups_of_le.description: The theorem states that if one index is less than or equal to another, then the value of the original function at the first index is less than or equal to the corresponding term in the monotone sequence generated by the function at the second index.

le_partialSups.code: le_partialSups.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [SemilatticeSup α] (f : ℕ → α) : f ≤ ⇑(partialSups f)
le_partialSups.description: The theorem states that the values of the original function are always less than or equal to the corresponding terms in the monotone sequence derived from it.

partialSups_le.code:

partialSups_le.description: The theorem asserts that if all terms of a monotone sequence up to a certain index are less than or equal to a value, then the corresponding term in the generated sequence is also less than or equal to that value.

partialSups.gi.fullDefinition: def partialSups.gi : GaloisInsertion (partialSups : (ℕ → α) → ℕ →o α) (↑) where   choice f h :=     ⟨f, by convert (partialSups f).monotone using 1; exact (le_partialSups f).antisymm h⟩   gc f g := by     refine ⟨(le_partialSups f).trans, fun h => ?_⟩     convert partialSups_mono h     exact OrderHom.ext _ _ g.monotone.partialSups_eq.symm   le_l_u f := le_partialSups f   choice_eq f h := OrderHom.ext _ _ ((le_partialSups f).antisymm h)
partialSups.gi.description: The definition indicates that the process of forming partial suprema forms a Galois insertion in conjunction with the coercion from monotone functions to functions.

Mathlib.Tactic.filterUpwards.comment:
`filter_upwards [h₁, ⋯, hₙ]` replaces a goal of the form `s ∈ f` and terms
`h₁ : t₁ ∈ f, ⋯, hₙ : tₙ ∈ f` with `∀ x, x ∈ t₁ → ⋯ → x ∈ tₙ → x ∈ s`.
The list is an optional parameter, `[]` being its default value.

`filter_upwards [h₁, ⋯, hₙ] with a₁ a₂ ⋯ aₖ` is a short form for
`{ filter_upwards [h₁, ⋯, hₙ], intros a₁ a₂ ⋯ aₖ }`.

`filter_upwards [h₁, ⋯, hₙ] using e` is a short form for
`{ filter_upwards [h1, ⋯, hn], exact e }`.

Combining both shortcuts is done by writing `filter_upwards [h₁, ⋯, hₙ] with a₁ a₂ ⋯ aₖ using e`.
Note that in this case, the `aᵢ` terms can be used in `e`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.eventually_of_mem.description: A theorem stating that if a set is in a filter and every element of that set satisfies a property, then that property holds for all but a finite number of elements in the filter.

Filter.Eventually.and.code:
Filter.Eventually.and.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} :
  Filter.Eventually p f → Filter.Eventually q f → ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∧ q x
Filter.Eventually.and.description: A theorem stating that if two properties hold eventually with respect to a filter, then their conjunction also holds eventually with respect to that filter.

Filter.eventually_true.code: Filter.eventually_true.{u} {α : Type u} (f : Filter α) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, True
Filter.eventually_true.description: A theorem asserting that within any filter, it holds that almost every element satisfies a universally true condition.

Filter.eventually_of_forall.code: Filter.eventually_of_forall.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∀ (x : α), p x) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x
Filter.eventually_of_forall.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds for all elements in a type, then it holds for almost all elements with respect to a given filter.

Filter.eventually_false_iff_eq_bot.code: Filter.eventually_false_iff_eq_bot.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, False) ↔ f = ⊥
Filter.eventually_false_iff_eq_bot.description: A theorem stating that a filter is equal to the trivial filter if and only if it eventually contains no elements.

Filter.eventually_const.code: Filter.eventually_const.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [t : f.NeBot] {p : Prop} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p) ↔ p
Filter.eventually_const.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds eventually in a non-empty filter, then that property must hold universally.

Filter.eventually_iff_exists_mem.code:
Filter.eventually_iff_exists_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ↔ ∃ v ∈ f, ∀ y ∈ v, p y
Filter.eventually_iff_exists_mem.description: A theorem establishing that a property eventually holds for a filter if and only if there exists a subset within the filter where the property holds for all its elements.

Filter.Eventually.exists_mem.code:
Filter.Eventually.exists_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) :
  ∃ v ∈ f, ∀ y ∈ v, p y
Filter.Eventually.exists_mem.description: A theorem asserting that if a property holds for most elements in a filter, then there exists a set within that filter where the property holds for all its elements.

Filter.Eventually.mp.code:
Filter.Eventually.mp.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hq : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x → q x) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x

explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.

Filter.Eventually.mp.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a filter and another property holds for almost all those elements that satisfy the first property, then the second property also holds for almost all elements in the filter.

Filter.Eventually.mono.code:
Filter.Eventually.mono.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hq : ∀ (x : α), p x → q x) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x

explanatories.Filter.NeBot.mono: A theorem stating that if one filter is non-empty and is less than or equal to another filter, then the second filter is also non-empty.
explanatories.Disjoint.mono: If one element in a lattice is disjoint from another, then a smaller element is disjoint from a smaller element, provided their respective order relations hold.

Filter.Eventually.mono.description: A theorem that states if a property holds for a filter and implies another property, then the latter property also holds for that filter.

Filter.forall_eventually_of_eventually_f.code:
Filter.forall_eventually_of_eventually_forall.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {f : Filter α} {p : α → β → Prop}
  (h : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, ∀ (y : β), p x y) (y : β) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x y
Filter.forall_eventually_of_eventually_f.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements of a filter for any element in a second type, then it also holds for that specific element for almost all elements in the filter.

Filter.eventually_and.code:
Filter.eventually_and.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∧ q x) ↔ (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∧ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.eventually_and.description: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements with respect to a filter if and only if both component properties hold for almost all elements.

Filter.Eventually.congr.code:
Filter.Eventually.congr.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p q : α → Prop} (h' : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (h : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ↔ q x) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.Eventually.congr.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a filter and another property is equivalent to the first for almost all those elements, then the second property also holds for almost all elements in the same filter.

Filter.eventually_congr.code:
Filter.eventually_congr.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ↔ q x) :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.eventually_congr.description: A theorem stating that if two properties are equivalent for almost all elements of a filter, then the occurrence of one property almost everywhere is equivalent to the occurrence of the other property almost everywhere.

Filter.eventually_all.code:
Filter.eventually_all.{u, u_2} {α : Type u} {ι : Sort u_2} [Finite ι] {l : Filter α} {p : ι → α → Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, ∀ (i : ι), p i x) ↔ ∀ (i : ι), ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p i x

explanatories.Set.Finite: A set is considered finite if there exists a natural number that demonstrates its equivalence to a finite set of natural numbers.
explanatories.ite: This defines a function that implements an "if-then-else" conditional structure, returning one of two values based on the truth of a given decidable proposition.

Filter.eventually_all.description: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements with respect to a filter for all indices if and only if it holds for each index with almost all elements in the same filter.

Filter.eventually_all_finite.code:
Filter.eventually_all_finite.{u, u_2} {α : Type u} {ι : Type u_2} {I : Set ι} (hI : I.Finite) {l : Filter α}
  {p : ι → α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, ∀ i ∈ I, p i x) ↔ ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p i x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.eventually_all_finite.description: A theorem asserting that a property holds for all elements of a finite set with respect to a filter if and only if it holds for each individual element of that set in the same filter.

Set.Finite.eventually_all.code:
Set.Finite.eventually_all.{u, u_2} {α : Type u} {ι : Type u_2} {I : Set ι} (hI : I.Finite) {l : Filter α}
  {p : ι → α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, ∀ i ∈ I, p i x) ↔ ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p i x

explanatories.Filter.eventually_all: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements with respect to a filter for all indices if and only if it holds for each index with almost all elements in the same filter.

Set.Finite.eventually_all.description: A theorem stating that for a finite set of indices, a property holding for all elements in a filter is equivalent to each individual index having the property eventually in that filter.

Filter.eventually_all_finset.code:
Filter.eventually_all_finset.{u, u_2} {α : Type u} {ι : Type u_2} (I : Finset ι) {l : Filter α} {p : ι → α → Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, ∀ i ∈ I, p i x) ↔ ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p i x
Filter.eventually_all_finset.description: A theorem that establishes an equivalence between the eventual truth of a property for all elements in a finite set with respect to a filter and the eventual truth of that property for each individual element in the finite set with respect to the same filter.

Finset.eventually_all.code:
Finset.eventually_all.{u, u_2} {α : Type u} {ι : Type u_2} (I : Finset ι) {l : Filter α} {p : ι → α → Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, ∀ i ∈ I, p i x) ↔ ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p i x

explanatories.Filter.eventually_all: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements with respect to a filter for all indices if and only if it holds for each index with almost all elements in the same filter.
explanatories.Set.Finite.eventually_all: A theorem stating that for a finite set of indices, a property holding for all elements in a filter is equivalent to each individual index having the property eventually in that filter.

Finset.eventually_all.description: A theorem stating that a property holds for all elements related by a finite set if and only if it holds uniformly for each of those elements within the specified filter.

Filter.eventually_or_distrib_left.code:
Filter.eventually_or_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : Prop} {q : α → Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x) ↔ p ∨ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.eventually_or_distrib_left.description: A theorem stating that a filter eventually satisfies the disjunction of a proposition and a property if and only if the proposition holds or the filter eventually satisfies the property for all elements.

Filter.eventually_or_distrib_right.code:
Filter.eventually_or_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : α → Prop} {q : Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∨ q) ↔ (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∨ q
Filter.eventually_or_distrib_right.description: A theorem stating that the event of a filter eventually satisfying either a property or a proposition is equivalent to the filter eventually satisfying the property or the proposition being true unconditionally.

Filter.eventually_imp_distrib_left.code:
Filter.eventually_imp_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : Prop} {q : α → Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p → q x) ↔ p → ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.eventually_imp_distrib_left.description: A theorem asserting that if a property eventually holds under a filter when a condition is satisfied, then that condition implies the property eventually holds for all elements of the filter.

Filter.eventually_bot.code: Filter.eventually_bot.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in ⊥, p x
Filter.eventually_bot.description: A theorem stating that every property holds for all elements in the bottom filter.

Filter.eventually_top.code: Filter.eventually_top.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in ⊤, p x) ↔ ∀ (x : α), p x
Filter.eventually_top.description: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements in the top filter if and only if it holds for all elements.

Filter.eventually_sup.code:
Filter.eventually_sup.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f g : Filter α} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f ⊔ g, p x) ↔ (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∧ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in g, p x
Filter.eventually_sup.description: A theorem that states that a property holds for almost all elements in the union of two filters if and only if it holds for almost all elements in each individual filter.

Filter.eventually_sSup.code:
Filter.eventually_sSup.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {fs : Set (Filter α)} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in sSup fs, p x) ↔ ∀ f ∈ fs, ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Filter.eventually_sSup.description: A theorem asserting that a property holds for almost all elements in the supremum of a set of filters if and only if it holds for almost all elements in each filter of that set.

Filter.eventually_iSup.code:
Filter.eventually_iSup.{u, x} {α : Type u} {ι : Sort x} {p : α → Prop} {fs : ι → Filter α} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in ⨆ b, fs b, p x) ↔ ∀ (b : ι), ∀ᶠ (x : α) in fs b, p x
Filter.eventually_iSup.description: A theorem stating that a property holds eventually with respect to the supremum of a collection of filters if and only if it holds eventually with respect to each individual filter in that collection.

Filter.eventually_principal.code: Filter.eventually_principal.{u} {α : Type u} {a : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in 𝓟 a, p x) ↔ ∀ x ∈ a, p x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.eventually_principal.description: A theorem that asserts a property holds for almost all elements in a principal filter generated by a set if and only if it holds for all elements within that set.

Filter.eventually_inf.code:
Filter.eventually_inf.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : Filter α} {p : α → Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f ⊓ g, p x) ↔ ∃ s ∈ f, ∃ t ∈ g, ∀ x ∈ s ∩ t, p x
Filter.eventually_inf.description: A theorem that states a property holds for elements in the intersection of two filters if and only if there exist sets from each filter whose intersection satisfies that property.

Filter.eventually_inf_principal.code:
Filter.eventually_inf_principal.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : α → Prop} {s : Set α} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f ⊓ 𝓟 s, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, x ∈ s → p x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.eventually_inf_principal.description: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements in the intersection of a filter and the filter generated by a set if and only if it holds for almost all elements in the filter, given that those elements belong to the set.

Filter.Frequently.code: Filter.Frequently.{u} {α : Type u} (p : α → Prop) (f : Filter α) : Prop
Filter.Frequently.comment:
`f.Frequently p` or `∃ᶠ x in f, p x` mean that `{x | ¬p x} ∉ f`. E.g., `∃ᶠ x in atTop, p x`
means that there exist arbitrarily large `x` for which `p` holds true.
Filter.Frequently.fullDefinition: protected def Frequently (p : α → Prop) (f : Filter α) : Prop :=   ¬∀ᶠ x in f, ¬p x
Filter.Frequently.description: A definition characterizing a property that a predicate holds frequently for elements in a given filter.

Filter.«term∃ᶠ_In_,_».description: A definition that specifies a parser description for a particular construction related to filters in the Lean4 proof assistant.

Filter.«term∃ᶠ_In_,_».delab.description: A definition for a pretty printer that formats a specific notation related to filters in a way suitable for display.

Filter.Eventually.frequently.code:
Filter.Eventually.frequently.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : α → Prop} (h : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) :
  ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x
Filter.Eventually.frequently.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds frequently with respect to a filter, then there exists a set of elements in that filter where the property continues to hold frequently.

Filter.frequently_of_forall.code:
Filter.frequently_of_forall.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : α → Prop} (h : ∀ (x : α), p x) :
  ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x
Filter.frequently_of_forall.description: If a property holds for every element in a given filter, then it holds for a frequent (non-empty) subset of that filter.

Filter.Frequently.mp.code:
Filter.Frequently.mp.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (h : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hpq : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x → q x) : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x

explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.mp: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a filter and another property holds for almost all those elements that satisfy the first property, then the second property also holds for almost all elements in the filter.

Filter.Frequently.mp.description: A theorem demonstrating that if a property holds frequently in a filter and frequently implies another property, then the second property also holds frequently in that filter.

Filter.Frequently.filter_mono.code:
Filter.Frequently.filter_mono.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f g : Filter α} (h : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hle : f ≤ g) : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in g, p x

explanatories.Filter.Eventually.filter_mono: A theorem stating that if one filter is less than or equal to another and a property holds for almost all elements in the larger filter, then it also holds for almost all elements in the smaller filter.

Filter.Frequently.filter_mono.description: A theorem that establishes that if a property frequently holds in one filter and that filter is less than or equal to another filter, then the property also frequently holds in the second filter.

Filter.Frequently.mono.code:
Filter.Frequently.mono.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (h : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hpq : ∀ (x : α), p x → q x) : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x

explanatories.Filter.NeBot.mono: A theorem stating that if one filter is non-empty and is less than or equal to another filter, then the second filter is also non-empty.
explanatories.Disjoint.mono: If one element in a lattice is disjoint from another, then a smaller element is disjoint from a smaller element, provided their respective order relations hold.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.mono: A theorem that states if a property holds for a filter and implies another property, then the latter property also holds for that filter.

Filter.Frequently.mono.description: A theorem that shows if a property holds frequently in a filter and any element satisfying that property also satisfies a second property, then the second property also holds frequently in the same filter.

Filter.Frequently.and_eventually.code:
Filter.Frequently.and_eventually.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hq : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x) : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∧ q x
Filter.Frequently.and_eventually.description: A theorem asserting that if a property holds frequently for a filter and another property holds eventually for the same filter, then there exists a set of elements for which both properties hold frequently.

Filter.Eventually.and_frequently.code:
Filter.Eventually.and_frequently.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x)
  (hq : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x) : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∧ q x
Filter.Eventually.and_frequently.description: A theorem asserting that if a property holds for sufficiently many elements in a filter and another property holds for infinitely many elements in the same filter, then both properties must hold together for sufficiently many elements as well.

Filter.Frequently.exists.code: Filter.Frequently.exists.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} (hp : ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) : ∃ x, p x

explanatories.Subtype.exists: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the existence of an element satisfying a certain property and the existence of a pair of elements from a subtype of those that satisfy the property.
explanatories.Function.Surjective.exists: This is an empty statement with no content to convey.

Filter.Frequently.exists.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds frequently in a filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property is true.

Filter.Eventually.exists.code: Filter.Eventually.exists.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] (hp : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) : ∃ x, p x

explanatories.Subtype.exists: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the existence of an element satisfying a certain property and the existence of a pair of elements from a subtype of those that satisfy the property.
explanatories.Filter.Frequently.exists: A theorem stating that if a property holds frequently in a filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property is true.
explanatories.Function.Surjective.exists: This is an empty statement with no content to convey.

Filter.Eventually.exists.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a non-empty filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property holds.

Filter.frequently_iff_neBot.code:
Filter.frequently_iff_neBot.{u} {α : Type u} {l : Filter α} {p : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in l, p x) ↔ (l ⊓ 𝓟 {x | p x}).NeBot
Filter.frequently_iff_neBot.description: A theorem that establishes the equivalence between the existence of elements in a filter that satisfy a property and the filter's intersection with the principal filter generated by those elements being non-empty.

Filter.frequently_iff_forall_eventually_.code:
Filter.frequently_iff_forall_eventually_exists_and.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ↔ ∀ {q : α → Prop}, (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x) → ∃ x, p x ∧ q x
Filter.frequently_iff_forall_eventually_.description: A theorem stating that the existence of elements satisfying a property frequently within a filter is equivalent to the condition that for every property that holds frequently, there is at least one element satisfying both properties.

Filter.frequently_iff.code:
Filter.frequently_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {P : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, P x) ↔ ∀ {U : Set α}, U ∈ f → ∃ x ∈ U, P x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.frequently_iff.description: A theorem stating that the existence of frequently occurring elements in a filter corresponds to the condition that for any set in the filter, there is at least one element from that set that satisfies a given property.

Filter.not_eventually.code: Filter.not_eventually.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} : (¬∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ↔ ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, ¬p x
Filter.not_eventually.description: A theorem stating that it is not the case that a property holds for all elements of a filter if and only if there exists at least one element in the filter for which the property does not hold.

Filter.not_frequently.code: Filter.not_frequently.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f : Filter α} : (¬∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, ¬p x
Filter.not_frequently.description: A theorem that states a property does not occur frequently in a filter if and only if the property is frequently false within that same filter.

Filter.frequently_true_iff_neBot.code: Filter.frequently_true_iff_neBot.{u} {α : Type u} (f : Filter α) : (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, True) ↔ f.NeBot
Filter.frequently_true_iff_neBot.description: A theorem stating that a filter frequently contains true propositions if and only if the filter is not empty.

Filter.frequently_false.code: Filter.frequently_false.{u} {α : Type u} (f : Filter α) : ¬∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, False
Filter.frequently_false.description: A theorem stating that if a filter is used, then it cannot contain any set of elements for which a false statement occurs frequently.

Filter.frequently_const.code: Filter.frequently_const.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : Prop} : (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p) ↔ p
Filter.frequently_const.description: A theorem asserting that if a property holds frequently with respect to a non-trivial filter, then that property must be true.

Filter.frequently_or_distrib.code:
Filter.frequently_or_distrib.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p q : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∨ q x) ↔ (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∨ ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.frequently_or_distrib.description: A theorem stating that a property occurs frequently in a filter if and only if at least one of two properties occurs frequently in that filter.

Filter.frequently_or_distrib_left.code:
Filter.frequently_or_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : Prop} {q : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x) ↔ p ∨ ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.frequently_or_distrib_left.description: A theorem stating that the property of a filter containing elements satisfying either one of two conditions is equivalent to either that first condition being true or the filter containing elements that satisfy the second condition.

Filter.frequently_or_distrib_right.code:
Filter.frequently_or_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : α → Prop} {q : Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∨ q) ↔ (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∨ q
Filter.frequently_or_distrib_right.description: A theorem stating that the existence of elements in a filter satisfying either of two predicates is equivalent to the existence of elements satisfying one predicate along with the truth of the other predicate.

Filter.frequently_imp_distrib.code:
Filter.frequently_imp_distrib.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p q : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x → q x) ↔ (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) → ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.frequently_imp_distrib.description: A theorem stating that the frequent implication between two predicates in a filter is equivalent to the condition that if the first predicate is frequently true, then the second predicate is also frequently true within that filter.

Filter.frequently_imp_distrib_left.code:
Filter.frequently_imp_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : Prop} {q : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p → q x) ↔ p → ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.frequently_imp_distrib_left.description: A theorem stating that if a property holds frequently under a filter, then it implies that whenever the property is true, there is also a frequent occurrence of another related property under the same filter.

Filter.frequently_imp_distrib_right.code:
Filter.frequently_imp_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} [f.NeBot] {p : α → Prop} {q : Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x → q) ↔ (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) → q
Filter.frequently_imp_distrib_right.description: A theorem establishing an equivalence between the frequent occurrence of a property implying another property and the universal quantification of that property leading to the conclusion.

Filter.eventually_imp_distrib_right.code:
Filter.eventually_imp_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : α → Prop} {q : Prop} :
  (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x → q) ↔ (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) → q
Filter.eventually_imp_distrib_right.description: A theorem expressing that if a property holds frequently for elements of a filter, then this frequent occurrence implies another proposition.

Filter.frequently_and_distrib_left.code:
Filter.frequently_and_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : Prop} {q : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∧ q x) ↔ p ∧ ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
Filter.frequently_and_distrib_left.description: A theorem stating that a conjunction of a property with a filter condition is equivalent to the property holding and another condition being satisfied frequently within that filter.

Filter.frequently_and_distrib_right.code:
Filter.frequently_and_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {p : α → Prop} {q : Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x ∧ q) ↔ (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∧ q
Filter.frequently_and_distrib_right.description: A theorem stating that a property being frequently true alongside another condition is equivalent to that property being frequently true along with the other condition holding true separately.

Filter.frequently_bot.code: Filter.frequently_bot.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} : ¬∃ᶠ (x : α) in ⊥, p x
Filter.frequently_bot.description: A theorem stating that a property cannot hold for elements in the bottom filter, which contains no sets.

Filter.frequently_top.code: Filter.frequently_top.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} : (∃ᶠ (x : α) in ⊤, p x) ↔ ∃ x, p x
Filter.frequently_top.description: A theorem stating that a property holds frequently in the top filter if and only if there exists at least one element for which the property holds.

Filter.frequently_principal.code: Filter.frequently_principal.{u} {α : Type u} {a : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : (∃ᶠ (x : α) in 𝓟 a, p x) ↔ ∃ x ∈ a, p x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.frequently_principal.description: A theorem stating that a property holds frequently for elements of a set if and only if there exists at least one element in that set for which the property holds.

Filter.frequently_inf_principal.code:
Filter.frequently_inf_principal.{u} {α : Type u} {f : Filter α} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f ⊓ 𝓟 s, p x) ↔ ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, x ∈ s ∧ p x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.frequently_inf_principal.description: A theorem that states the occurrence of a property frequently in the intersection of a filter and a principal filter is equivalent to that property occurring frequently for elements that also belong to the set associated with the principal filter.

Filter.frequently_sup.code:
Filter.frequently_sup.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {f g : Filter α} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f ⊔ g, p x) ↔ (∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x) ∨ ∃ᶠ (x : α) in g, p x
Filter.frequently_sup.description: A theorem that indicates a property is frequently satisfied by elements in the supremum of two filters if and only if it is frequently satisfied by elements in at least one of the individual filters.

Filter.frequently_sSup.code:
Filter.frequently_sSup.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {fs : Set (Filter α)} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in sSup fs, p x) ↔ ∃ f ∈ fs, ∃ᶠ (x : α) in f, p x

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.SupSet.sSup: A function that computes the supremum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Filter.frequently_sSup.description: A theorem stating that a property holds frequently in the supremum of a set of filters if and only if there exists a filter within that set where the property holds frequently.

Filter.frequently_iSup.code:
Filter.frequently_iSup.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {p : α → Prop} {fs : β → Filter α} :
  (∃ᶠ (x : α) in ⨆ b, fs b, p x) ↔ ∃ b, ∃ᶠ (x : α) in fs b, p x
Filter.frequently_iSup.description: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements of the supremum of a family of filters if and only if it holds for almost all elements of at least one filter in that family.

Filter.Eventually.choice.code:
Filter.Eventually.choice.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {r : α → β → Prop} {l : Filter α} [l.NeBot]
  (h : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, ∃ y, r x y) : ∃ f, ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, r x (f x)
Filter.Eventually.choice.description: A theorem that states if a filter contains elements for which a relation has associated values, then one can construct a function that provides those values for the elements of the filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.code: Filter.EventuallyEq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (l : Filter α) (f g : α → β) : Prop
Filter.EventuallyEq.comment:
Two functions `f` and `g` are *eventually equal* along a filter `l` if the set of `x` such that
`f x = g x` belongs to `l`.
Filter.EventuallyEq.fullDefinition: def EventuallyEq (l : Filter α) (f g : α → β) : Prop :=   ∀ᶠ x in l, f x = g x
Filter.EventuallyEq.description: A definition describing two functions as eventually equal along a filter if the set of points where they are equal belongs to that filter.

Filter.«term_=ᶠ[_]_».description: A definition describing a parser for the notation indicating membership of a set within a filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.eventually.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.eventually.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g : α → β} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) :
  ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, f x = g x
Filter.EventuallyEq.eventually.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then there exists a subset of the domain where the functions are equal for all its elements.

Filter.EventuallyEq.rw.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.rw.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g : α → β} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) (p : α → β → Prop)
  (hf : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p x (f x)) : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, p x (g x)
Filter.EventuallyEq.rw.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then a specified property holds for one function if it holds for the other at almost every point according to the same filter.

Filter.eventuallyEq_set.code: Filter.eventuallyEq_set.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {l : Filter α} : s =ᶠ[l] t ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.eventuallyEq_set.description: A theorem stating that two sets are eventually equal with respect to a filter if and only if they contain the same elements for all sufficiently frequent points within that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.mem_iff.code: Filter.EventuallyEq.mem_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {l : Filter α} : s =ᶠ[l] t → ∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.EventuallyEq.mem_iff.description: A theorem stating that two sets are eventually equal in a filter if and only if they contain the same elements for all except a negligible collection within that filter.

Filter.Eventually.set_eq.code: Filter.Eventually.set_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {l : Filter α} : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in l, x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t) → s =ᶠ[l] t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.Eventually.set_eq.description: A theorem asserting that if elements of two sets are equivalent under a certain filter, then the sets are considered equal in the context of that filter.

Filter.eventuallyEq_univ.code: Filter.eventuallyEq_univ.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {l : Filter α} : s =ᶠ[l] univ ↔ s ∈ l

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Filter.GenerateSets.univ: A theorem stating that the generation of sets from a given collection includes the universal set.
explanatories.Finset.univ: This definition represents the universal finite set of a type that is finitely enumerable.

Filter.eventuallyEq_univ.description: A theorem that establishes the equivalence between a set being eventually equal to the universal set in a filter and the set being a member of that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.exists_mem.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.exists_mem.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g : α → β} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) :
  ∃ s ∈ l, EqOn f g s

explanatories.Filter.Eventually.exists_mem: A theorem asserting that if a property holds for most elements in a filter, then there exists a set within that filter where the property holds for all its elements.
explanatories.Set.EqOn: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.

Filter.EventuallyEq.exists_mem.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then there exists a set in the filter on which the two functions are equal.

Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem.code:
Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g : α → β} {s : Set α} (hs : s ∈ l)
  (h : EqOn f g s) : f =ᶠ[l] g

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.EqOn: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.

Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem.description: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and two functions are equivalent on that set, then those functions are eventually equal with respect to the filter.

Filter.eventuallyEq_iff_exists_mem.code:
Filter.eventuallyEq_iff_exists_mem.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g : α → β} :
  f =ᶠ[l] g ↔ ∃ s ∈ l, EqOn f g s

explanatories.Set.EqOn: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.

Filter.eventuallyEq_iff_exists_mem.description: A theorem stating that a function is equal to another function under a filter if and only if there exists a set in the filter on which both functions are equal.

Filter.EventuallyEq.filter_mono.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.filter_mono.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l l' : Filter α} {f g : α → β} (h₁ : f =ᶠ[l] g)
  (h₂ : l' ≤ l) : f =ᶠ[l'] g

explanatories.Filter.Eventually.filter_mono: A theorem stating that if one filter is less than or equal to another and a property holds for almost all elements in the larger filter, then it also holds for almost all elements in the smaller filter.
explanatories.Filter.Frequently.filter_mono: A theorem that establishes that if a property frequently holds in one filter and that filter is less than or equal to another filter, then the property also frequently holds in the second filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.filter_mono.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are eventually equal with respect to one filter and the second filter is less than or equal to the first, then the functions are also eventually equal with respect to the second filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.refl.code: Filter.EventuallyEq.refl.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (l : Filter α) (f : α → β) : f =ᶠ[l] f
Filter.EventuallyEq.refl.description: A theorem that asserts a function is eventually equal to itself with respect to a given filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.rfl.code: Filter.EventuallyEq.rfl.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f : α → β} : f =ᶠ[l] f

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Set.Subset.rfl: Every set is a subset of itself.

Filter.EventuallyEq.rfl.description: A theorem stating that a function is considered eventually equal to itself with respect to a given filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.symm.code: Filter.EventuallyEq.symm.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {f g : α → β} {l : Filter α} (H : f =ᶠ[l] g) : g =ᶠ[l] f

explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

Filter.EventuallyEq.symm.description: A theorem asserting that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order with respect to that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.trans.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.trans.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g h : α → β} (H₁ : f =ᶠ[l] g)
  (H₂ : g =ᶠ[l] h) : f =ᶠ[l] h

explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Set.Subset.trans: The transitive property of set inclusion states that if one set is included in a second set, and that second set is included in a third set, then the first set is also included in the third set.
explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

Filter.EventuallyEq.trans.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, and one of those functions is equal to a third function almost everywhere with respect to the same filter, then the first and third functions are also equal almost everywhere with respect to that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.prod_mk.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.prod_mk.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type w} {l : Filter α} {f f' : α → β}
  (hf : f =ᶠ[l] f') {g g' : α → γ} (hg : g =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => (f x, g x)) =ᶠ[l] fun x => (f' x, g' x)
Filter.EventuallyEq.prod_mk.description: If two functions are eventually equal with respect to a filter, then their corresponding pairs will also be eventually equal under the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.fun_comp.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.fun_comp.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type w} {f g : α → β} {l : Filter α}
  (H : f =ᶠ[l] g) (h : β → γ) : h ∘ f =ᶠ[l] h ∘ g
Filter.EventuallyEq.fun_comp.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then their compositions with another function also remain equal almost everywhere with respect to that same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.comp₂.description: A theorem demonstrating that if two functions are eventually equal and a binary function is applied to them, then the composition of those functions is also eventually equal under the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.mul.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.mul.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Mul β] {f f' g g' : α → β} {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g)
  (h' : f' =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x * f' x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => g x * g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.mul.description: A theorem stating that the product of two functions that are eventually equal to two other functions is also eventually equal to the product of those two other functions.

Filter.EventuallyEq.add.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.add.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Add β] {f f' g g' : α → β} {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g)
  (h' : f' =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x + f' x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => g x + g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.add.description: A theorem stating that if two pairs of functions are eventually equal under a given filter, then their sum is also eventually equal under the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.const_smul.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.const_smul.{u, v, u_2} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type u_2} [SMul γ β] {f g : α → β}
  {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) (c : γ) : (fun x => c • f x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => c • g x
Filter.EventuallyEq.const_smul.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are almost equal with respect to a filter, then scaling both functions by a constant yields two functions that are also almost equal with respect to the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.inv.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.inv.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Inv β] {f g : α → β} {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) :
  (fun x => (f x)⁻¹) =ᶠ[l] fun x => (g x)⁻¹
Filter.EventuallyEq.inv.description: A theorem that asserts the inverse of two functions defined to be equal with respect to a filter also holds equality with respect to the same filter for their inverses.

Filter.EventuallyEq.neg.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.neg.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Neg β] {f g : α → β} {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) :
  (fun x => -f x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => -g x
Filter.EventuallyEq.neg.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are eventually equal under a filter, then their negations are also eventually equal under the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.div.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.div.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Div β] {f f' g g' : α → β} {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g)
  (h' : f' =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x / f' x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => g x / g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.div.description: A theorem establishing that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then the quotient of these functions is also equal almost everywhere with respect to the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.sub.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.sub.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Sub β] {f f' g g' : α → β} {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g)
  (h' : f' =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x - f' x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => g x - g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.sub.description: A theorem asserting that if two pairs of functions are eventually equal with respect to a filter, then the difference of the first pair is also eventually equal to the difference of the second pair with respect to the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.const_vadd.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.const_vadd.{u, v, u_2} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type u_2} [VAdd γ β] {f g : α → β}
  {l : Filter α} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) (c : γ) : (fun x => c +ᵥ f x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => c +ᵥ g x
Filter.EventuallyEq.const_vadd.description: If two functions are eventually equal with respect to a filter, then adding a constant vector to both functions preserves their eventual equality under the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.smul.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.smul.{u, v, u_2} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [SMul 𝕜 β] {l : Filter α} {f f' : α → 𝕜}
  {g g' : α → β} (hf : f =ᶠ[l] f') (hg : g =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x • g x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => f' x • g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.smul.description: A theorem asserting that if two functions converge in a filter to their respective limits, then their pointwise scalar multiplication also converges in that same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.vadd.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.vadd.{u, v, u_2} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [VAdd 𝕜 β] {l : Filter α} {f f' : α → 𝕜}
  {g g' : α → β} (hf : f =ᶠ[l] f') (hg : g =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x +ᵥ g x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => f' x +ᵥ g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.vadd.description: A theorem stating that if two functions converge to equivalent values under a certain filter, their pointwise sum also converges to the sum of their equivalent values under that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.sup.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.sup.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Sup β] {l : Filter α} {f f' g g' : α → β} (hf : f =ᶠ[l] f')
  (hg : g =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x ⊔ g x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => f' x ⊔ g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.sup.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are eventually equal to two other functions with respect to a filter, then the supremum of the original functions is eventually equal to the supremum of the latter functions.

Filter.EventuallyEq.inf.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.inf.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Inf β] {l : Filter α} {f f' g g' : α → β} (hf : f =ᶠ[l] f')
  (hg : g =ᶠ[l] g') : (fun x => f x ⊓ g x) =ᶠ[l] fun x => f' x ⊓ g' x
Filter.EventuallyEq.inf.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are eventually equal under a filter, then their infima are also eventually equal under the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.preimage.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.preimage.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {l : Filter α} {f g : α → β} (h : f =ᶠ[l] g) (s : Set β) :
  f ⁻¹' s =ᶠ[l] g ⁻¹' s

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.EventuallyEq.preimage.description: A theorem stating that if two functions are asymptotically equal with respect to a filter, their preimages under the same set are also asymptotically equal with respect to that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.inter.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t s' t' : Set α} {l : Filter α} (h : s =ᶠ[l] t) (h' : s' =ᶠ[l] t') :
  s ∩ s' =ᶠ[l] t ∩ t'

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.GenerateSets.inter: A theorem stating that if two sets are generated by a collection of sets, then their intersection is also generated by that same collection.

Filter.EventuallyEq.inter.description: A theorem stating that if two sets are equal to two other sets almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then their intersection is also equal to the intersection of the other two sets almost everywhere with respect to that filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.union.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.union.{u} {α : Type u} {s t s' t' : Set α} {l : Filter α} (h : s =ᶠ[l] t) (h' : s' =ᶠ[l] t') :
  s ∪ s' =ᶠ[l] t ∪ t'

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.Finite.union: The union of two finite sets is also a finite set.

Filter.EventuallyEq.union.description: A theorem asserting that the union of two sets that are eventually equal to two other sets also demonstrates eventual equality with the union of those sets.

Filter.EventuallyEq.compl.code: Filter.EventuallyEq.compl.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {l : Filter α} (h : s =ᶠ[l] t) : sᶜ =ᶠ[l] tᶜ

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Filter.EventuallyEq.compl.description: A theorem stating that if two sets are eventually equal with respect to a filter, then their complements are also eventually equal with respect to the same filter.

Filter.EventuallyEq.diff.code:
Filter.EventuallyEq.diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t s' t' : Set α} {l : Filter α} (h : s =ᶠ[l] t) (h' : s' =ᶠ[l] t') :

Filter.comap.comment:
The inverse map of a filter. A set `s` belongs to `Filter.comap m f` if either of the following
equivalent conditions hold.

1. There exists a set `t ∈ f` such that `m ⁻¹' t ⊆ s`. This is used as a definition.
2. The set `kernImage m s = {y | ∀ x, m x = y → x ∈ s}` belongs to `f`, see `Filter.mem_comap'`.
3. The set `(m '' sᶜ)ᶜ` belongs to `f`, see `Filter.mem_comap_iff_compl` and
`Filter.compl_mem_comap`.

Filter.kernMap.code: Filter.kernMap.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (m : α → β) (f : Filter α) : Filter β
Filter.kernMap.comment:
The analog of `kernImage` for filters. A set `s` belongs to `Filter.kernMap m f` if either of
the following equivalent conditions hold.

1. There exists a set `t ∈ f` such that `s = kernImage m t`. This is used as a definition.
2. There exists a set `t` such that `tᶜ ∈ f` and `sᶜ = m '' t`, see `Filter.mem_kernMap_iff_compl`
and `Filter.compl_mem_kernMap`.

This definition because it gives a right adjoint to `Filter.comap`, and because it has a nice
interpretation when working with `co-` filters (`Filter.cocompact`, `Filter.cofinite`, ...).
For example, `kernMap m (cocompact α)` is the filter generated by the complements of the sets
`m '' K` where `K` is a compact subset of `α`.

explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq: A definition describing two functions as eventually equal along a filter if the set of points where they are equal belongs to that filter.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.refl: A theorem that asserts a function is eventually equal to itself with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.symm: A theorem asserting that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order with respect to that filter.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.trans: A theorem stating that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, and one of those functions is equal to a third function almost everywhere with respect to the same filter, then the first and third functions are also equal almost everywhere with respect to that filter.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyLE.refl: A theorem asserting that a function is eventually less than or equal to itself with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyLE.trans: A theorem demonstrating that if a function is eventually less than or equal to a second function, and that second function is eventually less than or equal to a third function, then the first function is also eventually less than or equal to the third function.

Filter.germSetoid.description: A definition for a setoid structure that characterizes the space of germs for functions from a type to another type with respect to a given filter.

explanatories.Filter.eventually_of_forall: A theorem stating that if a property holds for all elements in a type, then it holds for almost all elements with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.mono: A theorem that states if a property holds for a filter and implies another property, then the latter property also holds for that filter.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.congr: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a filter and another property is equivalent to the first for almost all those elements, then the second property also holds for almost all elements in the same filter.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

Filter.productSetoid.fullDefinition: def productSetoid (l : Filter α) (ε : α → Type*) : Setoid ((a : _) → ε a) where   r f g := ∀ᶠ a in l, f a = g a   iseqv :=     ⟨fun _ => eventually_of_forall fun _ => rfl, fun h => h.mono fun _ => Eq.symm,       fun h1 h2 => h1.congr (h2.mono fun _ hx => hx ▸ Iff.rfl)⟩

Filter.Germ.IsConstant.fullDefinition: def IsConstant {l : Filter α} (P : Germ l β) : Prop :=   P.liftOn (fun f ↦ ∃ b : β, f =ᶠ[l] (fun _ ↦ b)) <| by     suffices ∀ f g : α → β, ∀ b : β, f =ᶠ[l] g → (f =ᶠ[l] fun _ ↦ b) → (g =ᶠ[l] fun _ ↦ b) from       fun f g h ↦ propext ⟨fun ⟨b, hb⟩ ↦ ⟨b, this f g b h hb⟩, fun ⟨b, hb⟩ ↦ ⟨b, h.trans hb⟩⟩     exact fun f g b hfg hf ↦ (hfg.symm).trans hf

Filter.Germ.map'.comment:
Given a map `F : (α → β) → (γ → δ)` that sends functions eventually equal at `l` to functions

Filter.Germ.map'.fullDefinition: def map' {lc : Filter γ} (F : (α → β) → γ → δ) (hF : (l.EventuallyEq ⇒ lc.EventuallyEq) F F) :     Germ l β → Germ lc δ :=   Quotient.map' F hF
Filter.Germ.map'.description: A definition for a mapping that transforms germs of functions with respect to one filter into germs of functions with respect to another filter, provided that the mapping preserves the property of being eventually equal under those filters.

Filter.Germ.liftOn.code:
Filter.Germ.liftOn.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {l : Filter α} {γ : Sort u_5} (f : l.Germ β)

Filter.Germ.liftOn.comment:
Given a germ `f : Germ l β` and a function `F : (α → β) → γ` sending eventually equal functions
to the same value, returns the value `F` takes on functions having germ `f` at `l`.

Filter.Germ.liftOn.description: A definition for retrieving the value assigned by a function to a germ of an equivalence class of functions, under the condition that the function treats eventually equal functions as equal.

Filter.Germ.map.fullDefinition: def map (op : β → γ) : Germ l β → Germ l γ :=   map' (op ∘ ·) fun _ _ H => H.mono fun _ H => congr_arg op H
Filter.Germ.map.description: A definition for a mapping that transfers a function from one type to another within the framework of germs associated with a given filter.

Filter.Germ.map_coe.code:

Filter.Germ.map_coe.description: The theorem states that applying a function to the output of a mapped germ and to the composition of that function with the original function results in equivalent germs under a specified filter.

Filter.Germ.map₂.code:
Filter.Germ.map₂.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} {l : Filter α}

Filter.Germ.map₂.fullDefinition: def map₂ (op : β → γ → δ) : Germ l β → Germ l γ → Germ l δ :=   Quotient.map₂' (fun f g x => op (f x) (g x)) fun f f' Hf g g' Hg =>     Hg.mp <| Hf.mono fun x Hf Hg => by simp only [Hf, Hg]

Filter.Germ.map₂_coe.code:

Filter.Germ.Tendsto.fullDefinition: protected def Tendsto (f : Germ l β) (lb : Filter β) : Prop :=   liftOn f (fun f => Tendsto f l lb) fun _f _g H => propext (tendsto_congr' H)

Filter.Germ.compTendsto.code:

Filter.Germ.instAddAction'.description: A definition that establishes an additive action of germs of two types over a filter, making it possible to add these germs in a coherent way.

Filter.Germ.instModule'.fullDefinition: instance instModule' [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] :     Module (Germ l R) (Germ l M) where   add_smul c₁ c₂ f :=     inductionOn₃ c₁ c₂ f fun c₁ c₂ f => by       norm_cast       simp [add_smul]   zero_smul f := inductionOn f fun f => by simp only [← coe_zero, ← coe_smul', zero_smul]

Filter.Germ.instExistsMulOfLE.fullDefinition: instance instExistsMulOfLE [Mul β] [LE β] [ExistsMulOfLE β] : ExistsMulOfLE (Germ l β) where   exists_mul_of_le {x y} := inductionOn₂ x y fun f g (h : f ≤ᶠ[l] g) ↦ by     classical     choose c hc using fun x (hx : f x ≤ g x) ↦ exists_mul_of_le hx     refine ⟨ofFun fun x ↦ if hx : f x ≤ g x then c x hx else f x, coe_eq.2 ?_⟩     filter_upwards [h] with x hx     rw [dif_pos hx, hc]

  (b : β) (i : ι) : (map (fun x => b) (𝓟 {a})).coprod (map id (𝓟 {i})) = 𝓟 ({b} ×ˢ univ ∪ univ ×ˢ {i})
Filter.map_const_principal_coprod_map_id.comment:
Characterization of the coproduct of the `Filter.map`s of two principal filters `𝓟 {a}` and
`𝓟 {i}`, the first under the constant function `fun a => b` and the second under the identity
function. Together with the next lemma, `map_prod_map_const_id_principal_coprod_principal`, this
provides an example showing that the inequality in the lemma `map_prod_map_coprod_le` can be strict.

explanatories.Filter.map: A definition describing a transformation of a filter through a function that maps elements from one type to another.

Filter.rmap.fullDefinition: def rmap (r : Rel α β) (l : Filter α) : Filter β where   sets := { s | r.core s ∈ l }   univ_sets := by simp   sets_of_superset hs st := mem_of_superset hs (Rel.core_mono _ st)   inter_sets hs ht := by     simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]     convert inter_mem hs ht     rw [← Rel.core_inter]

Filter.ofCountableUnion.comment:
Construct a filter with countable intersection property.
Similarly to `Filter.comk`, a set belongs to this filter if its complement satisfies the property.
Similarly to `Filter.ofCountableInter`,
this constructor deduces some properties from the countable intersection property
which becomes the countable union property because we take complements of all sets.

Filter.ofCountableUnion.fullDefinition: def Filter.ofCountableUnion (l : Set (Set α))     (hUnion : ∀ S : Set (Set α), S.Countable → (∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ l) → ⋃₀ S ∈ l)     (hmono : ∀ t ∈ l, ∀ s ⊆ t, s ∈ l) : Filter α := by   refine .ofCountableInter {s | sᶜ ∈ l} (fun S hSc hSp ↦ ?_) fun s t ht hsub ↦ ?_   · rw [mem_setOf_eq, compl_sInter]     apply hUnion (compl '' S) (hSc.image _)     intro s hs     rw [mem_image] at hs     rcases hs with ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩     apply hSp ht   · rw [mem_setOf_eq]     rw [← compl_subset_compl] at hsub     exact hmono sᶜ ht tᶜ hsub

countableInterFilter_inf.fullDefinition: instance countableInterFilter_inf (l₁ l₂ : Filter α) [CountableInterFilter l₁]     [CountableInterFilter l₂] : CountableInterFilter (l₁ ⊓ l₂) := by   refine ⟨fun S hSc hS => ?_⟩   choose s hs t ht hst using hS   replace hs : (⋂ i ∈ S, s i ‹_›) ∈ l₁ := (countable_bInter_mem hSc).2 hs   replace ht : (⋂ i ∈ S, t i ‹_›) ∈ l₂ := (countable_bInter_mem hSc).2 ht   refine mem_of_superset (inter_mem_inf hs ht) (subset_sInter fun i hi => ?_)   rw [hst i hi]   apply inter_subset_inter <;> exact iInter_subset_of_subset i (iInter_subset _ _)

`atTop` is the filter representing the limit `→ ∞` on an ordered set.
It is generated by the collection of up-sets `{b | a ≤ b}`.

and indeed is trivial when a top element exists.)

Filter.map_atTop_finset_prod_le_of_prod_.code:
Filter.map_atTop_finset_prod_le_of_prod_eq.{u_3, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_4} {γ : Type u_5} [CommMonoid α]
  {f : β → α} {g : γ → α}
  (h_eq : ∀ (u : Finset γ), ∃ v, ∀ (v' : Finset β), v ⊆ v' → ∃ u', u ⊆ u' ∧ ∏ x ∈ u', g x = ∏ b ∈ v', f b) :
  map (fun s => ∏ b ∈ s, f b) atTop ≤ map (fun s => ∏ x ∈ s, g x) atTop
Filter.map_atTop_finset_prod_le_of_prod_.comment:
Let `f` and `g` be two maps to the same commutative monoid. This lemma gives a sufficient
condition for comparison of the filter `atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ b ∈ s, f b)` with
`atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ b ∈ s, g b)`. This is useful to compare the set of limit points of
`Π b in s, f b` as `s → atTop` with the similar set for `g`.

explanatories.Prod.map: A mapping function transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

Filter.map_atTop_finset_prod_le_of_prod_.description: This theorem provides a criterion for comparing the behavior of two sequences of products in a commutative monoid, establishing that under certain conditions, the limit points of one sequence are less than or equal to those of another as they approach infinity.

Filter.tendsto_iff_seq_tendsto.{u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_4} {f : α → β} {k : Filter α} {l : Filter β}
  [k.IsCountablyGenerated] : Tendsto f k l ↔ ∀ (x : ℕ → α), Tendsto x atTop k → Tendsto (f ∘ x) atTop l
Filter.tendsto_iff_seq_tendsto.comment:
An abstract version of continuity of sequentially continuous functions on metric spaces:
if a filter `k` is countably generated then `Tendsto f k l` iff for every sequence `u`
converging to `k`, `f ∘ u` tends to `l`.

Function.Injective.map_atTop_finset_prod_eq.{u_3, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_4} {γ : Type u_5} [CommMonoid α]
  {g : γ → β} (hg : Function.Injective g) {f : β → α} (hf : ∀ x ∉ Set.range g, f x = 1) :
  Filter.map (fun s => ∏ i ∈ s, f (g i)) atTop = Filter.map (fun s => ∏ i ∈ s, f i) atTop
Function.Injective.map_atTop_finset_prod.comment:
Let `g : γ → β` be an injective function and `f : β → α` be a function from the codomain of `g`
to a commutative monoid. Suppose that `f x = 1` outside of the range of `g`. Then the filters
`atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ i ∈ s, f (g i))` and `atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ i ∈ s, f i)` coincide.

The additive version of this lemma is used to prove the equality `∑' x, f (g x) = ∑' y, f y` under
the same assumptions.

Filter.HasBasis.mem_lift_iff.comment:
If `(p : ι → Prop, s : ι → Set α)` is a basis of a filter `f`, `g` is a monotone function
`Set α → Filter γ`, and for each `i`, `(pg : β i → Prop, sg : β i → Set α)` is a basis
of the filter `g (s i)`, then
`(fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ p i ∧ pg i x, fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ sg i x)` is a basis
of the filter `f.lift g`.

This basis is parametrized by `i : ι` and `x : β i`, so in order to formulate this fact using
`Filter.HasBasis` one has to use `Σ i, β i` as the index type, see `Filter.HasBasis.lift`.
This lemma states the corresponding `mem_iff` statement without using a sigma type.

Filter.HasBasis.lift.comment:

of the filter `g (s i)`, then
`(fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ p i ∧ pg i x, fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ sg i x)`
is a basis of the filter `f.lift g`.

This basis is parametrized by `i : ι` and `x : β i`, so in order to formulate this fact using

for the corresponding `mem_iff` statement formulated without using a sigma type.

  {f : α → β} (hs : Tendsto s la lb.smallSets) (hf : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in la, f x ∈ s x) : Tendsto f la lb
Filter.Tendsto.of_smallSets.comment:
Generalized **squeeze theorem** (also known as **sandwich theorem**). If `s : α → Set β` is a
family of sets that tends to `Filter.smallSets lb` along `la` and `f : α → β` is a function such
that `f x ∈ s x` eventually along `la`, then `f` tends to `lb` along `la`.

If `s x` is the closed interval `[g x, h x]` for some functions `g`, `h` that tend to the same limit
`𝓝 y`, then we obtain the standard squeeze theorem, see
`tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'`.
