Filter.Tendsto.const_mul_atTop'.comment:
If a function tends to infinity along a filter, then this function multiplied by a positive
constant (on the left) also tends to infinity. The archimedean assumption is convenient to get a
statement that works on `ℕ`, `ℤ` and `ℝ`, although not necessary (a version in ordered fields is
given in `Filter.Tendsto.const_mul_atTop`).

  [self : TendstoIxxClass Ixx l₁ l₂] : Tendsto (fun p => Ixx p.1 p.2) (l₁ ×ˢ l₁) (smallSets l₂)
Filter.TendstoIxxClass.tendsto_Ixx.comment:
`Function.uncurry Ixx` tends to `l₂.smallSets` along `l₁ ×ˢ l₁`. In other words, for any
`s ∈ l₂` there exists `t ∈ l₁` such that `Ixx x y ⊆ s` whenever `x ∈ t` and `y ∈ t`.

Use lemmas like `Filter.Tendsto.Icc` instead.

filter.tendsto_uIcc_of_Icc.fullDefinition: instance tendsto_uIcc_of_Icc {l : Filter α} [TendstoIxxClass Icc l l] :     TendstoIxxClass uIcc l l := by   refine ⟨fun s hs => mem_map.2 <| mem_prod_self_iff.2 ?_⟩   obtain ⟨t, htl, hts⟩ : ∃ t ∈ l, ∀ p ∈ (t : Set α) ×ˢ t, Icc (p : α × α).1 p.2 ∈ s :=     mem_prod_self_iff.1 (mem_map.1 (tendsto_fst.Icc tendsto_snd hs))   refine ⟨t, htl, fun p hp => ?_⟩   rcases le_total p.1 p.2 with h | h   · rw [mem_preimage, uIcc_of_le h]     exact hts p hp   · rw [mem_preimage, uIcc_of_ge h]     exact hts ⟨p.2, p.1⟩ ⟨hp.2, hp.1⟩

  (hl : ∀ (S : Set (Set α)), #↑S < c → S ⊆ l → ⋂₀ S ∈ l) (h_mono : ∀ (s t : Set α), s ∈ l → s ⊆ t → t ∈ l) : Filter α
Filter.ofCardinalInter.comment:
Construct a filter with cardinal `c` intersection property. This constructor deduces
`Filter.univ_sets` and `Filter.inter_sets` from the cardinal `c` intersection property.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.lt_of_le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Set.sInter_empty: The intersection of an empty collection of sets is equal to the universal set.
explanatories.Cardinal.mk_eq_zero: This theorem asserts that the cardinality of an empty type is equal to zero.
explanatories.lt_trans: This theorem shows that in a preorder, if one element is less than a second and the second is less than a third, then the first is also less than the third.
explanatories.zero_lt_two: This theorem demonstrates that in any partially ordered set that functions as an additive monoid with one, zero is strictly less than two.
explanatories.Set.empty_subset: The empty set is a subset of any set.
explanatories.Set.sInter_pair: The intersection of a pair of sets is equal to the intersection of the set containing those two sets.
explanatories.Set.insert_subset_iff: The inclusion of a set that contains an element and another set is equivalent to the condition that the element is in the second set and the first set is a subset of the second set.
explanatories.Set.singleton_subset_iff: A singleton set is a subset of another set if and only if its single element is an element of that set.
explanatories.Filter.sets: A definition describing the collection of sets that are included within a given filter for a specific type.

Filter.ofCardinalInter.fullDefinition: def ofCardinalInter (l : Set (Set α)) (hc : 2 < c)     (hl : ∀ S : Set (Set α), (#S < c) → S ⊆ l → ⋂₀ S ∈ l)     (h_mono : ∀ s t, s ∈ l → s ⊆ t → t ∈ l) : Filter α where   sets := l   univ_sets :=     sInter_empty ▸ hl ∅ (mk_eq_zero (∅ : Set (Set α)) ▸ lt_trans zero_lt_two hc) (empty_subset _)   sets_of_superset := h_mono _ _   inter_sets {s t} hs ht := sInter_pair s t ▸ by     apply hl _ (?_) (insert_subset_iff.2 ⟨hs, singleton_subset_iff.2 ht⟩)     have : #({s, t} : Set (Set α)) ≤ 2 := by       calc       _ ≤ #({t} : Set (Set α)) + 1 := Cardinal.mk_insert_le       _ = 2 := by norm_num     exact lt_of_le_of_lt this hc
Filter.ofCardinalInter.description: A filter is constructed from a set of sets with a specific cardinality that satisfies an intersection property and includes conditions for monotonicity and subset inclusion.

explanatories.CardinalInterFilter.cardinal_sInter_mem: If a collection of sets, each belonging to a specific filter, has cardinality less than a certain size, then their intersection also belongs to that filter.
explanatories.CountableInterFilter.mk: A filter is defined as a countable intersection filter if it satisfies the condition that the intersection of any countable collection of sets in the filter is also contained within the filter.
explanatories.cardinal_sInter_mem: The intersection of a collection of sets belongs to a filter if and only if the cardinality of the collection is less than a specific size and all sets in the collection are members of that filter.

CardinalInterFilter.mk.description: This defines a structure that captures the idea that a filter satisfies certain intersection properties if it supports intersections of collections of sets with a cardinality smaller than a specified threshold.

Filter.ofCardinalUnion.code:
Filter.ofCardinalUnion.{u} {α : Type u} {c : Cardinal.{u}} (l : Set (Set α)) (hc : 2 < c)
  (hUnion : ∀ (S : Set (Set α)), #↑S < c → (∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ l) → ⋃₀ S ∈ l) (hmono : ∀ t ∈ l, ∀ s ⊆ t, s ∈ l) : Filter α
Filter.ofCardinalUnion.comment:
Construct a filter with cardinal `c` intersection property.
Similarly to `Filter.comk`, a set belongs to this filter if its complement satisfies the property.
Similarly to `Filter.ofCardinalInter`,
this constructor deduces some properties from the cardinal `c` intersection property
which becomes the cardinal `c` union property because we take complements of all sets.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.lt_of_le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Filter.ofCardinalInter: A filter is constructed from a set of sets with a specific cardinality that satisfies an intersection property and includes conditions for monotonicity and subset inclusion.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.Set.compl_sInter: The complement of the intersection of a collection of sets is equal to the union of the complements of those sets.
explanatories.Cardinal.mk_image_le: This theorem asserts that the cardinality of the image of a set under a function is less than or equal to the cardinality of the original set.
explanatories.Set.mem_image: An element is in the image of a set under a function if and only if there exists an element in the original set that maps to it via the function.
explanatories.Set.compl_subset_compl: The complement of one set is contained within the complement of another if and only if the second set is contained within the first set.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.

Filter.ofCardinalUnion.fullDefinition: def ofCardinalUnion (l : Set (Set α)) (hc : 2 < c)     (hUnion : ∀ S : Set (Set α), (#S < c) → (∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ l) → ⋃₀ S ∈ l)     (hmono : ∀ t ∈ l, ∀ s ⊆ t, s ∈ l) : Filter α := by   refine .ofCardinalInter {s | sᶜ ∈ l} hc (fun S hSc hSp ↦ ?_) fun s t ht hsub ↦ ?_   · rw [mem_setOf_eq, compl_sInter]     apply hUnion (compl '' S) (lt_of_le_of_lt mk_image_le hSc)     intro s hs     rw [mem_image] at hs     rcases hs with ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩     apply hSp ht   · rw [mem_setOf_eq]     rw [← compl_subset_compl] at hsub     exact hmono sᶜ ht tᶜ hsub
Filter.ofCardinalUnion.description: This defines a filter based on a collection of sets, ensuring that if the cardinality of a union of sets is less than a specific size, and each set belongs to the filter, then the union also belongs to the filter.

Filter.cardinalInterFilter_principal.fullDefinition: instance cardinalInterFilter_principal (s : Set α) : CardinalInterFilter (𝓟 s) c :=   ⟨fun _ _ hS => subset_sInter hS⟩

Filter.cardinalInterFilter_inf_eq.code:

explanatories.Filter.mem_of_superset: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and is a subset of another set, then that other set also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Filter.cardinal_bInter_mem: The nested intersection of sets indexed by a collection with cardinality less than a specified size belongs to a filter if and only if every set within the indexed family is a member of that filter.
explanatories.Set.subset_sInter: A set is a subset of the intersection of a collection of sets if it is a subset of each set within that collection.
explanatories.Filter.inter_mem_inf: A theorem stating that the intersection of two sets, each belonging to different filters, is also a member of the infimum of those filters.
explanatories.Set.inter_subset_inter: The intersection of two sets is a subset of the intersection of two other sets if each of the first sets is a subset of the corresponding second set.
explanatories.Set.iInter_subset_of_subset: The intersection of a family of sets is a subset of another set whenever each individual set in the family is contained within that other set.
explanatories.Set.iInter_subset: The intersection of a family of sets is a subset of any individual set in that family.

Filter.cardinalInterFilter_inf_eq.fullDefinition: instance cardinalInterFilter_inf_eq (l₁ l₂ : Filter α) [CardinalInterFilter l₁ c]     [CardinalInterFilter l₂ c] : CardinalInterFilter (l₁ ⊓ l₂) c := by   refine ⟨fun S hSc hS => ?_⟩   choose s hs t ht hst using hS   replace hs : (⋂ i ∈ S, s i ‹_›) ∈ l₁ := (cardinal_bInter_mem hSc).2 hs   replace ht : (⋂ i ∈ S, t i ‹_›) ∈ l₂ := (cardinal_bInter_mem hSc).2 ht   refine mem_of_superset (inter_mem_inf hs ht) (subset_sInter fun i hi => ?_)   rw [hst i hi]   apply inter_subset_inter <;> exact iInter_subset_of_subset i (iInter_subset _ _)
Filter.cardinalInterFilter_inf_eq.description: The infimum of two filters that both satisfy the cardinal intersection property also satisfies this property.

Filter.cardinalInterFilter_sup_eq.code:
Filter.cardinalInterFilter_sup_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {c : Cardinal.{u}} (l₁ l₂ : Filter α) [CardinalInterFilter l₁ c]
  [CardinalInterFilter l₂ c] : CardinalInterFilter (l₁ ⊔ l₂) c

explanatories.CardinalInterFilter.cardinal_sInter_mem: If a collection of sets, each belonging to a specific filter, has cardinality less than a certain size, then their intersection also belongs to that filter.
explanatories.cardinal_sInter_mem: The intersection of a collection of sets belongs to a filter if and only if the cardinality of the collection is less than a specific size and all sets in the collection are members of that filter.

Filter.cardinalInterFilter_sup_eq.fullDefinition: instance cardinalInterFilter_sup_eq (l₁ l₂ : Filter α) [CardinalInterFilter l₁ c]     [CardinalInterFilter l₂ c] : CardinalInterFilter (l₁ ⊔ l₂) c := by   refine ⟨fun S hSc hS => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩ <;> refine (cardinal_sInter_mem hSc).2 fun s hs => ?_   exacts [(hS s hs).1, (hS s hs).2]
Filter.cardinalInterFilter_sup_eq.description: The supremum of two filters that satisfy certain intersection properties is itself a filter that satisfies those same properties.

Filter.cocardinal.comment:
The filter defined by all sets that have a complement with at most cardinality `c`. For a union
of `c` sets of `c` elements to have `c` elements, we need that `c` is a regular cardinal.

explanatories.Filter.ofCardinalUnion: This defines a filter based on a collection of sets, ensuring that if the cardinality of a union of sets is less than a specific size, and each set belongs to the filter, then the union also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Cardinal.mk: This defines a function that assigns a cardinal number to a type, representing the size of that type.
explanatories.lt_of_lt_of_le: This theorem shows that if one element is less than a second element, and the second element is less than or equal to a third element, then the first element is also less than the third element in a preorder.
explanatories.Cardinal.nat_lt_aleph0: This theorem establishes that every natural number is less than the cardinality of the set of natural numbers.
explanatories.Cardinal.IsRegular.aleph0_le: Any regular cardinal is greater than or equal to the smallest infinite cardinal.
explanatories.lt_of_le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Cardinal.mk_sUnion_le: This theorem asserts that the cardinality of the union of sets from a collection is less than or equal to the product of the cardinality of the collection and the supremum of the cardinalities of the individual sets within that collection.
explanatories.Cardinal.mul_lt_of_lt: The product of two cardinals, each less than a given cardinality that is at least as large as the smallest infinite cardinal, is also less than that given cardinality.
explanatories.Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_isRegular: The supremum of a function mapping to cardinals remains less than a regular cardinal if each output is also less than that cardinal.
explanatories.Subtype.property: This theorem states that for any element of a subtype defined by a property, that element satisfies the property itself.
explanatories.Cardinal.mk_le_mk_of_subset: This theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another, then the cardinality of the first set is less than or equal to the cardinality of the second set.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.mk: A theorem that establishes a filter as having a basis if a set is a member of the filter if and only if it contains some set from that basis as a subset.

Filter.cocardinal.fullDefinition: def cocardinal (hreg : c.IsRegular) : Filter α := by   apply ofCardinalUnion {s | Cardinal.mk s < c} (lt_of_lt_of_le (nat_lt_aleph0 2) hreg.aleph0_le)   · refine fun s hS hSc ↦ lt_of_le_of_lt (mk_sUnion_le _) <| mul_lt_of_lt hreg.aleph0_le hS ?_     exact iSup_lt_of_isRegular hreg hS fun i ↦ hSc i i.property   · exact fun _ hSc _ ht ↦ lt_of_le_of_lt (mk_le_mk_of_subset ht) hSc
Filter.cocardinal.description: A definition that describes a filter consisting of all sets whose complements have a size at most equal to a specified regular cardinal.

supClosure.fullDefinition: def supClosure : ClosureOperator (Set α) := .ofPred   (fun s ↦ {a | ∃ (t : Finset α) (ht : t.Nonempty), ↑t ⊆ s ∧ t.sup' ht id = a})   SupClosed   (fun s a ha ↦ ⟨{a}, singleton_nonempty _, by simpa⟩)   (by     classical     rintro s _ ⟨t, ht, hts, rfl⟩ _ ⟨u, hu, hus, rfl⟩     refine ⟨_, ht.mono subset_union_left, ?_, sup'_union ht hu _⟩     rw [coe_union]     exact Set.union_subset hts hus)   (by rintro s₁ s₂ hs h₂ _ ⟨t, ht, hts, rfl⟩; exact h₂.finsetSup'_mem ht fun i hi ↦ hs <| hts hi)
supClosure.description: A closure operator is defined for any set in a join-semilattice to produce a set that is closed under the join operation.

disjointed.code: disjointed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (f : ℕ → α) : ℕ → α
disjointed.comment:
If `f : ℕ → α` is a sequence of elements, then `disjointed f` is the sequence formed by
subtracting each element from the nexts. This is the unique disjoint sequence whose partial sups
are the same as the original sequence.

explanatories.partialSups: This definition describes a function that produces a monotone sequence where each term is the supremum of the values of a given function up to that term's index.

disjointed.fullDefinition: def disjointed (f : ℕ → α) : ℕ → α   | 0 => f 0   | n + 1 => f (n + 1) \ partialSups f n
disjointed.description: This definition describes a sequence that is formed by subtracting each element from the next in an original sequence, resulting in a unique disjoint sequence that retains the same partial suprema as the original.

disjointed_zero.code: disjointed_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (f : ℕ → α) : disjointed f 0 = f 0
disjointed_zero.description: The theorem states that the first element of the disjointed sequence is equal to the first element of the original sequence.

disjointed_succ.code:
disjointed_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (f : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) :

disjointed_succ.description: This theorem establishes that in a disjoint sequence, each element is equal to its corresponding original element minus the supremum of the preceding elements.

disjointed_le_id.code: disjointed_le_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] : disjointed ≤ id
disjointed_le_id.description: This theorem asserts that the disjoint sequence is always less than or equal to the identity function.

disjointed_le.code: disjointed_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] (f : ℕ → α) : disjointed f ≤ f
disjointed_le.description: This theorem asserts that the disjoint sequence formed from an original sequence is always less than or equal to the original sequence.

explanatories.Pairwise: A relation is considered "pairwise" if it holds between every pair of distinct elements in its domain.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

disjoint_disjointed.description: This theorem asserts that the disjointed sequence formed from a given sequence is pairwise disjoint.

disjointedRec.code:
disjointedRec.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {f : ℕ → α} {p : α → Sort u_3}
  (hdiff : ⦃t : α⦄ → ⦃i : ℕ⦄ → p t → p (t \ f i)) ⦃n : ℕ⦄ : p (f n) → p (disjointed f n)
disjointedRec.comment:
An induction principle for `disjointed`. To define/prove something on `disjointed f n`, it's
enough to define/prove it for `f n` and being able to extend through diffs.

explanatories.partialSups: This definition describes a function that produces a monotone sequence where each term is the supremum of the values of a given function up to that term's index.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.partialSups_succ: The theorem asserts that the next term in the monotone sequence is equal to the supremum of the current term and the value of the original function at the next index.
explanatories.sdiff_sdiff_left: The symmetric difference of the left element with another element is equal to the symmetric difference of the left element with the join of the other two elements in a generalized coheyting algebra.

disjointedRec.fullDefinition: def disjointedRec {f : ℕ → α} {p : α → Sort*} (hdiff : ∀ ⦃t i⦄, p t → p (t \ f i)) :     ∀ ⦃n⦄, p (f n) → p (disjointed f n)   | 0 => id   | n + 1 => fun h => by     suffices H : ∀ k, p (f (n + 1) \ partialSups f k) from H n     rintro k     induction' k with k ih     · exact hdiff h     rw [partialSups_succ, ← sdiff_sdiff_left]     exact hdiff ih
disjointedRec.description: This definition provides an induction principle for a disjoint sequence, allowing the extension of properties from the original sequence to the disjoint sequence through differences.

disjointedRec_zero.code:
disjointedRec_zero.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {f : ℕ → α} {p : α → Sort u_3}
  (hdiff : ⦃t : α⦄ → ⦃i : ℕ⦄ → p t → p (t \ f i)) (h₀ : p (f 0)) : disjointedRec hdiff h₀ = h₀
disjointedRec_zero.description: This theorem establishes that under certain conditions, the recursive definition of a disjoint sequence starting from the first element is equal to that first element itself.

Monotone.disjointed_succ.code:
Monotone.disjointed_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {f : ℕ → α} (hf : Monotone f) (n : ℕ) :
  disjointed f (n + 1) = f (n + 1) \ f n
Monotone.disjointed_succ.description: This theorem shows that for a monotonically increasing sequence, the disjoint part at the next index is equal to the difference between the value at that index and the value at the previous index.

partialSups_disjointed.code:

disjointed_unique.code:
disjointed_unique.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] {f d : ℕ → α} (hdisj : Pairwise (Disjoint on d))
  (hsups : partialSups d = partialSups f) : d = disjointed f
disjointed_unique.comment:
`disjointed f` is the unique sequence that is pairwise disjoint and has the same partial sups
as `f`.

explanatories.partialSups: This definition describes a function that produces a monotone sequence where each term is the supremum of the values of a given function up to that term's index.
explanatories.Pairwise: A relation is considered "pairwise" if it holds between every pair of distinct elements in its domain.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

disjointed_unique.description: This theorem establishes that if a sequence is pairwise disjoint and shares the same partial supremum as another sequence, then it must be the unique disjointed sequence derived from that original sequence.

Finpartition.bind.fullDefinition: def bind (P : Finpartition a) (Q : ∀ i ∈ P.parts, Finpartition i) : Finpartition a where   parts := P.parts.attach.biUnion fun i ↦ (Q i.1 i.2).parts   supIndep := by     rw [supIndep_iff_pairwiseDisjoint]     rintro a ha b hb h     rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_biUnion] at ha hb     obtain ⟨⟨A, hA⟩, -, ha⟩ := ha     obtain ⟨⟨B, hB⟩, -, hb⟩ := hb     obtain rfl | hAB := eq_or_ne A B     · exact (Q A hA).disjoint ha hb h     · exact (P.disjoint hA hB hAB).mono ((Q A hA).le ha) ((Q B hB).le hb)   sup_parts := by     simp_rw [sup_biUnion]     trans (sup P.parts id)     · rw [eq_comm, ← Finset.sup_attach]       exact sup_congr rfl fun b _hb ↦ (Q b.1 b.2).sup_parts.symm     · exact P.sup_parts   not_bot_mem h := by     rw [Finset.mem_biUnion] at h     obtain ⟨⟨A, hA⟩, -, h⟩ := h     exact (Q A hA).not_bot_mem h

Finpartition.ofSetoid.fullDefinition: def ofSetoid (s : Setoid α) [DecidableRel s.r] : Finpartition (univ : Finset α) where   parts := univ.image fun a => univ.filter (s.r a)   supIndep := by     simp only [mem_univ, forall_true_left, supIndep_iff_pairwiseDisjoint, Set.PairwiseDisjoint,       Set.Pairwise, coe_image, coe_univ, Set.image_univ, Set.mem_range, ne_eq,       forall_exists_index, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff]     intro _ _ q     contrapose! q     rw [not_disjoint_iff] at q     obtain ⟨c, ⟨d1, d2⟩⟩ := q     rw [id_eq, mem_filter] at d1 d2     ext y     simp only [mem_univ, forall_true_left, mem_filter, true_and]     exact ⟨fun r1 => s.trans (s.trans d2.2 (s.symm d1.2)) r1,            fun r2 => s.trans (s.trans d1.2 (s.symm d2.2)) r2⟩   sup_parts := by     ext a     simp only [sup_image, Function.id_comp, mem_univ, mem_sup, mem_filter, true_and, iff_true]     use a; exact s.refl a   not_bot_mem := by     rw [bot_eq_empty, mem_image, not_exists]     intro a     simp only [filter_eq_empty_iff, not_forall, mem_univ, forall_true_left, true_and, not_not]     use a; exact s.refl a

Finpartition.atomise.fullDefinition: def atomise (s : Finset α) (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Finpartition s :=   ofErase (F.powerset.image fun Q ↦ s.filter fun i ↦ ∀ t ∈ F, t ∈ Q ↔ i ∈ t)     (Set.PairwiseDisjoint.supIndep fun x hx y hy h ↦       disjoint_left.mpr fun z hz1 hz2 ↦         h (by             rw [mem_coe, mem_image] at hx hy             obtain ⟨Q, hQ, rfl⟩ := hx             obtain ⟨R, hR, rfl⟩ := hy             suffices h' : Q = R by               subst h'               exact of_eq_true (eq_self (                 filter (fun i ↦ ∀ (t : Finset α), t ∈ F → (t ∈ Q ↔ i ∈ t)) s))             rw [id, mem_filter] at hz1 hz2             rw [mem_powerset] at hQ hR             ext i             refine ⟨fun hi ↦ ?_, fun hi ↦ ?_⟩             · rwa [hz2.2 _ (hQ hi), ← hz1.2 _ (hQ hi)]             · rwa [hz1.2 _ (hR hi), ← hz2.2 _ (hR hi)]))     (by       refine (Finset.sup_le fun t ht ↦ ?_).antisymm fun a ha ↦ ?_       · rw [mem_image] at ht         obtain ⟨A, _, rfl⟩ := ht         exact s.filter_subset _       · rw [mem_sup]         refine           ⟨s.filter fun i ↦ ∀ t, t ∈ F → ((t ∈ F.filter fun u ↦ a ∈ u) ↔ i ∈ t),             mem_image_of_mem _ (mem_powerset.2 <| filter_subset _ _),             mem_filter.2 ⟨ha, fun t ht ↦ ?_⟩⟩         rw [mem_filter]         exact and_iff_right ht)

explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.
explanatories.Finset.sup: This definition describes a function that computes the supremum of the images of elements from a finite set under a given function, using a specific order structure that includes a least element.
explanatories.Equiv.toOrderIso: This defines a construction that transforms an equivalence between two preordered types into an order isomorphism if both the forward and inverse mappings are monotone.
explanatories.Finset.sup_le: This theorem asserts that if every image of the elements in a finite set under a given function is less than or equal to a specified upper bound, then the supremum of those images does not exceed that upper bound.
explanatories.Set.mem_toFinset: This theorem states that an element belongs to a finite set if and only if it belongs to the corresponding set representation.
explanatories.exists_supIrred_decomposition: In a well-founded lattice, every element can be expressed as the supremum of a finite set of sup-irreducible elements.
explanatories.Finset.le_sup_of_le: If an element from a finite set is mapped to a value by a function and that value is greater than or equal to another element, then this other element is also less than or equal to the supremum of all images from that set under the function.
explanatories.Finset.le_sup: For any element in a finite set, its image under a function is less than or equal to the supremum of all images of elements in that set.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.SupIrred.supPrime: If an element in a distributive lattice is sup-irreducible, then it is also sup-prime.
explanatories.SupPrime.le_finset_sup: A sup-prime element in a partially ordered set is less than or equal to the supremum of a finite set if and only if it is less than or equal to at least one of the elements in that set.
explanatories.LowerSet.lower: The set represented by a lower set structure contains only elements that are less than or equal to every element within that set.
explanatories.le_trans': A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Finset.sup_mono: This theorem asserts that if one finite set is a subset of another, then the supremum of the images of the first set under a given function is less than or equal to the supremum of the images of the second set under the same function.
explanatories.Set.toFinset_mono: This theorem asserts that if one finite set is a subset of another, then its corresponding finite representation will also be a subset of the finite representation of the larger set.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Sup.sup: A function that computes the least upper bound of two elements in a set or lattice structure.

Filter.IsCobounded.code: Filter.IsCobounded.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (r : α → α → Prop) (f : Filter α) : Prop
Filter.IsCobounded.comment:
`IsCobounded (≺) f` states that the filter `f` does not tend to infinity w.r.t. `≺`. This is
also called frequently bounded. Will be usually instantiated with `≤` or `≥`.

There is a subtlety in this definition: we want `f.IsCobounded` to hold for any `f` in the case of
complete lattices. This will be relevant to deduce theorems on complete lattices from their
versions on conditionally complete lattices with additional assumptions. We have to be careful in
the edge case of the trivial filter containing the empty set: the other natural definition
  `¬ ∀ a, ∀ᶠ n in f, a ≤ n`
would not work as well in this case.
Filter.IsCobounded.fullDefinition: def IsCobounded (r : α → α → Prop) (f : Filter α) :=   ∃ b, ∀ a, (∀ᶠ x in f, r x a) → r b a
Filter.IsCobounded.description: A filter is considered frequently bounded if it does not diverge to infinity with respect to a specified relation.

Filter.tacticIsBoundedDefault.comment:
Filters are automatically bounded or cobounded in complete lattices. To use the same statements
in complete and conditionally complete lattices but let automation fill automatically the
boundedness proofs in complete lattices, we use the tactic `isBoundedDefault` in the statements,
in the form `(hf : f.IsBounded (≥) := by isBoundedDefault)`.

explanatories.Bot.bot: A function that retrieves the bottom element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.Top.top: A function that retrieves the top element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.Filter.isCobounded_le_of_bot: The theorem states that the filter is co-bounded above if the defined relationship indicates that all elements are less than or equal to a specific bound within the context of a preordered set with a least element.
explanatories.Filter.isCobounded_ge_of_top: A filter is considered frequently bounded above if it is bounded by the largest element in an ordered set.
explanatories.Filter.isBounded_le_of_top: A filter is eventually bounded from below when the elements are constrained by a specified upper limit.
explanatories.Filter.isBounded_ge_of_bot: A filter is bounded if all its elements are greater than or equal to some lower bound.
explanatories.Lean.Parser.Category.tactic: The tactic category in Lean represents the syntax for proof tactics that operate on the context of hypotheses to construct terms of the expected type following the `by` keyword in proofs.

Filter.tacticIsBoundedDefault.fullDefinition: macro "isBoundedDefault" : tactic =>   `(tactic| first     | apply isCobounded_le_of_bot     | apply isCobounded_ge_of_top     | apply isBounded_le_of_top     | apply isBounded_ge_of_bot     | assumption)
Filter.tacticIsBoundedDefault.description: This refers to a tactic used in complete lattices that automatically proves the boundedness of filters when using statements involving such filters.

Filter.liminf_reparam.code:
Filter.liminf_reparam.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_4} {ι' : Type u_5} [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α]
  (f : ι → α) (s : ι' → Set ι) (p : ι' → Prop) [Countable (Subtype p)] [Nonempty (Subtype p)] (j : Subtype p) :
  Subtype p
Filter.liminf_reparam.comment:
Given an indexed family of sets `s j` over `j : Subtype p` and a function `f`, then
`liminf_reparam j` is equal to `j` if `f` is bounded below on `s j`, and otherwise to some
index `k` such that `f` is bounded below on `s k` (if there exists one).
To ensure good measurability behavior, this index `k` is chosen as the minimal suitable index.
This function is used to write down a liminf in a measurable way,
in `Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_ciSup_ciInf` and `Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_ite`.

Filter.liminf_reparam.fullDefinition: noncomputable def liminf_reparam     (f : ι → α) (s : ι' → Set ι) (p : ι' → Prop) [Countable (Subtype p)] [Nonempty (Subtype p)]     (j : Subtype p) : Subtype p :=   let m : Set (Subtype p) := {j | BddBelow (range (fun (i : s j) ↦ f i))}   let g : ℕ → Subtype p := (exists_surjective_nat _).choose   have Z : ∃ n, g n ∈ m ∨ ∀ j, j ∉ m := by     by_cases H : ∃ j, j ∈ m     · rcases H with ⟨j, hj⟩       rcases (exists_surjective_nat (Subtype p)).choose_spec j with ⟨n, rfl⟩       exact ⟨n, Or.inl hj⟩     · push_neg at H       exact ⟨0, Or.inr H⟩   if j ∈ m then j else g (Nat.find Z)
Filter.liminf_reparam.description: This definition describes a reparameterization of the limit inferior for a function indexed by a family of sets, returning an index where the function is bounded below, specifically choosing the minimal suitable index if such an index exists.

Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_ciSup_ciInf.code:
Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_ciSup_ciInf.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_4} {ι' : Type u_5}
  [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] {v : Filter ι} {p : ι' → Prop} {s : ι' → Set ι} [Countable (Subtype p)]
  [Nonempty (Subtype p)] (hv : v.HasBasis p s) {f : ι → α} (hs : ∀ (j : Subtype p), (s ↑j).Nonempty)
  (H : ∃ j, BddBelow (range fun i => f ↑i)) : liminf f v = ⨆ j, ⨅ i, f ↑i
Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_ciSup_ciInf.comment:
Writing a liminf as a supremum of infimum, in a (possibly non-complete) conditionally complete
linear order. A reparametrization trick is needed to avoid taking the infimum of sets which are
not bounded below.

Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_ite.code:

krullDim.code: krullDim.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [Preorder α] : WithBot (WithTop ℕ)
krullDim.comment:
The **Krull dimension** of a preorder `α` is the supremum of the rightmost index of all relation
series of `α` order by `<`. If there is no series `a₀ < a₁ < ... < aₙ` in `α`, then its Krull
dimension is defined to be negative infinity; if the length of all series `a₀ < a₁ < ... < aₙ` is
unbounded, its Krull dimension is defined to be positive infinity.

explanatories.WithBot: This defines a type that includes a least element, denoted by a bottom element.
explanatories.WithTop: This definition creates a new type that extends a given type by adding a greatest element.
explanatories.LTSeries: A less than series is a specific type of relation series that arises from the less than relation in a preorder context.

krullDim.fullDefinition: noncomputable def krullDim : WithBot (WithTop ℕ) :=   ⨆ (p : LTSeries α), p.length
krullDim.description: The Krull dimension of a preorder is defined as the supremum of the lengths of all strictly increasing sequences within that preorder, with specific provisions for cases of no sequences or unbounded lengths, assigning negative infinity and positive infinity, respectively.

height.comment: Height of an element `a` of a preordered set `α` is the Krull dimension of the subset `(-∞, a]`

explanatories.WithBot: This defines a type that includes a least element, denoted by a bottom element.
explanatories.WithTop: This definition creates a new type that extends a given type by adding a greatest element.

explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.

height.fullDefinition: noncomputable def height (a : α) : WithBot (WithTop ℕ) := krullDim (Set.Iic a)
height.description: The height of an element in a preordered set is defined as the Krull dimension of the subset consisting of all elements less than or equal to that element.

krullDim_le_of_strictMono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β)
  (hf : StrictMono f) : krullDim α ≤ krullDim β

explanatories.StrictMono: A function is considered strictly monotone if it maintains the order relationship such that whenever one input is strictly less than another, the output corresponding to the first input is also strictly less than the output corresponding to the second input.

krullDim_le_of_strictMono.description: The Krull dimension of one preorder is less than or equal to that of another if there exists a strictly monotonic function mapping elements from the first preorder to the second.

krullDim_eq_length_of_finiteDimensionalO.description: The Krull dimension of a preorder is equal to the length of the longest strictly increasing sequence in that preorder when it possesses a finite dimensional structure.

explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.And.left: From a conjunction of two propositions, it is possible to extract and prove the first proposition.
explanatories.And.right: This theorem allows for the extraction of the second component from a conjunction when given a proof of that conjunction.
explanatories.Bot.bot: A function that retrieves the bottom element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.sSup_compact_le_eq: In a complete lattice that is compactly generated, the supremum of all compact elements less than or equal to a given element equals that element.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Set.Subset.trans: The transitive property of set inclusion states that if one set is included in a second set, and that second set is included in a third set, then the first set is also included in the third set.
explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_mk: This theorem shows that the value of an element formed by a subtype is equal to the underlying value itself when the property is satisfied.
explanatories.CompleteLattice.Iic_coatomic_of_compact_: In a complete lattice, if an element is compact, then the interval below that element contains maximal elements, making it coatomic.
explanatories.sSup_eq_bot: This theorem states that the supremum of a set is the least element if and only if all elements of the set are equal to that least element.
explanatories.Set.not_subset: The assertion that a set is not a subset of another is equivalent to the existence of at least one element in the first set that is not contained in the second set.
explanatories.isAtomic_iff_isCoatomic: In a modular complemented lattice, an atomic structure is equivalent to a coatomic structure.
explanatories.IsAtomic.eq_bot_or_exists_atom_le: Every element in a poset with a least element is either the least element itself or has an atom that is less than or equal to it.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.
explanatories.Subtype.ext_iff: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their corresponding values in the underlying set are equal.
explanatories.Set.Iic.coe_bot: The bottom element of a preorder structure corresponds to the least element represented by the given value.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_le_coe: A theorem stating that in a partially ordered set, the comparison of elements represented as subtypes depends directly on the comparison of their underlying values.
explanatories.IsAtom.of_isAtom_coe_Iic: If an element within a certain lower interval is an atom, then its corresponding element in the larger space also qualifies as an atom.

isAtomic_of_complementedLattice.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) isAtomic_of_complementedLattice [ComplementedLattice α] : IsAtomic α :=   ⟨fun b => by     by_cases h : { c : α | CompleteLattice.IsCompactElement c ∧ c ≤ b } ⊆ {⊥}     · left       rw [← sSup_compact_le_eq b, sSup_eq_bot]       exact h     · rcases Set.not_subset.1 h with ⟨c, ⟨hc, hcb⟩, hcbot⟩       right       have hc' := CompleteLattice.Iic_coatomic_of_compact_element hc       rw [← isAtomic_iff_isCoatomic] at hc'       haveI := hc'       obtain con | ⟨a, ha, hac⟩ := eq_bot_or_exists_atom_le (⟨c, le_refl c⟩ : Set.Iic c)       · exfalso         apply hcbot         simp only [Subtype.ext_iff, Set.Iic.coe_bot, Subtype.coe_mk] at con         exact con       rw [← Subtype.coe_le_coe, Subtype.coe_mk] at hac       exact ⟨a, ha.of_isAtom_coe_Iic, hac.trans hcb⟩⟩

isAtomistic_of_complementedLattice.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) isAtomistic_of_complementedLattice [ComplementedLattice α] :     IsAtomistic α :=   ⟨fun b =>     ⟨{ a | IsAtom a ∧ a ≤ b }, by       symm       have hle : sSup { a : α | IsAtom a ∧ a ≤ b } ≤ b := sSup_le fun _ => And.right       apply (lt_or_eq_of_le hle).resolve_left _       intro con       obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_isCompl (⟨sSup { a : α | IsAtom a ∧ a ≤ b }, hle⟩ : Set.Iic b)       obtain rfl | ⟨a, ha, hac⟩ := eq_bot_or_exists_atom_le c       · exact ne_of_lt con (Subtype.ext_iff.1 (eq_top_of_isCompl_bot hc))       · apply ha.1         rw [eq_bot_iff]         apply le_trans (le_inf _ hac) hc.disjoint.le_bot         rw [← Subtype.coe_le_coe, Subtype.coe_mk]         exact le_sSup ⟨ha.of_isAtom_coe_Iic, a.2⟩, fun _ => And.left⟩⟩

Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.IsBadSeq.comment:
In the context of partial well-orderings, a bad sequence is a nonincreasing sequence
whose range is contained in a particular set `s`. One exists if and only if `s` is not
partially well-ordered.
Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.IsBadSeq.fullDefinition: def IsBadSeq (r : α → α → Prop) (s : Set α) (f : ℕ → α) : Prop :=   (∀ n, f n ∈ s) ∧ ∀ m n : ℕ, m < n → ¬r (f m) (f n)
Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.IsBadSeq.description: This definition describes a bad sequence as a nonincreasing sequence that exists within a set if and only if the set is not partially well-ordered under a given relation.

Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.IsMinBadSeq.comment:

Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.IsMinBadSeq.description: This definition describes a condition under which every bad sequence that coincides with a given sequence in its first few terms has a rank that is at least as great as the rank of the corresponding term in the original sequence.

Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.partiallyWell.code:
Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.partiallyWellOrderedOn_sublistForall₂.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} (r : α → α → Prop) [IsRefl α r]
  [IsTrans α r] {s : Set α} (h : s.PartiallyWellOrderedOn r) :
  {l | ∀ x ∈ l, x ∈ s}.PartiallyWellOrderedOn (List.SublistForall₂ r)
Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.partiallyWell.comment:
Higman's Lemma, which states that for any reflexive, transitive relation `r` which is
partially well-ordered on a set `s`, the relation `List.SublistForall₂ r` is partially
well-ordered on the set of lists of elements of `s`. That relation is defined so that
`List.SublistForall₂ r l₁ l₂` whenever `l₁` related pointwise by `r` to a sublist of `l₂`.
Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.partiallyWell.description: This theorem shows that if a set is partially well-ordered under a reflexive and transitive relation, then every subset of that set, viewed through the relation on lists, is also partially well-ordered.

Pi.isPWO.comment:
A version of **Dickson's lemma** any subset of functions `Π s : σ, α s` is partially well
ordered, when `σ` is a `Fintype` and each `α s` is a linear well order.
This includes the classical case of Dickson's lemma that `ℕ ^ n` is a well partial order.
Some generalizations would be possible based on this proof, to include cases where the target is
partially well ordered, and also to consider the case of `Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn` instead of
`Set.IsPWO`.

explanatories.Set.mem_inter_iff: An element is a member of the intersection of two sets if and only if it is a member of both sets.
explanatories.Set.mem_union: An element belongs to the union of two sets if and only if it belongs to at least one of those sets.

IsCompactlyGenerated.BooleanGenerators.d.fullDefinition: def distribLattice_of_sSup_eq_top (h : sSup S = ⊤) : DistribLattice α where   le_sup_inf a b c := by     obtain ⟨Ta, hTa, rfl⟩ := hS.atomistic a (h ▸ le_top)     obtain ⟨Tb, hTb, rfl⟩ := hS.atomistic b (h ▸ le_top)     obtain ⟨Tc, hTc, rfl⟩ := hS.atomistic c (h ▸ le_top)     apply le_of_eq     rw [← sSup_union, ← sSup_union, ← hS.sSup_inter hTb hTc, ← hS.sSup_inter, ← sSup_union]     on_goal 1 => congr 1; ext     all_goals       simp only [Set.union_subset_iff, Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_union]       tauto
